items.title_orig: Joint Statement by the Patriarchs and Heads of Churches in Syria
items.sum:
Është me shqetësim të madh dhe indinjatë të thellë që kemi ndjekur dhe vazhdojmë të ndjekim, një sërë sulmesh të tmerrshme e të përsëritura që synojnë popullin sirian dhe veçanërisht të krishterët. Herë pas here, kemi ngritur zërat tanë dhe vazhdojmë ta bëjmë këtë, pasi kjo valë sulmesh ka vazhduar pa ndërprerje. Duke pasur parasysh autoritetet kompetente, të cilat nuk ja dolën të sigurojnë sigurinë dhe mbrojtjen në përgjigje të asaj që ka ndodhur dhe vazhdojnë të ndodhin, këto sulme janë përshkallëzuar edhe një herë në ditët e fundit, duke arritur në objektivin e kryepeshkopit Juhanna Abdo Arbanesh të arqipeshkopit katolik grek Melkit të Homsit, Hama, Al-Nabk, Jabroudit dhe Dpolesë së tyre.

MOR IGNATIUS APHREM II Patriark orthodhoks siriak i Antiokisë dhe i gjithë Lindjes dhe Kreu Suprem i Kishës Orthodhokse Universale të Siriakut
items.text_orig:
It is with grave concern and profound indignation that we have followed, and continue to follow, a series of heinous and recurring attacks targeting the Syrian people, and Christians in particular. Time and again, we have raised our voices, and we continue to do so, as this wave of attacks has persisted without interruption. These attacks are not, and have never been, isolated incidents. What has happened, and continues to happen, in many places, including most recently in Al-Suqaylabiyah, in the form of systematic assaults and kidnappings carried out for exorbitant ransom payments, constitutes a violation of the most basic human rights, as evidenced by the video showing the brutal torture of the jeweler Maher Sankari. In view of the competent authorities’ failure to provide security and protection in response to what has occurred and continues to occur, these attacks have once again escalated in recent days, culminating in the targeting of Archbishop Youhanna Abdo Arbash of the Melkite Greek Catholic Archdiocese of Homs, Hama, Al-Nabk, Yabroud, and their Dependencies. He was bound, blindfolded, and gagged, while his office was ransacked. The recurrence of these incidents, without any response or tangible results on the part of the authorities, confronts us, and public opinion alike, with a grave question regarding the future of Christians in this country. We condemn, in the strongest possible terms, what has occurred and continues to unfold. Once again, we raise our voices to demand an end to these attacks, and we call upon the competent authorities to fulfill their responsibilities, conduct the necessary investigations, and communicate their findings to us. Christians are not to be treated as easy targets for attack or as scapegoats. They will continue to maintain the closest possible relations with their Muslim brothers and sisters, on the basis of full and equal citizenship. May God protect Syria and preserve within it civil peace, a peace that must be safeguarded above all else.

JOHN X Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Antioch and All the East

MOR IGNATIUS APHREM II Syriac Orthodox Patriarch of Antioch and All the East, and Supreme Head of the Universal Syriac Orthodox Church

YOUSSEF I ABSI Melkite Greek Catholic Patriarch of Antioch and All the East

items.title_orig: Inaugural Archpastoral visit of Archbishop of Canada to the Holy Trinity Community in London Ontario
items.sum:
Të dielën, më 15 nëntor 2026, e diela tetë e Lukës dhe dita e parë e agjërimit të lindjes së Krishtit, kryepeshkopi Apostolos i Kanadasë bëri vizitën e tij të përuruar kryepastorale në Bashkësinë e Shenjtë Orthodhokse Greke të Londrës dhe Vikinitetit.

Kryepeshkopi Apostolos u mirëprit nga prifti drejtues i famullisë, Protopresbyter Konstantinos Çatis, presidenti i Këshillit të Bashkësisë Peter Çelonis, anëtarë të Këshillit dhe besnikë të komunitetit.

Kryepeshkopi Apostolos kryesoi Orthrosin dhe festoi Liturgjinë Hyjnore të Perëndisë në Kishën e Shenjtë Orthodhokse Greke.

Kryepeshkopi falenderoi Protopresbyter Konstantinos Chatzis për ministrinë e tij të përkushtuar ndaj komunitetit dhe për kontributin e tij në trainimin liturgjik të seminarëve në Akademinë Teologjike Patriarkale të Torontos.

Fëmijët nga shkolla greke dhe shkolla e së dielës, së bashku me të rinjtë nga komuniteti, të rinjtë dhe programet e kërcimit, paraqitën arkipeshkopin Apostolos me një kartë përkujtimore që përmban fotografi dhe përshëndetje.

Një drekë banketi për nder të kryepeshkopit Apostolos pasoi Qendrën e Bashkësisë Helenike. Hapësira u quajt kryepeshkopi Apostolos Atrium në nderim të kryepeshkopit të Rilindjes për të përuruar vizitën arkeologjike në Bashkësinë e Shenjtë Orthodhokse Greke të Londrës dhe Vikinitetit më 15 nëntor 2026.

Kryepeshkopi Apostolos falenderoi priftin e famullisë, komitetin organizator, Këshillin e Komunitetit, Motërsinë Filoptos dhe vullnetarët që ndihmuan në përgatitjen për vizitën.
items.text_orig:
On Sunday, November 15, 2026, the Eighth Sunday of Luke and the first day of the Nativity Fast, Archbishop Apostolos of Canada made his inaugural archpastoral visit to the Holy Trinity Greek Orthodox Community of London and Vicinity.

Archbishop Apostolos was welcomed by the parish’s presiding priest, Protopresbyter Konstantinos Chatzis, Community Council President Peter Chelonis, members of the Council, and the faithful of the community. Peter Fragiskatos, Member of Parliament for London Centre, was also in attendance.

Archbishop Apostolos presided at Orthros and celebrated the Hierarchical Divine Liturgy at Holy Trinity Greek Orthodox Church. More than 800 people gathered for the services, and many families came with their children.

In his homily, the Archbishop reflected on the Parable of the Good Samaritan (Luke 10:25–37). Drawing on the Lord’s words, “Go and do likewise,” he emphasized that we become neighbours to those in need by showing them mercy through our actions, regardless of where they come from or how they are connected to us. Linking the message of the parable to the beginning of the Nativity Fast, he called on the faithful to prepare for the Feast of the Nativity of Christ through prayer, forgiveness, and care for those facing hardship.

Addressing children and young people in particular, the Archbishop encouraged them to read Holy Scripture daily, make the sign of the Cross with reverence, and take an active part in the life of the Church. He encouraged parents to read the Gospel with their children and called on the community to support its Greek school, Sunday school, and youth programmes. He also spoke of the respect and care we owe our parents and grandparents. As he emphasized, the value of an offering before God is measured by the love with which it is given.

𝗣𝗿𝗮𝘆𝗲𝗿𝘀 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝗦𝗲𝗿𝘃𝗶𝗰𝗲 𝗶𝗻 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗛𝗼𝗹𝘆 𝗔𝗹𝘁𝗮𝗿 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗚𝗶𝗳𝘁𝘀 𝗳𝗿𝗼𝗺 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗖𝗼𝗺𝗺𝘂𝗻𝗶𝘁𝘆

Following the Divine Liturgy, Archbishop Apostolos read the prayer over six boys for their service at the Holy Altar. He invited the faithful to pray for them and expressed the hope that one of the boys, should he discern a vocation to the priesthood, might study at the Patriarchal Toronto Orthodox Theological Academy and one day serve the Church as a priest. In a separate prayer, Hirësia e Tij read the prayer for a reader over another boy.

The Archbishop thanked Protopresbyter Konstantinos Chatzis for his devoted ministry to the community and for his contribution to the liturgical training of seminarians at the Patriarchal Toronto Orthodox Theological Academy. He also thanked the chanters, the choir, the altar servers, and the girls who welcomed him dressed in white as the Myrrhbearers.

In his remarks, Fr. Konstantinos welcomed Hirësia e Tij on behalf of the community and spoke of the Archbishop’s initiatives for young people, scholarships for seminarians, and recognition of the service of the National Philoptochos Sisterhood. The faithful expressed their affection for the Archbishop with the acclamation “Axios!” (“Worthy!”).

Children from the Greek school and Sunday school, together with young people from the community’s youth and dance programmes, presented Archbishop Apostolos with a commemorative card containing photographs and greetings. The President and members of the Community Council then presented him, on behalf of the community, with an epitrachelion and an omophorion. The Archbishop thanked them warmly and said that whenever he wore these vestments, he would pray for the faithful of the community. The gathering in the church concluded with the distribution of antidoron and commemorative icons.

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗕𝗮𝗻𝗾𝘂𝗲𝘁 𝗟𝘂𝗻𝗰𝗵𝗲𝗼𝗻 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗗𝗲𝗱𝗶𝗰𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗼𝗳 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗔𝘁𝗿𝗶𝘂𝗺

A banquet luncheon in honour of Archbishop Apostolos followed at the Hellenic Community Centre. The third presentation of the day took place during the luncheon: the dedication of the Centre’s atrium. The space was named the Archbishop Apostolos Atrium in honour of the Archbishop’s inaugural archpastoral visit to the Holy Trinity Greek Orthodox Community of London and Vicinity on November 15, 2026.

Archbishop Apostolos thanked the parish priest, the organizing committee, the Community Council, the Philoptochos Sisterhood, and the volunteers who helped prepare for the visit. Special thanks were extended to Peter Chelonis and Bill Panopoulos of Accolade Consulting Group Inc. for their sponsorship of the luncheon.

items.title_orig: 710 more children join the Georgian Patriarch’s spiritual family
items.sum:
Më 15 nëntor 2026, ceremonia e 75-të e pagëzimit në grupin e 75-të për familjet e treta dhe të mëvonshme, me Catholicos-Patriark të të gjithë Gjeorgjisë që shërbejnë si kumbarë, u zhvillua në Katedralen Patriarkale të Trinitetit të Shenjtë në Tbilisi.

items.text_orig:
On November 15, 2026, the 75th group baptism ceremony for families’ third and subsequent children, with the Catholicos-Patriarch of All Georgia serving as their godfather, took place at the Holy Trinity Patriarchal Cathedral in Tbilisi.

A further 710 children were added to the spiritual family of the Primate of the Georgian Orthodox Church.

After the group baptisms, Patriarch Shio III arrived at the Holy Trinity Patriarchal Cathedral, where he blessed his spiritual children.

In his address, the Patriarch extended his best wishes to the parents of the newly baptized children, their godparents, and the entire Georgian people on this special day. He also spoke about the Sacrament of Baptism and its significance for the salvation of humankind, before once again blessing his spiritual children.

Finally, commemorative crosses were distributed to the newly baptized children. The crosses had been specially crafted to mark the 1,700th anniversary of the proclamation of Christianity as the official religion of the Georgian state.

Photos: Nino Sozashvili

items.title: Patriarch of Romania on the 20th Anniversary of the Implementation of the Law on Religious Communities
items.summary: On Monday, Patriarch Daniel of Romania delivered a message on the occasion of the international legal symposium entitled “Two Decades of Implementation of Law No. 489/2006”, which is being held at the Patriarchal Palace. The message was presented by Bishop Varlaam of Ploiești…
items.text:
On Monday, Patriarch Daniel of Romania delivered a message on the occasion of the international legal symposium entitled “Two Decades of Implementation of Law No. 489/2006”, which is being held at the Patriarchal Palace.

The message was presented by Bishop Varlaam of Ploiești and Patriarchal Vicar.

“Law No. 489/2006 on Religious Freedom and the General Regime of Religious Denominations is founded on three fundamental pillars of the modern legal understanding of religious affairs: religious freedom in both its individual and collective dimensions (including collective religious organization), the religious neutrality of the State, and the autonomy of recognized religious denominations.

Through this law, the Romanian State sought to highlight the religious, cultural and legal distinctiveness of recognized religious denominations, acknowledging their spiritual, educational, social, charitable and cultural roles, as well as their contribution to social harmony,” the Patriarch stated.

The symposium programme includes several sessions of presentations, which will conclude on Tuesday.

Read below the Message of Patriarch Daniel of Romania

The Religious Neutrality of the State and the Autonomy of Recognized Religious Denominations in Romania

An Assessment of Twenty Years of Implementation of Law No. 489/2006

Today, Romania is the only European country with a population of Latin origin, a Romance language and an Orthodox Christian faith. This distinctive character of Romania as a European country with a Romance language and an Orthodox Christian tradition has also influenced the way in which relations between Church and State are understood and regulated.

As a modern state (1859–2026), Romania has experienced various forms of political organization, including constitutional monarchy, military dictatorship, people’s and socialist republics and, today, pluralistic democracy. In Romania, religious freedom and the forms of its collective exercise through the organization of religious communities are regulated by Law No. 489/2006, which was promulgated on 26 December 2006.

Law No. 489/2006 on Religious Freedom and the General Regime of Religious Denominations is founded on three fundamental pillars of the modern legal understanding of religious affairs: religious freedom in both its individual and collective dimensions (including collective religious organization), the religious neutrality of the State, and the autonomy of recognized religious denominations.

About ensuring and protecting religious freedom as exercised collectively or through the establishment of organized communities, the legislation currently in force provides for three levels of recognition of religious communities, each corresponding to a different degree of public responsibility:

The first level is provisional and concerns religious groups, which take the form of associations without legal personality.

The second level is intermediate and concerns religious associations, which are legal entities governed by private law.

The third level is definitive and concerns legally recognized religious denominations, which are private-law legal entities serving the public benefit.

In this way, the Romanian State sought to highlight the religious, cultural and legal distinctiveness of recognized religious denominations. Law No. 489/2006 acknowledges their “spiritual, educational, social, charitable and cultural roles, as well as their capacity to contribute to social harmony” (Article 7, paragraph 1). It also recognizes “the important role of the Romanian Orthodox Church and of the other Churches and recognized religious denominations in Romania’s national history and in the life of Romanian society” (Article 7, paragraph 2).

Recognized religious denominations are not merely private entities established through the expression of the will of a number of founding members. Owing to their historical distinctiveness, the legislator classifies them as private-law legal entities serving the public benefit.

Their recognition as entities serving the public benefit ope legis (that is, by operation of law, as an immediate consequence of the law from the moment they acquire the status of a recognized religious denomination) does not constitute a political concession. Rather, it is a legal acknowledgment of the fact that recognized religious denominations in Romania have consistently demonstrated stability, predictability, and reliability over time, while fulfilling a fundamental social function: shaping collective identities, safeguarding the nation’s cultural and moral heritage, and providing spiritual and social support.

The sacred property of recognized religious denominations is protected, subject to strict conditions, by special provisions establishing its exemption from seizure and immunity from prescription. This constitutes a far more protective legal regime than the one applicable to the property of an ordinary association.

Furthermore, recognized religious denominations have the right to establish theological educational institutions; provide spiritual and religious care within the armed forces and other services operating under special regimes, as well as in hospitals and correctional facilities; and benefit from tax concessions.

At the same time, the Romanian State guarantees recognized religious denominations the right to organize and operate in accordance with their own Statutes, which, once approved by the competent public authorities, are also binding before the civil courts, within the limits of their internal autonomy.

Law No. 54 of 30 April 2026, which amended and supplemented Law No. 489/2006, includes provisions that apply exclusively to recognized religious denominations. These provisions protect the rights and identity of their clergy and safeguard their exclusive authority over religious forms of veneration and devotion directed towards persons who have been canonized as saints, declared blessed or venerable, enrolled among the righteous, or recognized as symbols of their distinctive identity.

All these rights, which are provided for under Romanian legislation and apply exclusively to recognized religious denominations, constitute the defining elements of their autonomy vis-à-vis the State and other public and private entities.

In this context, it is worth highlighting a mistake that occasionally occurs in public discourse but is unacceptable in academic circles: the semantic and legal conflation of a recognized religious denomination with a religious association.

From a legal standpoint, a religious association is a legal entity governed partly by special provisions that derogate from the general law governing associations and foundations (Government Ordinance No. 26/2000). It represents merely an intermediate stage in the organizational development of a religious community.

For this reason, the legislator has established clear requirements concerning stability (an uninterrupted presence on Romanian territory for at least 12 years) and representativeness (a membership amounting to at least 0.1% of the country’s population) for religious associations seeking to obtain the status of a recognized religious denomination.

The distinction between these two forms of religious organization is also reflected in the fact that, under Law No. 489/2006, only recognized religious denominations are entitled to the following forms of cooperation and relations with the State:

Institutional dialogue.

Social partnership.

Cooperation in areas of common interest.

On the basis of these specific legislative provisions, and at the initiative of the Romanian Patriarchate, the Consultative Council of Religious Denominations in Romania was established on 14 April 2011.

This is an autonomous, apolitical, non-governmental, non-profit moral body without legal personality. Its purpose is to articulate common positions on policies and action programmes in the fields of social welfare, healthcare, education and culture at regional, national and international levels, as well as to safeguard the religious and cultural identity of communities in the diaspora.

Over the years, the Consultative Council of Religious Denominations in Romania has held numerous meetings and published a series of statements and declarations addressing contemporary issues, thereby contributing to the resolution of matters of national importance.

At the same time, Romania’s recognized religious denominations have concluded agreements and cooperation protocols with various public institutions in the country in areas of common interest.

On the basis of these joint agreements, the recognized religious denominations, in cooperation with and with the support of public authorities, have established, organized and developed social, educational and cultural activities and institutions that actively contribute to the stability, social cohesion and development of Romanian society. In this way, recognized religious denominations serve as genuine pillars of stability and support, providing religious and social care within local communities.

Throughout the two decades of implementation of Law No. 489/2006, the Romanian State has sought to uphold its religious neutrality within the limits established by the Constitution and the legislation in force.

As a result, Romania has, by and large, avoided confusion and discrimination in the State’s relations with religious communities, while maintaining a clear distinction between the legal status of religious associations and that of recognized religious denominations.

Furthermore, the Romanian State has generally sought to guarantee and protect the autonomy of recognized religious denominations, as defined by the Constitution, legislation and their respective Statutes.

However, the autonomy of recognized religious denominations does not imply indifference, isolation or confrontation with public authorities. On the contrary, the Romanian State provides direct and indirect support to these denominations and cooperates with them for the benefit of Romanian society.

We may therefore conclude that, in general terms, the dynamics of relations between public authorities and religious denominations in Romania are shaped by the balance between the religious neutrality of the State and the autonomy of recognized religious denominations.

This framework of relations constitutes what is now known as the “Romanian model”. From time to time, it may require clarification and legislative amendments in order to protect the identity of each recognized religious denomination and promote social harmony.

In conclusion, we extend our congratulations to the organizers of this international legal symposium, the National Union of Notaries Public of Romania, to which we are pleased to present, as a token of our appreciation, the Diploma and Medal of the 2026 Year of Homage.

At the same time, we pray that God may bless all those participating in this event, expressing our hope that its proceedings and outcomes will contribute to a more comprehensive and meaningful assessment of the implementation of the Law on Religious Denominations over the past 20 years.

† Daniel

Patriarch of the Romanian Orthodox Church

Source: basilica.ro

items.summary: On November 13th and 14th, 2026, Metropolitan Cleopas of Sweden and All Scandinavia made his tenth pastoral visit to Iceland since assuming his episcopal duties, demonstrating his continued pastoral concern for the Greek community and the Orthodox faithful of this distant island…
items.ex: Më 13 dhe 14 nëntor, 2026, Metropolitan Cleopas i Suedisë dhe i gjithë Skandinavia bënë vizitën e tij të dhjetë baritore në Islandë që kur mori detyrat e tij episkopale, duke treguar shqetësimin e tij të vazhdueshëm baritore për komunitetin grek dhe për besimtarët orthodhoksë të këtij ishulli të largët
items.title_orig: Metropolitan of Sweden’s pastoral visit to Iceland
items.sum:
Më 13 dhe 14 nëntor, 2026, metropolitani Kleopas i Suedisë dhe i gjithë Skandinavia bënë vizitën e tij të dhjetë baritore në Islandë që kur mori detyrat e tij episkopale, duke treguar shqetësimin e tij të vazhdueshëm baritore për komunitetin grek dhe për besnikët orthodhoksë të këtij vendi të largët ishullor.

Si pjesë e vizitës, në greqisht dhe në anglisht, në Kishën Fririkskapella në Rajkjavík, një liturgji hierarkike Hyjnore festohej në gjuhën greke dhe angleze, duke u dhënë mundësi besnikëve të komunitetit shumëkombësh orthodhoks të Islandës të merrnin pjesë më plotësisht dhe të merrnin pjesë në lutje.

Të pranishmit në Liturgjinë Hyjnore përfshinin konsullin e Greqisë në Islandë, Rafn Aleksandër Sigurdson; presidentin e Komunitetit Helenik të Islandës, Eleni Latanioti dhe anëtarë të Këshillit Parish, të cilët nderuan mbledhjen me praninë e tyre.

Në fjalimin e tij, të shpërndarë në greqisht dhe anglisht, metropolitani tha: " Me emocione të thella dhe gëzim frymor, ne mblidhemi mes jush sot këtu në largësi, por megjithatë mirësevini, Reykjavík, Islandë, për të festuar së bashku kujtimin e shenjtë të apostullit të lavdishëm Filip.

Këtu sot, në këtë cep verior të Evropës, mendojmë se zemra e orthodhoksisë rreh me të njëjtën forcë dhe dashuri që bën në Kostandinopojë, Greqi dhe në çdo vend ku rrëfehet emri i Krishtit.

Kisha e Kostandinopojës, nën drejtimin e nderuar shpirtëror të patriarkut tonë ekumenik, Tersehenteria e Tij Bartolomeut, shërben pikërisht në këtë mision universal; për të sjellë dritën e Ungjillit në çdo vend dhe për të përqafuar çdo person, pavarësisht nga origjina kombëtare, gjuha ose kultura.

Ju i përkasin familjes së madhe frymore të Metropolisit të Shenjtë të Suedisë dhe të gjithë Skandinavisë, nën mbrojtjen e Kishës Nënë të Krishtit, Kishës së Madhe të Kostandinopojës.

Gjatë shoqërisë së tij me besimtarët, metropolitan Kleopas shprehu gjithashtu dashurinë e tij atërore dhe kishën lokale, merak të palëkundur për nevojat frymore të besimtarëve orthodhoksë që jetonin në Islandë.
items.text_orig:
On November 13th and 14th, 2026, Metropolitan Cleopas of Sweden and All Scandinavia made his tenth pastoral visit to Iceland since assuming his episcopal duties, demonstrating his continued pastoral concern for the Greek community and the Orthodox faithful of this distant island nation.

Metropolitan Cleopas was accompanied on this pastoral visit by Bishop Bartholomew of Elaia.

As part of the visit, a Hierarchical Divine Liturgy was celebrated in Greek and English at Friðrikskapella Chapel in Reykjavík, enabling the faithful of Iceland’s multinational Orthodox community to participate more fully and share in prayer.

Those in attendance at the Divine Liturgy included Consul of Greece in Iceland, Rafn Alexander Sigurdsson; the President of the Hellenic Community of Iceland, Eleni Latanioti; and members of the Parish Council, all of whom honored the gathering with their presence.

The presence of Sveinn Valgeirsson, Dean of Reykjavík’s historic Dómkirkjan Cathedral of the Evangelical Lutheran Church of Iceland, was especially significant. His attendance offered a further welcome expression of mutual respect, fraternal fellowship, and the strengthening of good relations among the country’s Christian communities.

In his address, delivered in Greek and English, the Metropolitan said: “With deep emotion and spiritual joy, we gather among you today here in distant, yet so welcoming, Reykjavík, Iceland, to celebrate together the sacred memory of the glorious Apostle Philip.

Our gathering today is more than another pastoral visit. It is a blessed opportunity to experience that the Church of Christ knows no geographical boundaries, is not limited by distance, and is not divided by seas and oceans.

Wherever there is faith in the risen Lord, wherever the Eucharist is celebrated, and wherever people gather “in one place” to glorify God, there the whole Church is alive and present.

Here today, in this northern corner of Europe, we feel that the heart of Orthodoxy beats with the same strength and love as it does in Constantinople, in Greece, and in every place where the name of Christ is confessed.

Today’s feast brings us to one of the most moving scenes in the Holy Gospel. The Evangelist John tells us that the Lord met Philip and gave him a brief but decisive invitation: “Follow Me” (John 1:44).

Only two words, yet they changed a man’s entire life. Philip encounters Christ, and that encounter becomes the beginning of a new life. He leaves his former path behind and follows the Lord. He does not yet know the hardships, persecutions, and sacrifices that apostolic ministry will bring, but he knows that he has found the One who gives meaning to human existence.

The Apostle Philip teaches us something else as well. As soon as he comes to know Christ, he does not keep this joy to himself. He seeks out Nathanael and tells him: “We have found the One about whom Moses wrote in the Law and the prophets also wrote—Jesus” (John 1:46).

Philip does not say, “I learned,” but “we have found.” He speaks of a discovery that fills his heart.

When Nathanael expresses his reservation, Philip answers with three simple words: “Come and see” (John 1:47). This invitation is the theology of mission.

This apostolic invitation takes on special meaning here in Iceland. In a country marked by the grandeur of nature—with its volcanoes, glaciers, vast distances, and long winters—the presence of an Orthodox parish is a meaningful witness to the faith.

In a world often tested by loneliness and a turning away from spiritual values, the parish is called to become a place of encounter, an open embrace offering the experience of a spiritual family.

At the same time, our parish is not called to be a closed community, limited to those who share the same heritage or speak the same language. Orthodoxy is universal. The Church of Constantinople, under the revered spiritual guidance of our Ecumenical Patriarch, Tërëshenjtëria e Tij Bartholomew, serves precisely this universal mission; to bring the light of the Gospel to every place and embrace every person, regardless of national origin, language, or culture.

Today I would especially like to address you, who make up this living church community. We know that sustaining parish life in a place so far from the great centers of Orthodoxy is not always easy. There are practical challenges, long distances, work commitments, and, at times, a sense that you are few in number. Yet the strength of the Church is not measured by numbers.

The Lord Himself assures us that where two or three are gathered in His name, He is there among them. This promise of Christ is the greatest support for every small parish community. Therefore, I urge you as a father to remain united and to support every effort that contributes to your spiritual growth.

When a small community is united around the Holy Altar, it can become a source of great spiritual blessing. Here, in a place where natural light is greatly diminished during the winter months, let us remember that the light of Christ never sets. It does not depend on the seasons, the weather, or human circumstances. It is the light of the Resurrection, which dispels the darkness of despair and gives people hope, even when everything around them seems difficult.

As we conclude our spiritual fellowship today, let us keep in our hearts the two great invitations associated with the Apostle Philip. The first is Christ’s invitation to the Apostle: “Follow Me”; the second is the Apostle’s invitation to Nathanael: “Come and see.” The first calls us to become true disciples of Christ. The second calls us to bear witness to His love in the world.

Finally, allow me to assure you that, despite the geographical distance, you are not alone. You belong to the great spiritual family of the Holy Metropolis of Sweden and All Scandinavia, under the protection of the Mother Church of Christ, the Great Church of Constantinople.

Our presence here today, together with Hirësia e Tij, Bishop Bartholomew of Elaia, is meant to express this unity precisely. I pray that the Apostle Philip, who readily answered the Lord’s call and devoted his entire life to spreading the Gospel, will intercede for you all.

May you have a blessed Christmas!”

During his fellowship with the faithful, Metropolitan Cleopas also expressed his fatherly love and the local Church’s unwavering concern for the spiritual needs of the Orthodox faithful living in Iceland. He emphasized the importance of preserving the Orthodox faith, ecclesiastical unity, the Greek language, and the values handed down by our forebears.

He also offered his heartfelt thanks to Rafn Alexander Sigurdsson, to whom he presented his book on the St. George Cathedral of Stockholm, to the President of the Hellenic Community, and to the members of the Parish Council for their presence, love, and continued support of the Church’s work.

He also thanked the Lutheran clergyman for honoring the gathering with his presence and for his spirit of Christian warmth.

items.sum:
Patriarku Porfirije i Serbisë i ka dërguar një mesazh pajtues presidentit të sapozgjedhur të Republikës Sërbska, Savo Miniç, me rastin e zgjedhjes së tij dhe supozimit të detyrës.

Në mesazhin e tij, Patriarku përcjell dëshirat e tij më të ngrohta dhe thekson përgjegjësinë e madhe të lidhur me zyrën si edhe rëndësinë e ruajtjes së paqes, trashëgimisë shpirtërore e kulturore dhe kujtesës historike të popullit serb.

Ne lutemi që Zoti yt të të bekojë, të na forcojë dhe të të forcojë, të jesh i durueshëm për atë që është e mirë dhe e fortë për t'u shpërblyer me të gjithë banorët e Sërbska.
items.text_orig:
Patriarch Porfirije of Serbia has sent a congratulatory message to the newly elected President of Republika Srpska, Savo Minić, on the occasion of his election and assumption of office.

In his message, the Patriarch conveys his warmest wishes and highlights the great responsibility associated with the office, as well as the importance of preserving peace, the spiritual and cultural heritage, and the historical memory of the Serbian people.

The message of the Patriarch of Serbia reads as follows:

Your Excellency,

Dear Mr. Minić,

It is Our honour and joy to extend to You Our warmest congratulations on the occasion of Your election and assumption of office as President of Republika Srpska. The office You are undertaking carries great responsibility, but it is also a particular honour and a calling, as You are entrusted with safeguarding the continued existence and progress of Republika Srpska, as well as the dignity and well-being of all its citizens.

In these times of many trials, when it is especially important to foster peace while safeguarding the spiritual and cultural heritage and the historical memory of our people, we have no doubt that, with Your eyes fixed upon Christ and the Christ-like figure of Saint Sava, You will carry out this high office with dedication throughout Your term.

We pray that the Lord may bless You, strengthen You, and grant You wisdom, resolve in pursuing what is good, and the strength to discharge the responsibilities entrusted to You for the benefit of all the citizens of Republika Srpska.

With God’s blessing,

Patriarch of Serbia Porfirije

items.title_orig: New auxiliary bishop ordained in Buenos Aires
items.sum:
Peshkopi Aleksandër i Nikopolit, deri tani Vikari i arqidioqezës orthodhokse greke të Amerikës (31s Slavic Vicariate, u caktua të dielën në episkopin e Buenos të Katedrales orthodhokse Theocos në Buenos Aires, gjatë festimeve që shënuan 30 vjetorin e Metropolisit të Shenjtë të Buenos Aires dhe Amerikës Jugore.

Kryepeshkopi Elpidofos i Amerikës mori pjesë si përfaqësues zyrtar i patriarkut ekumenik Bartolomeu, duke i përcjellë patriarkut të tij, nëpërmjet bekimeve të Metropolitanit Iosif të Buenos Aires dhe hierarkisë, klerit dhe besnikëve të Metropolisit.

Pasi u lirua në mënyrë kanonike nga Archdiocese, peshkopi Aleksandër u emërua nga patriarku ekumenik Bartolomeu si peshkopi i tij i Auxiliar, duke shërbyer në Metropolisin e Buenos Aires dhe të Amerikës së Jugut.

Patriarkati ekumenik, nën patriarkun ekumenik Bartolomeu, krijoi Metropolisin në korrik 1996, kur ndau arqidioqezën orthodhokse greke të Amerikës së Veriut dhe Jugore, e cila ishte shtrirë nga Alaska në skajin jugor të Amerikës së Jugut, në juridiksione të ndara për Shtetet e Bashkuara, Kanadanë, Amerikën Qendrore dhe Amerikën e Jugut.

Kryepeshkopi Elpidofos foli edhe për lidhjet midis Metropolisit dhe arqidioqezës së Amerikës, bashkësitë e të cilit i përkisnin një kryedioqesi të vetme të Amerikës së Veriut dhe të Jugut deri në vitin 1996.
items.text_orig:
Bishop Alexander of Nicopolis, until now the Vicar of the Greek Orthodox Archdiocese of America’s Slavic Vicariate, was ordained to the episcopacy on Sunday at the Dormition of the Theotokos Orthodox Cathedral in Buenos Aires, during celebrations marking the 30th anniversary of the Holy Metropolis of Buenos Aires and South America.

Archbishop Elpidophoros of America attended as the official representative of the Ecumenical Patriarch Bartholomew, conveying the Patriarch’s blessings to Metropolitan Iosif of Buenos Aires and to the hierarchy, clergy and faithful of the Metropolis.

After being canonically released by the Archdiocese, Bishop Alexander was appointed by the Ecumenical Patriarch Bartholomew as his Auxiliary Bishop, serving in the Metropolis of Buenos Aires and South America.

His departure leaves the post of Vicar of the Slavic Vicariate vacant. The Archdiocese said the matter will go before its Holy Eparchial Synod, which will appoint a successor.

The Archdiocese thanked Ecumenical Patriarch Bartholomew for the appointment, congratulated Bishop Alexander, and thanked him for his service to the faithful of the Slavic Vicariate.

The Ecumenical Patriarchate, under the Ecumenical Patriarch Bartholomew, created the Metropolis in July 1996, when it divided the Greek Orthodox Archdiocese of North and South America, which had stretched from Alaska to the southern tip of South America, into separate jurisdictions for the United States, Canada, Central America and South America. Metropolitan Gennadios of blessed memory, who had led the Church in Buenos Aires since 1979, served as the Metropolis’s first Metropolitan. Metropolitan Tarasios succeeded him in 2001, and in 2019 the Holy Synod of the Ecumenical Patriarchate elected the Argentine-born Metropolitan Iosif as the Metropolis’s third Metropolitan.

In his address, Archbishop Elpidophoros noted that the Metropolis’s 30th anniversary coincides with the completion of 35 years of the Ecumenical Patriarch’s ministry.

“This was far more than an administrative decision,” Archbishop Elpidophoros said of the Metropolis’s founding, calling it “an act of profound pastoral foresight” rooted in the conviction that the Church “must never remain confined to the boundaries of ethnicity, geography, or history.”

Archbishop Elpidophoros, who enthroned Metropolitan Iosif as the Patriarch’s representative on Feb. 29, 2020, recalled handing him the pastoral staff that the Ecumenical Patriarch Bartholomew had given Archbishop Elpidophoros at his own elevation to the episcopacy. He noted that Metropolitan Iosif was born and raised in Córdoba, Argentina, and said his election “demonstrated that Orthodoxy in South America is not a foreign presence, nor merely an inheritance carried across the oceans by earlier generations.”

Archbishop Elpidophoros also spoke of the ties between the Metropolis and the Archdiocese of America, whose communities belonged to a single Archdiocese of North and South America until 1996. “The historic reorganization of 1996 did not sever these bonds,” he said. The two, he added, “remain branches of the same spiritual vine, children of the same Mother Church of Constantinople.”

“This is the true meaning of Orthodox mission,” Archbishop Elpidophoros said. “It is not simply the preservation of what we have inherited, precious though that inheritance may be. It is the courageous and loving transmission of that inheritance to those who have yet to encounter its beauty.”

items.title_orig: St. Gregory the Wonderworker of Neocaesarea, and Gennadius, patriarch of Constantinople; St. Lazarus the iconographer
items.sum:
Shën Gregori, mjeshtri i çudirave, peshkopi i Neokaserës

Shën Gregori u bë student i Origjenit. Shën Gregori studioi për tetë vjet me Origjenin dhe u pagëzua prej tij.

Jeta asketike e Shën Gregorit, konteenca e tij, pastërtia dhe mungesa e lakmisë ngjallën zili midis bashkëmoshatarëve të tij mendjemëdhenj dhe të dashur nga mëkati, paganëve që ishin, dhe vendosën të shpifin për Shën Gregorin.

Shën Gregori tha një lutje për të, dhe djalli e la atë. Ky ishte fillimi i mrekullive të Shën Gregorit.

Peshkopi i qytetit të Kapadokisë, Amasea, Thedimos, pasi kishte mësuar për jetën asketike të Shën Gregorit, vendosi ta bënte peshkop të Neokaserës.

Ky episod në jetën e Shën Gregorit u rregjistrua nga Shën Gregori i Nyssës (janar). Ai tregon se Shën Gregori nga Neokaezarea mori dinjitetin episkopal vetëm pasi peshkopi Thedimos i Amazës kreu të gjitha ritet kanonike mbi të.

Shën Gregori shkroi gjithçka që Shën Xhon Teologu i zbuloi atij.

Misteri i simbolit të besimit, shkruar nga Shën Gregori i Neokaserës, është një zbulim i madh hyjnor në historinë e Kishës.

Pasi u bë peshkop, Shën Gregori u nis për në Neocasera.

Shën Gregori u kthye në Neokaesare pas fundit të persekutimit.

Kur Shën Gregori u ngjit për herë të parë në kathedra, në Neocasera kishte vetëm shtatëmbëdhjetë të krishterë.

Shën Zannadios, Patriarku i Kostandinopojës

Saint Gennadios, Patriarku i Kostandinopojës, u ngjit në fronin e Kishës së Kostandinopojës në vitin 458, gjatë mbretërimit të perandorit të shenjtë Leo të Madh (457-474).

Gjatë patriarkatit të Shën Xhennadios, u ndërtua një tempull për nder të Shën Gjonit, pararendësit. Kujdestari i kishës nën patriarkun e shenjtë Gennadius ishte Shën Marsian (janar).

Shën Xhennadiosi qeveriste Kishën e Kostandinopojës për trembëdhjetë vjet.
items.text_orig:
Saint Gregory the Wonderworker, Bishop of Neocaesarea

He was born in the city of Neocaesarea (northern Asia Minor) into a pagan family. Having received a fine education, from his youth he strived for Truth, but the thinkers of antiquity were not able to quench his thirst for knowledge. Truth was revealed to him only in the Holy Gospel, and the youth became a Christian.

For the continuation of his studies Saint Gregory went to Alexandria, known then as a center for pagan and Christian learning. The youth, eager for knowledge, went to the Alexandrian Catechetical School, where the presbyter Origen taught. Origen was a famous teacher, possessing a great strength of mind and profound knowledge.

Saint Gregory became a student of Origen. Afterwards, the saint wrote about his mentor: “This man received from God a sublime gift, to be an interpreter of the Word of God for people, to apprehend the Word of God, as God Himself did use it, and to explain it to people, insofar as they were able to understand it.” Saint Gregory studied for eight years with Origen, and was baptized by him.

The ascetic life of Saint Gregory, his continence, purity and lack of covetousness aroused envy among his conceited and sin-loving peers, pagans that they were, and they decided to slander Saint Gregory. Once, when he was conversing with philosophers and teachers in the city square, a notorious harlot came up to him and demanded payment for the sin he had supposedly committed with her.

At first Saint Gregory gently remonstrated with her, saying that she perhaps mistook him for someone else. But the profligate woman would not be quieted. He then asked a friend to give her the money. Just as the woman took the unjust payment, she immediately fell to the ground in a demonic fit, and the fraud became evident. Saint Gregory said a prayer over her, and the devil left her. This was the beginning of Saint Gregory’s miracles.

Having returned to Neocaesarea, the saint fled from the worldly affairs into which influential townsmen persistently sought to push him. He went into the desert, where by fasting and prayer he attained to high spiritual accomplishment and the gifts of clairvoyance and prophecy. Saint Gregory loved life in the wilderness and wanted to remain in solitude until the end of his days, but the Lord willed otherwise.

The bishop of the Cappadocian city of Amasea, Thedimos, having learned of Saint Gregory’s ascetic life, decided to have him made Bishop of Neocaesarea. But having foreseen in spirit the intent of Bishop Thedimos, the saint hid himself from the messengers of the bishop who were entrusted to find him.

Then Bishop Thedimos ordained the absent saint as Bishop of Neocaesarea, beseeching the Lord that He Himself would sanctify the unusual ordination. Saint Gregory perceived the extraordinary event as a manifestation of the will of God and he did not dare to protest.

This episode in the life of Saint Gregory was recorded by Saint Gregory of Nyssa (January 10). He relates that Saint Gregory of Neocaesarea received the episcopal dignity only after Bishop Thedimos of Amasea performed all the canonical rites over him.

During this time, the heresy of Sabellius and Paul of Samosata began to spread. They taught falsely concerning the Holy Trinity. Saint Gregory prayed fervently and diligently imploring God and His most pure Mother to reveal to him the true faith. The All-Holy Virgin Mary appeared to him, radiant like the sun, and with Her was the Apostle John the Theologian dressed in archepiscopal vestments.

By the command of the Mother of God, the Apostle John taught the saint how to correctly and properly confess the Mystery of the Most Holy Trinity. Saint Gregory wrote down everything that Saint John the Theologian revealed to him.

The Mystery of the Symbol of the Faith, written down by Saint Gregory of Neocaesarea, is a great divine revelation in the history of the Church. The teaching about the Holy Trinity in Orthodox Theology is based on it. Subsequently it was used by the holy Fathers of the Church: Basil the Great, Gregory the Theologian, and Gregory of Nyssa.

The Symbol of Saint Gregory of Neocaesarea was later examined and affirmed in the year 325 by the First Ecumenical Council, showing his enduring significance for Orthodoxy.

Having become a bishop, Saint Gregory set off to Neocaesarea. Along the way from Amasea he expelled devils from a pagan temple, the priest of which he converted to Christ. The convert was witness to still another miracle of the saint, at his word a large stone shifted from its place.

The preaching of the saint was direct, lively and fruitful. He taught and worked miracles in the name of Christ: he healed the sick, he helped the needy, he settled quarrels and complaints. Two brothers sharing an inheritance were not able to agree over the property of their dead father.

There was a large lake over which they argued, for each of the brothers wanted the lake for himself. They both gathered their friends together, and were ready to come to blows. Saint Gregory persuaded them to delay their fight until the following day, and he himself prayed all night long at the shore of the lake which sparked the quarrel.

When dawn broke, everyone saw that the lake had dried up or gone underground. Through the intense prayer of the saint, now there was only a stream, and its course defined the boundary line. Another time, during the construction of a church, he commanded a hill to move and make room at the place of the foundation.

When a persecution against Christians began under the emperor Decius (249-251), Saint Gregory led his flock to a faraway mountain. A certain pagan, knowing about the hiding place of the Christians, informed the persecutors.

Soldiers surrounded the mountain. The saint went out into an open place, raised up his hands to heaven and ordered to his deacon to do the same. The soldiers searched the whole mountain, and they went several times right past those praying, but not seeing them, they gave up and went away.

In the city they reported that there was nowhere to hide on the mountain: no one was there, and only two trees stood beside each other. The informer was struck with amazement, he repented of his ways and became a fervent Christian.

Saint Gregory returned to Neocaesarea after the end of the persecution. By his blessing church Feasts were established in honor of the martyrs who had suffered for Christ.

By his saintly life, his effective preaching, working of miracles and graced guiding of his flock, the saint steadily increased the number of converts to Christ. When Saint Gregory first ascended his cathedra, there were only seventeen Christians in Neocaesarea. At his death, only seventeen pagans remained in the city.

Troparion, tone 8: You became worthy of your name through your way of life: through your vigilance in prayer and your constant works of mercy. Therefore, O Father Gregory, beseech Christ God to enlighten our minds, that we may not sleep in sin, which leads to death!

Saint Gennadius, Patriarch of Constantinople

Saint Gennadius, Patriarch of Constantinople, ascended the throne of the Church of Constantinople in the year 458, during the reign of the holy emperor Leo the Great (457-474). His life is known from the book The Spiritual Meadow in which tales of Saints Sophronius and John, monks of Salamis monastery near Alexandria, were recorded. These monks were clergy of the Church of Constantinople under Patriarch Gennadius.

Saint Gennadius was distinguished for his mildness, tolerance, purity and abstinence. One may get some idea of the power of his prayer from the following instance: in the church of the holy Martyr Eleutherius at Constantinople was a disreputable reader Charisius, spending his life in idleness, impurity and even occupying himself with murder and sorcery. For a long time, Saint Gennadius admonished him with gentleness and patience, but Charisius did not change his conduct. The Patriarch resorted to strictness and gave orders to chastize and discipline the disreputable cleric. But even after the punishment, he did not correct himself.

Patriarch Gennadius then sent his emissary in his name to the holy Martyr Eleutherius (August 4) in whose church Charisius served as a reader. Entering the temple, the emissary of the Patriarch came before the altar, stretched out his hand to the grave of the martyr and said: “Holy Martyr Eleutherius! Patriarch Gennadius declares to you, through me a sinner, that the cleric Charisius, serving in your temple, does much iniquity and creates great scandal; therefore, either improve him or cut him off from the Church.”

On the following morning, Charisius was found dead.

Another instance, displaying the great strength of prayer of Saint Gennadius, occurred with one of the portrait painters who dared to paint an image of Christ, giving the Savior the features of the pagan god Zeus. The hand of the painter, having done such blasphemy, immediately withered. The repentant painter was brought in the church and confessed all his sins to the Patriarch. Saint Gennadius prayed over the sinner, and the hand of the painter was healed.

To settle iniquitous actions and false teachings arising in the Church, Saint Gennadius summoned a local Council which condemned the Eutychian heresy and prohibited simony (ordination for a payment of money). The saint would not ordain a man to the priesthood unless he was quite knowledgeable in Holy Scripture, and knew the Psalter by heart.

During the patriarchate of Saint Gennadius, a temple was built in honor of Saint John the Forerunner. Then a certain senator Studius of Rome founded a monastery which later became known as the Studion. The church steward under the holy Patriarch Gennadius was Saint Marcian (January 10). The Patriarch also ordained Saint Daniel the Stylite (December 11) to the priesthood.

Saint Gennadius was the author of dialogues and commentaries on the Prophet Daniel (the works have not survived). There is also his Encyclical Against Simony, affirmed by a Council of the year 459. Saint Gennadius governed the Church of Constantinople for thirteen years. He died peacefully in the year 471.

Saint Lazarus the Iconographer

He lived in Constantinople. He was a priest, led a strict ascetic life and painted holy icons. He fought against all heresy, enduring many afflictions from the Nestorians, Eutychians, and iconoclasts.

Under the iconoclast emperor Theophilus (829-842), he was arrested and after cruel tortures, thrown into prison. Theophilus ordered horseshoes to be placed in a fire until they glowed red with the heat. Then they were put upon the iconographer’s hands, because he dared to paint icons of Christ and the saints. He was saved from execution by the intervention of the empress Theodora.

Saint Lazarus died in the year 857 while returning from Rome, where he had been sent in a delegation on church matters to Pope Benedict III (855-858). His remains were taken to Constantinople and buried in the church of Saint Evandrus.

items.title: «Kisha» — aplikacioni i ri i Kishës Orthodhokse Autoqefale të Shqipërisë
items.summary: Aplikacioni i ri «Kisha»: e kremtja dhe shenjtorët e ditës, leximet me zë, Dhjata e Re dhe Psaltiri, shërbesat dhe lutjet, Tipikoja dinamike, lajmet, Radio «Ngjallja» dhe arkivi i pasur i faqes së re.
items.text:
Kisha Orthodhokse Autoqefale e Shqipërisë u vë në dispozicion besimtarëve aplikacionin e saj të ri, «Kisha», të lidhur me faqen e re të internetit orthodoxalbania.org. Në një vend të vetëm, në telefonin tuaj, gjendet jeta e përditshme e Kishës dhe një nga arkivat më të pasura orthodhokse në gjuhën shqipe.

Çdo ditë me Kishën

Sot në Kishë: e kremtja dhe shenjtorët e ditës, kreshma e ditës dhe nëse ka Liturgji Hyjnore.

Leximet e ditës: Apostulli dhe Ungjilli, me tekst dhe me zë; kur mbaron Apostulli, fillon vetë Ungjilli.

Mbi 3.000 jetë shenjtorësh , nga sinaksarët e shumë vendeve orthodhokse.

Jerontikoni: çdo ditë një histori nga Etërit e shkretëtirës, edhe me zë.

Shkrimi i Shenjtë me zë

Dhjata e Re e plotë dhe Psaltiri me 150 psalmet, me mijëra regjistrime zanore: një për çdo varg. Prekni një varg dhe dëgjimi fillon pikërisht prej aty.

Lutja dhe shërbesat

Shumica e shërbesave dhe e lutjeve të Kishës sonë: Mëngjesorja, Mbrëmësorja, Pasdarka e Vogël dhe e Madhe, Shërbesa e Mesnatës, Orët, Liturgjitë Hyjnore të Shën Joan Gojartit, të Shën Vasilit të Madh dhe e Dhuratave të Parashenjtëruara, Himni Akathist, Paraklisi, Përgatitja për Kungim, shërbesat e Mistereve dhe të varrimit.

Lutja e orës: aplikacioni ju sjell vetë lutjen që i përket çdo ore të ditës.

Tipikoja dinamike, deri në vitin 2040

Rregullimi i shërbesave për çdo ditë përpilohet nga një algoritëm i specializuar, i ndërtuar mbi Tipikonë e Kishës. Ai llogarit vetë të kremtet e lëvizshme, përkimet e të kremteve dhe leximet e çdo dite, deri në vitin 2040.

Lajmet dhe Radio «Ngjallja»

Lajmet më të fundit nga jeta e Kishës sonë në Shqipëri, si edhe lajme të rëndësishme nga mbarë bota që kanë të bëjnë me Orthodhoksinë mbarëbotërore.

Radio «Ngjallja» drejtpërdrejt dhe videot e saj më të fundit.

Njoftime para kreshmëve dhe të kremteve të mëdha.

Arkivi i faqes së re, i lidhur me aplikacionin

Mbi 10.000 artikuj nga gazeta historike «Ngjallja».

Revista «Kërkim»: 17 numra me 218 artikuj, secili edhe në PDF.

Mbi 10.000 video: predikime, mesazhe, jetë shenjtorësh dhe emisione të Radios «Ngjallja».

Mijëra lajme dhe shkrime , me kërkim në të gjithë faqen.

Katekizmi dhe Besimi Orthodhoks, Theologjia dhe Spiritualiteti, Muzika Bizantine, Tekste dhe Shpjegime Liturgjike.

Pyetje dhe përgjigje praktike dhe Organizimi kishtar: mitropolitë, enoritë, klerikët dhe numrat e telefonit.

I përshtatur për secilin

Aplikacioni është në shqip, por edhe në greqisht dhe anglisht, me shkronja që zmadhohen dhe me ngjyra dite ose nate. Në «Hapësira ime» ruani atë që doni ta rilexoni, dhe çdo gjë mund ta ndani me të tjerët.

Përdorimi i Inteligjencës Artificiale

Në faqen e internetit dhe në aplikacionin e Kishës, Inteligjenca Artificiale u përdor me maturi, vetëm si mjet, në këto fusha:

në organizimin e materialit dhe në kodin e faqes së internetit dhe të aplikacionit;

në krijimin e regjistrimeve zanore të Dhjatës së Re dhe të Psaltirit;

në krijimin e imazheve të shenjtorëve, në stilin bizantin.

Qëllimi ishte që besimtarëve t’u ofrohet një përvojë e bukur dhe e këndshme.

Inteligjenca Artificiale nuk u përdor për të prodhuar «dije artificiale» dhe as për të shtrembëruar informacionin. Thelbi i gjithçkaje që ofrohet në faqen e internetit dhe në aplikacionin e Kishës është autentikisht orthodhoks i krishterë dhe buron nga Tradita e saj.

Mjetet ndryshojnë; mesazhi mbetet i njëjti. Qëllimi përfundimtar i çdo mjeti që përdorim është të përcjellë mesazhin e besimit të krishterë orthodhoks dhe Traditën e tij të mirëfilltë.

Gjithnjë në pasurim

Aplikacioni pasurohet vazhdimisht me funksione dhe mundësi të reja, siç është Tipikoja dinamike, që sapo u shtua.

HAPENI APLIKACIONIN «KISHA»

Prej andej mund ta ruani në telefon me një prekje.

items.title_orig: Metropolitan Nicolae and Bishop Ioan Casian consecrate new church in Texas: The Christian’s spiritual journey leads from the Church to the Kingdom
items.sum:
⇩ Ecja jonë e krishterë frymore në këtë jetë është nga Kisha në Mbretëri, tha Hizhisia e Tij Nikolae, metropolitani orthodhoks rumun i Amerikës, pas shërbimit të kurvërimit dhe Liturgjia Hyjnore festoi të dielën në Kishën Orthodhokse Rumune të Shën Marisë në Sidër Park, pranë Ostinit, Teksas.

"Çdo Liturgji Hyjnore është një ftesë për të lënë botën dhe për të ardhur në Mbretërinë e qiejve, dhe jo për të shkuar prapa pa asnjë kuptim në botë, por për të sjellë në botë fjalën e Perëndisë, Trupit dhe gjakut të tij, 190 shtoi metropolitin orthodhoks rumun të Amerikës, duke shpjeguar fazat e procesionit që po ndodh gjatë shenjtërimit.

"Në fund të këtij shërbimi përçmues dhe Liturgjia Hyjnore, do të keni mundësinë të hyni në Altarin e Shenjtë dhe të nderoni tryezën e re të shenjtëruar të Shenjtë, Ungjillin dhe Kryqin, tha Hiria e Tij, duke shtuar se kjo ndodh vetëm në Kishën Orthodhokse Rumune.

Fro Alesandro Margheritino, kancelar i Kishës Orthodhokse në Amerikë, paraqiti metropolitin orthodhoks rumun Nikolae me një fragment të relikave të Shën Olgës së Alaskës, të talentuar nga metropolitani Tikhon.

Maria Bërankoveanu këtë vit në të cilin Kisha Orthodhokse Rumune nderon gratë e shenjta të kalendarit, 190 Metropolitan Tikhon i shkroi Metropolitan Nikolae.

Ata mbeten gjithashtu një shenjë e forcimit të lidhjeve të dashurisë vëllazërore midis kishës orthodhokse në Amerikë dhe Kishës Orthodhokse Rumune.

Shërbimi i shenjtërimit dhe Liturgjia Hyjnore u festua nga metropolitani Nikolae së bashku me peshkopin orthodhoks rumun Ioan Kasian të Kanadasë.

Relikat e shenjta do të jenë gjithashtu të pranishme në shenjtërimin e kishës orthodhokse rumune të Joakimit të drejtë dhe Anës në Siatëll, Uashington, planifikuar për më 21 nëntor 2026.

Të dhënat e kontaktit për Parisin orthodhoks Rumun në Sidër Park, Teksas, janë të disponueshme këtu dhe për Parisin orthodhoks Rumun në Siatëll, ato janë të disponueshme këtu.
items.text_orig:
“Our spiritual Christian proceeding in this life is from the Church to the Kingdom,” said Hirësia e Tij Nicolae, Romanian Orthodox Metropolitan of the Americas, following the Consecration service and the Divine Liturgy celebrated on Sunday at St Mary’s Romanian Orthodox Church in Cedar Park, near Austin, Texas.

“Every Divine Liturgy is an invitation to leave the world and to come into the Kingdom of Heaven, and not to go back without any understanding in the world, but to bring to the world the word of God and his Body and Blood,” added the Romanian Orthodox Metropolitan of the Americas, explaining the stages of the procession taking place during the consecration.

An invitation to a spiritual procession

The Metropolitan recalled that the Consecration service began with the exterior walls and continued with the consecration of the interior walls and the Holy Table.

“This is the first important moment of the consecration. We left the outside, the world, and we entered the Kingdom of Heaven,” Hirësia e Tij emphasised. “What is the first thing we see when we enter the church? The iconostasis.”

“The iconostasis is called a visual memorial of our salvation,” Metropolitan Nicolae recalled. “Seeing the iconostasis, we know that this is also a prophetic vision of the Kingdom of Heaven, which is to be accomplished at the end of the world.”

The spiritual journey of the faithful who attended the consecration was to reach its culmination through the veneration of the Holy Altar, Hirësia e Tij explained.

“This is an invitation to a spiritual procession, a spiritual pilgrimage from outside, from the world, to the church, to the Kingdom of Heaven,” explained Mitropolitan Nicolae.

“At the end of this Consecration service and Divine Liturgy, you will have the opportunity to enter the Holy Altar and to venerate the newly consecrated Holy Table, the Gospel, and the Cross,” said Hirësia e Tij, adding that this happens uniquely in the Romanian Orthodox Church.

“You will meet our Lord. The Holy Table is His Tomb and is His Throne of glory. You will meet His word, the Gospel, and the Cross,” emphasised the Romanian Orthodox metropolitan.

Orders and distinctions

At the end of the service, Metropolitan Nicolae presented Fr Gabriel Teofil Ilieș, the parish priest, with the Cross of the Metropolis of the Americas. He also offered the community a festal icon depicting the Nativity of the Mother of God, the main patronal feast of the Romanian church in Cedar Park.

In turn, Fr Gabriel Teofil Ilieș presented Metropolitan Nicolae with a mitre on behalf of the entire parish community.

Fr. Dumitru Ilieș, the former parish priest, and his wife received certificates and gifts, while Deacon Andrei Barcan was presented with a cross by the Metropolitan of the Americas.

Relics of St Olga of Alaska for the Romanian Metropolis of the Americas

An emotional moment followed. Fr Alessandro Margheritino, Chancellor of the Orthodox Church in America, presented Romanian Orthodox Metropolitan Nicolae with a fragment of the relics of St Olga of Alaska, gifted by Metropolitan Tikhon.

“It is my hope that these holy relics will be a source of great comfort and inspiration for Your Eminence and for Your clergy and faithful as they venerate St. Olga together with St. Matrona of Hurezi and St. Maria Brâncoveanu in this year in which the Romanian Orthodox Church honours the holy women of the calendar,” Metropolitan Tikhon wrote to Metropolitan Nicolae.

“May they also remain a sign of the strengthening of the bonds of brotherly love between the Orthodox Church in America and the Romanian Orthodox Church. May God, through the prayers of our Righteous Mother Olga, pour out his great mercy and bountiful grace upon all who venerate these holy relics,” further transmitted the Primate of the Orthodox Church in America in a message read by Fr. Alessandro Margheritino.

An effort of the entire community

The ceremonies concluded with small gifts – icons – and certificates being awarded to those who supported the church construction project in Cedar Park.

“I would like to give glory to God for this moment that He chose us to be part of it,” said Fr. Gabriel Teofil Ilieș. “It’s hard work behind it, but it’s not just the priest himself. It’s his wife, and then the entire community that you see.”

“A person cannot do these things by himself; you need a strong community to do such a beautiful church and, for that reason, I would like to say that this cross and this icon are for the entire community,” the parish priest added.

The Romanian Orthodox community in Cedar Park still has to repay the one-million-dollar loan taken out to build the church, complete the church’s iconographic painting – works estimated at approximately 200,000 dollars – and purchase a plot of land for parking.

Guests from all over the world

The consecration service and the Divine Liturgy were celebrated by Metropolitan Nicolae together with Romanian Orthodox Bishop Ioan Casian of Canada.

The concelebrating clergy included: Fr. Mercurie Daniel Apostol, Diocesan Vicar of the Archdiocese of Râmnic; Fr. Daniel Ene, Administrative Vicar of the Romanian Orthodox Archdiocese of the United States of America; Fr. Gheorghe Militaru, Administrative Vicar of the Romanian Orthodox Diocese of Italy; Archdeacon Nicolae Iftimie, Coordinating Patriarchal Counsellor and Director of the Basilica News Agency of the Romanian Patriarchate; and Archdeacon Gheorghe Popa, Coordinating Patriarchal Counsellor and Director of Trinitas TV, the television station of the Romanian Patriarchate.

The homily during the Divine Liturgy was delivered by Fr. Alessandro Margheritino.

“The difference between life and death for our neighbour can be as simple as our choice of whether or not to cross to the other side of the road. The Samaritan saw the wounded man lying by the roadside and, moved with compassion, set aside his own plans to care for him,” the clergyman emphasised, referring to the Gospel reading for the 25th Sunday after Pentecost.

The liturgical responses were offered by the Anastasios Byzantine Choir from Cluj-Napoca, Romania, conducted by neurosurgeon Iustinian Simion.

Relics brought on pilgrimage from Romania

Sunday’s Consecration and Divine Liturgy marked the culmination of a wider series of liturgical and cultural events , which also included a concert and a conference delivered by Dr Iustinian Simion.

Throughout the patronal feast celebrations, the faithful had the opportunity to honour a fragment of the relics of St. Matrona of Hurezi and a reliquary icon containing a fragment of the relics of St Maria Brâncoveanu, brought on pilgrimage from Hurezi Monastery in Vâlcea County, Romania.

The relics are accompanied on their journey to the United States by a delegation made up of: Fr Mercurie Daniel Apostol, Diocesan Vicar of the Archdiocese of Râmnic; Stavrophore Ambrozia Șerban, Abbess of Hurezi Monastery; and Nun Macrina Aream.

The holy relics will also be present at the consecration of the Romanian Orthodox Church of the Righteous Joachim and Anna in Seattle, Washington, scheduled for November 21, 2026.

The contact data for the Romanian Orthodox Parish in Cedar Park, Texas, are available here , and for the Romanian Orthodox Parish in Seattle, they are available here .

items.title_orig: Clergy and faithful pray for the health of the Metropolitan of Bačka
items.sum:
Të bashkuar në besim, shpresë dhe dashuri, kleri dhe njerëzit besnikë të Dioqezës së Shenjtë të Baçkës i bëjnë lutje të zjarrta Zotit, Perëndisë tonë, shëruesit të shpirtrave dhe të trupave tanë.

Një shërbim i posaçëm lutjesh për rimëkëmbjen e shpejtë të Metropolitanit Irinej festohet përditë në kishën e Katedrales së Shën Xhorxh Martirit të Madh në Novi Sad, si edhe në të gjitha kishat anembanë Dioqezës së Shenjtë të Baçkës, pas shërbimeve hyjnore si në mëngjes, ashtu edhe në mbrëmje.
items.text_orig:
United in faith, hope, and love, the clergy and faithful people of the Holy Diocese of Bačka offer fervent prayers to the Lord our God, the healer of our souls and bodies. They ask Him to strengthen and sustain Metropolitan Irinej of Bačka by His grace.

A special prayer service for the speedy recovery of Metropolitan Irinej is celebrated daily at the Cathedral Church of Saint George the Great Martyr in Novi Sad, as well as in all the churches throughout the Holy Diocese of Bačka, following both the morning and evening divine services.

On Friday 13 November, the eve of the Feast of the Holy Unmercenary Physicians and Wonderworkers Cosmas and Damian, the service was led by Metropolitan David of Kruševac, with Bishop Damaskin of Mohač joining in prayer.

At the conclusion of the service, Metropolitan David called upon the clergy and faithful to continue praying fervently, all “with one voice and one heart”, and to ask the Lord our God to heal and have mercy upon His servant, Metropolitan Irinej of Bačka.

Source: Holy Diocese of Bačka
