items.title_orig: Seventeen years since the repose of Patriarch Pavle of Serbia
items.sum:
Më 15 nëntor 2026, patriarku Porfijery i Serbisë festoi Liturgjinë Hyjnore në manastirin Rakovica, pas së cilës ai kryesoi një shërbim përkujtimor për patriarkun e vdekur Pavle të Serbisë, duke shënuar 17 vjetorin e pushimit të tij.

Prandaj, le të jemi një me Perëndinë dhe të bashkuar me njëri - tjetrin në shumëllojshmërinë tonë, jo nëpërmjet një mendimi, por nëpërmjet një besimi, një dashurie dhe një shprese.

Pas Liturgjisë Hyjnore, patriarku Porfijeva festoi shërbimin përkujtimor për patriarkun e ndjerë Pavle.

Të jesh njeri na është dhënë diçka, kjo është domethënia e mesazhit të patriarkut të shenjtë Pavle.

Prandaj, kur patriarku i shenjtë Pavle na nxiti të ishim qenie njerëzore, ai po na kujtonte se, edhe pse jemi njerëz, shpesh nuk jemi kështu në kuptimin e vërtetë. Ne nuk jemi qenie të vërteta njerëzore kur qëndrojmë jashtë Krishtit dhe jashtë Kishës së Tij, që është Trupi i Tij; kur krijojmë diçka ose dikë tjetër përveç Krishtit masën e jetës sonë, diçka që shpesh është kundër Atij. Kur ne vendosim si masën dhe parimin drejtues të jetës sonë diçka jashtë Kishës, diçka që nuk i përket Kishës së Krishtit apo që ndonjëherë kthehet kundër saj, atëherë ne në të vërtetë nuk jemi duke u bërë qenie njerëzore ne jemi thirrur që të jemi sipas planit të Zotit, për ne.

Vetëm atëherë jeni njerëz dhe unë jam njeri; kur Perëndia është thelbi i ekzistencës sime dhe kur të jem një i vetëm me Perëndinë, Zotin tonë Jezu Krisht.

Kjo do të thotë, të bëhemi njerëz nëpërmjet të cilëve Krishti mendon, nëpërmjet të cilëve Krishti flet dhe ndien dhe brenda të cilëve banon Krishti.

Në festën e takimit të Zotit, 15 shkurt 1992, festimi i Liturgjisë Hyjnore nga patriarku serb Pavle dhe Metropolitan Irinej i Graçanicës së Re, u rivendos pas shumë dekadash, uniteti i plotë liturgjik dhe kanonik i kishës orthodhokse serbe në diasporë.
items.text_orig:
On November 15, 2026, Patriarch Porfirije of Serbia celebrated the Divine Liturgy at Rakovica Monastery, after which he presided over a memorial service for the late Patriarch Pavle of Serbia, marking the 17th anniversary of his repose.

Reflecting on the Gospel reading about the healing of the woman with the issue of blood and the raising of Jairus’s daughter, Patriarch Porfirije emphasized: “In the example of the woman with the issue of blood, we see the truth to which the Holy Fathers bear witness and which we proclaim in the prayer ‘O Heavenly King’ when we address the Holy Spirit and say: ‘Who art everywhere present and fillest all things.’ The Holy Spirit, the grace of God, is therefore present everywhere, in every place. But where does He act, where is His presence manifested and made visible? Where faith is found. And behold, in the case of the woman with the issue of blood, we see that through the touch of faith, even if only upon the garments of our Lord Jesus Christ, as the Evangelist tells us, immediately the fountain of her blood was dried up.’ She was healed at once. Thus, wherever there is true and genuine faith, the obstacles and barriers that hinder the action of the Holy Spirit, the action of His grace, are overcome.

“Let us preserve our Orthodox faith, not merely in words, but through our very lives, every day, by keeping God’s commandments. For through faith and the observance of the divine commandments, our souls are purified and our hearts cleansed, while the prospect opens before us of knowing God and encountering Him. The way is opened to that deeper knowledge attained by the saints of God and the Apostles, who no longer have any doubt about what is good and what is evil. For the Apostle Paul says: ‘It is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me.’

“Through his faith, which is life, humility and a path of the Cross, he reached the point at which Christ was formed within him: Christ spoke through him and thought within him. Christ henceforth directed the thoughts, words and deeds of the Apostle Paul, as He does those of all the saints who have become like Him.

“This is our heavenly calling. And as we journey towards the knowledge of the living God, with faith and love for Him, we begin to know ourselves, to understand life, its meaning and our fellow human beings. Then we understand Christ’s words: ‘You shall love your neighbour as yourself,’ because we first love God and have Him as the law and measure of our lives.

“Then we understand that we need one another and that we must be ready to forgive one another, for this is the meaning of our life. We must not reject or hate one another, because there is no greater poison than hatred. Hatred poisons the person who allows it to take hold within and is carried away by it.

“Let us, therefore, be one with God and united with one another in our diversity, not through uniformity of thought, but through one faith, one love and one hope. Let us never lose hope, but live in faith and make love the beginning and the end of our lives: love for God and love for our neighbour,” the Patriarch of Serbia said.

Following the Divine Liturgy, Patriarch Porfirije celebrated the memorial service for the late Patriarch Pavle. In his address, he said: “Brothers and sisters, we have celebrated the memorial service for the late Serbian Patriarch Pavle. We have prayed for the repose of his soul, but we have also prayed that he intercede for us, so that we may become what he wished us to be and what he urged us to become: ‘Let us be human beings.’

“This means, brothers and sisters, that the fact that we are human does not necessarily mean that we are authentic, true human beings. Being human is something given to us; this is the meaning of the message of the holy Patriarch Pavle. It is therefore a gift, but at the same time a calling. We were created as human beings in the image and likeness of God, and we have been given gifts. Whether, however, we ultimately allow the grace of God to multiply these gifts and make us truly worthy of becoming like Christ, so that we may become true and genuine human beings, depends on us and on our personal choice.

“Therefore, when the holy Patriarch Pavle urged us to be human beings, he was reminding us that, although we are human, we often fail to be so in the true sense. We are not true human beings when we stand outside Christ and outside His Church, which is His Body; when we make something or someone other than Christ the measure of our lives, something that is often even opposed to Him. When we establish as the measure and guiding principle of our lives something outside the Church, something that does not belong to the Church of Christ or that, at times, turns against it, then we are indeed failing to become the human beings we are called to be according to the Lord’s plan for us.

“To be human means to be in Christ, to live in God. Only then are we truly human. Only then are you human and I am human: when God is the framework of my existence and when I have become one with God, our Lord Jesus Christ.

“This is the legacy and blessing of the late Patriarch Pavle. This is his prayer. Therefore, as we have gathered here today and pray for the repose of his soul, we also pray, just as much, if not even more, that he intercede for us, together with Saint Sava, the holy Prince Lazar, Saint Deacon Avakum, Saint Vukašin of Klepci, Saint Bishop Nikolaj, Saint Abba Justin and all the saints of our people, so that we may truly become human beings. That is, may we become people through whom Christ thinks, through whom Christ speaks and feels, and within whom Christ dwells. May his memory be eternal. May God grant rest to his soul!”

Following the memorial service, Patriarch Porfirije welcomed approximately 150 pupils from the “Patriarch Pavle” Gymnasium, who had arrived at the monastery in a procession from their school. They were accompanied by their principal, Jasmin Nikolovski, numerous teachers, and Religious Education teachers Slaviša Kostić and Deacon Vuk Erceg.

The Life of late Patriarch Pavle of Serbia

Patriarch Pavle was born Gojko Stojčević on September 11, 1914, in the village of Kućanci in Slavonia, near Donji Miholjac. He was orphaned at an early age, and from the age of three he was cared for by his aunt.

He completed the lower grades of gymnasium in Tuzla and the upper grades in Belgrade. After matriculating at the Sarajevo Seminary in 1936, he enrolled at the Faculty of Theology in Belgrade, from which he graduated in 1942.

During the Second World War, he served as a catechist at an institution for refugee children in Banja Koviljača. In August 1944, he contracted tuberculosis, and doctors predicted that he had only three months to live. However, he recovered following prayer at Vujan Monastery. In gratitude to God, who had restored his health, he carved a wooden cross, which is preserved at the monastery to this day.

Following a period of testing as a novice, he was tonsured a monk in 1948 at the Monastery of the Annunciation in the Ovčar-Kablar region, receiving the monastic name Pavle in honour of the Apostle Paul.

From 1949 to 1955, he was a member of the brotherhood of Rača Monastery. During the 1950–1951 academic year, he served as a teacher at the Seminary of Saints Cyril and Methodius in Prizren. He was ordained to the priesthood in 1954, receiving the rank of hieromonk.

From 1955 to 1957, he pursued postgraduate studies at the Faculty of Theology in Athens. In May 1957, he was elected Bishop of Raška and Prizren. In September of that year, he was consecrated a bishop by Serbian Patriarch Vikentije at the Cathedral in Belgrade. His enthronement as Bishop of Raška and Prizren took place on October 13, 1957.

During his ministry in the Diocese of Raška and Prizren, he restored old and damaged churches and oversaw the construction of new ones. He devoted considerable effort to the spiritual formation and development of young clergy and monastics. He also made frequent pastoral visits, celebrating the Divine Liturgy throughout the diocese.

He took particular care of the Theological Seminary in Prizren, where he taught Church music and Church Slavonic. As a bishop and teacher, he formed generations of young workers in the Lord’s vineyard.

He served as hierarch in Kosovo and Metohija for more than 33 years, during an especially difficult period for the Serbian people and the Serbian Church. He regularly informed the Holy Synod, the Holy Assembly of Bishops, and state authorities about attacks by Albanians against Church property, monastics, clergy, and the Serbian population, many of whom were forced to leave their homes as a result of the pressure they faced.

He himself endured insults and physical assaults with Christian humility and patience. He also testified before the United Nations and numerous state officials, describing the suffering of the Serbian people in Kosovo and Metohija.

On December 1, 1990, the Holy Assembly of Bishops of the Serbian Orthodox Church elected him as its 44th Primate. On Sunday, December 2, 1990, he was enthroned at the Cathedral in Belgrade as Archbishop of Peć, Metropolitan of Belgrade and Karlovci, and Serbian Patriarch. On May 22, 1994, he was also enthroned at the historic patriarchal see of the Monastery of Peć.

During his patriarchate, several Church dioceses were re-established or founded. In 1992, the Seminary of Saint Peter of Cetinje was re-established in Cetinje. The following year, the Academy of Arts and Conservation of the Serbian Orthodox Church began its work.

In 1994, the Theological Academy of Saint Basil of Ostrog was established in Foča, while in 1997 the Seminary of Saint John Chrysostom opened in Kragujevac.

At the end of 1998, the Information Service of the Serbian Orthodox Church was established. In 2001, Religious Education was reintroduced in public schools in the Republic of Serbia, and in 2004 the Faculty of Theology was reintegrated into the University of Belgrade.

Patriarch Pavle took a particular interest in the construction of the great votive church of the Serbian people, the Temple of Saint Sava in Vračar. During his patriarchate, the exterior construction was completed in 2004, marking a major milestone in the realization of this historic undertaking.

Patriarch Pavle made a significant contribution to the unity of the Orthodox Church. He met with Ecumenical Patriarch Bartholomew I; Patriarch Alexy II of Moscow and All Russia; Archbishop Christodoulos of Athens and All Greece; Patriarch Peter VII of Alexandria and All Africa; and other Primates of the local Orthodox Churches.

Inspired by Christ’s words, “that they all may be one, as Thou, Father, art in Me, and I in Thee,” in September 2006 he declared open the work of the Joint International Commission for Theological Dialogue between the Orthodox Church and the Roman Catholic Church, which was hosted in Belgrade.

On the Feast of the Meeting of the Lord, February 15, 1992, the celebration of the Divine Liturgy by Serbian Patriarch Pavle and Metropolitan Irinej of New Gracanica restored, after many decades, the full liturgical and canonical unity of the Serbian Orthodox Church in the diaspora.

He also made particular efforts to heal the schism in what was then the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia.

Through meetings with religious leaders of the Roman Catholic Church and Islam, as well as through direct and written appeals to political leaders at home and abroad, during the tragic wars in the territory of the former Yugoslavia and NATO’s attack on Serbia, Patriarch Pavle advocated the peaceful and just resolution of conflicts in an evangelical spirit.

He chaired the Holy Synod’s Commission for the translation of the New Testament, which was published in 1984, and also chaired the Commission for the preparation of the Serbian-language liturgical service book.

items.title_orig: Fr. Viorel Sava, on the eve of Texas church consecration: God can surprisingly change our vocations
items.sum:
Për çudi, Perëndia mund t'i ndryshojë ato që kemi bërë, theksoi Fri Viorel Sava të shtunën në Shën Merios Parish në Sidër Park, Teksas, në prag të shenjtërimit të kishës.

Ngjarjet kushtuar shenjtërimit të kishës vazhduan të shtunën mbrëma me kremtimin e Vespers dhe një konferencë të mbajtur nga neurokirurgu rumun Iustinian Ioachim Simonion.

Për shenjtërimin e kishës orthodhokse rumune në Teksas, u sollën në pelegrinazh nga manastiri Hurezi, Rumani, fragmente të relikave të Shenjtorëve Maria Bërankoveanu dhe Matrona e Hurezit, nga manastiri Hurezi, nga Fri Daniel Mercurie Apostol, Vikar i Archdiocess of Râmnic.

Përkushtimi i kishës së re orthodhokse rome në Sidër Park, jo larg nga Ostini i Teksasit, ishte caktuar për të dielën, 4:30 pasdite (kohë rumune) dhe u transmetua drejtpërdrejt këtu.
items.text_orig:
„God can surprisingly change our vocations”, emphasised Fr. Viorel Sava on Saturday at St Mary’s Parish in Cedar Park, Texas, on the eve of the consecration of the church.

The Divine Liturgy was celebrated by Hirësia e Tij Ioan Casian, Romanian Orthodox Bishop of Canada, together with a concelebrating group of priests. The liturgical responses were offered by the Anastasios Byzantine Choir from Cluj-Napoca, Romania, conducted by neurosurgeon Iustinian Ioachim Simion.

Fr Viorel Sava, Professor at the “St Dumitru Stăniloae” Faculty of Orthodox Theology in Iași, Romania, highlighted the similarities between building a place of worship and the spiritual transformation of the faithful.

Starting with the repurposing of the site for building a church, the priest emphasised God’s work in the life of every person.

“What does it mean to change the house or the place where we live?” the clergyman asked, urging the faithful to transform their living spaces into places of encounter with God through prayer and the renewal of their daily lives.

Faith, medicine and peace of soul

The events dedicated to the consecration of the church continued on Saturday evening with the celebration of Vespers and a conference delivered by Romanian neurosurgeon Iustinian Ioachim Simion. Entitled “Faith, Medicine and Peace of Soul”, the conference focused on the dialogue between spirituality and medicine.

For the consecration of the Romanian Orthodox church in Texas, fragments of the relics of Saints Maria Brâncoveanu and Matrona of Hurezi were brought in pilgrimage from Hurezi Monastery, Romania, by Fr Daniel Mercurie Apostol, Vicar of the Archdiocese of Râmnic.

The consecration of the new Romaian Orthodox church in Cedar Park, not far from Austin, Texas, was scheduled for Sunday, 4:30 pm (Romanian time), and was broadcast live here .

Photo credit: St Mary’s Parish in Cedar Park

items.title_orig: Vespers Service for the Preservation of Creation ahead of COP31 in Antalya
items.sum:
Të dielën, më 15 nëntor 2026, në orën 5 pasdite p.e.s., në Kishën e Shën Alipiut në Antalia u kremtua një shërbim për Vëzhgimin e Krijimit në Kostandinopojë.

Si kujdestarë të krijimit, ne jemi të thirrur për t'u bërë priftërinj të përgjegjshëm të Krijimit, duke ia ofruar atë Perëndisë në dhënie falënderimesh dhe me një frymë kungimi, në vend që ta shfrytëzojmë atë ose të konsumojmë tepër burimet e saj.

Më parë po atë ditë, në zyrat e Metropolisit të Shenjtë të Pisidisë, Metropoliti Job i Pisidisë mori arkipeshkopin Etore Balestrero, Nuncio Apostolike dhe Observerin e përhershëm të Selisë së Shenjtë për Kombet e Bashkuara dhe agjenci të tjera të specializuara në Gjenevë, si edhe për Organizatën Botërore të Tregtisë.
items.text_orig:
On Sunday, November 15, 2026, at 5:00 p.m., a Vespers service for the Preservation of Creation was celebrated at the Church of Saint Alypius in Antalya, on the occasion of COP31 convening in Constantinople.

Many faithful attended the sacred service, praying for the protection of the natural environment.

In his message, Metropolitan Job of Pisidia emphasized that, as Christians, we must acknowledge our responsibility to preserve Creation. Each of us is called to repent of the “sin against Creation” by changing our way of life and our behaviour.

As stewards of Creation, we are called to become responsible “priests of Creation,” offering it to God in thanksgiving and with a Eucharistic spirit, rather than exploiting it or consuming its resources excessively. The antidote to greed, selfishness and the excessive exploitation of natural resources, which lead to environmental degradation, lies in cultivating an ascetic spirit, embracing voluntary simplicity, fasting and self-restraint.

Earlier that same day, at the offices of the Holy Metropolis of Pisidia, Metropolitan Job of Pisidia received Archbishop Ettore Balestrero, Apostolic Nuncio and Permanent Observer of the Holy See to the United Nations and other Specialized Agencies in Geneva, as well as to the World Trade Organization.

His Excellency was accompanied by the Roman Catholic priest, Fr. Lutger Paskert. The meeting provided an opportunity for a constructive exchange of views on matters of mutual interest.

Following the Vespers service, refreshments were served at the Saint Paul Protestant Cultural Centre, located immediately adjacent to the Church of Saint Alypius.

items.title_orig: Patriarch of Alexandria welcomed Bishop of Delčevo and Kamenica
items.sum:
Midis një atmosfere gëzimi shpirtëror dhe dashurie vëllazërore, Selia historike e apostullit dhe evangjelisti Mark mirëpriti të dielën më 15 nëntor 2026, Peshkopin Mark të Delçevos dhe Kamenicës, një Hirark i Kishës Orthodhokse të Ohrit, i cili vizitoi Qytetin e Madh të Aleksandrisë si kreun e një grupi pelegrinësh nga provinca e tij kishtare.

Me lejen kanonike dhe bekimin e Papës dhe patriarkut Teodor II të Aleksandrisë dhe të gjithë Afrikës, Hirarku vizitues kryesonte kremtimin e Liturgjisë Hyjnore në manastirin historik patriarkal të Shën Sabatit, Sançtifikuar, në zemër të Aleksandrisë.

Në përfundim të Liturgjisë Hyjnore, patriarku i mbajti një fjalim të ngrohtë Hierakut dhe pelegrinëve që po vizitonin, duke shprehur gëzimin e tij të veçantë dhe emocionet e thella në praninë e tyre në shfaqjen historike të fronit të dytë të orthodhoksisë.

Duke iu referuar Kishës Orthodhokse të Ohrit, patriarku shprehu gëzimin e tij të veçantë për restaurimin e kungimit Eukaristik, duke theksuar rëndësinë e vendimit historik të marrë nga Patriarkati Ekumenik në maj 2022, i cili hapi rrugën për hierarkinë, klerin dhe besniknë e kësaj kishe për t'u kthyer në bashkimin e Eukaristikës me Kishën Orthodhokse.

Me emocione të veçanta, ai i bëri një ftesë të përzemërt dhe të përzemërt kryepeshkopit Stefan për të vizituar Selinë Historike dhe Apostolike të Aleksandrisë, duke shprehur dëshirën e tij personale dhe gëzimin e madh për ta mirëpritur në qytetin e apostullit dhe të ungjillëzuesit Mark dhe duke e shoqëruar atë para Altarit të Shenjtë.

Po atë ditë, patriarku mori gjithashtu grupe pelegrinësh nga Athina, Trikala, Patras dhe Kreta, të cilët Ai i mirëpriti ngrohtësisht, duke shprehur emocionin dhe gëzimin e thellë të Tij në praninë e tyre në Selinë historike të apostullit dhe Evangjelistit Mark.
items.text_orig:
Amid an atmosphere of spiritual joy and fraternal love, the historic See of the Apostle and Evangelist Mark welcomed, on Sunday, November 15, 2026, Bishop Mark of Delčevo and Kamenica, a Hierarch of the Orthodox Church of Ohrid, who visited the Great City of Alexandria as the head of a group of pilgrims from his ecclesiastical province.

With the canonical permission and blessing of Pope and Patriarch Theodore II of Alexandria and All Africa, the visiting Hierarch presided over the celebration of the Divine Liturgy at the historic Patriarchal Monastery of Saint Sabbas the Sanctified, in the heart of Alexandria.

During the Divine Liturgy, Patriarch Theodore II of Alexandria was present in prayer, accompanied by Metropolitan Germanos of Tamiathis and Bishop Damaskinos of Mareotis.

At the conclusion of the Divine Liturgy, the Patriarch delivered a warm address to the visiting Hierarch and the pilgrims, expressing his particular joy and deep emotion at their presence in the historic See of the Second Throne of Orthodoxy.

The Alexandrian Primate warmly welcomed Bishop Mark, a fluent speaker of Greek and a graduate of the School of Theology at Aristotle University of Thessaloniki, who maintains particularly close spiritual and theological ties with Greece and the Greek Orthodox tradition.

He made particular reference to the Bishop’s ecclesiastical journey, noting that he was elevated to the episcopacy on December 7, 2003, during the Patriarchate of the late Patriarch Pavle of Serbia, one of the most revered and ascetic figures of contemporary Orthodoxy.

The Patriarch recalled with profound reverence the saintly life, humility, and spiritual radiance of the late Patriarch Pavle, who, through the simplicity of his life and his unwavering devotion to the Gospel, became a living example of pastoral self-sacrifice and ecclesiastical ethos, bequeathing a precious spiritual legacy to generations to come.

Referring to the Orthodox Church of Ohrid, the Patriarch expressed His particular joy at the restoration of Eucharistic communion, underscoring the significance of the historic decision taken by the Ecumenical Patriarchate in May 2022, which paved the way for the Hierarchy, clergy, and faithful of this Church to return to Eucharistic communion with the Orthodox Church.

He emphasised that the unity of Orthodoxy is an invaluable gift of divine grace and, at the same time, a sacred responsibility entrusted to all the Church’s shepherds, who are called to safeguard the bonds of faith, peace, and love in Christ, rising above every trial and adversity.

The Patriarch further underlined that Alexandria, the city of the Apostle and Evangelist Mark, has throughout the centuries been a meeting place of peoples, cultures, and traditions, but above all, a beacon of the Orthodox faith and the universal witness of the Gospel.

He then spoke at length about the multifaceted missionary, pastoral, educational, and charitable work carried out throughout the African continent, emphasising that the Patriarchate of Alexandria, faithful to its apostolic heritage, continues unceasingly to proclaim the message of the Gospel and the hope of the Resurrection in every corner of Africa.

With particular emotion, he referred to the labours and sacrifices of the Hierarchs, clergy, monastics, and lay collaborators in the missionary ministry, who, very often under extremely challenging circumstances, devote themselves daily to serving their fellow human beings. Through their efforts, they establish churches, schools, hospitals, medical centres, and charitable institutions, offering not merely material relief, but, above all, the hope and love of Christ.

He further observed that the Church of Alexandria, with its two-thousand-year history, is not merely the custodian of a glorious ecclesiastical tradition, but a living, dynamic, and missionary Church, which continues to write new chapters of Christian witness, service, and sacrificial love each and every day.

For his part, Bishop Mark expressed his profound gratitude to the Patriarch for the warm welcome, his fatherly love, and the blessing granted to him to celebrate the Divine Liturgy at the historic Patriarchal Monastery of Saint Sabbas the Sanctified.

He also conveyed to the Alexandrian Primate the heartfelt good wishes and fraternal greetings of Archbishop Stefan of Ohrid, expressing the joy and deep emotion of the pilgrims at the opportunity to visit the historic land of Egypt and venerate at the apostolic See of the Church of Alexandria.

In response, the Patriarch warmly reciprocated these fraternal greetings, expressing his sincere love in Christ and profound fraternal esteem for Archbishop Stefan of Ohrid. He emphasised that the restoration of ecclesiastical communion is a source of spiritual joy and blessing for the whole of Orthodoxy.

With particular emotion, he extended a warm and heartfelt invitation to Archbishop Stefan to visit the historic and apostolic See of Alexandria, expressing his personal desire and great joy at the prospect of welcoming him to the city of the Apostle and Evangelist Mark and concelebrating the Divine Liturgy with him before the Holy Altar. Such a concelebration, he noted, would serve as a profound affirmation, through their common celebration of the Holy Eucharist, of the bonds of brotherhood in Christ, ecclesiastical unity, and mutual love between the two Churches.

The Patriarch also presented Bishop Mark with an episcopal encolpion as a blessing and a token of his esteem.

This blessed encounter served as yet another living testimony to the unity of Orthodoxy, reminding all that the common faith and participation in the same Chalice of Life transcend borders, languages, and historical trials, uniting the faithful into one great spiritual family: the Church of Christ.

From Alexandria, the city of the Apostle Mark, where for two millennia the Orthodox faith has been faithfully proclaimed and handed down from generation to generation, this encounter once again highlighted the power of ecclesiastical unity and fraternal love. For the Church, even amid the trials of history, remains the place where distances are bridged, wounds are healed, and hearts are united in Christ, in accordance with our Lord’s High Priestly Prayer: “that they may all be one” (John 17:21).

On the same day, the Patriarch also received groups of pilgrims from Athens, Trikala, Patras, and Crete, whom He warmly welcomed, expressing His deep emotion and joy at their presence in the historic See of the Apostle and Evangelist Mark.

items.text:
Fortlumturia e Tij, Papa dhe Patriarku i Aleksandrisë dhe i Gjithë Afrikës, Theodhori II, e ftoi Kryepiskopin e Ohrit, Imzot Stefanin, të vizitojë selinë apostolike të Aleksandrisë dhe të bashkëmeshojnë. Patriarku shprehu dëshirën e tij të përzemërt për ta pritur në qytetin e Apostullit dhe Ungjilltarit Mark dhe për të qëndruar së bashku përpara Tryezës së Shenjtë.

Ky mesazh vëllazëror u përcoll gjatë vizitës së Hirësisë së Tij, Episkopit të Dellçevës dhe Kamenicës, Imzot Markut, në Aleksandri, të dielën, më 15 nëntor 2026. Hierarku i Kishës së Ohrit mbërriti në Qytetin e Madh në krye të një grupi pelegrinësh nga eparkia e tij dhe u prit në selinë historike të Ungjilltarit Mark në një atmosferë gëzimi shpirtëror dhe dashurie vëllazërore.

Me lejen kanonike dhe bekimin e Patriarkut Theodhor, episkopi mysafir kryesoi Liturgjinë Hyjnore në Manastirin e Shenjtë Patriarkal historik të Oshënar Savës së Shenjtëruar, në qendër të Aleksandrisë. Fortlumturia e Tij ishte i pranishëm duke u lutur, i shoqëruar nga Hirësia e Tij, Mitropoliti i Tamiathis, Imzot Gjermanoi, dhe Hirësia e Tij, Episkopi i Mareotidës, Imzot Damaskinos.

Pas përfundimit të Liturgjisë Hyjnore, Patriarku iu drejtua me përzemërsi episkopit dhe pelegrinëve. Ai i mirëpriti në selinë e Patriarkanës që zë vendin e dytë në radhën e nderit të Orthodhoksisë, duke shprehur gëzimin dhe emocionin për praninë e tyre.

Ai e mirëpriti veçanërisht Episkopin Mark, i cili njeh gjuhën greke, është diplomuar në Fakultetin e Theologjisë të Universitetit Aristoteli të Selanikut dhe ruan lidhje të veçanta shpirtërore dhe theologjike me Greqinë dhe me traditën orthodhokse greke.

U ndal edhe në rrugëtimin e tij kishtar, duke kujtuar se u ngrit në shkallën episkopale më 7 dhjetor 2003, në kohën e të ndjerit Patriark Pavël të Serbisë, një prej figurave më të nderuara dhe asketike të Orthodhoksisë bashkëkohore.

Me respekt të thellë foli për jetën e shenjtë të Patriarkut Pavël, për përulësinë dhe rrezatimin e tij shpirtëror. Thjeshtësia dhe përkushtimi i palëkundur ndaj Ungjillit, theksoi ai, e bënë një shembull të gjallë të etikës kishtare dhe të vetëflijimit në shërbimin baritor, duke u lënë brezave të ardhshëm një trashëgimi të çmuar shpirtërore.

Duke folur për Kishën e Ohrit, Patriarku Theodhor shprehu gëzimin e veçantë për rivendosjen e kungimit eukaristik. Ai nënvizoi rëndësinë e vendimit historik të Patriarkanës Ekumenike, në maj 2022, për rikthimin e hierarkisë, të klerit dhe të popullit të kësaj Kishe në unitetin eukaristik me Kishën Orthodhokse.

Uniteti i Orthodhoksisë, theksoi ai, është një dhuratë e paçmuar e hirit hyjnor, por edhe përgjegjësi e shenjtë e të gjithë barinjve të Kishës. Përmes çdo sprove, ata duhet të ruajnë lidhjet e besimit, të paqes dhe të dashurisë më Krishtin.

Për Aleksandrinë, qytetin e Apostullit dhe Ungjilltarit Mark, vuri në dukje se gjatë gjithë historisë së saj ka qenë vend takimi i popujve, i kulturave dhe i traditave. Mbi të gjitha, ajo ka qenë një far i besimit orthodhoks dhe i dëshmisë së Ungjillit në mbarë botën.

Më pas foli gjerësisht për veprën e shumanshme të Kishës në kontinentin afrikan: misionin, shërbimin baritor, arsimin dhe filantropinë. Duke i qëndruar besnike trashëgimisë së saj apostolike, Patriarkana e Aleksandrisë vazhdon pa ndërprerje të përcjellë në çdo skaj të Afrikës mesazhin e Ungjillit dhe shpresën e Ngjalljes.

U shpreh me emocion të veçantë për mundimet dhe sakrificat e hierarkëve, të klerikëve, të murgjve dhe të bashkëpunëtorëve laikë të misionit. Shpesh në kushte të vështira, ata i shërbejnë çdo ditë njeriut, duke themeluar kisha, shkolla, spitale, qendra mjekësore dhe institucione bamirëse. Kontributi i tyre nuk kufizohet te lehtësimi i nevojave materiale, por përcjell para së gjithash dashurinë dhe shpresën e Krishtit.

Kisha e Aleksandrisë, me historinë e saj dymijëvjeçare, nuk është vetëm ruajtëse e një tradite të lavdishme, shtoi Fortlumturia e Tij. Ajo mbetet një Kishë e gjallë, që përpiqet dhe zhvillon mision, duke shkruar çdo ditë faqe të reja dëshmie, shërbimi dhe dashurie vetëflijuese.

Në përgjigjen e tij, Episkopi Mark e falënderoi thellësisht Patriarkun për mikpritjen e përzemërt, dashurinë atërore dhe bekimin që të kryente Liturgjinë Hyjnore në Manastirin Patriarkal historik të Oshënar Savës së Shenjtëruar.

Ai përcolli gjithashtu urimet e ngrohta dhe përshëndetjen vëllazërore të Kryepiskopit të Ohrit, Imzot Stefanit. Njëkohësisht shprehu gëzimin dhe emocionin e pelegrinëve që patën mundësinë të vizitonin tokën historike të Egjiptit dhe të kryenin pelegrinazh në selinë apostolike të Kishës së Aleksandrisë.

Duke iu përgjigjur përshëndetjeve, Patriarku Theodhor shprehu dashurinë e tij të sinqertë më Krishtin dhe vlerësimin e thellë vëllazëror për Kryepiskopin Stefan. Rivendosja e kungimit kishtar, nënvizoi ai, sjell gëzim shpirtëror dhe bekim për mbarë Orthodhoksinë.

Në këtë frymë, ai i drejtoi Kryepiskopit të Ohrit ftesën e përzemërt për të vizituar selinë historike apostolike të Aleksandrisë. Shprehu emocionin, dëshirën personale dhe gëzimin për ta pritur në qytetin e Ungjilltarit Mark dhe për të bashkëmeshuar me të. Kryerja e përbashkët e Eukaristisë Hyjnore përpara Tryezës së Shenjtë do të vuloste lidhjet e vëllazërisë më Krishtin, të unitetit kishtar dhe të dashurisë së ndërsjellë mes dy Kishave.

Si bekim, Fortlumturia e Tij i dhuroi episkopit mysafir një engolpion arhieratik.

Takimi dha një tjetër dëshmi të gjallë të unitetit orthodhoks. Besimi i përbashkët dhe pjesëmarrja në të njëjtin Potir të Jetës kapërcejnë kufijtë, gjuhët dhe sprovat e historisë, duke i lidhur besimtarët në një familje të madhe shpirtërore, Kishën e Krishtit.

Nga Aleksandria e Apostullit Mark, ku besimi orthodhoks dëshmohet dhe përcillet nga brezi në brez prej dy mijë vjetësh, u shfaq sërish fuqia e unitetit kishtar dhe e dashurisë vëllazërore. Mes sprovave historike, Kisha mbetet vendi ku kapërcehen largësitë, shërohen plagët dhe zemrat takohen më Krishtin, sipas lutjes kryepriftërore të Zotit: «që të gjithë të jenë një» (Gjoni 17:21).

Po atë ditë, Patriarku priti gjithashtu grupe pelegrinësh nga Athina, Trikalla, Patra dhe Kreta. Ai i mirëpriti përzemërsisht, duke shprehur emocionin për praninë e tyre në selinë historike të Apostullit dhe Ungjilltarit Mark.

items.title_orig: Holy Apostle and Evangelist Matthew
items.sum:
I dërguari i shenjtë dhe ungjillëzuesi Mateu

Me kërkesë të judenjve të kthyer në Jerusalem, apostulli i shenjtë Mate shkroi Ungjillin e tij që përshkruante jetën tokësore të Shpëtimtarit, para se të largohej për të predikuar Ungjillin në vende të largëta.

Apostulli Mate predikoi mes njerëzve që pritnin Mesinë.

Mbretëria e qiejve dhe e Kishës janë të ndërlidhura ngushtë me përvojën frymore të krishterimit: Kisha është mishërimi historik i Mbretërisë së qiejve në botë dhe Mbretëria e qiejve është Kisha e Krishtit në përsosmërinë e saj ekologjike (M.

Apostulli i shenjtë solli ungjillin e Krishtit në Siri, Medi, Persi, Parthi dhe përfundoi predikimin e tij në Etiopi me një martir vdekjeje. Apostulli i shenjtë Mattheu i ktheu disa nga idhujtar në besim te Krishti.

Kur apostulli i shenjtë e çoi shkopin drejt kishës, gruaja dhe biri i sundimtarit të vendit, Fulvian, të cilin e kishin prekur frymërat e ndyra. Në emër të Krishtit, apostulli i shenjtë i shëroi.

Kur zjarri u ndez, të gjithë panë se zjarri nuk i bëri keq Shën Mateut.

Duke bërë këtë Fulvian tha se nëse Perëndia i Mateut do ta ruante trupin e apostullit në ujë, siç e ruajti në zjarr, kjo do të ishte arsyeja e duhur për ta adhuruar këtë Perëndi të vetëm të vërtetë.

Atë natë, apostulli Mate iu shfaq peshkopit Platoni në ëndërr dhe e urdhëroi të shkonte me klerin në bregun e detit dhe të gjente trupin e tij atje. Pastaj Fulvian kërkoi falje nga profeti i shenjtë Mate, pas të cilit peshkopi Platoni e pagëzoi, duke i dhënë emrin Mateu në bindje të urdhrit të Perëndisë.

Së shpejti Shën Fulvian-Mathew abrovoi rregullin e tij dhe u bë një presbiter. Pas vdekjes së peshkopit Platoni, apostullit Mate iu shfaq dhe e nxiti të udhëhiqte Kishën Etiopiane. Pasi u bë peshkop, Shën Fulvian-Mateu u mundua të predikonte Fjalën e Perëndisë, duke vazhduar veprën e mbrojtësit të tij qiellor.
items.text_orig:
Holy Apostle and Evangelist Matthew

Also named Levi (Mark 2:14; Luke 5:27), he was one of the 12 Apostles (Mark 3:18; Luke 6:45; Acts 1:13), and brother of Apostle James Alphaeus (Mark 2:14). He was a publican, or tax-collector for Rome, in a time when the Jews were under the rule of the Roman Empire.

He lived in the Galilean city of Capernaum. When Matthew heard the voice of Jesus Christ: “Come, follow Me” (Mt. 9:9), left everything and followed the Savior. Christ and His disciples did not refuse Matthew’s invitation and they visited his house, where they shared table with the publican’s friends and acquaintances. Like the host, they were also publicans and known sinners. This event disturbed the pharisees and scribes a great deal.

Publicans who collected taxes from their countrymen did this with great profit for themselves. Usually greedy and cruel people, the Jews considered them pernicious betrayers of their country and religion. The word “publican” for the Jews had the connotation of “public sinner” and “idol-worshipper.” To even speak with a tax-collector was considered a sin, and to associate with one was defilement. But the Jewish teachers were not able to comprehend that the Lord had “come to call not the righteous, but sinners to repentance” (Mt. 9:13).

Matthew, acknowledging his sinfulness, repaid fourfold anyone he had cheated, and he distributed his remaining possessions to the poor, and he followed after Christ with the other apostles.

Saint Matthew was attentive to the instructions of the Divine Teacher, he beheld His innumerable miracles, he went together with the Twelve Apostles preaching to “the lost sheep of the house of Israel” (Mt. 10:6). He was a witness to the suffering, death, and Resurrection of the Savior, and of His glorious Ascension into Heaven.

Having received the grace of the Holy Spirit, which descended upon the Apostles on the day of Pentecost, Saint Matthew preached in Palestine for several years. At the request of the Jewish converts at Jerusalem, the holy Apostle Matthew wrote his Gospel describing the earthly life of the Savior, before leaving to preach the Gospel in faraway lands.

In the order of the books of the New Testament, the Gospel of Matthew comes first. Palestine is said to be the place where the Gospel was written. Saint Matthew wrote in Aramaic, and then it was translated into Greek. The Aramaic text has not survived, but many of the linguistic and cultural-historical peculiarities of the Greek translation give indications of it.

The Apostle Matthew preached among people who were awaiting the Messiah. His Gospel manifests itself as a vivid proof that Jesus Christ is the Messiah foretold by the prophets, and that there would not be another (Mt. 11:3).

The preaching and deeds of the Savior are presented by the evangelist in three divisions, constituting three aspects of the service of the Messiah: as Prophet and Law-Giver (Ch. 5-7), Lord over the world both visible and invisible (Ch. 8-25), and finally as High Priest offered as Sacrifice for the sins of all mankind (Ch. 26-27).

The theological content of the Gospel, besides the Christological themes, includes also the teaching about the Kingdom of God and about the Church, which the Lord sets forth in parables about the inner preparation for entering into the Kingdom (Ch. 5-7), about the worthiness of servers of the Church in the world (Ch. 10-11), about the signs of the Kingdom and its growth in the souls of mankind (Ch. 13), about the humility and simplicity of the inheritors of the Kingdom (Mt. 18:1-35; 19 13-30; 20:1-16; 25-27; 23:1-28), and about the eschatological revelations of the Kingdom in the Second Coming of Christ within the daily spiritual life of the Church (Ch. 24-25).

The Kingdom of Heaven and the Church are closely interconnected in the spiritual experience of Christianity: the Church is the historical embodiment of the Kingdom of Heaven in the world, and the Kingdom of Heaven is the Church of Christ in its eschatological perfection (Mt. 16:18-19; 28:18-20).

The holy Apostle brought the Gospel of Christ to Syria, Media, Persia, Parthia, and finishing his preaching in Ethiopia with a martyr’s death. This land was inhabited by tribes of cannibals with primitive customs and beliefs. The holy Apostle Matthew converted some of the idol-worshippers to faith in Christ. He founded the Church and built a temple in the city of Mirmena, establishing there his companion Platon as bishop.

When the holy apostle was fervently entreating God for the conversion of the Ethiopians the Lord Himself appeared to him in the form of a youth. He gave him a staff, and commanded him to plant it at the doors of the church. The Lord said that a tree would grow from this staff and it would bear fruit, and from its roots would flow a stream of water. When the Ethiopians washed themselves in the water and ate the fruit, they lost their wild ways and became gentle and good.

When the holy apostle carried the staff towards the church, he was met by the wife and son of the ruler of the land, Fulvian, who were afflicted by unclean spirits. In the Name of Christ the holy apostle healed them. This miracle converted a number of the pagans to the Lord. But the ruler did not want his subjects to become Christians and cease worshiping the pagan gods. He accused the apostle of sorcery and gave orders to execute him.

They put Saint Matthew head downwards, piled up brushwood and ignited it. When the fire flared up, everyone then saw that the fire did not harm Saint Matthew. Then Fulvian gave orders to add more wood to the fire, and frenzied with boldness, he commanded to set up twelve idols around the fire. But the flames melted the idols and flared up toward Fulvian. The frightened Ethiopian turned to the saint with an entreaty for mercy, and by the prayer of the martyr the flame went out. The body of the holy apostle remained unharmed, and he departed to the Lord.

The ruler Fulvian deeply repented of his deed, but still he had doubts. By his command, they put the body of Saint Matthew into an iron coffin and threw it into the sea. In doing this Fulvian said that if the God of Matthew would preserve the body of the apostle in the water as He preserved him in the fire, then this would be proper reason to worship this One True God.

That night the Apostle Matthew appeared to Bishop Platon in a dream, and commanded him to go with clergy to the shore of the sea and to find his body there. The righteous Fulvian and his retinue went with the bishop to the shore of the sea. The coffin carried by the waves was taken to the church built by the apostle. Then Fulvian begged forgiveness of the holy Apostle Matthew, after which Bishop Platon baptized him, giving him the name Matthew in obedience to a command of God.

Soon Saint Fulvian-Matthew abdicated his rule and became a presbyter. Upon the death of Bishop Platon, the Apostle Matthew appeared to him and exhorted him to head the Ethiopian Church. Having become a bishop, Saint Fulvian-Matthew toiled at preaching the Word of God, continuing the work of his heavenly patron.

Troparion — Tone 3 With zeal, you followed Christ the Master, who in His goodness, appeared on earth to mankind. Summoning you from the custom house, He revealed you as a chosen apostle: the proclaimer of the Gospel to the whole world! Therefore, divinely eloquent Matthew, we honor your precious memory! Entreat merciful God that He may grant our souls remission of transgressions.

items.title_orig: Patriarch of Serbia commemorated 17th anniversary of Patriarch Pavle’s repose
items.sum:
Patriarku Porfijeria i Serbisë festoi Liturgjinë Hyjnore në manastirin Rakovica në Beograd të dielën, 15 nëntor 2026, duke shënuar 17 vjetorin e pushimit të patriarkut Pavle të Serbisë.

Pas Liturgjisë, Patriarku Porfijevie u përfshi në një shërbim përkujtimor për paraardhësin e tij, i cili vdiq më 15 nëntor 2009, dhe u varros në manastir.

Në predikimin e tij, duke medituar për tregimet e Ungjijve për shërimin e gruas që vuante nga hemorragjia dhe rritja e vajzës Jairus, patriarku Porfije, theksoi fuqinë e besimit të vërtetë.

Gjatë shërbimit përkujtimor, Patriarku Porfijery kujtoi patriarkun Pavlees duke duruar mesazhin: ⇩ Le të jemi njerëz.

Pas përkujtimeve, patriarku Porfije përshëndeti rreth 150 studentë nga patriarku Pavle Gymnasium, i cili arriti në manastir në procesion, shoqëruar nga mësuesit dhe drejtori i shkollës.
items.text_orig:
Patriarch Porfirije of Serbia celebrated the Divine Liturgy at Rakovica Monastery in Belgrade on Sunday, November 15, 2026, marking the 17th anniversary of the repose of Patriarch Pavle of Serbia.

Following the Liturgy, Patriarch Porfirije officiated at a memorial service for his predecessor, who died on November 15, 2009, and was buried at the monastery.

In his sermon, reflecting on the Gospel accounts of the healing of the woman suffering from a hemorrhage and the raising of Jairus’ daughter, Patriarch Porfirije emphasized the power of genuine faith.

“The Holy Spirit, the grace of God, is present everywhere. But where does it act, where does it manifest itself? Wherever faith appears,” he said.

He urged the faithful to preserve their Orthodox faith through their daily lives, stressing the importance of humility, forgiveness, and love.

“Let us never lose hope. Let us live by faith, and let love be the beginning and the end of our lives, love for God and for our neighbor,” he emphasized.

During the memorial service, Patriarch Porfirije recalled Patriarch Pavle’s enduring message: “Let us be human.”

He explained that the late Patriarch’s words were a call to live according to Christ’s example, emphasizing that becoming truly human requires spiritual commitment and a life rooted in faith.

“We were created in the image and likeness of God as human beings, and we have been given gifts. But whether we allow God’s grace to multiply those gifts and become truly Christlike depends on us and on our choices,” he stated.

The service was attended by clergy, monastics, and numerous faithful. Among those concelebrating were Bishops Ilarion of Novo Brdo and Dositej of Lipljan.

Following the commemorations, Patriarch Porfirije welcomed approximately 150 students from the Patriarch Pavle Gymnasium, who arrived at the monastery in procession, accompanied by their teachers and school principal.

Patriarch Pavle, born Gojko Stojčević in 1914, served as Bishop of Raška and Prizren for more than three decades before his election as Patriarch of the Serbian Orthodox Church in 1990.

He passed away on November 15, 2009, and was buried at Rakovica Monastery four days later.

Source: Serbian Orthodox Church

items.title_orig: Archbishop of Cyprus: Consequences of illegal declaration in occupied territories remain “open wounds”
items.sum:
Kryepeshkopi Georgios i Qipros dënoi deklaratën e njëanëshme të njësisë së shkëputur në territoret e populluara turke të Republikës së Qipros, duke shënuar 43 vjetorin e shpalljes së saj në 15 nëntor 1983.

Në një deklaratë lëshuar nga zyra e tij të dielën, më 15 nëntor 2026, kryepeshkopi i përshkroi pasojat e deklaratës si plagë të hapura që vazhdojnë të prekin Qipron.

Kryepeshkopi ripohoi se Kisha e Qipros qëndron fuqishëm së bashku me popullin qipriot dhe Republikën e Qipros, duke mbështetur përpjekjet për të arritur një zgjidhje të drejtë dhe të qëndrueshme të çështjes së Qipros.
items.text_orig:
Archbishop Georgios of Cyprus condemned the unilateral declaration of the breakaway entity in the Turkish-occupied territories of the Republic of Cyprus, marking the 43rd anniversary of its proclamation on November 15, 1983.

In a statement issued by his office on Sunday, November 15, 2026, the Archbishop described the consequences of the declaration as “open wounds” that continue to affect Cyprus.

“On November 15, 1983, an act of sacrilege against peace, justice, Cypriot Hellenism, and international legality was committed,” Archbishop Georgios stated.

He argued that the declaration exposed the intentions and objectives of the occupying power, emphasizing the continuing consequences of the island’s division.

The Archbishop reaffirmed that the Church of Cyprus stands firmly alongside the Cypriot people and the Republic of Cyprus, supporting efforts to achieve a just and lasting settlement of the Cyprus issue.

He stressed that any solution must be based on the principles of the United Nations and the European Union, with full respect for international law.

Archbishop Georgios also called on the people of Cyprus to maintain their determination and resilience, drawing strength from their faith in God and the values of Hellenism.

“The Church of Cyprus will never cease to support and strengthen every action that will lead to the liberation of Cyprus,” he concluded.

The statement was issued on the anniversary of the 1983 unilateral declaration in the Turkish-occupied northern part of Cyprus, which the United Nations Security Council declared legally invalid iof Cyprusn Resolution 541.

items.title_orig: †) St. Paisius (Velichkovsky) of Moldavia and Mt. Athos; Holy Martyrs and Confessors Gurias, Samonas and Abibus (Beginning of Nativity Fast); 25th Sunday after Pentecost
items.sum:
Moisiu i besueshëm (Velikovski) i Moldovisë dhe Malit.

Shën Moisiu Velikovski lindi në Poltava në Rusinë e Vogël më 21 dhjetor 1722 dhe ishte i njëmbëdhjeti nga dymbëdhjetë fëmijët.

Pasi u bë një murg rassofore (një i bekuar për të veshur rasson, por jo ende të mbushur me rroba) në manastirin Shën Nikolas Medvedevski me emrin Platoni, ai gjeti se atje nuk kishte plak me përvojë që mund t'i mësonte atij bindjen ose t'i jepte drejtim shpirtëror.

Plaku urdhëroi që vakti të vonohej kur dërgoi një Atë Athanasius për të zbuluar se çfarë i kishte ndodhur Platonit.

Ai erdhi edhe tek Ati Moisiu dhe i kërkoi t'i thoshte diçka për shpëtimin e shpirtit të tij.

Ai ra në këmbët e Atit Moisi, duke iu përgjëruar të ishte Plaku i tij.

Ati Moisiu nuk donte të ishte ndonjë plak plak, duke dëshiruar në vend të kësaj të ishte nën autoritetin e vet. Babai Besarion qëndroi tri ditë duke qarë derisa babai Moisiu pranoi ta pranonte si mik dhe jo si dishepull.

Në vitin 1754, babait Moisiu iu caktua priftëria e shenjtë dhe iu dha Sketa e profetit Elias, ku filloi të pranonte edhe më shumë dishepuj. Saint Moisius qëndroi në malin Atos për një total prej shtatëmbëdhjetë vjetësh, duke kopjuar librat grek patristik dhe duke i përkthyer ata në sllavishte.

Në 1763 Atë Moisiu shkoi në Moldavi me gjashtëdhjetë e katër dishepuj dhe iu dha manastiri Dragomirna pranë qytetit Sochava dhe në kufirin midis Bukovinës dhe Moldavisë.

Miku i tij, Hieromonk Aleksius, erdhi për ta vizituar nga vllehia dhe babai Moisiu i kërkoi ta mbushte me ton në Sma. Kur ishte në Dragomirna, Atë Moisiu ndreqi përkthimet sllave të librave të lashtë, duke i krahasuar me dorëshkrimet greke që kishte kopjuar në malin Athos.

Më 14 gusht 1779, Shën Moisiu u transferua në manastirin Neamts ku kaloi 15 vitet e fundit të jetës së tij duke përkthyer shkrimet e Etërve të Shenjtë.

Kryepeshkopi Ambroz vizitoi Saint Moisius në Neamts në 1790, duke qëndruar për dy ditë për të biseduar me Plakun.

Shën Hermani u mësua nga pleqtë, formimi frymor i të cilëve u drejtua nga Shën Moisiu.
items.text_orig:
Venerable Paisius (Velichkovsky) of Moldavia and Mt. Athos

Saint Paisius Velichkovsky was born in Poltava in Little Russia on December 21, 1722, and was the eleventh of twelve children. His father John was a priest, who named him Peter at his Baptism, in honor of Saint Peter the Metropolitan of Moscow, on whose Feast he was born.

After the children’s father died, their mother Irene raised them in piety. Peter was sent to study at the Moghila Academy in Kiev in 1735. After four years, Peter decided to leave the world and become a monk. At the age of seventeen, he went in search of a monastery and a good spiritual Father. For seven years Peter visited various monasteries, including the Kiev Caves Lavra, but he did not feel drawn to any of the monasteries of Ukraine.

After being made a rassophore monk (one blessed to wear the rasson, but not yet tonsured “into the mantle”) at the Saint Nicholas Medvedevsky Monastery with the name Platon, he found that there was no experienced Elder there who could teach him obedience or give him spiritual direction. Not wishing to begin his monastic life without such guidance, he left the monastery a week after his tonsure with the blessing of his Elder.

At first, he went to Kiev, where he happened to meet his sister-in-law, the widow of his older brother Archpriest John. She informed him of his mother’s sorrow when he left Kiev, and her mind seemed to be affected by her grief. Then one day an angel appeared to her and told her that instead of loving the Creator with her whole heart and soul, she loved His creation (her son) more.

Because of this excessive love, the angel went on, she was thinking of starving herself to death, which would result in her eternal condemnation. The angel said that by God’s grace, her son would become a monk, and that she should also renounce the world and become a nun. After this, she became calm and accepted God’s will. She entered a convent and was tonsured with the name Juliana. After about ten years, she departed to the Lord.

While at Kiev, Platon met two monks from Romania who were about to return to their country. After crossing the border into Moldavia, they came to Vlachia and the Skete of Saint Nicholas, which is called Treisteny, around 1745.

The Elder of the Skete, Hieroschemamonk Michael, was away on business in Ukraine, so Platon and his companions were welcomed by the Superior, Father Demetrius. Platon was placed under a general obedience and given a cell near the Skete, from which the church was visible.

As he was sleeping one night, the semantron was sounded calling the monks to Sunday Matins, but Platon did not hear it. He woke up and ran to the church, only to find that the Gospel had already been read, and the Canon was being sung. In his grief and shame, he did not enter the church, but returned to his cell and wept bitter tears. After the Liturgy, when it was time for the meal, the Superior and the Elder were surprised that Platon had not been seen at the services.

The Elder ordered that the meal be delayed while he sent a Father Athanasius to find out what had happened to Platon. Father Athanasius found him and asked why he was weeping. With difficulty, Platon was able to tell him the cause of his sorrow. Father Athanasius tried to console him and urged him to come to the Skete, where the others were waiting for him. Finally, he was persuaded to go.

Seeing the brethren at table but not eating, Platon fell down before them weeping and asking forgiveness. The Elder and the Superior lifted him up and heard from Father Athanasius the reason for his sorrow. The Elder told Platon not to grieve so over something that had happened involuntarily, and did his best to console him. From that time, however, the saint would not sleep lying down in bed, but sitting up on a bench.

One day the Elder Onuphrius of Kyrkoul visited the Skete and spoke about his Skete at Kyrkoul. Platon long to see Kyrkoul, and so he returned there with Father Onuphrius. He remained there for a time, conversing with Father Onuphrius about overcoming the passions, the struggle with demons, unceasing prayer, and other soul-profiting topics. This seed fell on good ground, later bearing spiritual fruit a hundredfold.

The time came when Platon was filled with a longing to visit Mount Athos. He asked the brethren of the Skete, and those of other Sketes, for their forgiveness and blessing for the journey. He also thanked them for their kindness and their paternal instruction. They blessed him and let him go in peace. At that time he was just twenty-four years old.

Platon went to Mount Athos in 1746, arriving at the Great Lavra on July 4, the eve of the Feast of Saint Athanasius of Athos. His traveling companion, Hieromonk Tryphon fell ill and died after four days. Platon would have died from the same illness, if not for the care of the Russian monks. He recovered and lived in solitude in a cell called Kaparis near the Pantokrator Monastery. He went around visiting the ascetics and solitaries, looking for a spiritual Father, but was unable to find anyone suitable.

In 1750 Saint Basil of Poiana Marului (April 15) visited the Holy Mountain and spent some time with Platon, who asked him for monastic tonsure. Elder Basil granted his request, giving him the name Paisius. Then Father Basil returned to his Skete at Vlachia.

About three months later, a young monk named Bessarion came to the Holy Mountain from Vlachia. He went around to the monasteries searching for an instructor, but did not find one. He also came to Father Paisius and asked him to tell him something about saving his soul.

Father Paisius sighed and told him that he himself had been looking for an instructor without success. Yet, feeling compassion for Father Bessarion, he talked to him a little about the qualifications necessary for a true instructor, and about the Jesus Prayer. After hearing him, Father Bessarion said, “What more do I seek?” He fell down at the feet of Father Paisius, entreating him to be his Elder.

Father Paisius did not want to be anyone’s Elder, wishing instead to be under authority himself. Father Bessarion remained for three days weeping until Father Paisius agreed to accept him as a friend, and not as a disciple. For about four years they lived together fulfilling God’s commandments, cutting off their own will and obeying one another as equals.

Other disciples began to join them, and their number continued to increase. Since they needed a priest and a confessor, they begged Father Paisius to accept ordination. He did not want to hear of this, and repeatedly refused to consent. They did not give up, however. They asked him how he could expect to teach the brethren obedience and cutting off their own will, when he disobeyed the tearful entreaties of those who wanted him to accept. Finally, he said, “May the will of God be done.”

In 1754 Father Paisius was ordained to the holy priesthood and was given the Skete of the Prophet Elias, where he began to accept even more disciples. Saint Paisius remained on Mt Athos for a total of seventeen years, copying Greek patristic books and translating them into Slavonic.

In 1763 Father Paisius went to Moldavia with sixty-four disciples, and was given the Dragomirna Monastery near the city of Sochava and on the border between Bukovina and Moldavia. Here he remained for twelve years, and the number of monks increased to three hundred and fifty.

His friend Hieromonk Alexius came to visit him from Vlachia, and Father Paisius asked him to tonsure him into the Schema. Father Alexius did so, but without changing his name. While at Dragomirna, Father Paisius corrected the Slavonic translations of patristic books by comparing them to the Greek manuscripts he had copied on Mt Athos.

The Russo-Turkish war broke out in 1768, and Moldavia and Vlachia saw many battles. Dragomirna and the forests around it became filled with refugees from the villages near the battlegrounds. Another catastrophe appeared in 1771 with the outbreak of plague. When Dragomirna and Bukovina came under the control of Austrian Catholics, Saint Paisius and his flock fled to Moldavia. In October of 1775, he went to Secu (“Beheading”) Monastery, which was dedicated to Saint John the Baptist, with many of his monks.

Secu was too small for the number of brethren, who were crowded with three to five monks in a cell. In the spring, more brethren were due to arrive from Dragomirna, so new cells had to be built. After three years of labor one hundred cells were completed, and everyone had a place. Still, the numbers increased and they had to look for a larger monastery.

Prince Constantine Muruz wrote to the Elder saying that there was no larger monastery than Neamts, about two hours from Secul. On August 14, 1779, Saint Paisius moved to Neamts Monastery where he spent the last fifteen years of his life translating the writings of the Holy Fathers. He organized the community according to the Typikon (Rule) of Mt Athos.

He gathered about a thousand monks in the monastery, instructing them in the unceasing prayer of the heart.

Archbishop Ambrose visited Saint Paisius at Neamts in 1790, staying for two days to converse with the Elder. During the Sunday Liturgy, he raised Saint Paisius to the rank of Archimandrite. He remained two more days, then departed after blessing everyone.

Saint Paisius fell asleep in the Lord on November 15, 1794 at the age of seventy-two. It is possible that God revealed the date of his death to him beforehand, for he stopped translating books. He only reviewed and corrected what had already been translated.

He was ill for four days, but felt well enough to attend the Liturgy on Sunday. After the service, he asked everyone to come and receive his blessing. He said farewell to them all, then returned to his cell and would not receive anyone.

A few days later, on November 15, he received the Holy Mysteries again and surrendered his soul to God. His funeral was conducted by Bishop Benjamin of Tuma, and was attended by multitudes of priests, monks, laymen, nobles and ordinary people.

The holy relics of Saint Paisius were uncovered in 1846, 1853, 1861 and 1872, and were found to be incorrupt.

Saint Paisius has had an enormous influence, not only in Romania, but throughout the Orthodox world. His disciples traveled to Russia, sparking the spiritual revival of the nineteenth century with Slavonic translations of the PHILOKALIA and the tradition of eldership which they had learned from Saint Paisius.

This influence has been felt even in America through Saint Herman of Alaska (December 13). Saint Herman was taught by Elders whose spiritual formation was guided by Saint Paisius. He first met Father Nazarius, who became his Elder at Valaam, at Sarov, then followed him to Sanaxar when Saint Theodore (February 19) was their igumen.

One of the books that Saint Herman brought with him to America was the Slavonic PHILOKALIA, printed in 1794. He absorbed the spiritual wisdom that it contained, and imparted it to others.

Troparion — Tone 2

Having become a stranger on earth, / you reached the heavenly homeland, venerable Father Paisius. / You taught the faithful to lift up their minds to God, / crying out to Him with all their hearts: / “Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, have mercy on me a sinner!”

items.text:
Të shtunën, më 14 nëntor 2026, në Manastirin e Shën Vlashit, u zhvillua takimi i parë i priftërinjve dhe priftëreshave të Kryepiskopatës së Shenjtë të Tiranës, Durrësit dhe gjithë Shqipërisë, me temë “Të mbash gjallë dhuntinë e Perëndisë” (2 Timoteut 1:6). Takimi u organizua me përkujdesjen dhe bekimin atëror të Fortlumturisë së Tij, Kryepiskopit Joan, i cili mori pjesë dhe përcolli këshilla e fjalë inkurajuese për klerikët dhe familjet e tyre. I ftuar ishte Protopresviter Atë Mattheo Halaris, i cili, duke u mbështetur në përvojën e tij të pasur shpirtërore dhe baritore, zhvilloi temën mbi thirrjen priftërore dhe rëndësinë e ruajtjes së gjallë të dhuntisë së priftërisë.

Gjatë ligjëratës së tij, Atë Mattheo u përqendrua në tri shtylla themelore të jetës priftërore: unitetin dhe marrëdhënien shpirtërore të klerikut me Episkopin e tij, jetën dhe kultivimin shpirtëror të familjes priftërore, si dhe shërbimin baritor dhe rigjallërimin e enorive. Takimi u zhvillua në një atmosferë të ngrohtë e vëllazërore, duke krijuar mundësi për reflektim shpirtëror, bashkëbisedim dhe forcimin e lidhjeve ndërmjet familjeve priftërore. Kjo veprimtari shënon fillimin e një nisme që synon të vazhdojë edhe me takime të tjera, duke nxitur frymën e komunitetit, mbështetjen e ndërsjellë dhe përkushtimin në shërbimin ndaj Kishës dhe besimtarëve. Një falënderim i përzemërt u drejtohet të gjithë atyre që kontribuan me përkushtim në organizimin, përgatitjen dhe mbarëvajtjen e këtij takimi, duke ndihmuar që kjo ditë të ishte një përvojë e bukur dhe e bekuar.

items.title_orig: Archbishop of America approved four new ordinations to the diaconate
items.sum:
Kryepeshkopi Elpidofos i Amerikës ka miratuar bashkërendimin e katër burrave në Diakonatin e Shenjtë, duke i caktuar ata të shërbejnë në famullitë orthodhokse greke dhe në komunitetet misionare në Shtetet e Bashkuara dhe Amerikën Qendrore.

Emanuel Salem është miratuar për bashkërendimin e Diakonatit të Shenjtë dhe është caktuar të shërbejë në Anunciation of theocos Church në Akron, Ohajo, brenda Metropolisit të Shenjtë të Pitsburgut.

Në mënyrë të ngjashme, Xhorxh Damiris është miratuar për bashkërendimin e Diakonatit të Shenjtë dhe është caktuar si një dhjak i përhershëm në Kishën e Shenjtë të Trinitetit në Uiçita, Kansas, edhe brenda Metropolisit të Shenjtë të Denverit.
items.text_orig:
Archbishop Elpidophoros of America has approved the ordination of four men to the Holy Diaconate, assigning them to serve in Greek Orthodox parishes and missionary communities in the United States and Central America.

According to an announcement published by the Orthodox Observer on November 12, 2026, the Archbishop approved the ordinations in accordance with his responsibilities under the Charter of the Greek Orthodox Archdiocese of America.

Emmanuel Salem has been approved for ordination to the Holy Diaconate and assigned to serve at the Annunciation of the Theotokos Church in Akron, Ohio, within the Holy Metropolis of Pittsburgh.

Jesse Brandow has also been approved for ordination to the Holy Diaconate and assigned to serve in the Holy Metropolis of Mexico. He will remain under the canonical jurisdiction of the Greek Orthodox Archdiocese of America while continuing his missionary work through the Orthodox Christian Mission Center (OCMC) in Guatemala and the surrounding region.

Troy Vinson Montanez has been approved for ordination to the Holy Diaconate and assigned to serve as a permanent deacon at the Annunciation of the Theotokos Church in Lincoln, Nebraska, within the Holy Metropolis of Denver.

Similarly, George Damiris has been approved for ordination to the Holy Diaconate and assigned as a permanent deacon at Holy Trinity Church in Wichita, Kansas, also within the Holy Metropolis of Denver.

Photo by Orthodox Observer/Dimitrios Panagos

Ylli serb i tenisit Novak Gjokoviç vizitoi Malin Atos, Greqi, ku ndoqi festimet fetare në manastirin historik Hilandar për nder të Shën Milutin, mbretit të Serbisë dhe një nga bamirësitë më të rëndësishëm të manastirit.

Të premten, 13 nëntor 2026, atleti i njohur ndërkombëtarisht mori pjesë në shërbimin festive mbajtur në manastirin e kishës kryesore të manastirit, duke shënuar festën e Shën Milutinit, i cili përnderohet për kontributin e tij të rëndësishëm në manastirin orthodhoks serb.
items.text_orig:
Serbian tennis star Novak Djokovic visited Mount Athos, Greece, where he attended religious celebrations at the historic Hilandar Monastery in honor of Saint Milutin, King of Serbia and one of the monastery’s most important benefactors.

On Friday, November 13, 2026, the internationally renowned athlete participated in the festive service held at the monastery’s main church, marking the feast of Saint Milutin, who is venerated for his significant contributions to the Serbian Orthodox monastery.

During his visit, Djokovic also recited the Lord’s Prayer, the “Our Father,” inside the monastery’s main church.

The Serbian tennis player’s participation in the religious celebrations formed part of his pilgrimage to Mount Athos, the monastic peninsula traditionally known as the “Garden of the Virgin Mary.”

Hilandar Monastery holds particular spiritual and historical significance for the Serbian Orthodox Church, serving as an important center of Serbian Orthodox monasticism and religious heritage.

items.summary: The Romanian church in Cedar Park, Texas, United States, has prepared for the consecration of its church by bringing from Romania fragments of the relics of Holy Princess Maria Brâncoveanu and Venerable Matrona of Hurezi. The events began on Friday evening with the celebration…
items.text:
The Romanian church in Cedar Park, Texas, United States, has prepared for the consecration of its church by bringing from Romania fragments of the relics of Holy Princess Maria Brâncoveanu and Venerable Matrona of Hurezi.

The events began on Friday evening with the celebration of Vespers, officiated by Hirësia e Tij Ioan Casian, Romanian Orthodox Bishop of Canada, at St Mary’s Church in Cedar Park.

At the end of the service, Fr Daniel Mercurie Apostol, Vicar of the Archdiocese of Râmnic, delivered a sermon highlighting the role of holy women in the life of the Romanian communities in the diaspora.

The clergyman brought in pilgrimage to Texas fragments of the relics of Saint Maria Brâncoveanu and Saint Matrona of Hurezi, giving the faithful the opportunity to honour them and learn more about the lives of the two new saints.

Christmas carols and Byzantine music concert

Friday evening’s cultural programme included a concert of Christmas carols and Byzantine music performed by the Anastasios Byzantine Choir from Cluj-Napoca, Romania, conducted by neurosurgeon Iustinian Ioachim Simion.

The schedule of events linked to the Sunday consecration also included two conferences delivered by Dr Iustinian Simion and Archdeacon Sorin Mihalache.

St Mary’s Parish in Cedar Park, located near the city of Austin, began its activity as a Romanian Orthodox mission in the state of Texas in 2002. The construction of the church to be consecrated began in 2024.

items.sum:
Kisha Orthodhokse gjeorgjiane përkujtoi të premten, më 13 nëntor 2026, 100.000 martirët e Tbilisit, duke nderuar të krishterët që u vranë gjatë pushtimit të Gjeorgjisë në shekullin e 13 - të.

Patriarku u bashkua me Metropolitan Teodorin e Akhaltsikhe dhe Tao-Klarjeti, Chorbishop të Catholicos-Patriark; Metropolitian Andria e Gori dhe Ateni; Peshkopi Melkicedeku i Margvetit dhe Ubisa; Peshkopi Grigol i Tsalkës; Peshkopi Vaktang i Nikortstimes dhe anëtarë të tjerë të klerit.
items.text_orig:
The Georgian Orthodox Church commemorated the 100,000 Martyrs of Tbilisi on Friday, November 13, 2026, honoring the Christians who were killed during the Khwarazmian invasion of Georgia in the 13th century.

Catholicos-Patriarch Shio III of All Georgia, Archbishop of Mtskheta-Tbilisi and Metropolitan of Bichvinta and Tskhum-Abkhazia, presided over a memorial prayer service at Metekhi Bridge in Tbilisi, the site traditionally associated with the martyrdom.

The Patriarch was joined by Metropolitan Theodore of Akhaltsikhe and Tao-Klarjeti, Chorbishop of the Catholicos-Patriarch; Metropolitan Andria of Gori and Ateni; Bishop Melchizedek of Margveti and Ubisa; Bishop Grigol of Tsalka; Bishop Vakhtang of Nikortsminda; and other members of the clergy.

Following the service, Patriarch Shio addressed those gathered, delivering a sermon on the spiritual and historical significance of the commemoration.

The annual observance honors the memory of the 100,000 Christians who, according to Georgian Orthodox tradition, were martyred in Tbilisi in 1227 after refusing to renounce their faith during the invasion led by Jalal ad-Din.

The commemoration remains an important occasion in the Georgian Orthodox Church’s calendar, recalling the martyrs’ steadfast faith and their place in Georgia’s religious history.

items.title_orig: Patriarch of Antioch: Church unity requires solidarity and mutual trust
items.sum:
Patriarku Ioanis X i Antiokisë dhe i gjithë Lindjes përshëndetën pjesëmarrësit në Konferencën e Përgjithshme të Lëvizjes Orthodhokse të Rinisë në manastirin patriarkal të Zonjës sonë të Balamandit të premten, më 13 nëntor 2026.

Pas shërbimit Vespers, patriarku iu drejtua pjesëmarrësve, duke i inkurajuar të përqafonin besimin e tyre të krishterë si pjesë e gjallë dhe e pandashme e ekzistencës së tyre, pavarësisht nga presionet dhe sfidat e jetës së përditshme.

Duke iu referuar misionit dhe veprimtarive të Lëvizjes Orthodhokse të Rinisë, patriarku Xhon paralajmëroi kundër bashkimit tepër të lidhur me strukturat e ashpra institucionale, duke u kërkuar anëtarëve të ruajnë frymën dhe entuziazmin e lëvizjes prej themeluesve të saj.
items.text_orig:
Patriarch Ioannis X of Antioch and All the East welcomed participants in the General Conference of the Orthodox Youth Movement at the Patriarchal Monastery of Our Lady of Balamand on Friday, November 13, 2026.

Following the Vespers service, the Patriarch addressed the participants, encouraging them to embrace their Christian faith as a living and inseparable part of their existence, despite the pressures and challenges of everyday life.

He placed particular emphasis on prayer and spiritual vigilance, describing them as essential elements of the journey toward self-knowledge, purification, illumination, and ultimately sanctification.

Referring to the mission and activities of the Orthodox Youth Movement, Patriarch John warned against becoming overly attached to rigid institutional structures, urging members to preserve the spirit and enthusiasm of the movement’s founders.

“You, the members of the Movement, must remain people of action, drawing inspiration from the flame of the first pioneers who came before you,” he stated.

Concluding his address, the Patriarch emphasized the importance of unity within the Church, calling on participants to avoid unilateral actions and instead cultivate a spirit of cooperation, solidarity, mutual listening, and trust.

His remarks highlighted the importance of maintaining a living faith and strengthening the bonds of communion within the Orthodox Church.
