Apostulli Filip flitet disa herë në Ungjillin e Shenjtë: ai i solli Krishtit, apostullit Nataniel (ai).

Dokumentet e zbuluara kohët e fundit dëshmojnë se apostulli i Shenjtë Filip shoqëroi profetin e shenjtë Endrju në Shitia (dobja e sotme). Emilian Popesku pohon: Studimi i fundit ka arritur në përfundimin se apostulli i Shenjtë Filip mund të vendoset së bashku me apostullin e shenjtë Endrju si misionarë në tokën rumune dhe kështu për ne rumunët, kjo ditë është po aq e rëndësishme sa ai që i është kushtuar apostullit të Shenjtë Endrju.

Apostulli Filip u siguroi një peshkop, me emrin Narcis (një nga shtatëdhjetë apostujt, 4 janar).

Nga Azotusi, apostulli Filip u nis për në Hieropolis sirian (ka disa qytete të këtij emri) ku, të nxitura nga farisenjtë, judenjtë dogjën shtëpinë e Heroit, i cili kishte marrë me vete apostullin Filip dhe donin ta vritnin apostullin.

Pastaj, apostulli Filip mbërriti në qytetin e Frigjian Hieropolit, ku kishte shumë tempuj paganë. Apostulli Filip me fuqinë e lutjes vrau gjarprin dhe shëroi shumë prej tyre, të kafshuar nga gjarpërinjtë.

Pasi mori vesh se gruaja e tij kishte pranuar krishterimin, guvernatori Amfipatos urdhëroi të arrestonin Shën Filipin, motrën e tij dhe apostullin Bartolomeu që udhëtonin me ta.

Apostulli i shenjtë Filip nuk duhet ngatërruar me Saint Filip Dikonin (në 11 tetor), një nga të shtatëdhjetat.

Troparioni Tone 3.

Shën Gregori Palama, kryepeshkopi i Selanikut

Pas rënies së Nikodemit të Vjetër, Shën Gregori kaloi tetë vjet të luftës frymore nën udhëheqjen e Bosforit të Vjetër dhe pas vdekjes së dytë, Gregori u transferua në Lavra të Shën Athanasiusit (5 korrik).

Më 1331 shenjtori u tërhoq në malin Atos dhe jetoi i vetmuar në Sketën e Shën Savës, pranë Lavrës së Shën Athanasiusit.
items.text_orig:
Holy Apostle Philip

He was a native of the city of Bethsaida in Galilee. He had a profound depth of knowledge of the Holy Scripture, and rightly discerning the meaning of the Old Testament prophecies, he awaited the coming of the Messiah.

Through the call of the Savior (John 1:43), Philip followed Him. The Apostle Philip is spoken about several times in the Holy Gospel: he brought to Christ the Apostle Nathaniel (i.e. Bartholomew, April 22, June 30, and August 25. See John. 1:46). The Lord asks him where to buy bread for five thousand men (John. 6: 5-7). He brought certain of the Hellenized Jews wanting to see Jesus (John. 12:21-22); and finally, at the Last Supper he asked Christ to show them the Father (John. 14:8).

Recently discovered documents attest that Holy Apostle Philip accompanied Holy Apostle Andrew to Schitya (present-day Dobrudja). Prof. Emilian Popescu states: “Recent research has concluded that Holy Apostle Philip can be placed alongside Holy Apostle Andrew as missionaries on Romanian soil, and therefore, for us Romanians, this day is just as important as the one dedicated to Holy Apostle Andrew.”

After the Ascension of the Lord, the Apostle Philip preached the Word of God in Galilee, accompanying his preaching with miracles. Thus, he restored to life a dead infant in the arms of its mother. From Galilee he went to Greece, and preached among the Jews that had settled there. Some of them reported the preaching of the Apostle to Jerusalem. In response, some scribes arrived in Greece from Jerusalem, with one of the Jewish chief priests at their head, to interrogate the Apostle Philip.

The Apostle Philip exposed the lie of the chief priest, who said that the disciples of Christ had stolen away and hidden the body of Christ. Philip told instead how the Pharisees had bribed the soldiers on watch, to deliberately spread this rumor.

When the Jewish chief priest and his companions began to insult the Lord and lunged at the Apostle Philip, they suddenly were struck blind. By his prayer the Apostle restored everyone’s sight. Seeing this miracle, many believed in Christ. The Apostle Philip provided a bishop for them, by the name of Narcissus (one of the Seventy Apostles, January 4).

From Greece the Apostle Philip went to Parthia, and then to the city of Azotus, where he healed an eye affliction of the daughter of a local resident named Nikoklides, who had received him into his home, and then baptized his whole family.

From Azotus the Apostle Philip set out to Syrian Hieropolis (there were several cities of this name) where, stirred up by the Pharisees, the Jews burned the house of Heros, who had taken in the Apostle Philip, and they wanted to kill the apostle. The apostle performed several miracles: the healing of the hand of the city official Aristarchus, withered when he attempted to strike the apostle; and restoring a dead child to life.

When they saw these marvels, they repented and many accepted holy Baptism. After making Heros the bishop at Hieropolis, the Apostle Philip went on to Syria, Asia Minor, Lydia, Emessa, and everywhere preaching the Gospel and undergoing sufferings. Both he and his sister Mariamne (February 17) were pelted with stones, locked up in prison, and thrown out of villages.

Then the Apostle Philip arrived in the city of Phrygian Hieropolis, where there were many pagan temples. There was also a pagan temple where people worshiped an enormous serpent as a god. The Apostle Philip by the power of prayer killed the serpent and healed many bitten by snakes.

Among those healed was the wife of the city prefect, Amphipatos. Having learned that his wife had accepted Christianity, the prefect Amphipatos gave orders to arrest Saint Philip, his sister, and the Apostle Bartholomew traveling with them. At the urging of the pagan priests of the temple of the serpent, Amphipatos ordered the holy Apostles Philip and Bartholomew to be crucified.

Suddenly, an earthquake struck, and it knocked down all those present at the place of judgment. Hanging upon the cross by the pagan temple of the serpent, the Apostle Philip prayed for those who had crucified him, asking God to save them from the ravages of the earthquake. Seeing this happen, the people believed in Christ and began to demand that the apostles be taken down from the crosses. The Apostle Bartholomew was still alive when he was taken down, and he baptized all those believing and established a bishop for them.

But the Apostle Philip, through whose prayers everyone remained alive, except for Amphipatos and the pagan priests, died on the cross.

Mariamne his sister buried his body, and went with the Apostle Bartholomew to preach in Armenia, where the Apostle Bartholomew was crucified (June 11); Mariamne herself then preached until her own death at Lykaonia.

The holy Apostle Philip is not to be confused with Saint Philip the Deacon (October 11), one of the Seventy.

Troparion — Tone 3 Holy Apostle Philip, / entreat the merciful God / to grant our souls forgiveness of transgressions.

Saint Gregory Palamas, Archbishop of Thessalonica

He was born in the year 1296 in Constantinople. Saint Gregory’s father became a prominent dignitary at the court of Andronicus II Paleologos (1282-1328), but he soon died, and Andronicus himself took part in the raising and education of the fatherless boy.

Endowed with fine abilities and great diligence, Gregory mastered all the subjects which then comprised the full course of medieval higher education. The emperor hoped that the youth would devote himself to government work. But Gregory, barely twenty years old, withdrew to Mount Athos in the year 1316 (other sources say 1318) and became a novice in the Vatopedi monastery under the guidance of the monastic Elder Saint Nicodemus of Vatopedi (July 11).

There he was tonsured and began on the path of asceticism. A year later, the holy Evangelist John the Theologian appeared to him in a vision and promised him his spiritual protection. Gregory’s mother and sisters also became monastics.

After the demise of the Elder Nicodemus, Saint Gregory spent eight years of spiritual struggle under the guidance of the Elder Nicephorus, and after the latter’s death, Gregory transferred to the Lavra of Saint Athanasius (July 5). Here he served in the trapeza, and then became a church singer. But after three years, he resettled in the small skete of Glossia, striving for a greater degree of spiritual perfection.

The head of this monastery began to teach the young man the method of unceasing prayer and mental activity, which had been cultivated by monastics, beginning with the great desert ascetics of the fourth century: Evagrius Pontikos and Saint Macarius of Egypt (January 19).

Later on, in the eleventh century Saint Simeon the New Theologian (March 12) provided detailed instruction in mental activity for those praying in an outward manner, and the ascetics of Athos put it into practice. The experienced use of mental prayer (or prayer of the heart), requiring solitude and quiet, is called “Hesychasm” (from the Greek “hesychia” meaning calm, silence), and those practicing it were called “hesychasts.”

During his stay at Glossia the future hierarch Gregory became fully imbued with the spirit of hesychasm and adopted it as an essential part of his life. In the year 1326, because of the threat of Turkish invasions, he and the brethren retreated to Thessalonica, where he was then ordained to the holy priesthood.

Saint Gregory combined his priestly duties with the life of a hermit. Five days of the week he spent in silence and prayer, and only on Saturday and Sunday did he come out to his people. He celebrated divine services and preached sermons.

For those present in church, his teaching often evoked both tenderness and tears. Sometimes he visited theological gatherings of the city’s educated youth, headed by the future patriarch, Isidore. After he returned from a visit to Constantinople, he found a place suitable for solitary life near Thessalonica the region of Bereia. Soon he gathered here a small community of solitary monks and guided it for five years.

In 1331 the saint withdrew to Mt Athos and lived in solitude at the skete of Saint Sava, near the Lavra of Saint Athanasius. In 1333 he was appointed Igumen of the Esphigmenou monastery in the northern part of the Holy Mountain. In 1336 the saint returned to the skete of Saint Sava, where he devoted himself to theological works, continuing with this until the end of his life.

In the 1330s events took place in the life of the Eastern Church which put Saint Gregory among the most significant universal apologists of Orthodoxy, and brought him great renown as a teacher of hesychasm.

About the year 1330 the learned monk Barlaam had arrived in Constantinople from Calabria, in Italy. He was the author of treatises on logic and astronomy, a skilled and sharp-witted orator, and he received a university chair in the capital city and began to expound on the works of Saint Dionysius the Areopagite (October 3), whose “apophatic” (“negative”, in contrast to “kataphatic” or “positive”) theology was acclaimed in equal measure in both the Eastern and the Western Churches.

Soon Barlaam journeyed to Mt Athos, where he became acquainted with the spiritual life of the hesychasts’. Saying that it was impossible to know the essence of God, he declared mental prayer a heretical error.

Journeying from Mount Athos to Thessalonica, and from there to Constantinople, and later again to Thessalonica, Barlaam entered into disputes with the monks and attempted to demonstrate the created, material nature of the light of Tabor (i.e. at the Transfiguration). He ridiculed the teachings of the monks about the methods of prayer and about the uncreated light seen by the hesychasts.

Saint Gregory, at the request of the Athonite monks, replied with verbal admonitions at first. But seeing the futility of such efforts, he put his theological arguments in writing. Thus appeared the “Triads in Defense of the Holy Hesychasts” (1338). Towards the year 1340 the Athonite ascetics, with the assistance of the saint, compiled a general response to the attacks of Barlaam, the so-called “Hagiorite Tome.”

At the Constantinople Council of 1341 in the church of Hagia Sophia Saint Gregory Palamas debated with Barlaam, focusing upon the nature of the light of Mount Tabor. On May 27, 1341 the Council accepted the position of Saint Gregory Palamas, that God, unapproachable in His Essence, reveals Himself through His energies, which are directed towards the world and are able to be perceived, like the light of Tabor, but which are neither material nor created. The teachings of Barlaam were condemned as heresy, and he himself was anathemized and fled to Calabria.

But the dispute between the Palamites and the Barlaamites was far from over. To these latter belonged Barlaam’s disciple, the Bulgarian monk Akyndinos, and also Patriarch John XIV Kalekos (1341-1347); the emperor Andronicus III Paleologos (1328-1341) was also inclined toward their opinion. Akyndinos, whose name means “one who inflicts no harm,” actually caused great harm by his heretical teaching.

Akyndinos wrote a series of tracts in which he declared Saint Gregory and the Athonite monks guilty of causing church disorders. The saint, in turn, wrote a detailed refutation of Akyndinos’ errors.

The patriarch supported Akyndinos and called Saint Gregory the cause of all disorders and disturbances in the Church (1344) and had him locked up in prison for four years. In 1347, when John the XIV was replaced on the patriarchal throne by Isidore (1347-1349), Saint Gregory Palamas was set free and was made Archbishop of Thessalonica.

Në këtë mesazh solemn, kryepeshkopi kujton ata që kanë humbur jetën e tyre, ofron lutje për shërimin e të plagosurve dhe kthimin e sigurt të atyre që janë ende të humbur dhe i shpreh mirënjohjen e tij të thellë për reagjeruesit e parë dhe personelin e emergjencës, guximi, dedikimi dhe shërbimi vetëmohues, vazhdojnë të sjellin shpresë në mes të kësaj tragjedie të tmerrshme.
items.text_orig:
In the wake of the tragic collapse of an apartment building on Flatbush Avenue in Brooklyn, Archbishop Elpidophoros of America expressed the profound sorrow and heartfelt prayers of the Greek Orthodox Archdiocese of America.

In this solemn message, the Archbishop remembers those who have lost their lives, offers prayers for the healing of the injured and the safe return of those still missing, and extends his deepest gratitude to the first responders and emergency personnel whose courage, dedication, and selfless service continue to bring hope amid this heartbreaking tragedy.

Read below the message of Archbishop Elpidophoros of America:

We are heartbroken by the collapse of the apartment building on Flatbush Avenue. We pray for the souls of those who have died. May their memory be eternal. We ask God to heal the injured, and we pray with all our hearts that every one of our neighbors will be found and brought home to their families. Our parishes, especially those in Brooklyn, join us in this prayer.

The women and men of the FDNY, its EMS crews, the NYPD, and every agency at the site have worked through the night and into the rain, searching for any sign of life. They are giving everything they have to people they have never met. We owe them gratitude, and we ask the Lord to keep them safe as their work goes on.

Në 12 nëntor të këtij viti, Catholicos-Patriark Shio III i të gjithë Gjeorgjisë mori përfaqësues të Federatës së Futbollit Gjeorgjian dhe anëtarë të ekipit kombëtar gjeorgjian të futbollit në Rezidencën Patriarkale.

Gjithashtu të pranishëm në takim ishin Metropolitan Gerasimos (Shrashenidze) i Zugdidit dhe Tsaishit, Kreu i Departamentit të Punëve të Jashtme të Patriarkatit të viteve; Metropoliti Endrju (Gvazava) i Gori dhe Atenit; Peshkopi Vaktang (Liparteliani) i Nikortstimes dhe sekretari i Catholicos-Patriark, Kryepriftërtari Majkëll Botkoveli.

Gjatë takimit, patriarku theksoi se pjesëmarrja e ekipit kombëtar në Kampionatin Evropian i kishte sjellë gëzim të madh të gjithë vendit.
items.text_orig:
On 12 November of this year, Catholicos-Patriarch Shio III of All Georgia received representatives of the Georgian Football Federation and members of the Georgian national football team at the Patriarchal Residence.

Also present at the meeting were Metropolitan Gerasimos (Sharashenidze) of Zugdidi and Tsaishi, Head of the Patriarchate’s Department of Foreign Affairs; Metropolitan Andrew (Gvazava) of Gori and Ateni; Bishop Vakhtang (Liparteliani) of Nikortsminda; and the Secretary to the Catholicos-Patriarch, Archpriest Michael Botkoveli.

During the meeting, the Patriarch emphasised that the national team’s participation in the European Championship had brought immense joy to the entire country. He placed particular emphasis on the athletes’ faith and the example they set in public life, demonstrating Christian values both on and off the pitch.

He also offered the members of the national team fatherly spiritual guidance, expressing his wish that they excel not only in sporting competitions but also in their spiritual lives.

The President of the Georgian Football Federation, Mr Levan Kobiashvili, thanked the Patriarch for his support and blessing. He noted that the team is fully aware of its responsibility towards the younger generation and is working with dedication and consistency in pursuit of further achievements in the future.

For his part, the Federation’s Vice-President, Mr Kakha Chuburidze, thanked the Catholicos-Patriarch for his warm hospitality and, on behalf of the national team and the Federation, conveyed their love and profound respect for him.

He further stressed that the prayers and blessings of the Patriarch and the clergy are of particular importance to the team, adding that the visit to the Patriarchate was a source of great joy and honour for them.

At the conclusion of the meeting, the Patriarch presented each of his guests with a cross as a blessing.

Photos: Nino Sozashvili

Të enjten, 12 nëntor 2026, dita në të cilën Kisha Orthodhokse Serbe përkujton Saint Milutin, patriarku Porfijeria i Serbisë kryesoi Liturgjinë Hyjnore në kishën e Shën Markut, lajmëtarin në qarkun Tashman të Beogradit, me rastin e festës së Shërbimit Ushtarak të Forcave të Armatosura Serbe.

Koncelebrat me Primatën e Kishës Orthodhokse Serbe qenë Metropolitan Arsenije i Nish, Metropolitan Jovan i Shumadija, Metropolitan Ilarion i Timok dhe Peshkopi Dositj i Lipljanit, i cili shërben gjithashtu si peshkop ushtarak.

Rasti shënoi gjithashtu një përvjetor të rëndësishëm: përvjetorin e pesëmbëdhjetë të nënshkrimit, në emër të Kishës lokale, të një marrëveshjeje midis patriarkut të vdekur serb Irinej dhe Ministrisë së Mbrojtjes së Republikës së Serbisë, që parashikon rifutjen e klerit dhe kishës në vend të Forcave të Armatosura.

Stojan Batiniç, gjeneral-brigadier në pension, për kontributin e tij të paçmueshëm në ngritjen e Shërbimit Ushtarak të Kalapisë brenda Brigadës së parë të Forcave Tokësore.

Zoran Lummura, gjeneral-brigadier në pension, për kontributin e tij të paçmueshëm në ngritjen e Shërbimit Ushtarak të Kalapturës brenda Brigadës së 4-të të Forcave Tokësore.

Nenad Nendiriç, Oficer i Varrantit të Forcave të Armatosura Serbe, në njohjen e dedikimit të tij ndaj shërbimit të tij ndaj kishës si ndihmës kapiten ushtarak në batalionin e 41-të të këmbësorisë të Brigadës së 4-të të Forcave tokësore.

Dezhan Ivkoviç, oficer i pensionuar i Uorrantit, në vlerësim të dedikimit të tij ndaj shërbimit të tij ndaj Kishës si ndihmës i kapitenit ushtarak në brigadën e parë të forcave tokësore.

Sinisha Trbojeviç, oficere në pension, në shenjë mirënjohjeje për përkushtimin e tij ndaj shërbimit të tij ndaj kishës si një ndihmës kapiten ushtarak në Brigadën e 204-të Ajrore.

Angelko Stojkov, oficer i pensionuar i Varrantit, në mirënjohje të dedikimit të tij ndaj shërbimit të tij si ndihmës i kapitenit ushtarak në Akademinë Ushtarake Mjekësore.
items.text_orig:
On Thursday, November 12, 2026, the day on which the Serbian Orthodox Church commemorates Saint King Milutin, Patriarch Porfirije of Serbia presided over the Divine Liturgy at the Church of Saint Mark the Apostle in the Tašmajdan district of Belgrade, on the occasion of the feast of the Military Chaplaincy Service of the Serbian Armed Forces.

Concelebrating with the Primate of the Serbian Orthodox Church were Metropolitan Arsenije of Niš, Metropolitan Jovan of Šumadija, Metropolitan Ilarion of Timok, and Bishop Dositej of Lipljan, who also serves as Military Bishop.

The occasion also marked an important anniversary: the fifteenth anniversary of the signing, on behalf of the local Church, of an agreement between the late Serbian Patriarch Irinej and the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Serbia, providing for the reintroduction of clergy and the Church into the country’s Armed Forces.

At the conclusion of the Divine Liturgy, Patriarch Porfirije, accompanied by his brother hierarchs, the clergy, and the faithful, celebrated the blessing and sanctification of the festive bread before delivering an address.

At the beginning of his homily, the Patriarch emphasized that “the human person was not created as a mosaic composed of separate pieces, of many different parts, but as a unity, as an indivisible whole, which is revealed and affirmed as the image of God through the various aspects and different circumstances of human life.”

For this reason, he stressed, human life cannot be divided into a sacred sphere, concerning prayer and the Church, and a secular sphere, concerning life in the world.

“For us, such a division does not exist. Everything has been created to become Church,” the Patriarch said. He continued:

“The Church is broader, deeper, and higher than time and space. It encompasses everything and permeates everything. There is nothing in this world that can restrict it or contain the Church within itself. This is why the Church is present in the world: so that it may be present at every moment of history. Therefore, it is neither paradoxical nor strange that the Church is also present in the army of our people, in the Armed Forces of our state, and that priests constitute an integral part of military life.”

Speaking more specifically about the mission of a military chaplain, Serbian Patriarch Porfirije noted:

“The priest is there to celebrate the Divine Liturgy and pray to God on behalf of all those serving in the Armed Forces. He is not there to provoke conflicts or fuel hostilities. Neither in the military nor anywhere else is a priest called to divide people.

“A priest who uses expressions such as ‘our own’ and ‘outsiders’ is in the wrong place. Although he bears the grace of God, he is failing to fulfil his calling and is bringing harm upon himself. This, of course, has wider consequences, as it becomes a stumbling block and creates confusion among those who seek salvation and the meaning of their existence in the Church.

“Therefore, a priest is not in the military to divide people, considering some to be his own and others strangers. Everyone is his own, because everyone belongs to Christ. With the blessing of his Bishop and his Church, which stands in the place of Christ, he is there to bear witness to Christ, proclaim the Kingdom of Heaven, and stand alongside the soldier, teaching him prayer and humility.

“He is to teach him not only courage, but above all moral character and nobility of soul, as our people say. This means spiritual discipline and the struggle against one’s passions, especially pride, self-love, and spiritual blindness, for these are the very ground in which hatred takes root.

“The priest is there to teach the soldier to pray to God, to show mercy, and to cultivate a contrite heart. Only in this way can every soldier truly and authentically fulfil both his mission and his purpose.”

Also concelebrating at the Divine Liturgy were Archimandrite Nektarios, Secretary-General of the Holy Synod of Bishops of the Serbian Orthodox Church; Protopresbyter-Stavrophor Branislav Borota; Protopresbyter Georgije Stojisavljević, Director of the Patriarchal Office; Protopresbyter Siniša Piljanović of the Diocese of Niš; Protod eacon Professor Dragan Radić; Protodeacon Nikola Eraković of the Diocese of Niš; Hierodeacon Ilija of the Diocese of Timok; and Deacons Nikola Kostić, Vasilije Perić, and Lazar Marjanović of the Diocese of Šumadija.

Military chaplains also took part in the Divine Liturgy. They included Protopresbyter and Major Predrag Đokić, Head of the Military Chaplaincy Service; Protopresbyters and Majors Georgije Dimić and Ivan Avramović from Niš, as well as Nemanja Petrović from Belgrade; Protopresbyter Aleksandar Šovil, Major, from Belgrade; Priests and First-Class Captains Goran Sandić from Belgrade, Aleksandar Sekulić from Pančevo, Aleksandar Sarčanski from Novi Sad, Vladan Vuković from Kraljevo, and Ivan Ganić and Aleksandar Milovanović from Niš; Priests and Lieutenants Stefan Petrović from Kruševac, Miloš Kočić from Raška, and Srđan Vasiljević from Zaječar; as well as Priest and Second Lieutenant Milijan Kočanović from Kuršumlija.

On this official occasion, Serbian Patriarch Porfirije, acting in accordance with a decision of the Holy Synod of Bishops of the Serbian Orthodox Church, conferred the Church’s highest distinction, the Order of Saint Varnava of Hvostan, upon the following individuals:

Mr. Željko Petrović, retired Major General, in recognition of his service to the 1st Land Forces Brigade, the Training Command, and the Defence Inspectorate.

Mr. Stojan Batinić, retired Brigadier General, for his invaluable contribution to establishing the Military Chaplaincy Service within the 1st Land Forces Brigade.

Mr. Marinko Pavlović, retired Brigadier General, for his invaluable contribution to the 2nd Land Forces Brigade.

Mr. Zoran Lumbura, retired Brigadier General, for his invaluable contribution to establishing the Military Chaplaincy Service within the 4th Land Forces Brigade.

Mr. Nenad Ćirić, Warrant Officer of the Serbian Armed Forces, in recognition of his dedication to his service to the Church as an assistant military chaplain in the 41st Infantry Battalion of the 4th Land Forces Brigade.

Mr. Dejan Ivković, retired Warrant Officer, in recognition of his dedication to his service to the Church as an assistant military chaplain in the 1st Land Forces Brigade.

Mr. Siniša Trbojević, retired Warrant Officer, in recognition of his dedication to his service to the Church as an assistant military chaplain in the 204th Air Brigade.

Mr. Anđelko Stojkov, retired Warrant Officer, in recognition of his dedication to his service as an assistant military chaplain at the Military Medical Academy.

items.title_orig: Patriarch of Alexandria to be conferred with an Honorary Doctorate by the School of Medicine of the University of Crete
items.sum:
Papa dhe patriarku Teodori II i Aleksandrisë dhe i gjithë Afrikës do të këshillohen me një Doktor të Nderit nga Shkolla e Mjekësisë e Universitetit të Kretës, në njohjen e kontributeve të tij të shumëanshme kishtare, misionare, sociale dhe humanitare, si dhe me veprimtaritë e tij ndërkombëtare dhe me rolin e tij të rëndësishëm në nxitjen e dialogut dhe bashkëpunimit midis popujve dhe komuniteteve fetare.

Dhënia e këtij dallimi nderi përbën një nder të veçantë për Universitetin e Kretës, siç ka kaluar nderi i shquar, për pothuajse dyzet vjet, kryerja e një vepre misionare të rëndësishme dhe shumëfaqeshe nëpër kontinentin afrikan, njëzet e dy prej të cilave janë shpenzuar si Primate e Kishës së Aleksandrisë.
items.text_orig:
Pope and Patriarch Theodore II of Alexandria and All Africa will be conferred with an Honorary Doctorate by the School of Medicine of the University of Crete, in recognition of his multifaceted ecclesiastical, missionary, social, and humanitarian contributions, as well as his international activities and his significant role in promoting dialogue and cooperation among peoples and religious communities.

The award ceremony will take place on Tuesday, 24 November 2026, at 12:00 noon, at the Nikos Petridis Auditorium of the Department of Mathematics and Applied Mathematics, at the University’s Voutes Campus in Heraklion, Crete.

The conferment of this honorary distinction constitutes a particular honour for the University of Crete, as the distinguished honouree has, for almost forty years, carried out significant and multifaceted missionary work across the African continent, twenty-two of which have been spent serving as the Primate of the Church of Alexandria.

The ceremony holds special significance given the Patriarch’s Cretan origins: he was born in Crete, where he also completed his primary and secondary education. His profound spiritual and emotional ties to his birthplace remain an integral part of his personal journey.

items.sum: Patriarku Xhon X mori pjesëmarrësit e Konferencës së Përgjithshme të Lëvizjes Orthodhokse të Rinisë në Manastirin Patriarkal të Zonjës sonë të Balamandit. Pas shërbimit Vespers, Fortlumturia e Tij iu drejtua pjesëmarrësve, duke u bërë thirrje atyre të lejojnë krishterimin të jetë gjendja e tyre e gjallë e të qënit mes presioneve të jetës.
items.text_orig: Patriarch John X received the participants of the General Conference of the Orthodox Youth Movement at the Patriarchal Monastery of Our Lady of Balamand. Following the Vespers service, Fortlumturia e Tij addressed the participants, calling on them to let Christianity be their live state of being amidst the pressures of life. He emphasized the centrality of prayer and spiritual vigilance on the journey toward self-knowledge, purification, illumination, and ultimately, sanctification. On organizational matters, Fortlumturia e Tij warned against stagnating within rigid “institutional” molds, urging them: “O members of the Movement, be true to the Movement, drawing inspiration from the flame of the early pioneers who came before you.” He concluded by affirming the unity of the ecclesial body, calling on them to reject individualism and hold fast to solidarity, attentive listening, and mutual trust.

items.title_orig: †) St. John Chrysostom, archbishop of Constantinople, and his mother, St. Anthusa
items.sum:
▪ Shën Xhon Krisotomi, kryepeshkopi i Kostandinopojës dhe nëna e tij, S.

Shën Xhon Krisostomi, kryepeshkopi i Kostandinopojës, një nga tre Hirarkët [janar 30 janar], lindi në Antioki rreth vitit 347 në familjen e një komandanti ushtarak.

Shën Meleci, peshkopi i Antiokisë (shkurt 12 shkurt), e donte Gjonin si një djalë, e udhëhoqi në besim dhe në vitin 367 e pagëzuan.

Në vitin 386 Shën Xhoni u caktua prebiter nga peshkopi Flavian i Antiokisë.

Në Paskën, vitin që pasoi, shenjtori filloi homiet e tij mbi Ungjillin e Gjonit dhe nga fundi i vitit 389 mori Ungjillin e Mateut.

Fama e predikuesit të shenjtë u rrit dhe në vitin 397 me vdekjen e kryepeshkopit Nektarius të Kostandinopojës, pasues i Shën Gregorit, teologut Shën Xhon Krisostomit, u thirr nga Antiokia dhe u zgjodh për të parë Kostandinopojën.

Eudoksia u ndez nga urrejtja për shenjtorin kur meshkujt i thanë se shenjtori me sa duket e kishte në mendje gjatë predikimit të tij mbi gratë e kota.

Ky gjyq gjykimi deklaroi se Shën Gjoni hoqi dorë dhe se u ekzekutua për fyerjen që i bëri Impressit.

Për të shmangur një trazirë, Shën Gjoni iu nënshtrua autoriteteve.

Në mars të 404 - s, u mblodh një këshill i padrejtë që dekretoi mërgimin e Shën Gjonit.

Në dimrin e 406 - s, Shën Gjonit, ai ishte i kufizuar në shtratin e tij me sëmundje, por armiqtë e tij nuk duheshin qetësuar.

Në kript të Shën Baziliskut (22 maj), Shën Xhoni u ngushëllua nga një vizion i martirit, i cili tha, "jo " vëlla Xhon!

Reliktet e shenjta të Shën Xhon Krisotomit u transferuan solemnisht në Kostandinopojë në vitin 438.

Edhe pse vdiq më 14 shtator, festimi i Shën Gjonit u transferua edhe sot e kësaj dite për shkak të festës së Elevimit të Kryqit të Shenjtë. Shën Xhon Krisotom festohet gjithashtu më 27 janar dhe 30 janar.
items.text_orig:
†) St. John Chrysostom, archbishop of Constantinople, and his mother, St. Anthusa

Saint John Chrysostom, Archbishop of Constantinople, one of the Three Hierarchs [January 30], was born at Antioch in about the year 347 into the family of a military commander. His father, Secundus, died soon after the birth of his son. His mother, Anthusa, widowed at twenty years of age, did not seek to remarry but rather devoted all her efforts to the raising of her son in Christian piety.

The youth studied under the finest philosophers and rhetoricians. But, scorning the vain disciplines of pagan knowledge, the future hierarch turned himself to the profound study of Holy Scripture and prayerful contemplation. Saint Meletius, Bishop of Antioch (February 12), loved John like a son, guided him in the Faith, and in the year 367 baptized him.

After three years John was tonsured as a Reader. When Saint Meletius had been sent into exile by the emperor Valens in the year 372, John and Theodore (afterwards Bishop of Mopsuestia) studied under the experienced instructors of ascetic life, the presbyters Flavian and Diodorus of Tarsus. The highly refined Diodorus had particular influence upon the youth. When John’s mother died, he embraced monasticism, which he called the “true philosophy.” Soon John and his friend Basil were being considered as candidates for the episcopal office, and they decided to withdraw into the wilderness to avoid this. While Saint John avoided the episcopal rank out of humility, he secretly assisted in Basil’s consecration.

During this period Saint John wrote his “Six Discourses on the Priesthood,” a great work of Orthodox pastoral theology. The saint spent four years struggling in the wilderness, living the ascetic life under the guidance of an experienced spiritual guide.

And here he wrote three books entitled, “Against the Opponents of Those Attracted to the Monastic Life”, and a collection entitled, “A Comparison of the Monk with the Emperor” (also known as “Comparison of Imperial Power, Wealth and Eminence, with the True and Christian Wisdom-Loving Monastic Life”), both works which are marked by a profound reflection of the worthiness of the monastic vocation.

For two years, the saint lived in a cave in complete silence, but was obliged to return to Antioch to recover his health. Saint Meletius, the Bishop of Antioch, ordained him deacon in the year 381. The following years were devoted to work on new theological writings: “Concerning Providence” (“To the Ascetic Stagirios”), “Book Concerning Virginity,” “To a Young Widow” (2 discourses), and the “Book of Saint Babylos, and Against Julian and the Pagans.”

In the year 386 Saint John was ordained presbyter by Bishop Flavian of Antioch. Saint John was a splendid preacher, and his inspired words earned him the name “Golden-Mouthed” (“Chrysostom”). For twelve years the saint preached in church, usually twice a week, but sometimes daily, deeply stirring the hearts of his listeners.

In his pastoral zeal to provide Christians with a better understanding of Holy Scripture, Saint John employed hermeneutics, an interpretation and analysis of the Word of God (i.e. exegesis).

Among his exegetical works are commentaries on entire books of the Holy Scripture (Genesis, the Psalter, the Gospels of Matthew and John, the Epistles of the Apostle Paul), and also many homilies on individual texts of the Holy Bible, but also instructions on the Feastdays, laudations on the Saints, and also apologetic (i.e. defensive) homilies (against Anomoeans, Judaizers and pagans).

As a priest, Saint John zealously fulfilled the Lord’s command to care for the needy. Under Saint John, the Antiochian Church provided sustenance each day to as many as 3,000 virgins and widows, not including in this number the shut-ins, wanderers and the sick.

Saint John began his commentary on Genesis at the beginning of Great Lent in 388, preaching thirty-two homilies during the forty day period. During Holy Week he spoke of how Christ was betrayed, and about the Cross. During Bright Week, his pastoral discourse was devoted to the Resurrection. His exegesis of the Book of Genesis was concluded only at the end of October (388).

At Pascha in the following year the saint began his homilies on the Gospel of John, and toward the end of the year 389 he took up the Gospel of Matthew. In the year 391 the Antioch Christians listened to his commentary on the Epistles of the holy Apostle Paul to the Romans and to the Corinthians.

In 393 he explained the Epistles to the Galatians, the Ephesians, Timothy, Titus, and the Psalms. In his homily on the Epistle to the Ephesians, Saint John denounced a schism in Antioch, “I tell you and I witness before you, that to tear asunder the Church means nothing less than to fall into heresy. The Church is the house of the heavenly Father, one Body and one Spirit.”

The fame of the holy preacher grew, and in the year 397 with the death of Archbishop Nectarius of Constantinople, successor to Saint Gregory the Theologian, Saint John Chrysostom was summoned from Antioch, and elected to the See of Constantinople. At the capital, the holy archpastor was not able to preach as often as he had at Antioch.

Many matters awaited the saint’s attention, and he began with the most important — the spiritual perfection of the priesthood. He himself was the best example of this. The financial means apportioned for the archbishop were channeled by the saint into the upkeep of several hospices for the sick and two hostels for pilgrims. He fasted strictly and ate very little food, and usually refused invitations to dine because of his delicate stomach.

The saint’s zeal in spreading the Christian Faith extended not only to the inhabitants of Constantinople, but also to Thrace to include Slavs and Goths, and to Asia Minor and the Pontine region. He established a bishop for the Bosphorus Church in the Crimea. Saint John sent off zealous missionaries to Phoenicia, to Persia, and to the Scythians, to convert pagans to Christ.

He also wrote letters to Syria to bring back the Marcionites into the Church, and he accomplished this. Preserving the unity of the Church, the saint would not permit a powerful Gothic military commander, who wanted the emperor to reward his bravery in battle, to open an Arian church at Constantinople. The saint exerted much effort in enhancing the splendor of the church services: he compiled a Liturgy, he introduced antiphonal singing for the all-night Vigil, and he wrote several prayers for the rite of anointing the sick with oil.

The saintly hierarch denounced the dissolute morals of people in the capital, especially at the imperial court, irrespective of person. When the empress Eudoxia connived to confiscate the last properties of the widow and children of a disgraced dignitary, the saint rose to their defense.

The arrogant empress would not relent, and nursed a grudge against the archpastor. Eudoxia’s hatred of the saint blazed forth anew when malefactors told her that the saint apparently had her in mind during his sermon on vain women. A court was convened composed of hierarchs who had been justly condemned by Chrysostom: Theophilus of Alexandria, Bishop Severian of Gabala, who had been banished from the capital because of improprieties, and others.

This court of judgment declared Saint John deposed, and that he be executed for his insult to the empress. The emperor decided on exile instead of execution. An angry crowd gathered at the church, resolved to defend their pastor.

In order to avoid a riot, Saint John submitted to the authorities. That very night there was an earthquake at Constantinople. The terrified Eudoxia urgently requested the emperor to bring the saint back, and promptly sent a letter to the banished pastor, beseeching him to return. Once more, in the capital church, the saint praised the Lord in a short talk, “For All His Ways.”

The slanderers fled to Alexandria. But after only two months a new denunciation provoked the wrath of Eudoxia. In March 404, an unjust council was convened, decreeing the exile of Saint John. Upon his removal from the capital, a fire reduced the church of Hagia Sophia and also the Senate building to ashes. Devastating barbarian incursions soon followed, and Eudoxia died in October 404. Even pagans regarded these events as God’s punishment for the unjust judgment against the saint.

In Armenia, the saint strove all the more to encourage his spiritual children. In numerous letters (245 are preserved) to bishops in Asia, Africa, Europe and particularly to his friends in Constantinople, Saint John consoled the suffering, guiding and giving support to his followers. In the winter of 406 Saint John was confined to his bed with sickness, but his enemies were not to be appeased.

From the capital came orders to transfer Saint John to desolate Pityus in Abkhazia on the Black Sea. Worn out by sickness, the saint began his final journey under military escort, traveling for three months in the rain and frost. He never arrived at his place of exile, for his strength failed him at Comana.

At the crypt of Saint Basiliscus (May 22), Saint John was comforted by a vision of the martyr, who said, “Despair not, brother John! Tomorrow we shall be together.” After receiving the Holy Mysteries, the hierarch fell asleep in the Lord on September 14, 407. His last words were, “Glory to God for all things!”

The holy relics of Saint John Chrysostom were solemnly transferred to Constantinople in the year 438. The disciple of Saint John, the venerable Isidore of Pelusium (February 4), wrote: “The house of David is grown strong, and the house of Saul enfeebled. He is victor over the storms of life, and has entered into heavenly repose.”

Although he died on September 14, Saint John’s celebration was transferred to this day because of the Feast of the Elevation of the Holy Cross. Saint John Chrysostom is also celebrated on January 27 and January 30.

Troparion — Tone 8

Grace shining forth from your lips like a beacon has enlightened the universe. / It has shown to the world the riches of poverty; / it has revealed to us the heights of humility. / Teaching us by your words, O Father John Chrysostom, / intercede before the Word, Christ our God, to save our souls!

Tr by oca.org

items.text_orig: Fortlumturia e Tij John X Patriarch of Antioch and All the East received a delegation from the Association of Theological Institutes in the Middle East (ATIME), comprising members of the Executive Committee and a group of students representing 19 theological institutes and faculties from Lebanon, Syria, and Egypt. During the meeting, Fortlumturia e Tij emphasized the importance of Christians being witnesses of peace and love in the Levant, calling upon the students to translate theology into a lived experience and a living witness to Christ in their churches and communities. He also wished them a pleasant stay in Lebanon, the land of message, encounter, and living witness to coexistence.

Patriarkati i Serbisë ka lëshuar një deklaratë duke u bërë thirrje besimtarëve të ofrojnë lutje të zjarrta për rimëkëmbjen e Metropolitanit Irinej të Baçkës.

items.text_orig:
The Patriarchate of Serbia has issued a statement calling on the faithful to offer fervent prayers for the recovery of Metropolitan Irinej of Bačka.

Specifically, it urges them to offer heartfelt prayers to the Lord and the Most Holy Theotokos this evening, asking for his swift recovery.

“We invite you to offer fervent prayers to the Lord and the Mother of God this evening for the recovery of Metropolitan Irinej of Bačka,” the statement reads.

items.sum:
Më 11 nëntor 2026, Patriarku Shio i Gjeorgjisë mori në Partinë Patriarkale Ambasadorin e Pazakonshëm dhe Plenipotentiar të Rumanisë në Gjeorgji, Razvan Rotu.

Gjatë takimit, diskutimet u përqëndruan në lidhjet e vjetra historike, shpirtërore e kulturore midis popujve gjeorgjianë dhe rumunë.

Gjatë takimit, u përmend gjithashtu një zhvillim tjetër i rëndësishëm: pas një vendimi nga Sinodi i Shenjtë i Kishës Orthodhokse Rumune, përkujtimi i Gabriel Rrëfyesit dhe budallait për Krishtin (Urregebadze) është përfshirë në kalendarin e Kishës Rumune.
items.text_orig:
On November 11, 2026, Patriarch Shio of Georgia received at the Patriarchal Residence the Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Romania to Georgia, Razvan Rotundu.

The introductory meeting was also attended by the Head of the Patriarchate’s Public Relations Department, Archpriest Andria Jagmaidze.

During the meeting, discussions focused on the centuries-old historical, spiritual and cultural ties between the Georgian and Romanian peoples. The meeting also highlighted the multifaceted work and contribution of Saint Anthimos the Iberian, as well as his enduring historical legacy.

According to information provided by the Romanian Ambassador, Radu Vodă Monastery, located near Bucharest, is planning to establish a new monastic foundation, with Equal-to-the-Apostles Saint Nino, the Enlightener of Georgia, chosen as its patron saint.

During the meeting, another significant development was also mentioned: following a decision by the Holy Synod of the Romanian Orthodox Church, the commemoration of Venerable Gabriel the Confessor and Fool for Christ (Urgebadze) has been included in the Romanian Church calendar. This feast will be officially celebrated in Romania for the first time this year.

At the conclusion of the meeting, the hosts thanked the Ambassador for his visit, after which the two sides exchanged commemorative gifts.

Photos: Nino Sozashvili

items.title: +) Martyrs and Confessors of Nasaud: Athanasius, Basil, Gregory and Basil; St. John the Merciful, patriarch of Alexandria; St. Nilus the Faster of Sinai
items.summary: Orthodox Calendar, November 12 Martyrs and Confessors of Nasaud: The Holy Martyr Athanasius Todoran He was born in Bichigiu village, Sălăuţa valley, Năsăud region of Transylvania, to a family of Orthodox Christians. Few things are known about his childhood; it is only known that…
items.text:
Martyrs and Confessors of Nasaud:

The Holy Martyr Athanasius Todoran

He was born in Bichigiu village, Sălăuţa valley, Năsăud region of Transylvania, to a family of Orthodox Christians. Few things are known about his childhood; it is only known that he was an outstanding person in his community, an educated person, who has been administrator and tax collector in the communes on Bichigiu and Sălăuţa valleys.

Given his virtues and courage he was a member of a military regiment of the empire from Vienna ever since his youth. Hence, as his retirement was postponed, he left the army of his masters, who had a different faith, and went back home. Followed by the people of the empire, he took refuge in Ţibleş Mountains, in Maramureş and Chioaru land. While in this exile, he always prayed God for him and for his fellow human beings who were suffering and in all kind of humiliations.

His pains grew when the ones of other faiths caught and imprisoned him for a few years in the Hoopers’ Tower, in Bistriţa citadel. Once released from prison, he went back to Bichigiu village, where the Orthodox faith of his forerunners was threatened by uniatism. Thus, because the village had no Orthodox priest, he firmly refused to confess to and take Holy Communion from a uniate priest.

He has always manifested his faith in God and desire for justice and truth. Therefore, from 1761-1762 he held talks with the government in Vienna, together with some other leaders, for the militarisation of 21 communes in Bichigiu, Sălăuţa and Great Someş valleys. He went to Vienna together with other Romanians where the pact with the government was concluded and where they were assured that, after joining the frontier guard, the Romanians from Năsăud area would enjoy more facilities and would not be forced to give up their faith.

When he came back home expecting to enjoy the results of the agreement, blessed Athanasius realised that the Romanians’ demands were not taken into account, so that he started openly opposing the attempts of conversion to the papal church.

On 10 May 1763, the fight flags were to be blessed and nine companies of the recently set up frontier guard were to be sworn in Salva locality, at the place called “At the Marsh”.

General Bukov sent by the Court of Vienna to survey and accelerate the conversion of the Romanians to Catholicism in Transylvania, came to attend the swearing in of the frontier guards of Năsăud and the blessing of the flag, accompanied by the uniate bishop. At that time of hard trials for the Orthodox Christians, when the militaries were prepared to swear in, “old Tănase Todoran”, aged 104 at the time, came in front of the crowd riding a horse and delivered a speech for the Romanian frontier guards. He said: “ We have been frontier guards for two years and we have not received papers from the empress to confirm we were free people, as we were promised!… So, we shall not bear arms to see our holy faith mocked! Let down your arms! ”.

The passionate words of the pious old man bore fruits in the hearts of his listeners and so the soldiers who were about to swear in the oath of faith to Vienna took Athanasius’ side and put down their arms.

Soon afterwards, the authorities undertook investigations in order to punish the Saints confessors. Thus, on 12 November 1763, the supporters of the centuries old faith and of the freedoms of the Romanian people were tortured on the same plateau of Salva.

The bones of the righteous martyr Athanasius were broken with a wheel from head to toes and his head was tied to a wheel, “ because he hindered the people to convert to uniatism and join the frontier guard …”. Three other faithful died a martyr’s death together with him: Basil from Mocod, Gregory from Zagra and Basil from Telciu.

Nineteen other Orthodox Christians were whipped, many of them to death. The heads of the martyr saints were put on pillars at the gates of the houses were they had lived and pieces of their bodies cut to pieces were laid at crossroads.

This was the martyr’s death of the worth of remembering Holy Martyr Athanasius, who shed his blood for the faith of the forefathers and for the rights of his Romanian brothers from Transylvania. His suffering and those of those who died together with him have been always honoured in the souls of the Orthodox faithful of Năsăud area.

The Holy Synod of the Romanian Orthodox Church, through the Tomos of 22 October 2007, placed them among the saints, celebrated on 12 November.

Through their holy prayers, Lord Jesus Christ, our God, have mercy on us. Amen.

Troparion, Tone 4:

Your life well-pleasing to God has shone like a brilliant star in the land of Năsăud, oh, Holy Martyrs Athanasius of Bichigiu, Basil of Mocod, Gregory of Zagra and Basil of Telciu; for being strengthened by the divine grace you became protectors and confessors of Orthodoxy against rulers of other origin and faith. Therefore, suffering to the very shedding of your blood, you have been crowned in Heaven by Christ our God, to Whom do pray for our souls.

Saint John the Merciful, Patriarch of Alexandria

He was born on Cyprus in the seventh century into the family of the illustrious dignitary Epiphanius. At the wish of his parents he entered into marriage and had children. When the wife and the children of the saint died, he became a monk. He was zealous in fasting and prayer, and had great love for those around him.

His spiritual exploits won him honor among men, and even the emperor revered him. When the Patriarchal throne of Alexandria fell vacant, the emperor Heraclius and all the clergy begged Saint John to occupy the Patriarchal throne.

The saint worthily assumed his archpastoral service, concerning himself with the moral and dogmatic welfare of his flock. As patriarch he denounced every soul-destroying heresy, and drove out from Alexandria the Monophysite Phyllonos of Antioch.

He considered his chief task to be charitable and to give help all those in need. At the beginning of his patriarchal service he ordered his stewards to compile a list of all the poor and downtrodden in Alexandria, which turned out to be over seven thousand men. The saint ordered that all of these unfortunates be provided for each day out of the church’s treasury.

Twice during the week, on Wednesdays and Fridays, he emerged from the doors of the patriarchal cathedral, and sitting on the church portico, he received everyone in need. He settled quarrels, helped the wronged, and distributed alms.

Three times a week he visited the sick-houses, and rendered assistance to the suffering. It was during this period that the emperor Heraclius led a tremendous army against the Persian emperor Chosroes II. The Persians ravaged and burned Jerusalem, taking a multitude of captives. The holy Patriarch John gave a large portion of the church treasury for their ransom.

The saint never refused suppliants. One day, when the saint was visiting the sick, he met a beggar and commanded that he be given six silver coins.

The beggar changed his clothes, ran on ahead of the Patriarch, and again asked for alms. Saint John gave him six more silver coins. When, however, the beggar sought charity a third time, and the servants began to chase the fellow away, the Patriarch ordered that he be given twelve pieces of silver, saying, “Perhaps he is Christ putting me to the test.”

Twice the saint gave money to a merchant that had suffered shipwreck, and a third time gave him a ship belonging to the Patriarchate and filled with grain, with which the merchant had a successful journey and repaid his obligations.

Saint John the Merciful was known for his gentle attitude towards people. Once, the saint was compelled to excommunicate two clergymen for a certain time because of some offense. One of them repented, but the other fellow became angry with the Patriarch and fell into greater sins. The saint wanted to summon him and calm him with kind words, but it slipped his mind.

When he was celebrating the Divine Liturgy, the saint was suddenly reminded by the words of the Gospel: “If you bring your gift to the altar and remember that your brother has something against you, leave your gift before the altar … first, be reconciled with your brother, and then come and offer your gift” (Mt. 5:23-24).

The saint came out of the altar, called the offending clergyman to him, and falling down on his knees before him in front of all the people he asked forgiveness. The cleric, filled with remorse, repented of his sin, corrected himself, and afterwards was found worthy to be ordained to the priesthood.

There was a time when a certain citizen insulted George, the Patriarch’s nephew. George asked the saint to avenge the wrong. The saint promised to deal with the offender so that all of Alexandria would marvel at what he had done. This calmed George, and Saint John began to instruct him, speaking of the necessity for meekness and humility.

Then he summoned the man who insulted George. When Saint John learned that the man lived in a house owned by the church, he declared that he would excuse him from paying rent for an entire year. Alexandria indeed was amazed by such a “revenge,” and George learned from his uncle how to forgive offenses and to bear insults for God’s sake.

Saint John, a strict ascetic and man of prayer, was always mindful of his soul, and of death. He ordered a coffin for himself, but told the craftsmen not to finish it. Instead, he would have them come each feastday and ask if it was time to finish the work.

Saint John was persuaded to accompany the governor Nicetas on a visit to the emperor in Constantinople. While on his way to visit the earthly king, he dreamed of a resplendent man who said to him, “The King of Kings summons you.” He sailed to his native island of Cyprus, and died at Amanthos, the saint peacefully fell asleep in the Lord (616-620).

Troparion — Tone 8

By endurance you gained your reward, venerable Father; / you persevered in prayer unceasingly; / you loved the poor and provided for them in all things. / Blessed John the Merciful, intercede with Christ God that our souls may be saved.

Saint Nilus the Faster of Sinai

A native of Constantinople. He lived during the fifth century and was a disciple of Saint John Chrysostom. Having received a fine education, the saint was appointed to the important post of prefect of the capital while still a young man.

During this period, Nilus was married and had children, but the pomp of courtly life bothered the couple. Saint John Chrysostom exerted a tremendous influence upon their lives and their strivings. The spouses decided to separate and devote themselves to the monastic life.

The wife and daughter of Nilus went to one of the women’s monasteries in Egypt, and Saint Nilus and his son Theodulus went to Sinai, where they settled in a cave dug out by their own hands. For forty years this cave served as the dwelling of Saint Nilus.

By fasting, prayer and works, the monk attained a high degree of spiritual perfection. People began to come to him from every occupation and social rank from the emperor down to the farmer, and each found counsel and comfort from the saint.

At Sinai, Saint Nilus wrote many soul-profiting works to guide Christians on the path of salvation. In one of his letters there is an angry denunciation of the emperor Arcadius, who had exiled Saint John Chrysostom.

The ascetic works of the venerable Nilus are widely known: they are perfectly executed in form, profoundly Orthodox in content, and are clear and lucid in expression. His Ascetic Discourse is found in Volume I of the English PHILOKALIA.

Saint Nilus suffered many misfortunes in the wilderness. Once, Saracens captured his son Theodulus, whom they intended to offer as a sacrifice to their pagan gods. Through the prayers of the saint the Lord saved Theodulus, and his father found him with the Bishop of Emessa, who had ransomed the young man from the barbarians.

items.title: Vizitë baritore e Mitropolitit Asti në enoritë e Vlorës
items.summary: VIZITË BARITORE E MITROPOLITIT TË BERATIT, VLORËS DHE KANINËS, HIRËSI ASTI, NË ZËVENDËSINË ARKIHIERATIKE TË VLORËS.
items.text:
VIZITË BARITORE E MITROPOLITIT TË BERATIT, VLORËS DHE KANINËS, HIRËSI ASTI, NË ZËVENDËSINË ARKIHIERATIKE TË VLORËS.

Në datat 9 dhe 10 nëntor 2026, Mitropoliti i Beratit, Vlorës dhe Kaninës, hirësi Asti, i shoqëruar nga Epitropi arkihieratik i Zëvendësisë Vlorë, ikonom atë Kostandin Prifti, vizituan enoritë e Zëvendësisë.

Konkretisht ata vizituan Enorinë e kishës “Burimi Jetëdhënës” Zvërnec, Enorinë e kishës “Shën e Diela” Nartë, Enorinë e kishës “Shën Theodhorët” Vlorë, kishën “Pesë Martirët” në enorinë e Bestrovës, kishën “Shën Nikolla” në enorinë e Poros dhe Dëllënjës, kishën “Ngjallja” të enorisë së Novoselës, Mifolit dhe Skrofotinës, kishat shën Dhimitri dhe shën Sotiri në enorinë e Mekatit dhe Beshishtit dhe kishën “Shën Athanasi” në Enorinë e Selenicës dhe Armenit, ku u pritën nga klerikët që shërbejnë në këto enori.

Në këto takime morën pjesë edhe anëtarët e këshillave kishtare të cilët ndihmojnë në mbarëvajtjen e punëve në kishë, ku të gjithë diskutuan për ecurinë dhe zhvillimin shpirtëror e social, bashkë me angazhimet, detyrat, punimet e kryera dhe porositë në takimet e zhvilluara në muajin shkurt të po këtij viti, në kishat e Zëvendësisë.

Një vizitë e veçantë u krye edhe në kopshtin e fëmijëve, Frymë dashurie të qytetit të Vlorës ku Mitropoliti u prit nga stafi pedagogjik dhe nga fëmijët, frekuentues të këtij kopshti. Ishin momente vërtet emocionuese kur dëgjoje fëmijët të luanin e të këndonin këngë të ndryshme në prani të Mitropolitit, i cili përgëzoi stafin për përkushtimin dhe kujdesin e treguar në edukimin e tyre dhe u uroi atyre shëndet e suksese në këtë mision të vështirë. Pasi u përshëndet me fëmijët Mitropoliti u premtoi se do të jetë përherë vizitor i kopshtit të tyre.

Atë Spiro Bulika.

items.title_orig: Archbishop of America honors Veterans and their sacrifices
items.sum:
Kryepeshkopi Elpidofos i Amerikës i bëri nderime veteranëve amerikanë në Ditën e Veteranëve, 11 nëntor 2026, duke theksuar rëndësinë e mbrojtjes së parimeve kushtetuese dhe mbrojtjes së lirive të të gjithë qytetarëve.

Në Ditën e Veteranëve, ne nderojmë me të vërtetë ata që kanë shërbyer për të mbrojtur kushtetutën tonë, ndërsa vazhdojmë të mbështetim parimet e saj dhe të ruajmë liritë e bashkëqytetarëve tanë, deklaroi ai.
items.text_orig:
Archbishop Elpidophoros of America paid tribute to American veterans on Veterans Day, November 11, 2026, emphasizing the importance of defending constitutional principles and protecting the freedoms of all citizens.

In a message shared on social media, the Archbishop expressed his gratitude to those who have served in the United States Armed Forces, highlighting the values they have defended.

“On Veterans Day, we truly honor those who have served to defend our Constitution as we continue to uphold its principles and safeguard the liberties of our fellow citizens,” he stated.

Archbishop Elpidophoros also recalled the words of President John F. Kennedy, a Navy veteran of World War II, during his inaugural address in 1961.

“The rights of man come not from the generosity of the state, but from the hand of God,” he quoted, underscoring the connection between human dignity, freedom, and faith.

Concluding his message, the Archbishop offered prayers for veterans and their families, acknowledging the sacrifices made by both those who served and their loved ones.

“With grateful hearts, we lift up our veterans in prayer, together with the families who shared in their sacrifices,” he said.

items.title_orig: Metropolitan of Sliven visits victims of tragic road accident in hospital
items.sum:
Metropolitan Arseni i Sliven dhe Kryetari i Bashkisë Stefan Radev vizituan spitalin Dr. Ivan Seliminski në Sliven, Bullgari, më 11 nëntor 2026, për të ofruar mbështetje për të plagosurit në një aksident serioz rrugor një ditë më parë.

Metropolitani dhe kryetari i bashkisë u mirëpritën nga drejtori i spitalit dr.

Metropolitan Arseni ofroi lutje për rimëkëmbjen e shpejtë të viktimave dhe shprehu solidaritetin e tij me familjet e tyre.

Metropolisi i Slivenit i hapi ngushëllimet e tij familjeve të atyre që humbën jetën në aksident dhe që bënë lutje për prehjen e shpirtit të tyre, shërimin e të plagosurve dhe ngushëllimin për të gjithë ata që u prekën nga tragjedia.
items.text_orig:
Metropolitan Arseniy of Sliven and Mayor Stefan Radev visited Dr. Ivan Seliminski Hospital in Sliven, Bulgaria, on November 11, 2026, to offer support to those injured in a serious road accident the previous day.

The Metropolitan and the Mayor were welcomed by hospital director Dr. Vesislav Petrov, who briefed them on the condition of the injured and the medical efforts underway to ensure their recovery.

Metropolitan Arseniy offered prayers for the swift recovery of the victims and expressed his solidarity with their families.

“When human life is put to the test, no one should be left alone in their suffering,” he stated, emphasizing the importance of compassion and solidarity during difficult times.

The Metropolitan also called for greater responsibility and caution on the roads, stressing that human life is an invaluable gift from God.

“No moment of haste, no act of carelessness or recklessness on the road is worth a human life,” he said.

He expressed his gratitude to the hospital’s doctors, nurses, and medical staff for their dedication and care.

The Metropolis of Sliven extended its condolences to the families of those who lost their lives in the accident and offered prayers for the repose of their souls, the healing of the injured, and comfort for all those affected by the tragedy.

items.title: Arnaia: Shërbimi kishtar i Kryepiskopit Anastas në Sinaksinë Priftërore, me folës Mihail Tritos
items.summary: Mihail Tritos paraqiti në Arnaia personalitetin dhe shërbimin e të lumurit Kryepiskopit Anastas, me referencë të veçantë në Kishën e Shqipërisë dhe në etosin e tij ngjallësor.
items.text:
Në Kishën e Shenjtë historike Mitropolitane të Shën Stefanit në Arnaia u zhvillua të martën, më 10 nëntor 2026, Sinaksia e dytë Priftërore e Mitropolisë së Shenjtë të Ierisosit, Malit të Shenjtë dhe Ardamerit për vitin aktual kishtar. Të gjithë klerikët iu përgjigjën ftesës së Mitropolitit, Imzot Theoklitit, duke marrë pjesë në bashkësinë e Shpirtit të Shenjtë, brenda frymës së unitetit, të vëllazërisë dhe të dashurisë që përbën jetën e Kishës.

Pas lutjes, Hirësia e Tij informoi klerikët për çështje aktuale administrative dhe prezantoi folësin e ftuar, z. Mihail Tritos, Profesor Emerit dhe ish-Dekan i Fakultetit Theologjik të Universitetit të Aristotelit në Selanik, si edhe mbajtës i titullit të nderit «Archon Hieromnemon» të Patriarkanës Ekumenike. Miqësia e ngushtë që i lidh daton që nga viti 1973, kur të dy studionin shkencën e shenjtë të Theologjisë në Fakultetin Theologjik të Universitetit të Athinës.

Kumtesa e Profesorit kishte si temë: «Kryepiskopi Anastas si model i shërbimit kishtar».

Pasi kishte qenë student dhe bashkëpunëtor i ngushtë i të lumurit Kryepiskopit Anastas, z. Tritos paraqiti personalitetin e Kryehierarkut të paharruar përmes kësaj marrëdhënieje të drejtpërdrejtë.

Ai u ndal në kontributin e tij misionar në Afrikë dhe në veprën e tij mësimdhënëse në Universitetin e Athinës si profesor i Historisë së Feve. Vend qendror në fjalim zuri shërbimi i tij në Kishën e Shqipërisë, të cilën fjalë për fjalë e ngjalli nga gërmadhat, duke i dhënë lavdinë e Kishës së krishterimit të hershëm.

Përmendje e veçantë iu bë etosit ngjallësor të të lumurit Kryepiskopit. Duke marrë tekste të përzgjedhura nga veprat e tij, referuesi nxori në pah përmasën ngjallësore të mësimdhënies së tij si tejkalim dhe çmitizim i vdekjes.

Me përfundimin e fjalimit, Profesori iu përgjigj pyetjeve të priftërinjve.

items.title_orig: Patriarch of Bulgaria: “Human life is a precious gift from God”
items.sum:
Pas dy aksidenteve tragjike rrugore që ndodhën në Bullgari, Sinoda e Shenjtë e Patriarkatit të Bullgarisë lëshoi një deklaratë duke shprehur pikëllimin e saj të thellë rreth humbjes së jetës njerëzore, duke shprehur fjalë simpatie dhe mbështetje për familjet e viktimave dhe duke bërë thirrje për lutje për pushimin e të ndjerit dhe rimëkëmbjen e të plagosurve.

Ishte me pikëllim të thellë dhe pikëllim të madh që morëm lajmin e dy aksidenteve të rënda rrugore që ndodhën në orët e para të 10 nëntorit në Autostradën Trakia, duke sjellë si pasojë humbjen tragjike të jetës së çmuar njerëzore dhe duke zhytur në zi e trishtim dhjetra familje.

Ne i lutemi Zotit që t'u japë prehje shpirtrave të atyre që kanë vdekur në një vend drite, në një vend të gjelbër, në një vend freskimi, në të cilin dhimbja, dhembja dhe rënkimi janë larguar, ku jeta është e përjetshme dhe për t'i marrë në banesën e Tij qiellore.

Sinodin e Shenjtë i bën thirrje klerit të devotshëm, manastireve dhe të gjithë fëmijëve besnikë të Kishës Orthodhokse Bullgare, si dhe të gjithë bashkëpatriotëve tanë, t'i bëjnë lutje të zjarrta e të pareshtura Perëndisë për pushimin e shpirtit të të ndjerit, për shëndetin dhe shërimin e shpejtë të të plagosurve dhe për ngushëllimin e familjeve dhe të njerëzve të tyre të dashur.
items.text_orig:
Following the two tragic road accidents that occurred in Bulgaria, the Holy Synod of the Patriarchate of Bulgaria issued a statement expressing its profound sorrow over the loss of human life, extending words of sympathy and support to the families of the victims, and calling for prayers for the repose of the departed and the recovery of those injured.

Read below the statement:

Beloved brothers and sisters in the Lord,

It was with profound sorrow and grief that we received the news of the two serious road accidents that occurred in the early hours of 10 November on the Trakia Motorway, resulting in the tragic loss of precious human lives and plunging dozens of families into mourning and sorrow.

In these difficult hours for us all, the Holy Synod of the Bulgarian Orthodox Church – Bulgarian Patriarchate extends its most heartfelt condolences to the families and loved ones of those who lost their lives. We wholeheartedly share in their immeasurable pain and offer fervent prayers to Almighty and All-Merciful God, asking Him to grant them consolation, spiritual strength, and steadfast faith, so that they may endure the grievous trial that has befallen them.

At moments such as this, human words prove inadequate to express the depth of sorrow caused by the loss of our loved ones. Yet, as Christians, we place our hope in our Lord Jesus Christ, Who assures us:

“I am the resurrection and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live” (John 11:25).

We beseech the Lord to grant repose to the souls of those who perished in a place of light, a place of verdure, a place of refreshment, where pain, sorrow and sighing have fled away, and where life is everlasting, and to receive them into His heavenly dwelling places.

The Holy Synod calls upon the devout clergy, monastics and all the faithful children of the Bulgarian Orthodox Church, as well as all our compatriots, to offer fervent and unceasing prayers to God for the repose of the souls of the departed, for the health and speedy recovery of those injured, and for the consolation of their families and loved ones.

With fatherly concern, we also address all those who use the roads: let us act with prudence, vigilance, patience, and responsibility! Let us remember that human life is a precious gift from God, which we are called upon to safeguard. Through every action we take on the road, let us demonstrate genuine care and love for our neighbour, fully aware of our responsibility not only for our own lives, but also for the lives of all those around us.

We believe that, with God’s help, through collective effort, a greater sense of responsibility and mutual care, we can prevent similar tragedies and safeguard the lives and health of our fellow human beings.

May God forgive and grant rest to the souls of those who have departed this life! May He grant health and strength to the injured, consolation and hope to those who mourn, and prudence, humility, and love for one another to us all!

10 November 2026

Sofia
