items.sum:
Menët e mëdhenj të shenjtë të Egjiptit

Kur perandorët filluan përndjekjen më të ashpër kundër të krishterëve në histori, shenjtori nuk pranoi t'u shërbente këtyre persekutuesve.

Shën Teodor Rrëfuesi, Aboti i Studios

Ndër etërit e Këshillit ishte Shën Platoni (prill), një xhaxha i Shën Teodorit dhe i cili për një kohë të gjatë kishte jetuar në malin Olimpos. Një plak i mbushur me hirin e Shpirtit të Shenjtë, Shën Platoni, në përfundim të Këshillit, thirri nipin e tij Teodorin dhe vëllezërit e tij, Jozefin dhe Euthimin, në jetën në shkretëtirë.

Jeta e Shën Teodorit ishte me të vërtetë asketike.

Saint Teodori e lexoi në mënyrë të pagabueshme Shkrimet e Shenjta dhe veprat e Etërve të shenjtë, sidomos veprat e Shën Bazilit të Madh, që ishin si ushqim për shpirtin e tij.

Pas disa vjetësh jete në manastir, Shën Teodori u caktua prift sipas vullnetit të Atit të tij frymor. Kur Shën Platoni shkoi në pushimin e tij, vëllezërit zgjodhën njëzëri Shën Teodorin si Igumen të manastirit.

Saint Teodor dhe dhjetë nga bashkë-sketikët e tij u dërguan në mërgim në qytetin e Selanikut. Kur u kthye në fron në vitin 796, Shën Irene liroi Shën Teodorin dhe e bëri atë iguamen të manastirit të Studios (i kushtuar Shën Gjonit Baptist) në Kostandinopojë, ku kishte vetëm dymbëdhjetë murgj.

Shën Teodori kompozoi një rregull të jetës në manastir, të quajtur Rregulla e Staditëve, për të qeverisur manastirin. Edhe Shën Teodori shkroi shumë letra kundër ikonakalasëve. Për veprat e tij dogmatike, si edhe për kanonët e tij dhe kanonët tre-Ode, Shën Theoktistusi e quajti Shën Teodori, mësues i zjarrtë i Kishës.

Saint Teodor përsëri denoncoi perandorin.

Shën Teodori u lirua nga perandori i butë dhe i devotshëm Mikael, i cili arriti në fron pas vdekjes së Nicefosit dhe të birit të tij, Staurikios, në një luftë kundër barbarëve. Vdekja e tyre ishte parashikuar nga Shën Teodori për një kohë të gjatë.

Pastaj perandori dënoi Shën Teodorin dhe dishepullin e tij Nikol
items.text_orig:
Holy Great Martyr Menas of Egypt

An Egyptian by birth, was a military officer and served in the Kotyaeion region of Phrygia under the centurion Firmilian during the reign of the emperors Diocletian (284-305) and Maximian (305-311). When the emperors began the fiercest persecution against Christians in history, the saint refused to serve these persecutors. He removed his soldier’s belt (a sign of military rank) and withdrew to a mountain, where he lived an ascetic life of fasting and prayer.

Once he happened to arrive in the city during a pagan festival. At the climax of the games the saint’s accusing voice rang out, preaching faith in Christ, the Savior of the world. At his trial before the prefect Pyrrhus, the saint bravely confessed his faith, saying that he had come to denounce the impious. The prefect was angered, and had Menas arrested.

Pyrrhus offered to restore the saint’s former rank if he would offer sacrifice to the pagan gods. When he refused, he was put to cruel tortures, then he was beheaded. This occurred in the year 304. Christians gathered up the martyr’s relics by night and hid them until the end of the persecution. Later, they were brought to Egypt and placed in a church dedicated to Saint Menas southwest of Alexandria.

The saint received grace from God to work miracles, and to help those in need. Saint Menas is noted for healing various illnesses, delivering people from possession by demons, and as a protector, especially during times of war. We also ask his help in finding lost objects.

Troparion — Tone 4

Your holy martyrs, O Lord, / through their sufferings have received incorruptible crowns from You, our God. / For having Your strength, they laid low their adversaries, / and shattered the powerless boldness of demons. / Through their intercessions, save our souls!

Holy Martyr Victor at Damascus

He was a soldier during the reign of the emperor Marcus Aurelius the Philosopher (161-180). When the emperor began a persecution against Christians, Victor refused to offer sacrifice to the pagan gods. Such obligatory sacrifices were a test of a soldier’s loyalty to the gods, the emperor and the state. The saint was given over to torture, but he came through all the torments unharmed. By the power of prayer he was victorious over a sorcerer, who from that point gave up give sorcery and became a Christian.

Through Saint Victor’s prayers, blind soldiers suddenly received their sight. Witnessing the miracle worked by the Lord through Saint Victor, Stephanida, the young Christian wife of one of the torturers, openly glorified Christ, for which she was condemned to a cruel death. She was tied to two palm trees bent to the ground, which when released, sprung back and tore her apart. She was fifteen years old.

The torturer ordered that the holy Martyr Victor be beheaded. Hearing the commander’s order, Saint Vincent told his executioners that they would all die in twelve days, and that the commander would be captured by the enemy in twenty-four days. As he foretold, so it came to pass.

The martyrs suffered in the second century at Damascus, where their venerable relics were buried.

Holy Martyr Vincent of Spain

From his childhood, he was the disciple of a wise pastor Valerian, the bishop of the city of Augustopolis (now Saragossa, Spain). When he reached mature age, the virtuous, educated and eloquent Vincent was ordained deacon by Bishop Valerian. Since the bishop himself was not adept in speech, he gave a blessing to his deacon, an eloquent orator, to preach in church and among the people.

Diocletian (284-305) sent the governor Dacian to the city of Valencia, Spain with full authority to find and execute Christians. People denounced the wise bishop and his deacon to the governor, who arrested them. The soldiers, mounted on horses, dragged the Elder and his disciple behind them in chains from Augustopolis to Valencia, and there they cast them into prison beaten and tortured, giving them neither food nor water.

They subjected the bishop to the first interrogation. The Elder spoke quietly, but seemed tongue-tied and uncertain. Then Saint Vincent came forward and made the most eloquent speech of his life before the judges and assembled people. After he sent the bishop back to prison, the persecutor gave orders to torture the holy deacon.

The martyr underwent many torments: while nailed to a cross, he was whipped and burned with red-hot rods. When he was removed from the cross, he then himself joyfully climbed back upon it, saying that the executioners were lazy and had not fulfilled their master’s orders. They became angry and tortured him again, until they were all exhausted.

After the tortures they threw the martyr back into prison. That night the astonished guard heard him singing Psalms, and saw an unearthly radiant light in the prison. The next morning the holy martyr was condemned to be burned on a gridiron. Christians took the saint’s body and buried it with reverence. This occurred in the year 304.

Saint Stephanida

She witnessed the martyrdom of the Holy Martyr Victor at Damascus, a soldier during the reign of the emperor Marcus Aurelius the Philosopher (161-180). He was tortured, but he came through all the torments unharmed. By the power of prayer he was victorious over a sorcerer, who from that point gave up give sorcery and became a Christian.

Through Saint Victor’s prayers, blind soldiers suddenly received their sight. Witnessing the miracle worked by the Lord through Saint Victor, Stephanida, the young Christian wife of one of the torturers, openly glorified Christ, for which she was condemned to a cruel death. She was tied to two palm trees bent to the ground, which when released, sprung back and tore her apart. She was fifteen years old.

The martyrs suffered in the second century at Damascus, where their venerable relics were buried.

Troparion of Holy Martyrs Victor, Vincent and Stephanida — Tone 4

Your holy martyrs, O Lord, / through their sufferings have received incorruptible crowns from You, our God. / For having Your strength, they laid low their adversaries, / and shattered the powerless boldness of demons. / Through their intercessions, save our souls!

Saint Theodore the Confessor, Abbot of the Studion

He was born in the year 758 at Constantinople into a family of the imperial tax-collector Photinus and his spouse Theoctiste, both pious Christians. Saint Theodore received a good education from the best rhetoricians, philosophers and theologians in the capital city.

During this time the Iconoclast heresy had become widespread in the Byzantine Empire, and it was supported also by the impious emperor Constantine Kopronymos (741-775). The views of the emperor and his court conflicted with the religious beliefs of Photinus, who was a fervent adherent of Orthodoxy, and so he left government service. Later, Saint Theodore’s parents, by mutual consent, gave away their substance to the poor, took their leave of each other and accepted monastic tonsure. Their son Theodore soon became widely known in the capital for his participation of the numerous disputes concerning icon-veneration.

Saint Theodore was accomplished in oratory, and had a command of the terminology and logic of the philosophers, so he frequently debated with the heretics. His knowledge of Holy Scripture and Christian dogma was so profound that no one could get the better of him.

The Seventh Ecumenical Council put an end to dissension and brought peace to the Church under the empress Irene. The Ecumenical Council, as the highest authority in the life of the Church, forever condemned and rejected Iconoclasm.

Among the Fathers of the Council was Saint Platon (April 5), an uncle of Saint Theodore, and who for a long time had lived the ascetic life on Mount Olympos. An Elder filled with the grace of the Holy Spirit, Saint Platon, at the conclusion of the Council, summoned his nephew Theodore and his brothers Joseph and Euthymius to the monastic life in the wilderness.

After leaving Constantinople, they went to Sakkoudion, not far from Olympos. The solitude and the beauty of the place, and its difficulty of access, met with the approval of the Elder and his nephews, and they decided to remain here. The brothers built a church dedicated to Saint John the Theologian, and gradually the number of monks began to increase. A monastery was formed, and Saint Platon was the igumen.

Saint Theodore’s life was truly ascetic. He toiled at heavy and dirty work. He strictly kept the fasts, and each day he confessed to his spiritual Father, the Elder Platon, revealing to him all his deeds and thoughts, carefully fulfilling all his counsels and instructions.

Theodore made time for daily spiritual reflection, baring his soul to God. Untroubled by any earthly concern, he offered Him mystic worship. Saint Theodore unfailingly read the Holy Scripture and works of the holy Fathers, especially the works of Saint Basil the Great, which were like food for his soul.

After several years of monastic life, Saint Theodore was ordained a priest according to the will of his spiritual Father. When Saint Platon went to his rest, the brethren unanimously chose Saint Theodore as Igumen of the monastery. Unable to oppose the wish of his confessor, Saint Theodore accepted the choice of the brethren, but imposed upon himself still greater deeds of asceticism. He taught the others by the example of his own virtuous life and also by fervent fatherly instruction.

When the emperor transgressed against the Church’s canons, the events of outside life disturbed the tranquility in the monastic cells. Saint Theodore bravely distributed a letter to the other monasteries, in which he declared the emperor Constantine VI (780-797) excommunicated from the Church by his own actions for abusing the divine regulations concerning Christian marriage.

Saint Theodore and ten of his co-ascetics were sent into exile to the city of Thessalonica. But there also the accusing voice of the monk continued to speak out. Upon her return to the throne in 796, Saint Irene freed Saint Theodore and made him igumen of the Studion monastery (dedicated to Saint John the Baptist) in Constantinople, in which there were only twelve monks. The saint soon restored and enlarged the monastery, attracting about 1,000 monks who wished to have him as their spiritual guide.

Saint Theodore composed a Rule of monastic life, called the “Studite Rule” to govern the monastery. Saint Theodore also wrote many letters against the Iconoclasts. For his dogmatic works, and also for his Canons and Three-Ode Canons, Saint Theoctistus called Saint Theodore “a fiery teacher of the Church.”

When Nicephorus seized the imperial throne, deposing the pious Empress Irene, he also violated Church regulations by restoring to the Church a previously excommunicated priest on his own authority. Saint Theodore again denounced the emperor. After torture, the monk was sent into exile once again, where he spent more than two years.

Saint Theodore was freed by the gentle and pious emperor Michael, who succeeded to the throne upon the death of Nicephoros and his son Staurikios in a war against barbarians. Their death had been predicted by Saint Theodore for a long while. In order to avert civil war, the emperor Michael abdicated the throne in favor of his military commander Leo the Armenian.

The new emperor proved to be an iconoclast. The hierarchs and teachers of the Church attempted to reason with the impious emperor, but in vain. Leo prohibited the veneration of holy icons and desecrated them. Grieved by such iniquity, Saint Theodore and the brethren made a religious procession around the monastery with icons raised high, singing of the troparion to the icon of the Savior Not-Made-by-Hands (August 16).

items.title_orig: Patriarch of Romania sent a message of solidarity to the Patriarch of Bulgaria following the traffic accident in Bulgaria
items.sum:
Patriarku Daniel i Rumanisë i dërgoi një mesazh solidariteti të martën patriarkut Daniel të Bullgarisë, pas aksidentit të trafikut në juglindje të Bullgarisë.

items.text_orig:
Patriarch Daniel of Romania sent a message of solidarity on Tuesday to Patriarch Daniel of Bulgaria, following the traffic accident in South-East of Bulgaria.

“In these moments of sorrow for the Bulgarian people, we pray to the Merciful God to grant eternal rest to the souls of those who lost their lives in this tragic event, to grant a speedy recovery to the injured, and to offer comfort to the bereaved families”, the message of the Patriarch of Romania states.

Read below the message:

Bucharest, 10 November 2026

Fortlumturia e Tij DANIIL, Patriarch of Bulgaria

Your Fortlumturia,

It is with deep sorrow that we received the tragic news of the traffic accident involving dozens of vehicles on a highway in southeastern Bulgaria on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, which caused the deaths of twelve people and left others seriously injured.

In these moments of sorrow for the Bulgarian people, we pray to the Merciful God to grant eternal rest to the souls of those who lost their lives in this tragic event, to grant a speedy recovery to the injured, and to offer comfort to the bereaved families.

With brotherly love in Christ the Lord,

† DANIEL Patriarch of the Romanian Orthodox Church

items.title_orig: Patriarch of Alexandria pays tribute to Late Archbishop Chrysostomos II of Cyprus
items.sum:
Patriarku Teodori II i Aleksandrisë dhe e gjithë Afrika filluan një shërbim lutjesh të hënën, më 9 nëntor 2026, për pushimin e shpirtit të kryepeshkopit të vdekur Krisostomos II të Qipros, duke shënuar përvjetorin e katërt të kalimit të tij më 7 nëntor 2022.

Shërbimi i Trisagonit u mbajt në manastirin historik patriarkal të Shën Savasit të Sançit në Aleksandri, një vend me lidhje të gjata shpirtërore me Kishën e Qipros.

Oborri i manastirit ka një statujë të kryepeshkopit të vdekur Makarios III të Qipros, një mirëbërës i madh i Patriarkatit të Aleksandrisë, duke i ofruar përkujtimit një domethënie të veçantë historike dhe simbolike.

Si kryepeshkopi Makarios III, ashtu edhe kryepeshkopi Krisostomos II luajtën rol të rëndësishëm në mbështetjen e veprës misionare të Patriarkatit të Aleksandrisë anembanë Afrikës.

Shërbimi i lutjes solli ndër mend edhe kujtimet e nëntorit 2022, kur patriarku Teodor udhëtoi për në Qipro për t'i dhënë lamtumirën mikut të tij të ngushtë dhe të shokut të tij hieark, duke shprehur mirënjohjen e Kishës së Aleksandrisë për Kryepeshkopin Krisostomos për bujarinë dhe kontributet e paçmueshme.
items.text_orig:
Patriarch Theodore II of Alexandria and All Africa officiated at a memorial prayer service on Monday, November 9, 2026, for the repose of the soul of the late Archbishop Chrysostomos II of Cyprus, marking the fourth anniversary of his passing on November 7, 2022.

The Trisagion service was held at the historic Patriarchal Monastery of Saint Savvas the Sanctified in Alexandria, a site with longstanding spiritual ties to the Church of Cyprus.

The monastery’s courtyard houses a statue of the late Archbishop Makarios III of Cyprus, a major benefactor of the Patriarchate of Alexandria, offering particular historical and symbolic significance to the commemoration.

Both Archbishop Makarios III and Archbishop Chrysostomos II played important roles in supporting the missionary work of the Patriarchate of Alexandria across Africa.

In 1971, Archbishop Makarios III founded and funded the construction of the Patriarchal Seminary named after him in Kenya, which he subsequently donated to the Patriarchate of Alexandria.

Archbishop Chrysostomos II, meanwhile, was a close supporter of Patriarch Theodore II and his missionary initiatives, contributing significantly to the establishment of the Patriarchal Exarchate of Alexandria in Nicosia, Cyprus.

The commemoration also recalled the close spiritual relationship between the two late Cypriot Archbishops. On November 12, 1972, Archbishop Makarios III ordained Chrysostomos II to the priesthood and appointed him abbot of the Monastery of Saint Neophytos.

For Patriarch Theodore II, the memorial service carried deep personal significance, reflecting the longstanding friendship, brotherly love, and mutual respect he shared with Archbishop Chrysostomos II.

Their relationship had developed over many years through their common ecclesiastical ministry and shared commitment to Orthodox unity.

The prayer service also brought back memories of November 2022, when Patriarch Theodore traveled to Cyprus to bid farewell to his close friend and fellow hierarch, expressing the gratitude of the Church of Alexandria for Archbishop Chrysostomos’ generosity and invaluable contributions.

Four years later, the memorial service served as a reminder of the enduring spiritual bonds between the Patriarchates of Alexandria and the Church of Cyprus.

Through their dedication to the Church and their support for Orthodox missionary work, Archbishops Makarios III and Chrysostomos II left a lasting legacy of solidarity and cooperation between the two Apostolic Churches.

The commemoration also expressed Patriarch Theodore’s continuing brotherly love for the Church of Cyprus and his hope that the spiritual legacy of its departed Archbishops would continue to inspire unity, fraternity, and their shared Christian witness.

May the memory of Archbishop Chrysostomos II of Cyprus be eternal.

items.text:
U KREMTUA AGRIPNIA E SHENJTË ME RASTIN E FESTËS SË SHËN NEKTARIT TË PENTAPOJËS

Me bekimin dhe praninë e Fortlumturisë së Tij, Kryepiskopit Joan, ditën e diel, më 8 nëntor 2026, u kremtua Agripnia e Shenjtë me rastin e festës së Shën Nektarit të Pentapojës, një prej shenjtorëve më të dashur dhe më të nderuar të Kishës sonë Orthodhokse.

Shërbesat e shenjta nisën në orën 21:00, në një atmosferë të thellë lutjeje, përkushtimi dhe përshpirtërie. Besimtarë të shumtë orthodhoksë u mblodhën për të marrë pjesë në këtë kremtim të veçantë, duke iu bashkuar lutjeve dhe himneve kishtare në nderim të shenjtorit.

Gjatë Agripnisë, të pranishmit patën mundësinë të përjetojnë bukurinë dhe solemnitetin e traditës liturgjike orthodhokse, duke iu lutur Shën Nektarit për ndërmjetësimin dhe bekimin e tij.

Shën Nektari i Pentapojës, i njohur për përulësinë, durimin, dashurinë dhe besimin e tij të palëkundur te Perëndia, mbetet një shembull i gjallë i jetës së krishterë dhe një burim frymëzimi e shprese për të gjithë besimtarët.

Kremtimi i kësaj Agripnie u bë një rast i veçantë bashkimi shpirtëror, lutjeje dhe falënderimi ndaj Perëndisë, duke rikujtuar edhe një herë rëndësinë e trashëgimisë sonë të shenjtë orthodhokse dhe të shembullit të shenjtorëve në jetën e Kishës.

Shën Nektari i Pentapojës, ndërmjeto për ne!

MEDIA NGJALLJA, 9/11/2026

items.title: Argos Orestiko nderoi Shën Nektarin me pjesëmarrjen e Mitropolitit të Korçës, Anastasit
items.summary: Mitropoliti i Korçës, Hirësia e Tij, Imzot Anastasi, kryesoi shërbesat për Shën Nektarin në Argos Orestiko më 8 dhe 9 nëntor. Në qendër të kremtimeve ishin shembulli i shenjtorit dhe lidhjet shpirtërore ndërmjet Korçës dhe Kastorias.
items.text:
Në kishën madhështore të Shën Nektarit, qyteti Argos Orestiko, në Mitropolinë e Shenjtë të Kastorias, nderoi më 8 dhe 9 nëntor, si çdo vit, bashkëmbrojtësin dhe bashkëpatronin e tij, Shën Nektarin, Episkopin e Pentapojës, mrekullibërësin.

Shërbesat festive të këtij viti i kryesoi Mitropoliti i Korçës, Hirësia e Tij, Imzot Anastasi, i Kishës Orthodhokse Autoqefale të Shqipërisë, me ftesë të bariut vendas, Mitropolitit të Kastorias, Hirësisë së Tij, Imzot Kalinikut. Kishën e Shqipërisë e lidhin marrëdhënie historike dhe kishtare me Mitropolinë e Kastorias. Të njëjtin kremtim, në vitin 2024, e kishte kryesuar Mitropoliti i atëhershëm i Korçës dhe Kryepiskopi i sotëm i Shqipërisë, Fortlumturia e Tij, Imzot Joani.

Mbrëmësorja festive

Pasditen e së dielës, më 8 nëntor 2026, u krye Mbrëmësorja me pjesëmarrjen e dy kryepriftërinjve dhe me bekimin e pesë bukëve. Shërbesën e kryesoi dhe predikoi Mitropoliti i Korçës, Imzot Anastasi, ndërsa bashkë me të mori pjesë në kryesimin e saj Mitropoliti i Kastorias, Imzot Kaliniku.

Duke i uruar mirëseardhjen në Kastoria hierarkut të ftuar, Imzot Kaliniku foli fillimisht për Shën Nektarin, shenjtorin e madh bashkëkohor të Kishës, i cili u bë i dashur për popullin. Ai kujtoi se, me praninë dhe shërbimin e tij, shenjtori shenjtëroi vendet ku kaloi: Thrakën dhe Konstandinopojën, Hiosin, Aleksandrinë, Athinën dhe, së fundi, Eginën, ku themeloi Manastirin e Trinisë së Shenjtë.

Mitropoliti u ndal te dashuria, përulësia dhe formimi arsimor i shenjtorit. Siç theksoi, Shën Nektari i përballoi shpifjet dhe padrejtësinë me durim të krishterë, duke ndjekur shembullin e Krishtit, dhe kështu u bë një shenjtor e mrekullibërës që nderohet në mbarë botën.

Ai e cilësoi bekim të veçantë për Mitropolinë e Kastorias praninë në Argos Orestiko të kishës madhështore të Shën Nektarit, e cila u ndërtua me nismën e Mitropolitit të lumur Serafim. Shpjegoi se punimet për përfundimin e kishës vazhdojnë, pasi mbetet ende për t’u realizuar zbukurimi ikonografik. Gjithashtu njoftoi se vitin e ardhshëm do të përurohet Qendra Shpirtërore pranë kishës, e cila synohet të bëhet një vatër e gjallë e veprimtarisë shpirtërore dhe kishtare.

Duke shprehur gëzimin për praninë e Mitropolitit të ri të Korçës, Imzot Anastasit, Imzot Kaliniku iu kthye vizitës së paraardhësit të tij, Imzot Joanit, dy vjet më parë. Ai kujtoi se, pak muaj pas asaj vizite, Mitropoliti i atëhershëm i Korçës u zgjodh Kryepiskop i Tiranës dhe i Gjithë Shqipërisë. Ai takim, theksoi, krijoi një lidhje të veçantë shpirtërore, të cilën Mitropolia dëshiron ta ruajë dhe ta forcojë me Kishën e vendit fqinj.

Në praninë edhe të përfaqësuesve të pushtetit rajonal dhe vendor, ai uroi që lëvizjet ndërmjet Greqisë dhe Shqipërisë të bëhen ashtu siç ndodh tashmë me Bullgarinë, në dobi të dy popujve fqinjë, të shteteve të tyre dhe të dy Kishave motra Orthodhokse.

Në përfundim të përshëndetjes, ai përmendi veçanërisht formimin, studimet dhe zellin për punë të Imzot Anastasit, si edhe angazhimin e tij në fusha bashkëkohore që i shërbejnë përparimit dhe zhvillimit të një zone.

Mitropoliti i Korçës: Të ndjekim shembullin e Shën Nektarit

Në predikimin e Mbrëmësores, Mitropoliti i Korçës, Imzot Anastasi, mori shkas nga fjala apostolike: «Mos u mund nga e keqja, por munde të keqen me të mirën». Ai foli për fuqinë e dashurisë së krishterë përballë padrejtësisë, shpifjes dhe sprovave të jetës, duke vënë në dukje se shenjtorët e Kishës, pavarësisht përndjekjeve dhe hidhërimeve që përjetuan, e ruajtën zemrën plot dashuri dhe gatishmëri për të falur.

Për shenjtorin që kremtohej, ai theksoi përulësinë, jetën asketike dhe formimin e thellë teologjik. Megjithatë, vëmendje të veçantë i kushtoi mënyrës se si ai i përballoi shpifjet dhe padrejtësitë: nuk lejoi që dhimbja të kthehej në urrejtje, por qëndroi i palëkundur, duke ruajtur frymën e tij kishtare dhe dashurinë për Krishtin dhe Kishën e Tij.

Një vend të veçantë në predikim zuri Kryepiskopi i lumur i Shqipërisë, Anastasi, të cilin Mitropoliti i Korçës pati bekimin ta njihte dhe t’i shërbente. Ai foli për sprovat gjatë shërbimit të tij shumëvjeçar dhe për përkushtimin e dashurinë me të cilat punoi për ringritjen e Kishës Orthodhokse Autoqefale të Shqipërisë.

Imzot Anastasi falënderoi përzemërsisht Mitropolitin Imzot Kalinik për ftesën dhe përcolli urimet e klerit dhe të popullit të Mitropolisë së Korçës. Ai theksoi gjithashtu lidhjet historike dhe shpirtërore të dy Mitropolive fqinje, të cilat mbështeten në besimin e përbashkët orthodhoks dhe në kungimin nga i njëjti Potir i Shenjtë, duke uruar që marrëdhënia e tyre vëllazërore të forcohet më tej.

Në përfundim, ai i ftoi besimtarët të ndjekin shembullin e Shën Nektarit: ta ruajnë zemrën të lirë nga mëria, të falin dhe të duan me dashurinë e Krishtit, në mënyrë që vetë jeta e tyre të dëshmojë praninë e Tij në botë.

Bashkëmeshimi kryepriftëror dhe litania

Të hënën, më 9 nëntor, ditën e festës, u kryen Mëngjesorja dhe më pas bashkëmeshimi kryepriftëror. Predikoi Arkimandriti atë Stefan Schinas, klerik i Mitropolisë së Shenjtë të Kastorias, i cili jep mësim në Qendrën e Mësimit të Gjuhës Greke «Aristoteli» në Korçë.

Atë Stefani foli për qëndrimin e Shën Nektarit ndaj padrejtësisë. Pavarësisht sprovave dhe largimit nga detyra e tij kishtare, vuri në dukje ai, shenjtori mbeti i përulur, i duruar dhe besnik ndaj Krishtit dhe Kishës. Ai nuk e ktheu të keqen me të keqe dhe nuk lejoi që urrejtja e hakmarrja të mbizotëronin në shpirtin e tij, por i përballoi vështirësitë me besim dhe falje. Predikuesi vërejti gjithashtu se smira, ambicia dhe dëshira për pushtet, si dobësi njerëzore, mund të shfaqen edhe brenda Kishës, pa e cenuar për këtë arsye shenjtërinë e saj.

Në përfundim, ai i nxiti besimtarët të luftojnë për të vërtetën dhe drejtësinë pa urrejtje apo hakmarrje, të falin pa e përligjur të keqen dhe t’i besojnë gjykimit të drejtë dhe mëshirës së Perëndisë. Drejtësia përfundimtare, theksoi, është në duart e Perëndisë dhe jo të njerëzve.

Në fund të Eukaristisë Hyjnore u bekuan kolivat festive të shenjtorit. Më pas, Mitropoliti Imzot Kaliniku kreu hirothesinë në anagnostë (lexues kishtarë) të Nikolla Toulias dhe Foti Karafotis, të cilët shërbejnë në analogjët e kishës.

Gjatë përlëshimit, Mitropoliti i Kastorias falënderoi nga zemra Mitropolitin e Korçës, Imzot Anastasin, që pranoi ftesën dhe për praninë e tij vëllazërore në Kastoria. Ai theksoi sërish lidhjet historike dhe shpirtërore ndërmjet dy Mitropolive të Shenjta fqinje.

Ai foli gjithashtu për mënyrën e përballimit të padrejtësisë dhe për dashurinë ndaj Kishës, edhe kur njerëzit e saj gabojnë. Kisha, siç tha duke iu referuar Mitropolitit të Nafpaktos, Imzot Hierotheut, është një spital shpirtëror që ofron shërim shpirtëror për plagët dhe dobësitë.

Më pas përkujtoi figura të rëndësishme kishtare të Shqipërisë: Kryepiskopin e lumur Anastas, Episkopin e Apollonisë Kozma dhe Mitropolitin e Beratit Ignat. Ai foli edhe për paraardhësin e tij, Mitropolitin e Kastorias Grigori III, duke vlerësuar dashurinë me të cilën priti dhe strehoi vëllezërit e sprovuar nga Shqipëria kur u hapën kufijtë. Me këtë rast njoftoi veprimtari të Mitropolisë më 18 dhe 19 nëntor, në kuadër të kushtimit të vitit 2026 përvjetorit të 30-të të fjetjes së Grigorit III.

Imzot Kaliniku falënderoi priftërinjtë e kishës, atë Paskal Moutzikis dhe atë Pavël Lazongas, për organizimin e festës, së bashku me bashkëpunëtorët e tyre, këshillin kishtar, vullnetarët dhe vullnetaret, psaltët dhe djemtë që shërbejnë në altar.

Ai përkujtoi dhe falënderoi edhe ktitorët e kishës: paraardhësin e tij të lumur Serafim; atë Leonid Bardos, priftin e Kishës së Shën Parashqevisë në Argos Orestiko, i cili shërbente si prift i enorisë në kohën e hedhjes së themeleve dhe të ndërtimit; si edhe familjen e Spiridhon Grigoriadis dhe vëllezërit e motrën e tij, Aleksandrin, Nikollën dhe Magdalininë.

Ai falënderoi gjithashtu priftërinjtë dhe dhjakët që bashkëmeshuan, veçanërisht klerikët e Kishës së Shqipërisë, si edhe autoritetet e pranishme. Falënderoi Bandën Frymore të Bashkisë së Argos Orestikos, zjarrfikësit dhe Shoqatën e Pontikëve për pjesëmarrjen në litani, Policinë dhe Policinë Rrugore për ruajtjen e rendit, si edhe të gjithë popullin, enoritët dhe të gjithë banorët e Argosit, të cilët e duan enorinë e tyre dhe nderojnë Shën Nektarin, duke marrë edhe vetë nderimin dhe bekimin e shenjtorit.

Më pas u zhvillua litania me ikonën e shenjtë dhe lipsanet e shenjtorit rreth kishës, me pjesëmarrjen e klerit dhe të popullit. Në krye të procesionit ishin Banda Frymore e Bashkisë së Argos Orestikos, burra të Shërbimit Zjarrfikës të Njësisë së Argos Orestikos dhe burra të Shoqatës së Pontikëve, të cilët mbanin ikonat e shenjta të Hyjlindëses dhe të Shën Nektarit, që kremtohej.

Mbrëmësorja pas festës dhe ligjërata

Pasditen e së njëjtës ditë u kryen Mbrëmësorja pas festës dhe Paraklisi për kujtimin e Oshënar Arsenit të Kapadokisë.

Pas shërbesave, Igumeni i Manastirit të Shenjtë të Sparmosit në Olimp, Arkimandriti atë Nikanor, shtjelloi temën «Arti i ecjes së bashku me atin shpirtëror, sipas Shën Nektarit». Në ligjëratë ishte i pranishëm edhe Mitropoliti, Hirësia e Tij, Imzot Kaliniku.
items.ex: Mitropoliti i Korçës, Hirësia e Tij, Imzot Anastasi, kryesoi shërbesat për Shën Nektarin në Argos Orestiko më 8 dhe 9 nëntor. Në qendër të kremtimeve ishin shembulli i shenjtorit dhe lidhjet shpirtërore ndërmjet Korçës dhe Kastorias.
items.sum:
Në kishën madhështore të Shën Nektarit, qyteti Argos Orestiko, në Mitropolinë e Shenjtë të Kastorias, nderoi më 8 dhe 9 nëntor, si çdo vit, bashkëmbrojtësin dhe bashkëpatronin e tij, Shën Nektarin, Episkopin e Pentapojës, mrekullibërësin.

Shërbesat festive të këtij viti i kryesoi Mitropoliti i Korçës, Hirësia e Tij, Imzot Anastasi, i Kishës Orthodhokse Autoqefale të Shqipërisë, me ftesë të bariut vendas, Mitropolitit të Kastorias, Hirësisë së Tij, Imzot Kalinikut. Kishën e Shqipërisë e lidhin marrëdhënie historike dhe kishtare me Mitropolinë e Kastorias. Të njëjtin kremtim, në vitin 2024, e kishte kryesuar Mitropoliti i atëhershëm i Korçës dhe Kryepiskopi i sotëm i Shqipërisë, Fortlumturia e Tij, Imzot Joani.

Shërbesën e kryesoi dhe predikoi Mitropoliti i Korçës, Imzot Anastasi, ndërsa bashkë me të mori pjesë në kryesimin e saj Mitropoliti i Kastorias, Imzot Kaliniku.

Duke i uruar mirëseardhjen në Kastoria hierarkut të ftuar, Imzot Kaliniku foli fillimisht për Shën Nektarin, shenjtorin e madh bashkëkohor të Kishës, i cili u bë i dashur për popullin.

Ai e cilësoi bekim të veçantë për Mitropolinë e Kastorias praninë në Argos Orestiko të kishës madhështore të Shën Nektarit, e cila u ndërtua me nismën e Mitropolitit të lumur Serafim.

Duke shprehur gëzimin për praninë e Mitropolitit të ri të Korçës, Imzot Anastasit, Imzot Kaliniku iu kthye vizitës së paraardhësit të tij, Imzot Joanit, dy vjet më parë.

Mitropoliti i Korçës: Të ndjekim shembullin e Shën Nektarit

Në predikimin e Mbrëmësores, Mitropoliti i Korçës, Imzot Anastasi, mori shkas nga fjala apostolike: «Mos u mund nga e keqja, por munde të keqen me të mirën».

Një vend të veçantë në predikim zuri Kryepiskopi i lumur i Shqipërisë, Anastasi, të cilin Mitropoliti i Korçës pati bekimin ta njihte dhe t’i shërbente. Ai foli për sprovat gjatë shërbimit të tij shumëvjeçar dhe për përkushtimin e dashurinë me të cilat punoi për ringritjen e Kishës Orthodhokse Autoqefale të Shqipërisë.

Imzot Anastasi falënderoi përzemërsisht Mitropolitin Imzot Kalinik për ftesën dhe përcolli urimet e klerit dhe të popullit të Mitropolisë së Korçës.

Më pas, Mitropoliti Imzot Kaliniku kreu hirothesinë në anagnostë (lexues kishtarë) të Nikolla Toulias dhe Foti Karafotis, të cilët shërbejnë në analogjët e kishës.

Gjatë përlëshimit, Mitropoliti i Kastorias falënderoi nga zemra Mitropolitin e Korçës, Imzot Anastasin, që pranoi ftesën dhe për praninë e tij vëllazërore në Kastoria.

Imzot Kaliniku falënderoi priftërinjtë e kishës, atë Paskal Moutzikis dhe atë Pavël Lazongas, për organizimin e festës, së bashku me bashkëpunëtorët e tyre, këshillin kishtar, vullnetarët dhe vullnetaret, psaltët dhe djemtë që shërbejnë në altar.

Ai përkujtoi dhe falënderoi edhe ktitorët e kishës: paraardhësin e tij të lumur Serafim; atë Leonid Bardos, priftin e Kishës së Shën Parashqevisë në Argos Orestiko, i cili shërbente si prift i enorisë në kohën e hedhjes së themeleve dhe të ndërtimit; si edhe familjen e Spiridhon Grigoriadis dhe vëllezërit e motrën e tij, Aleksandrin, Nikollën dhe Magdalininë.

Në ligjëratë ishte i pranishëm edhe Mitropoliti, Hirësia e Tij, Imzot Kaliniku.

items.title_orig: Archbishop of America warns of intensifying Russian attacks on Ecumenical Patriarchate
items.sum:
Kryepeshkopi Elpidofos i Amerikës vlerësoi misionin e përhershëm të Greqisë në Kombet e Bashkuara për sigurimin e një rezolute të Këshillit të Sigurimit që forcon mbrojtjen për fëmijët e prekur nga konflikti i armatosur, duke thënë se arritja kishte rëndësi të veçantë për të si një hierarki e Kishës Orthodhokse Greke.

Ambasadori vizitues Aglaia Balta, përfaqësuese e përhershme e Greqisë, në zyrat e misionit, kryepeshkopi e uroi atë dhe delegacionin për punën e tyre të madhe gjatë qëndrimit të Këshillit të Sigurimit të Greqisë. Kryepeshkopi Elpidophos vlerësoi ambasadorin Balta për kalimin e suksesshëm të Rezolutës 2832.

Balta tha se Greqia synonte të vazhdonte nismat e saj mbi fëmijët dhe sigurinë detare përtej mandatit të saj të Këshillit, me një seminar mbi fëmijët e planifikuar për në krye të 2027.
items.text_orig:
Archbishop Elpidophoros of America praised Greece’s Permanent Mission to the United Nations for securing a Security Council resolution strengthening protections for children affected by armed conflict, saying the achievement held particular significance for him as a hierarch of the Greek Orthodox Church.

Visiting Ambassador Aglaia Balta, Greece’s permanent representative, at the mission’s offices, the Archbishop congratulated her and the delegation on their great work during Greece’s Security Council tenure. Archbishop Elpidophoros praised Ambassador Balta on the successful passage of Resolution 2832. Drafted by Greece and adopted unanimously on Oct. 19, it addresses abuses against children in armed conflict that are enabled or intensified by digital technologies, including recruitment and exploitation.

The resolution calls for stronger safeguards and accountability, while encouraging the safe use of technology to support education and child protection. Balta said Greece intended to continue its initiatives on children and maritime security beyond its Council term, with a workshop on children planned for early 2027.

The discussion turned to Russia’s continuing invasion of Ukraine and the prospects for ending the war. Archbishop Elpidophoros also expressed concern over intensifying Russian attacks on the Ecumenical Patriarchate, describing efforts by Russian state and affiliated actors to undermine the institution.

On Cyprus, Archbishop Elpidophoros stressed the importance of keeping the issue on the U.N. agenda until a just and viable settlement is achieved. Also discussed was the United Nations’ potential role in establishing an international framework for artificial intelligence. The Archbishop said a U.N. body could help bring countries and other key participants worldwide into the development of shared rules and safeguards. Balta emphasized the need for U.N. leadership with the political foresight to address such emerging challenges.

Photos by Orthodox Observer/Dimitrios Panagos

items.title_orig: †) Apostles Erastus, Olympas, Herodion, Sosipater, Quartus, and Tertius of the Seventy; Martyr Orestes of Cappadocia, Holy Venerable Martyr Bessarion of Lainici
items.sum:
Apostujt e shenjtë të të shtatëdhjetëve: Olimpa, Erasti, Rodioni, Sosipateri, Kuarti dhe Terci

Shën Rodioni, (prill 8 prill) ishte i afërm i apostullit Pavël (Romakët 16:11) dhe e la fronin e peshkopit në Patras për të shkuar në Romë me apostullin Pjetër. Shën Olimpasi ishte edhe shok i apostullit Pjetër.

Shën Olimpas u përmend nga apostulli i shenjtë Pavël (Rom 16:15).

Apostujt e shenjtë Sosipatri (prill 28 prill), Erasti, Kuarti dhe Terci ( 30 tetor) ishin dishepuj të Shën Pavlit.

Shën Tertius është përmendur në Epistle për romakët: "Unë, Terci, që shkroi këtë letër, ju përshëndes në Zotërinë 16:22 " .

Shën Terci, të cilit Shën Pali ua diktoi Epistlën romakëve, ishte peshkopi i dytë i Ikonisë, ku vdiq edhe ai.

Troparoni, toni 3: Apostujt e Shenjtë, Erasti, Olimpi, Herodioni, Sosipatri, Kuarti dhe Terci, i luten Perëndisë së mëshirshëm, për të na falur shpirtrat e shkeljeve.

Prokurori ofroi pasuritë e shenjta, nderimet dhe namin për të hequr dorë nga Perëndia, por Shën Orestsi ishte i palëkundur.

Në vitin 1685, kur Shën Dhimitri, më vonë peshkopi i Rostovit, (tetor 28 tetor) po përgatiste jetën e Shën Orestit që do të shtypej nga shpellat Kiev Lavra, ai u lodh dhe ra në gjumë. Martiri i shenjtë Oresti iu shfaq në ëndërr.

Martiri i shenjtë shikoi Shën Dhimitrin dhe tha: " Shiko, kam vuajtur më shumë mundime për Krishtin, sesa ke përshkruar ti. "

Troparoni, toni 4: Priftëtari juaj i shenjtë Oresti, O Zot, me anë të vuajtjeve të tij, ka marrë një kurorë të pakorruptueshme nga Ti, Perëndia ynë.

Vite më vonë, këto relika të shenjta duheshin rizbuluar në rastin e kanonizimit të Shën Irodionit më 2011.

Me anë të ndërhyrjeve të tij të shenjta, Zoti Jezu Krisht, Perëndia ynë, ka mëshirë për ne.

Troparioni Tone 3 Ju treguat një vepër të mrekullueshme në manastirin Lainici, O Atë i Shenjtë Bessarion, nëpërmjet agjërimit, zgjimit dhe lutjeve, nëpërmjet dashurisë së përsosur për Perëndinë dhe për fqinjin tuaj, ju e treguat veten një mrekullibërës.
items.text_orig:
The Holy Apostles of the Seventy: Olympas, Erastus, Rodion, Sosipater, Quartus and Tertius

They lived in the first century.

Saint Rodion, or Herodion (April 8), was a kinsman of the Apostle Paul (Romans 16:11), and left the bishop’s throne at Patras to go to Rome with the Apostle Peter. Saint Olympas was also a companion of the Apostle Peter. Saints Rodion and Olympas were beheaded on the very day and hour when Saint Peter was crucified.

Saint Olympas was mentioned by the holy Apostle Paul (Rom 16:15). He was also a companion of the Apostle Peter. He was beheaded on the very day and hour when Saint Peter was crucified.

The holy Apostles Sosipater (April 28), Erastus, Quartus and Tertius (October 30) were disciples of Saint Paul.

Saint Sosipater, a native of Achaia, was Bishop of Iconium, where also he died. Saint Paul mentions him in Romans 16:21.

The Apostle to the Gentiles speaks of Erastus and Quartus in the Epistle to the Romans, “And Erastus, the city treasurer, greets you, and Quartus, a brother” (Rom 16: 23).

Saint Quartus endured much suffering for his piety and converted many pagans to Christ, dying peacefully as a bishop in the city of Beirut.

Saint Tertius is mentioned in the Epistle to the Romans, “ I, Tertius, who wrote this epistle, salute you in the Lord” (Rom 16:22).

Saint Tertius, to whom Saint Paul dictated the Epistle to the Romans, was the second Bishop of Iconium, where also he died.

Troparion, tone 3: Holy Apostles, Erastus, Olympas, Herodion, Sosipater, Quartus and Tertius, entreat the merciful God, to grant our souls forgiveness of transgressions.

Martyr Orestes the Physician of Cappadocia

He lived at the end of the third century in the city of Tyana in Cappadocia in the time of the emperor Diocletian (284-311). He was an illustrious and capable soldier, and from childhood Saint Orestes was truly a good Christian.

By order of the emperor, the military officer Maximinus was sent to Tyana to deal with Christianity, which then had spread widely throughout Cappadocia. Orestes was among the first brought to trial to Maximinus. He bravely and openly confessed his faith in the Crucified and Risen Lord, Jesus Christ. The prosecutor offered the saint riches, honors and renown to renounce God, but Saint Orestes was unyielding.

At the order of Maximinus, they took Orestes to a resplendant pagan temple and again demanded that he worship idols. When he refused, forty soldiers, took turns one after the other, beating the holy martyr with lashes, with rods, with rawhide, and then they tormented him with fire. Saint Orestes cried out to the Lord, “Establish with me a sign for good, let those who hate me see it and be put to shame (Ps. 85/86:17). “And the Lord heard His true servant. The earth began to tremble, and the idols fell down and were smashed. Everyone rushed out of the temple, and when Saint Orestes came out, the very temple tumbled down.

Infuriated, Maximinus ordered the holy martyr to be locked up in prison for seven days giving him neither food nor drink, and on the eighth day to continue with the torture. They hammered twenty nails into the martyr’s legs, and then tied him to a wild horse. Dragged over the stones, the holy martyr departed to the Lord in the year 304. His relics were thrown into the sea.

In 1685, when Saint Demetrius, later the Bishop of Rostov, (October 28) was preparing the Life of Saint Orestes to be printed by the Kiev Caves Lavra, he became tired and fell asleep. The holy martyr Orestes appeared to him in a dream.

He showed him the deep wound in his left side, his wounded and severed arms, and his legs which had been cut off. The holy martyr looked at Saint Demetrius and said, “You see, I suffered more torments for Christ than you have described.” The humble monk wondered whether this was Saint Orestes, one of the Five Martyrs of Sebaste (December 13). The martyr said, “I am not that Orestes, but he whose Life you have just finished writing.”

Troparion, tone 4: Your holy martyr Orestes, O Lord, through his sufferings has received an incorruptible crown from You, our God. For having Your strength, he laid low his adversaries, and shattered the powerless boldness of demons. Through his intercessions, save our souls!

Saint Bessarion was born in Secuieni, Bacău County, on May 28, 1884. His parents, Gheorghe and Ilinca, were simple people, who loved God. At his baptism he received the name of his father, Gheorghe.

From an early age, loving the church, church services and church music, he attended the School for Church Chanters in Roman.

Growing spiritually, under the guidance of his spiritual father, Bishop Gherasim Safirin, he felt the calling of God and, not long after, he entered as a novice at the Holy Monastery of Frăsinei, being tonsured a monk with the name Bessarion.

Having received the angelic schema, Bessarion showed even more zeal in spiritual needs, in piety towards the holy things, in silence and obedience. Many times, when he chanted, his angelic voice penetrated the hearts of those who heard him, bringing tears of repentance.

Abbot Porfirie, seeing his growth in virtue, proposed him for the priesthood in 1922. From then on, he celebrated the Divine Liturgy with great piety and love, bringing a longing for God into the hearts of those who heard him. As a confessor, he was a great guide to monastics and pilgrims, praying for them and comforting them in their troubles and needs.

In the spring of 1929, Bessarion was appointed abbot of Lainici Monastery. His task was to rebuild Lainici Monastery, ruined by the war. He founded a community pleasing to God and, having the spiritual grace and experience, he established, in addition to the church services, the hesychastic rite of unceasing recitation of the Jesus prayer.

Also, every work was carried out with blessing, obedience and good will, so that the whole life of Lainici Monastery was conducted in an atmosphere of love, joy and hope of eternal life.

The love of Byzantine music did not leave St. Bessarion even in this obedience, he continued to share with his disciples the gift of church chanting, so that all with one heart and one mouth to praise God.

Although preoccupied with so many worries and burdened by so many sufferings, he respected his monastic duties, he did not miss the Divine Liturgy, he prayed and fasted, he kept vigil all night and read holy books for the benefit of his own soul and that of his disciples.

Because his heart was full of love for his fellow humans, he also helped to organize a hospital for those suffering on the construction sites on the banks of the Jiu River. At the same time, the monastery and the community grew in both spiritual and material terms. New cells were added, as well as land and dwellings for the inhabitants.

He also had the blessing to find the holy relics of his predecessor, St. Irodion, which he placed in a small coffin and hid them as a treasure of great price and deeper in the bowels of the earth, to protect them from the profanation of the unbelievers. Years later, these holy relics were to be rediscovered on the occasion of the canonization of Saint Irodion in 2011.

For his virtues and his labours, accompanied by great humility, God gave him the gift of spiritual guidance and marvelous healings. His deeds remained vivid in the memory of the monastery and of the faithful who came to this holy place for prayer.

The miracle of 1950, when a mute man heard in a dream a voice that told him to go to Lainici Monastery to be healed, is still recorded. He came to Abbot Bessarion, who read prayers of deliverance and healing, made three times the Divine Liturgy, confessed him and gave him many counsels useful to the soul.

At that time, Lainici Monastery came to be occupied by the soldiers of the communist regime, who disturbed the monastic life and the church services. One afternoon, however, the eldest of these soldiers, being overcome by drunkenness, beat the blessed abbot without guilt, asking him to leave his cell.

The saint tried to soothe him with kind words, but he beat him even more severely, trampling him underfoot and throwing him from the porch of his cell. He was knocked to the ground, broke his leg, and remained for a long time in a pool of blood.

Moreover, the officer threatened them that “if anyone in the monastery says anything about this, they will all be killed”. A few days after the ordeal, Father’s wounds and fractured leg became infected and the doctors had to amputate his leg. Sensing that his end was near, the Blessed Father asked to receive the great schema, and shortly afterwards, on November 8, 1951, at the age of 67, he fell asleep in the Lord. He was laid in the tomb next to St. Irodion, his predecessor.

Through his holy intercessions, Lord Jesus Christ, our God, have mercy on us. Amen.

Troparion – Tone 3 You showed a wonderful work at Lainici monastery, O Holy Father Bessarion, through fasting, vigils and prayer, through perfect love of God and your neighbor, you showed yourself a wonderworker. You suffered at the hands of unbelievers, and were crowned with glory in heaven. Therefore, intercede with Christ God to save our souls.

Today we also commemorate Saint Arsenios the Cappadocian .

items.text_orig:
As part of the Divine Liturgy celebrated at the Horrendous Golgotha on the morning of Monday, 9 November 2026, presided over by Archbishop Philoumenos of Pella, the fortieth-day Memorial Service was held for the late Archimandrite Ioustinos of the Holy Sepulchre Brotherhood, Hegumen of Jacob’s Well in Samaria.

The Memorial Service was presided over by Father and Patriarch Theophilos III of Jerusalem, with the participation of Hierarchs of the Holy Sepulchre Brotherhood, other Fathers of the Brotherhood, and faithful, all joining in prayer that the Lord may grant rest to his soul in the abode of the living.

May his memory be eternal.

Source: Patriarchate of Jerusalem

items.sum:
Patriarku Teodori II i Aleksandrisë dhe i gjithë Afrikës kryesoi të dielën më 8 nëntor 2026, në manastirin patriarkal të Shën Savasit, Sançtifikuar në Aleksandri.

Në fjalimin e tij, patriarku Teodor foli emocionalisht për lidhjen e tij frymore me Shën Nektashin, duke theksuar përulësinë e shenjtë, durimin, faljen dhe besimin e palëkundur, pavarësisht nga vështirësitë dhe padrejtësitë që duroi.

Patriarku kujtoi gjithashtu Kishën e Shën Nektashit në Kamerun, ndërtuar gjatë qëndrimit të tij si metropolitan i Kamerunit dhe ndau përvoja të mrekullive që i atribuoheshin ndërmjetësve të shenjtë.

Shërbimi përfundoi me Patriarkun e 19-të, duke bekuar dhe lutur për Kishën e Aleksandrisë, kontinentin afrikan dhe gjithë botën, duke ndërmjetësuar për të gjithë ata që përballen me vuajtje dhe vështirësi.
items.text_orig:
Patriarch Theodore II of Alexandria and All Africa presided over the Great Patriarchal Vespers in honor of Saint Nektarios, Bishop of Pentapolis and Wonderworker, at the Patriarchal Monastery of Saint Savvas the Sanctified in Alexandria on Sunday, November 8, 2026.

The Patriarch was joined by Metropolitan Germanos of Tamiathis, spiritual father of the monastery, and Bishop Damaskinos of Mareotis, Patriarchal Vicar of Alexandria. The service was attended by the Consul General of Greece in Alexandria, Vasilis Zarambalis, and members of the historic Greek community of Alexandria.

The celebration held particular historical significance, as Saint Nektarios was ordained a priest at the same monastery on March 23, 1886, by Patriarch Sophronios IV of Alexandria.

In his address, Patriarch Theodore spoke emotionally about his personal spiritual connection with Saint Nektarios, emphasizing the saint’s humility, patience, forgiveness, and unwavering faith despite the hardships and injustices he endured.

The Patriarch also recalled the Church of Saint Nektarios in Cameroon, built during his tenure as Metropolitan of Cameroon, and shared personal experiences of miracles attributed to the saint’s intercessions.

With tears in his eyes, he referred to the Church of Saint Nektarios in Geri, Nicosia, which belongs to the Patriarchate’s Exarchate in Cyprus. He expressed his heartfelt hope that the entire complex would soon be completed and fully opened for worship, supporting the missionary work of the Patriarchate of Alexandria.

Patriarch Theodore stressed that every church, regardless of its patron saint, should remain a living place of prayer, spiritual refuge, and consolation, with its doors open to all who seek God’s love and hope.

He offered special prayers for those suffering from illness, particularly cancer patients and their families, asking for strength, patience, relief, and healing through the intercessions of Saint Nektarios.

The service concluded with the Patriarch’s blessing and prayers for the Church of Alexandria, the African continent, and the entire world, invoking Saint Nektarios’ intercessions for all those facing suffering and hardship.

items.sum:
Saint Nektashios

Meqë familja e tij ishte e varfër, Anastasi shkoi në Kostandinopojë kur ishte katërmbëdhjetë vjeç për të gjetur punë.

Disa nga kolegët e tij u bënë xhelozë për të për shkak të virtyteve të tij të mëdha, për shkak të predikimeve të tij frymëzuese, dhe për shkak të çdo gjëje tjetër që dalloi Shën Nektariusin prej tyre.

Metropolitët e tjerë dhe peshkopët e Patriarkatit të Aleksandrisë u mbushën me keqdashje ndaj shenjtorit, prandaj i thanë patriarkut Sofronio se Nektariusi po komplotonte të bëhej vetë patriark.

Kështu që patriarku dhe sinodi i tij hoqën Shën Nektariusin nga pamja e tij. Patriarku Sofroni shkroi një letër të paqartë pezullimi, e cila provokoi skandal dhe spekulime rreth arsyeve të vërteta për heqjen e shenjtorëve nga pozita e tij.

Megjithatë, Shën Nektariusi nuk u hoq nga rangu i tij.

Saint Nektariusi i duroi sprovat me shumë durim, por ata që e donin, filluan të kërkonin të dinin pse ishte hequr.

Një ditë, ndërsa po largohej nga zyra e ministrit, Shën Nektariusi takoi një mik që e kishte njohur në Egjipt.

Pra, Saint Nektarius u emërua predikues i përulur në dioqezën e Vitineisë dhe Euboeas.

Me ndihmën dhe ndikimin e tyre, Shën Nektarius u emërua drejtor i Seminarit Rizarios në Athinë më 8 mars 1894.

Meqë ishte njeri i qetë, Shën Nektariusi nuk u kujdes për zhurmën dhe rrëmujën e Athinës.

Për dy muaj, Shën Nektariusi vuajti nga një sëmundje e fshikëzës.

Në shtratin pranë Shën Nektariusit ishte një njeri i paralizuar.

Shën Nektariusi u varros në Manastirin e Shenjtë të Trinitetit në Aegina.

Perëndia i dha lavdi Shën Nektariusit, sepse e gjithë jeta e tij ishte një doksologji e vazhdueshme për Zotërinë. Si gjatë jetës, ashtu edhe pas vdekjes së tij, Shën Nektariusi ka kryer mijëra mrekulli, veçanërisht për ata që vuajnë nga kanceri. Ka më shumë kisha kushtuar Shën Nektariusit sesa çdo shenjtori tjetër modern orthodhoks.
items.text_orig:
Saint Nektarios

The great wonderworker of modern times, was born Anastasius Kephalas in Selebria, Thrace on October 1, 1846.

Since his family was poor, Anastasius went to Constantinople when he was fourteen in order to find work. Although he had no money, he asked the captain of a boat to take him. The captain told him to take a walk and then come back. Anastasius understood, and sadly walked away.

The captain gave the order to start the engines, but nothing happened. After several unsuccessful attempts, he looked up into the eyes of Anastasius who stood on the dock. Taking pity on the boy, the captain told him to come aboard. Immediately, the engines started and the boat began to move.

Anastasius found a job with a tobacco merchant in Constantinople, who did not pay him very much. In his desire to share useful information with others, Anastasius wrote down short maxims from spiritual books on the paper bags and packages of the tobacco shop. The customers would read them out of curiosity, and might perhaps derive some benefit from them.

The boy went about barefoot and in ragged clothing, but he trusted in God. Seeing that the merchant received many letters, Anastasius also wanted to write a letter. To whom could he write? Not to his parents, because there were no mail deliveries to his village. Not to his friends, because he had none. Therefore, he decided to write to Christ to tell Him of his needs.

“My little Christ,” he wrote. “I do not have an apron or shoes. You send them to me. You know how much I love you.”

Anastasius sealed the letter and wrote on the outside: “To the Lord Jesus Christ in Heaven.” On his way to mail the letter, he ran into the man who owned a shop opposite the one in which he worked. The man asked him where he was going, and Anastasius whispered something in reply. Seeing the letter in his hands, the man offered to mail it for him, since he was on his way to the post office.

The merchant put the letter in his pocket and assured Anastasius that he would mail it with his own letters. The boy returned to the tobacco shop, filled with happiness. When he took the letter from his pocket to mail it, the merchant happened to notice the address.

Astonished and curious, the man could not resist opening the letter to read it. Touched by the boy’s simple faith, the merchant placed some money in an envelope and sent it to him anonymously. Anastasius was filled with joy, and he gave thanks to God.

A few days later, seeing Anastasius dressed somewhat better than usual, his employer thought he had stolen money from him and began to beat him. Anastasius cried out, “I have never stolen anything. My little Christ sent me the money.”

Hearing the commotion, the other merchant came and took the tobacco seller aside and explained the situation to him.

When he was still a young man, Anastasius made a pilgrimage to the Holy Land. During the voyage, the ship was in danger of sinking in a storm. Anastasius looked at the raging sea, and then at the captain. He went and stood beside the captain and took the helm, praying for God to save them.

Then he took off the cross his grandmother had given him (containing a piece of the Cross of Christ) and tied it to his belt. Leaning over the side, he dipped the cross into the water three times and commanded the sea, “Silence! Be still.” At once, the wind died down and the sea became calm.

Anastasius was saddened, however, because his cross had fallen into the sea and was lost. As the boat sailed on, sounds of knocking seemed to come from the hull below the water line. When the ship docked, the young man got off and started to walk away.

Suddenly, the captain began shouting, “Kephalas, Kephalas, come back here.” The captain had ordered some men into a small boat to examine the hull in order to discover the source of the knocking, and they discovered the cross stuck to the hull. Anastasius was elated to receive his “Treasure,” and always wore it from that time forward. There is a photograph taken many years later, showing the saint in his monastic skufia. The cross is clearly visible in the photo.

On November 7, 1875, Anastasius received monastic tonsure at the Nea Moni Monastery on Chios, and the new name Lazarus. Two years later, he was ordained a deacon. On that occasion, his name was changed to Nectarius.

Later, when he was a priest, Father Nectarius left Chios and went to Egypt. There he was elected Metropolitan of Pentapolis. Some of his colleagues became jealous of him because of his great virtues, because of his inspiring sermons, and because of everything else which distinguished Saint Nectarius from them.

Other Metropolitans and bishops of the Patriarchate of Alexandria became filled with malice toward the saint, so they told Patriarch Sophronius that Nectarius was plotting to become patriarch himself.

They told the patriarch that the Metropolitan of Pentapolis merely made an outward show of piety in order to win favor with the people. So the patriarch and his synod removed Saint Nectarius from his See. Patriarch Sophronius wrote an ambiguous letter of suspension which provoked scandal and speculation about the true reasons for the saint’s removal from his position.

Saint Nectarius was not deposed from his rank, however. He was still allowed to function as a bishop. If anyone invited him to perform a wedding or a baptism he could do so, as long as he obtained permission from the local bishop.

Saint Nectarius bore his trials with great patience, but those who loved him began to demand to know why he had been removed. Seeing that this was causing a disturbance in the Church of Alexandria, he decided to go to Greece. He arrived in Athens to find that false rumors about him had already reached that city. His letter of suspension said only that he had been removed “for reasons known to the Patriarchate,” and so all the slanders about him were believed.

Since the state and ecclesiastical authorities would not give him a position, the former Metropolitan was left with no means of support, and no place to live. Every day he went to the Minister of Religion asking for assistance. They soon tired of him and began to mistreat him.

One day, as he was leaving the Minister’s office, Saint Nectarius met a friend whom he had known in Egypt. Surprised to find the beloved bishop in such a condition, the man spoke to the Minister of Religion and Education and asked that something be found for him.

So, Saint Nectarius was appointed to be a humble preacher in the diocese of Vitineia and Euboea. The saint did not regard this as humiliating for him, even though a simple monk could have filled that position. He went to Euboea to preach in the churches, eagerly embracing his duties.

Yet even here, the rumors of scandal followed him. Sometimes, while he was preaching, people began to laugh and whisper.

Therefore, the blameless one resigned his position and returned to Athens. By then some people had begun to realize that the rumors were untrue, because they saw nothing in his life or conversation to suggest that he was guilty of anything. With their help and influence, Saint Nectarius was appointed Director of the Rizarios Seminary in Athens on March 8, 1894. He was to remain in that position until December of 1908.

The saint celebrated the services in the seminary church, taught the students, and wrote several edifying and useful books. Since he was a quiet man, Saint Nectarius did not care for the noise and bustle of Athens. He wanted to retire somewhere where he could pray. On the island of Aegina he found an abandoned monastery dedicated to the Holy Trinity, which he began to repair with his own hands.

He gathered a community of nuns, appointing the blind nun Xenia as abbess, while he himself served as Father Confessor. Since he had a gift for spiritual direction, many people came to Aegina to confess to him.

Eventually, the community grew to thirty nuns. He used to tell them, “I am building a lighthouse for you, and God shall put a light in it that will shine forth to the world. Many will see this light and come to Aegina.” They did not understand what he was telling them, that he himself would be that beacon, and that people would come there to venerate his holy relics.

On September 20, 1920 the nun Euphemia brought an old man in black robes, who was obviously in pain, to the Aretaieion Hospital in Athens. This was a state hospital for the poor. The intern asked the nun for information about the patient.

“Is he a monk?” he asked.

“No, he is a bishop.”

The intern laughed and said, “Stop joking and tell me his name, Mother, so that I can enter it in the register.”

“He is indeed a bishop, my child. He is the Most Reverend Metropolitan of Pentapolis.”

The intern muttered, “For the first time in my life I see a bishop without a panagia or cross, and more significantly, without money.”

Then the nun showed the saint’s credentials to the astonished intern who then admitted him. For two months Saint Nectarius suffered from a disease of the bladder. At ten thirty on the evening of November 8, 1920, he surrendered his holy soul to God. He died in peace at the age of seventy-four.

In the bed next to Saint Nectarius was a man who was paralyzed. As soon as the saint had breathed his last, the nurse and the nun who sat with him began to dress him in clean clothing to prepare him for burial at Aegina. They removed his sweater and placed it on the paralyzed man’s bed. Immediately, the paralytic got up from his bed, glorifying God.

Saint Nectarius was buried at the Holy Trinity Monastery on Aegina. Several years later, his grave was opened to remove his bones (as is the custom in Greece). His body was found whole and incorrupt, as if he had been buried that very day.

Word was sent to the Archbishop of Athens, who came to see the relics for himself. Archbishop Chrysostomos told the nuns to leave them out in the sun for a few days, then to rebury them so that they would decay. A month or two after this, they opened the grave again and found the saint incorrupt. Then the relics were placed in a marble sarcophagus.

Several years later, the holy relics dissolved, leaving only the bones. The saint’s head was placed in a bishop’s mitre, and the top was opened to allow people to kiss his head.

Saint Nectarius was glorified by God, since his whole life was a continuous doxology to the Lord. Both during his life and after his death, Saint Nectarius has performed thousands of miracles, especially for those suffering from cancer. There are more churches dedicated to Saint Nectarius than to any other modern Orthodox saint.

Troparion — Tone 1

O faithful, let us honor Nectarius the divine servant of Christ, / offspring of Silyvria and guardian of Aegina, / who appeared in these last times as a true friend of virtue, / pouring forth all manner of healing upon those who reverently cry: / Glory to Him who gave you strength! / Glory to Him who granted you a crown! / Glory to Him who through you grants healing to all!

Martyrs Claudius, Castor, Sempronian, Nicostrat and Semplicius, their apprentice

They were martyred during the reign of Diocletian (284-305). They were very good sculptors in the city of Smirnum.

The emperor to pride in their skill. In the meantime, they converted their apprentice, Semplicius.

The other 600 workers were pagan and full of envy. When the martyrs refused to sculpt the face of pagan idol Asclepios, believed to have healing powers, the emperor gave them into Lampadius’s hands, a judge who had to make them renounce their faith.

While they were tormented in front of him, Lampadius fell dead from his judging seat, “as is tricken by a bad spirit”. His relatives believed the five Christias were to be blamed, also the emperor, although reluctantly, decided to sacrifice them in order to avoid a mutiny.

He had them closed in lead coffins and thrown into the wateres of Saba river, an affluent of Danube.

Holy Martyrs

items.text_orig:
Patriarch Theophilos III of Jerusalem visited the families of the victims of the terrorist attack on the Greek Orthodox Church of Saint George in the Hammoud area of Karak, Jordan, accompanied by clergy of the Patriarchate of Jerusalem.

The Patriarch expressed his condolences and deep sympathy to the victims’ relatives, assuring them that the Patriarchate of Jerusalem would continue to stand by their side.

During the visit, Patriarch Theophilos offered words of comfort and hope, emphasizing that faith in the Risen Christ is a source of strength in the face of suffering and loss.

He stressed that prayers would continue to be offered at the Holy Sepulchre and in churches everywhere for the repose of the souls of the victims and the consolation of their families.

The Patriarch also emphasized that members of the Church form one family, united by faith and love, which no trials or hardships can divide.

Patriarch Theophilos further underlined that the memory of the victims would remain alive in the consciousness of the Church, noting that belief in the Resurrection and eternal life forms the foundation of Christian hope.

Concluding his visit, the Patriarch prayed that God would grant comfort, strength, and patience to the families of the victims and protect Jordan and its people from all evil.

items.sum:
Parashikimi mbushi Katedralen metropolitane të Shën Gjonit, Theologisë në Tenafli, Nju Xhersi, ndërsa qindra veta mblidheshin për kurorëzimin e Athenagorës metropolitane të Nju Xhersit, duke shënuar fillimin e shërbimit të tij si udhëheqës shpirtëror të besimtarëve orthodhoksë grekë në Metropolisin e Nju Xhersit.

Pas një përshëndetjeje entuziaste në katedralen e saj, hapat përpara nga udhëheqësit, fëmijët dhe anëtarët e këshillit të famullive të komunitetit, Atthegora metropolitane u shoqërua në katedrale nga kryepeshkopi Elpidophos i Amerikës dhe metropoliti Cleopas i Suedisë dhe të gjithë Skandinavisë, Përfaqësuesi Patriarkal për Patriarkun Ekumenik Bartolomeu.

Kryepeshkopi Elpidofos i dha zemër Athenagorës metropolitane që të ndante talentet e tij me anë të dashurisë dhe dhembshurisë së madhe, duke i kujtuar atij se vetë besimtarët përbëjnë Trupin e Krishtit të besuar në kujdesin e tij baritore.

Ata do të të mbështetin dhe do të të inkurajojnë, prandaj mbështetu tek ata dhe lejo që dashuria e tyre të të mbajë e të të ushqejë, tha kryepeshkopi.

Duke paraqitur Athenagorën metropolitane me personelin e tij baritore, kryepeshkopi Elpidophos ofroi një akuzë përfundimtare:

Gjithashtu, Metropoliti Kleopa i vuri theks të veçantë ruajtjes së unitetit, duke u lutur që shërbimi i ri metropolitan do të siguronte se çdo person, pavarësisht nga prejardhja ose rrethanat, mund të ndihet i mirëpritur brenda përqafimit të Kishës.

Në fjalimin e tij të kurorëzimit, Athenagora, metropolitane, u dha mirënjohje nga zemra të gjithë atyre që e kanë shoqëruar me lutjet, udhëheqjen dhe dashurinë e tyre gjatë gjithë jetës dhe shërbimit.

Ai foli ngrohtësisht për miqësinë e tij të gjatë me kryepeshkopin Elpidophros, duke kujtuar se ata u takuan për herë të parë kur metropolitan Athenagora ishte 12 vjeç dhe kryepeshkopi i ardhshëm ishte 15 vjeç.

Në atë kohë ishim vëllezër dhe tani jemi vëllezër, tha Athenagora metropolitane.

Kam arritur të të njoh, të të dëgjoj dhe të të dua.
items.text_orig:
Anticipation filled the Metropolitan Cathedral of St. John the Theologian in Tenafly, New Jersey as hundreds gathered for the enthronement of Metropolitan Athenagoras of New Jersey, marking the beginning of his ministry as spiritual leader of the Greek Orthodox faithful in the Metropolis of New Jersey.

The Metropolis encompasses 55 parishes throughout New Jersey, eastern Pennsylvania, Delaware, Maryland and Virginia.

After an enthusiastic greeting on the cathedral’s front steps from the community’s leaders, children, and parish council members, Metropolitan Athenagoras was escorted into the cathedral by Archbishop Elpidophoros of America and Metropolitan Cleopas of Sweden and All Scandinavia, Patriarchal Representative for Ecumenical Patriarch Bartholomew. Clergy and faithful jubilantly proclaimed “Axios!” as the new Metropolitan ascended to the episcopal throne.

The cathedral was filled to standing-room-only with hierarchs, dignitaries, ecumenical leaders, clergy, and faithful from across the country and Metropolis. Metropolitan Athenagoras’s mother, Fotini; brother, Yiannis; and other family members were seated in the front row for the emotional service. Also attending were Her Excellency Iphigenia Kanara, Consul General of the Hellenic Republic; Kyriakos Pogiatzis, Consul General of Cyprus; and Edward LaPorte, Deputy Chief of Staff Office of the Secretary of State of New Jersey. A number of ecumenical leaders also attended, including Archbishop El-Kassis, Permanent Observer of the Holy See to the United Nations.

Following the ascent to the throne, the doxology was sung by chanters from the Metropolis, followed by the reading of the Patriarchal and Synodical Letter of the Announcement of Election of Metropolitan Athenagoras by Archdeacon Dionysios Papiris.

In his moving Archpastoral Exhortation, Archbishop Elpidophoros spoke of the two hierarchs’ decades-long friendship and their remarkable journeys to the United States. Calling upon the new Metropolitan to place his gifts entirely at the service of his flock, the Archbishop said:

“Your life as the Shepherd of this Holy Metropolis of New Jersey, will be one of giving and sharing, and indeed of sacrificing yourself, as our Lord sacrificed Himself for the life of the world. Therefore, my Beloved Brother, Metropolitan Athenagoras: Δωρεὰν ἐλάβετε, δωρεὰν δότε. Freely you have received, freely give. Share your marvelous talents with all through abundant love and compassion. And whatever sacrifice you are called to, make it with love, and thereby you will glorify the God of love … the God Who is love.”

Archbishop Elpidophoros encouraged Metropolitan Athenagoras to share his talents through “abundant love and compassion,” reminding him that the faithful themselves constitute the Body of Christ entrusted to his pastoral care.

“They will support you and encourage you, so lean on them and allow their love to sustain and nurture you,” the Archbishop said.

Presenting Metropolitan Athenagoras with his pastoral staff, Archbishop Elpidophoros offered a final charge:

“Receive this Staff of God’s Powerful Love, this Ράβδων Δυνάμεως, a symbol of how you will guide your People to spiritual pastures that are fertile with virtue and peaceful, and which flow with springs of love and mercy. May you ever be worthy of it! ΑΞΙΟΣ!”

Metropolitan Cleopas, serving as Patriarchal Representative, spoke of the many responsibilities entrusted to a bishop, emphasizing unity, youth ministry, pastoral presence and the importance of responding wisely to the challenges of contemporary life. His remarks underscored that the episcopacy is a ministry of “love, responsibility, and service,” calling the bishop to strengthen the weak, seek those who have grown distant and lead the faithful toward unity.

He encouraged Metropolitan Athenagoras to give particular attention to young people “seeking meaning and direction” and also addressed the growing influence of artificial intelligence and new technologies.

Technology, Metropolitan Cleopas said, can serve as “a useful means of communication and service,” but it must always serve the human person and the community “without replacing personal presence and genuine human encounter.”

Metropolitan Cleopas also placed particular emphasis on the preservation of unity, praying that the new Metropolitan’s ministry would ensure that “every person, regardless of background or circumstance, may feel welcomed within the embrace of the Church.” In a personal reflection, he spoke of Metropolitan Athenagoras’s “radiant smile,” encouraging him to continue meeting people with kindness, patience and warmth in a world where many are weary and troubled.

In his enthronement address, Metropolitan Athenagoras offered heartfelt gratitude to all those who have accompanied him with their prayers, guidance and love throughout his life and ministry.

He spoke warmly of his lifelong friendship with Archbishop Elpidophoros, recalling that they first met when Metropolitan Athenagoras was 12 and the future Archbishop was 15.

“We were brothers then, and we are brothers now,” Metropolitan Athenagoras said.

He also paid tribute to his family, remembering his father, Demetrios, of blessed memory, and thanking his mother, Fotini, his brother Yiannis and his family for the encouragement and guidance that helped prepare him for the responsibility he now assumes.

Acknowledging those who shepherded the Metropolis before him, Metropolitan Athenagoras pledged to honor and strengthen the foundation entrusted to him. “I stand on the foundation others have laid. My calling is to guard what I have received, and to build on it with love,” he said.

Turning directly to the clergy and faithful, Metropolitan Athenagoras pledged a ministry rooted in listening, presence and personal encounter.

“Now I extend my hand to you, my beloved faithful of the Holy Metropolis of New Jersey. I come to know you, to listen to you, and to love you. I want to meet you exactly where you are. In our churches and parish halls, in our classrooms and homes, in days of celebration and days of struggle, I want to hear your stories, share your worries, and rejoice in what you have done. I long for us to be a true spiritual family, bound together by His love.”

Metropolitan Athenagoras also announced the establishment of the Ecumenical Patriarch Bartholomew Scholarship, created in honor of Tërëshenjtëria e Tij as the Church celebrates the 35th anniversary of his election and elevation to the Ecumenical Throne.

Metropolitan Athenagoras described the scholarship as a unified commitment to the educational future of young people through two paths: priestly vocation and higher education. The fund currently stands at $500,000.

In a poignant conclusion, the new Metropolitan offered his vision for the future of the Metropolis and, above all, asked the faithful to accompany him with their prayers.

“This is my prayer for our Holy Metropolis: a Church whose heartbeat is prayer, that serves with sleeves rolled up, and welcomes every person with the love of Christ!”

“And I humbly ask for your prayers as I take my first steps as your Metropolitan,” he continued. “Pray that God will give me wisdom when I must decide, courage when I must lead, humility when I must listen, and tenderness when someone is hurting. Above all, pray that I never forget whom I serve, and whose Church this is.”

“May we begin this journey together, with open hearts, growing faith, and the joy of the risen Christ. Σας αγαπώ!”

Photos by Orthodox Observer/Dimitrios Panagos & Brittainy Newman
