items.title_orig: †) Synaxis of the Archangel Michael and the other Bodiless Powers
items.sum:
◯ Sinaksi i Kryeengjëllit Mikael dhe pushteteve të tjera pa vlerë

Sinaksi i shefit të mikpritësve qiellorë, kryeengjëlli Mikael dhe Fuqitë e tjera qiellore të Bodisë: Kryeengjëjit Gabriel, Rafael, Uriel, Selafiel, Jehudiel, Baraçiel dhe Jeremiel u themeluan në fillim të shekullit të katërt në Këshillin e Laodicesë, i cili u takua disa vjet përpara Këshillit të Parë Ekumenik.

Ato shkëlqejnë me dritën e njohurisë së Perëndisë dhe me njohurinë për misteret e Perëndisë.

Ata i ndriçojnë njerëzit që të njohin e të kuptojnë vullnetin e Perëndisë, përhapin besimin te Perëndia mes njerëzve, duke ndriçuar mendjet e tyre me dritën e Ungjillit të Shenjtë.

Ata zbulojnë misteret më të vogla të Perëndisë dhe qëllimet e Tij, duke i udhëhequr njerëzit drejt një jete të virtytshme dhe të shenjtë.

Mbi të gjitha nëntë vendet, Zotëria emëroi Kryeengjëllin e Shenjtë Mikael (emri i tij në hebraisht do të thotë, që është si Perëndia), si Kryekomandantin besnik të Perëndisë.

Nëpërmjet vullnetit të Perëndisë, komandanti Mikael transportoi profetin Habbakuk (2 dhjetor) nga Judea në Babiloni, për t'i dhënë ushqim Danielit në gropën e luanëve (Dan.

Për mëkatet tona, perandori i pafe Agarene Batu gëlltiti dhe vuri flakën e vendit rus dhe arriti në Novgorod, dhe Perëndia dhe Teokosi më i Shenjtë e mbrojtën me një pamje të Mikael Kryeengjëllit, i cili e ndaloi të hynte në të.

Ndërhyrja për qytetet ruse nga Mbretëresha më e Shenjtë e Qiejve përfshinte gjithmonë pamjen e saj me mikpritësit Qiellorë, nën udhëheqjen e Kryeengjëllit Mikael. Mirënjohësi Rus, Nëna më e pastër e Perëndisë dhe Kryeengjëlli Mikael në himnet e kishës.

Në Rus nuk kishte qytet, ku nuk kishte kishë apo kishë kushtuar kryeengjëllit Mikael.

Ai njofton misteret e Perëndisë.

Ai i lutet Perëndisë për njerëzit.

Dhe (ky është) një kumtim prej mëshirës së All-llahut, i cili ka mëshirë për njerëzit.

Jeremiel: ngritja e Perëndisë (3 Ezdras 4:36)
items.text_orig:
†) Synaxis of the Archangel Michael and the other Bodiless Powers

The Synaxis of the Chief of the Heavenly Hosts, Archangel Michael and the Other Heavenly Bodiless Powers: Archangels Gabriel, Raphael, Uriel, Selaphiel, Jehudiel, Barachiel, and Jeremiel was established at the beginning of the fourth century at the Council of Laodicea, which met several years before the First Ecumenical Council.

The 35th Canon of the Council of Laodicea condemned and denounced as heretical the worship of angels as gods and rulers of the world, but affirmed their proper veneration.

Feastday was established in November, the ninth month after March (with which the year began in ancient times) since there are Nine Ranks of Angels. The eighth day of the month was chosen for the Synaxis of all the Bodiless Powers of Heaven since the Day of the Dread Last Judgment is called the Eighth Day by the holy Fathers. After the end of this age (characterized by its seven days of Creation) will come the Eighth Day, and then “the Son of Man shall come in His Glory and all the holy Angels with Him” (Mt. 25:31).

The Angelic Ranks are divided into three Hierarchies: highest, middle, and lowest.

The Highest Hierarchy includes: the Seraphim, Cherubim and Thrones.

The six-winged SERAPHIM (Flaming, Fiery) (Is 6:12) stand closest of all to the Most Holy Trinity. They blaze with love for God and kindle such love in others.

The many-eyed CHERUBIM (outpouring of wisdom, enlightenment) (Gen 3:24) stand before the Lord after the Seraphim. They are radiant with the light of knowledge of God, and knowledge of the mysteries of God. Through them wisdom is poured forth, and people’s minds are enlightened so they may know God and behold His glory.

The THRONES (Col 1:16) stand after the Cherubim, mysteriously and incomprehensibly bearing God through the grace given them for their service. They are ministers of God’s justice, giving to tribunals, kings, etc. the capacity for righteous judgment.

The Middle Angelic Hierarchy consists of three Ranks: Dominions, Powers, and Authorities:

DOMINIONS (Col 1:16) hold dominion over the angels subject to them. They instruct the earthly authorities, established by God, to rule wisely, and to govern their lands well. The Dominions teach us to subdue sinful impulses, to subject the flesh to the spirit, to master our will, and to conquer temptation.

POWERS (1 Pet 3:22) fulfill the will of God without hesitation. They work great miracles and give the grace of wonderworking and clairvoyance to saints pleasing to God. The Powers assist people in fulfilling obediences. They also encourage them to be patient, and give them spiritual strength and fortitude.

AUTHORITIES (1 Pet 3:22, Col 1:16) have authority over the devil. They protect people from demonic temptations, and prevent demons from harming people as they would wish. They also uphold ascetics and guard them, helping people in the struggle with evil thoughts.

The Lowest Hierarchy includes the three Ranks: Principalities, Archangels, and Angels:

PRINIPALITIES (Col 1:16) have command over the lower angels, instructing them in the fulfilling of God’s commands. They watch over the world and protect lands, nations and peoples. Principalities instruct people to render proper honor to those in authority, as befits their station. They teach those in authority to use their position, not for personal glory and gain, but to honor God, and to spread word of Him, for the benefit of those under them.

ARCHANGELS (1 Thess 4:16) are messengers of great and wondrous tidings. They reveal prophecies and the mysteries of the faith. They enlighten people to know and understand the will of God, they spread faith in God among the people, illuminating their minds with the light of the Holy Gospel.

ANGELS (1 Pet 3:22) are in the lowest rank of the heavenly hierarchy, and closest to people. They reveal the lesser mysteries of God and His intentions, guiding people to virtuous and holy life. They support those who remain steadfast, and they raise up the fallen. They never abandon us and they are always prepared to help us, if we desire it.

All the Ranks of the Heavenly Powers are called angels, although each has its own name and position by virtue of their service. The Lord reveals His will to the highest ranks of the angels, and they in turn inform the others.

Over all the Nine Ranks, the Lord appointed the Holy Archangel Michael (his name in Hebrew means “who is like unto God”), the faithful servitor of God, as Chief Commander. He cast down from Heaven the arrogantly proud Lucifer and the other fallen spirits when they rebelled against God. Michael summoned the ranks of angels and cried out, “Let us attend! Let us stand aright before our Creator and do not consider doing what is displeasing unto God!”

According to Church Tradition, and in the church services to the Archangel Michael, he participated in many other Old Testament events.

During the Exodus of the Israelites from Egypt he went before them in the form of a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night. Through him the power of the Lord was made manifest, annihilating the Egyptians and Pharaoh who were in pursuit of the Israelites. The Archangel Michael defended Israel in all its misfortunes.

He appeared to Joshua Son of Navi and revealed the will of the Lord at the taking of Jericho (Josh 5:13-16). The power of the great Chief Commander of God was manifest in the annihilation of the 185 thousand soldiers of the Assyrian emperor Sennacherib (4/2 Kings 19:35); also in the smiting of the impious leader Heliodorus (2 Macc. 3: 24-26); and in the protection of the Three Holy Youths: Ananias, Azarias and Misail, thrown into the fiery furnace for their refusal to worship an idol (Dan 3:22-25).

Through the will of God, the Chief Commander Michael transported the Prophet Habbakuk (December 2) from Judea to Babylon, to give food to Daniel in the lions’ den (Dan. 14:33-37).

The Archangel Michael disputed with the devil over the body of the holy Prophet Moses (Jude 1:9).

The holy Archangel Michael showed his power when he miraculously saved a young man, cast into the sea by robbers with a stone about his neck on the shores of Mt Athos. This story is found in the Athonite Paterikon, and in the Life of Saint Neophytus of Docheiariou (November 9).

From ancient times the Archangel Michael was famed for his miracles in Rus. In the Volokolamsk Paterikon is a narrative of Saint Paphnutius of Borov with an account of Tatar tax-gatherers concerning the miraculous saving of Novgorod the Great: “Therefore Great Novgorod was never taken by the Hagarenes… when… for our sins the godless Hagarene emperor Batu devoured and set the Russian land aflame and came to Novgorod, and God and the Most Holy Theotokos shielded it with an appearance of Michael the Archangel, who forbade him to enter into it. He [Batu] was come to the Lithuanian city and came toward Kiev and saw the stone church, over the doors of which the great Archangel Michael had written and spoken to the prince his allotted fate, ‘By this we have forbidden you entry into Great Novgorod’.”

Intercession for Russian cities by the Most Holy Queen of Heaven always involved Her appearances with the Heavenly Hosts, under the leadership of the Archangel Michael. Grateful Rus acclaimed the Most Pure Mother of God and the Archangel Michael in church hymns. Many monasteries, cathedrals, court and merchant churches are dedicated to the Chief Commander Michael.

In old Kiev at the time of the accepting of Christianity, a cathedral of the Archangel was built, and a monastery also was named for him. Archangel cathedrals are found at Smolensk, Nizhni Novgorod, Staritsa, at Great Ustiug (beginning of the thirteenth century), and a cathedral at Sviyazhsk. In Rus there was not a city, where there was not a church or chapel dedicated to the Archangel Michael.

One of the chief temples of the city of Moscow, the burial church in the Kremlin, is dedicated to him. Numerous and beautiful icons of the Chief Commander of the Heavenly Hosts are also in his Cathedral. One of these, the Icon “Blessed Soldiery,” was painted in the Dormition Cathedral of the Moscow Kremlin. The saintly soldiers, Russian princes, are depicted under the leadership of the Archangel Michael.

We invoke Saint Michael for protection from invasion by enemies and from civil war, and for the defeat of adversaries on the field of battle. He conquers all spiritual enemies.

Holy Scripture and Tradition give us the names of the Archangels:

Gabriel: strength (power) of God, herald and servitor of Divine omnipotence (Dan 8:16, Luke 1:26). He announces the mysteries of God.

Raphael: the healing of God, the curer of human infirmities (Tobit 3:16, 12:15)

Uriel: the fire or light of God, enlightener (3 Ezdras 5:20). We pray for him to enlighten those with darkened minds.

Selaphiel: the prayer of God, impelling to prayer (3 Ezdras 5:16). He prays to God for mankind.

Jehudiel: the glorifying of God, encouraging exertion for the glory of the Lord and interceding for the reward of efforts.

Barachiel: distributor of the blessings of God for good deeds, entreats the mercy of God for people.

Jeremiel: the raising up to God (3 Ezdras 4:36)

On icons the Archangels are depicted in according to the character of their service:

Michael tramples the devil underfoot, and in his left hand holds a green date-tree branch, and in his right hand a spear with a white banner (or sometimes a fiery sword), on which is outlined a scarlet cross.

Gabriel with a branch from Paradise, presented by him to the Most Holy Virgin, or with a shining lantern in his right hand and with a mirror made of jasper in his left.

Raphael holds a vessel with healing medications in his left hand, and with his right hand leads Tobias, carrying a fish for healing (Tobit 5-8).

Uriel in his raised right hand holds a naked sword at the level of his chest, and in his lowered left hand “a fiery flame.”

Selaphiel in a prayerful posture, gazing downwards, hands folded on the chest.

Jehudiel holds a golden crown in his right hand, in his left, a whip of three red (or black) thongs.

Barachiel is shown with a white rose on his breast.

Jeremiel holds balance-scales in his hand.

Each person has a guardian angel, and every nation also receives its own guardian angel from God (Dan. 10:13). When a church is consecrated, it also receives a guardian angel (Palladius, Dial. Ch. 10).

Troparion — Tone 4

Commanders of the heavenly hosts, / we who are unworthy beseech you, / by your prayers encompass us beneath the wings of your immaterial glory, / and faithfully preserve us who fall down and cry to you: / “Deliver us from all harm, for you are the commanders of the powers on high!”

Tr by oca.org

items.title_orig: Patriarch Daniel of Bulgaria honored Patriarch Maxim 14 years after his repose
items.sum:
Patriarku Daniel i Bullgarisë kryesoi një përkujtimor të Liturgjisë Hyjnore dhe Panikidës në manastirin Trojan më 6 nëntor 2026, duke shënuar 14 vjetorin e pushimit të patriarkut Maksim të Bullgarisë, i cili vdiq më 2012.

Duke folur me gazetarët, patriarku Daniel i bëri nderime paraardhësit të tij të cilit i kushtohej për gjithë jetën kishës orthodhokse bullgare.

Patriarku përherë i fuqishëm bullgar Maksim ishte një njeri i Zotit.

Duke u njohur me patriarkun Daniel, ishin Metropoliti Xhon i Varnës dhe Veliki Prelav, metropolitani i Nevrokopit, metropoliti Pakomi i Vidinit, peshkopi Gerasim i Melnikut, Kryesekretari i Sinodit të Shenjtë, peshkopi Vasil i Dragovitisë, Aboti i manastirit të Trojës, Peshkopi Mikael i Konstancës, Vitar i metropolit të Loveçit dhe peshkopi Xhon i Branitsës, i Parë i metropolitanit të Sofjes, së bashku me klerin tjetër.

Peshkopi Vasil theksoi patriarkun Maksimios lidhje të ngushta me manastirin Trojan, të cilin vetë patriarku i vdekur e kishte përshkruar si racisti i fatit të tij kishtar dhe shpirtëror.

Ai e përshkroi patriarkun Maksimios legjitimitetin dhe autoritetin personal si një spirancë të patundur për kishën orthodhokse bullgare gjatë atyre viteve të vështira.

Duke përfunduar fjalimin e tij, peshkopi Vasil kujtoi patriarkun Maksimis që ai nuk kishte komprometuar kurrë besimin e tij dhe angazhimin e tij të përjetshëm për të ruajtur unitetin e Kishës Orthodhokse Bullgare.
items.text_orig:
Patriarch Daniel of Bulgaria presided over a memorial Divine Liturgy and Panikhida at Troyan Monastery on November 6, 2026, marking the 14th anniversary of the repose of Patriarch Maxim of Bulgaria, who passed away in 2012.

Speaking to journalists, Patriarch Daniel paid tribute to his predecessor’s lifelong dedication to the Bulgarian Orthodox Church.

“The ever-memorable Bulgarian Patriarch Maxim was a man of God. Of his 98 years, he devoted 86 to the Church,” Patriarch Daniel said.

He emphasized that Patriarch Maxim served the Church through three distinct historical periods: the monarchy, militant atheism under communism, and democracy. Despite political upheavals and social challenges, he remained steadfast in his faith and devotion to God.

Concelebrating with Patriarch Daniel were Metropolitan John of Varna and Veliki Preslav, Metropolitan Seraphim of Nevrokop, Metropolitan Pachomius of Vidin, Bishop Gerasim of Melnik, Chief Secretary of the Holy Synod, Bishop Vasil of Dragovitia, Abbot of Troyan Monastery, Bishop Michael of Constantia, Vicar of the Metropolitan of Lovech, and Bishop John of Branitsa, First Vicar of the Metropolitan of Sofia, together with other clergy.

Patriarch Daniel provides update on Metropolitan Gabriel’s health

Before the Divine Liturgy, Patriarch Daniel also addressed the health condition of Metropolitan Gabriel of Lovech, who had been admitted to the Military Medical Academy in Sofia with acute pancreatitis.

“He has been admitted to the Military Medical Academy with acute pancreatic inflammation. He is currently intubated, but since yesterday there has been some improvement in his condition,” Patriarch Daniel stated.

The Patriarch called on Orthodox Christians to pray for the Metropolitan’s recovery.

“Let all Orthodox Christians offer fervent prayers to God. Metropolitan Gabriel is a worthy hierarch. May God prolong his days, grant him health, and allow him to continue serving in health and dignity,” he said.

Remembering Patriarch Maxim’s Legacy

Following the memorial Divine Liturgy, a Panikhida was celebrated, during which Bishop Vasil of Dragovitia delivered an address commemorating Patriarch Maxim’s life and ministry.

He recalled that on the morning of November 6, 2012, the Bulgarian people received the sorrowful news of the death of their spiritual leader.

Bishop Vasil highlighted Patriarch Maxim’s close connection with Troyan Monastery, which the late Patriarch himself had described as the “cradle of his ecclesiastical and spiritual destiny.”

He also recalled important milestones in Patriarch Maxim’s ecclesiastical career, including his ordination as a hieromonk in 1944, elevation to archimandrite in 1947, appointment as head of the Bulgarian Church representation in Moscow in 1950, and subsequent appointment as Chief Secretary of the Holy Synod in 1955.

On December 30, 1956, he was consecrated Bishop of Branitsa at the Patriarchal Cathedral of Saint Alexander Nevsky in Sofia.

Particular emphasis was placed on Patriarch Maxim’s role in overcoming the schism that divided the Bulgarian Orthodox Church during the post-communist period.

Bishop Vasil recalled that Patriarch Maxim faced personal attacks and political accusations during the crisis but refused to respond with hostility.

“Despite all this, he did not respond to the slander, did not utter a single bad word against anyone, and preserved both his own dignity and that of the Church,” the Bishop said.

He described Patriarch Maxim’s canonical legitimacy and personal authority as an unwavering anchor for the Bulgarian Orthodox Church during those difficult years.

Concluding his address, Bishop Vasil recalled Patriarch Maxim’s insistence that he had never compromised his faith and his lifelong commitment to preserving the unity of the Bulgarian Orthodox Church.

Source, photos and video: Patriarchate of Bulgaria / Angel Karadakov

items.text_orig:
Dimitris Koutsoumbas, General Secretary of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of Greece (KKE), visited the Ionian Center of the Holy Metropolis of Nea Ionia, Philadelphia, Heraklion, and Chalcedon on Saturday, November 7, 2026, where he was warmly welcomed by Metropolitan Gabriel.

During the reception, Metropolitan Gabriel greeted Koutsoumbas with the words, “We welcome our good neighbor,” referring to the Ionian Center’s proximity to the headquarters of the KKE Central Committee in Perissos, Nea Ionia.

Metropolitan Gabriel then guided the KKE leader through the Center’s facilities, presenting the vision behind the project, its architectural design, organizational structure, and the various opportunities offered by its modern infrastructure.

Particular attention was given to the newly constructed Church of Saint George of Neapolis, patron saint of the Holy Metropolis, where his incorrupt holy relics are now enshrined.

The tour also included the Center for Culture and Youth, the modern amphitheater, the library, and the Center’s educational and social facilities.

Metropolitan Gabriel explained the multifaceted mission of the Ionian Center, describing it as a modern landmark for the wider region that combines spiritual development, education, and social outreach.

He emphasized that the Center is open and accessible to everyone, serving society as a whole, with particular attention to supporting young people and families.

The Metropolitan also highlighted the Center’s commitment to preserving historical memory and promoting the cultural heritage of Asia Minor Hellenism.

During their meeting, Metropolitan Gabriel and Koutsoumbas exchanged views on issues of social and cultural interest.

Their discussions focused particularly on the importance of preserving historical memory and supporting initiatives that promote education, culture, and social solidarity.

items.title_orig: Holy 33 Martyrs of Melitene; St. Lazarus the Wonderworker of Mt. Galesion near Ephesus
items.sum:
Të shenjtë 33 martirë të Melitenës

Në qytetin e Tianas, në Kapadokinë e madhe, lindi martiri i shenjtë Hieron.

Mes atyre që ishin të shtyrë në shërbim, Lisia urdhëroi, gjithashtu, që njerëzit e tij të rekrutonin Hieronin, i cili dallohej nga forca e tij e madhe fizike dhe nga deksteriteti.

Me këshillën e Siriakut, një nga miqtë e Hieronës, Lisia ngriti rrethimin e shpellës dhe u tërhoq nga grupi i tij.

Hieroni dhe tridhjetë e dy ushtarë të tjerë refuzuan ta bënin këtë dhe e pranuan hapur besimin e tyre në Krishtin.

Kur persekutimet më në fund pushuan, ai ndërtoi një kishë në vendin ku ekzekutonin martirët e shenjtë dhe vendosi në të kokën e gërryeshme.

Tridhjetë e tre martirët e tu të shenjtë, o Zot, për shkak të vuajtjeve të tyre kanë marrë kurora të pakorruptueshme nga ti, Perëndia ynë.

Saint Lazari, çudibërësi i Malit Galesius, afër Efesit

Një i ri i arsimuar që e donte Perëndinë, Lazari u bë murg në manastirin e Shën Savës, themeluesit të devotshmërisë së madhe asketike në Palestinë.

I drejtuar nga priftëria e shenjtë nga Patriarku i Jerusalemit, Shën Lazari u kthye në vendin e tij dhe u vendos pranë Efesit, në malin e shkretuar Galesius.

Në vendin ku shenjtori pa këtë vizion, ai ndërtoi një kishë në nder të ringjalljes së Krishtit dhe mori mbi vete veprimin e shtyllave.

Nëpërmjet lutjeve lotsjellëse të të gjithë murgjve, Zoti e zgjati jetën tokësore të Shën Lazarit për 15 vjet të tjerë.

Shën Lazari vdiq në moshën 72 - vjeçare, në vitin 1053. Vëllezërit varrosën trupin e të shenjtit në shtyllën mbi të cilën kishte luftuar në asketizëm.

Shën Lazari përkujtohet gjithashtu më 17 korrik.
items.text_orig:
Holy 33 Martyrs of Melitene

Holy martyr Hieron was born in the city of Tiana in great Cappadocia. Raised by a pious mother, he was a kindly and good Christian.

The co-ruling emperors Diocletian (284-305) and Maximian (284-305) sent a large military detachment headed by Lysias to Cappadocia to eradicate Christianity there, and also to conscript healthy and strong men into the imperial army.

Among those pressed into service, Lysias also ordered his men to draft Hieron, who was distinguished by his great physical strength and dexterity. But Hieron refused to serve emperors who persecuted Christians.

When they attempted to seize him by force and bring him to Lysias, he took a stick and started beating the soldiers who had been sent to bring him. The soldiers scattered, ashamed of being defeated by a single man. Hieron then hid in a cave with eighteen other Christians. Lysias would not risk losing his soldiers by storming the cave.

Upon the advice of Cyriacus, one of Hieron’s friends, Lysias lifted the siege of the cave and withdrew his detachment. Then Cyriacus persuaded Hieron not to offer resistance to the authorities. He and the other new conscripts and accompanying soldiers were sent to the nearby city of Melitene.

Soon Hieron had a vision in his sleep, in which his impending martyrdom was foretold. Lysias told the soldiers gathered at Melitene to offer sacrifice to the pagan gods. Hieron and another thirty-two soldiers refused to do this, and openly confessed their faith in Christ. Then the persecutor gave orders to beat the martyrs and to cut off Hieron’s arm at the elbow. After cruel tortures, they threw the martyrs into prison barely alive, and they beheaded them four days later.

A certain rich and illustrious Christian by the name of Chrysanthus ransomed Hieron’s head from Lysias. When the persecutions finally ceased, he built a church on the place where they executed the holy martyrs, and he placed the venerable head in it. The bodies of all the executed saints were secretly buried by Christians. In the reign of the emperor Justinian, during the construction of the church of Hagia Eirene (Holy Peace), the venerable relics were uncovered and found incorrupt.

The other martyrs are: Hesychius, Nicander, Athanasius, Mamas, Barachius, Callinicus, Theogenes, Nikon, Longinus, Theodore, Valerius, Xanthius, Theodoulus, Callimachus, Eugene, Theodochus, Ostrychius, Epiphanius, Maximian, Ducitius, Claudian, Theophilus, Gigantius, Dorotheus, Theodotus, Castrichius, Anicletus, Themelius, Eutychius, Hilarion, Diodotus and Amonitus.

Troparion — Tone 4

Your thirty-three holy martyrs, O Lord, / through their sufferings have received incorruptible crowns from You, our God. / For having Your strength, they laid low their adversaries, / and shattered the powerless boldness of demons. / Through their intercessions, save our souls!

Saint Lazarus the Wonderworker of Mt Galesius near Ephesus

He was born in Lydia, in the city of Magnesium. An educated young man who loved God, Lazarus became a monk at the monastery of Saint Sava, the founder of great ascetic piety in Palestine. He spent ten years within the walls of the monastery, winning the love and respect of the brethren for his intense monastic struggles.

Ordained to the holy priesthood by the Patriarch of Jerusalem, Saint Lazarus returned to his native country and settled near Ephesus, on desolate Mount Galesius. Here he saw a wondrous vision: a fiery pillar, rising up to the heavens, was encircled by angels singing, “Let God arise and let His enemies be scattered.”

On the place where the saint beheld this vision, he built a church in honor of the Resurrection of Christ and took upon himself the feat of pillar-dwelling. Monks soon began to flock to the great ascetic, thirsting for spiritual nourishment by the divinely-inspired words and blessed example of the saint, and a monastery was established there.

Having received a revelation about the day of his death, the saint told the brethren. Through the tearful prayers of all the monks, the Lord prolonged the earthly life of Saint Lazarus for another fifteen years.

Saint Lazarus died at 72 years of age, in the year 1053. The brethren buried the body of the saint at the pillar upon which he had struggled in asceticism. He was glorified by many miracles after his death.

Saint Lazarus is also commemorated on July 17.

Troparion — Tone 8

You watered your pillar with prayerful vigils and flowing tears; / you brought forth fruit a hundredfold with sighs from the depths of your soul. / You were a shepherd, granting the requests of all. / Entreat Christ God, venerable Lazarus our father, that our souls may be saved.

Tr by oca.org

items.title_orig: Patriarch of Jerusalem concludes visit to Moscow
items.sum:
Patriarku Theophilos III i Jerusalemit përfundoi vizitën e tij tre-ditore në Moskë të premten, 6 nëntor 2026, pas një serie takimesh me krerët fetarë e politikë rusë, duke përfshirë presidentin Vladimir Putin dhe patriarkun Kirill të Moskës.

Primate i Kishës Orthodhokse të Jerusalemit mbërriti në kryeqytetin rus më 4 nëntor për një vizitë që përfshinte shërbesa fetare dhe mbledhje zyrtare.

Më 5 nëntor, patriarku Theophilos vizitoi Konvenin Stavror të Pokrovskit në Moskë, ku ai i ra shkurt në një shërbim lutjeje përpara ribashkimit që përmbante relikat e Shën Matronisë së Moskës.
items.text_orig:
Patriarch Theophilos III of Jerusalem concluded his three-day visit to Moscow on Friday, November 6, 2026, following a series of meetings with Russian religious and political leaders, including President Vladimir Putin and Patriarch Kirill of Moscow.

The Primate of the Orthodox Church of Jerusalem arrived in the Russian capital on November 4 for a visit that included religious services and official meetings.

On November 5, Patriarch Theophilos visited the Pokrovsky Stavropegial Convent in Moscow, where he officiated at a prayer service before the reliquary containing the relics of Saint Matrona of Moscow.

Later that day, he met with Patriarch Kirill at the Patriarchal Residence in Chisty Lane, Moscow, for discussions between the Primates of the Russian and Jerusalem Orthodox Churches.

In the evening, the two Patriarchs were received at the Kremlin by Russian President Vladimir Putin.

During the meeting, Putin presented Patriarch Theophilos III with the Order of Friendship of the Russian Federation in recognition of his “significant contribution to strengthening friendship, cooperation, and spiritual ties with Russia.”

The visit concluded on November 6, when Patriarch Theophilos departed from Vnukovo-3 Airport.

He was seen off by Metropolitan Anthony of Volokolamsk, Chairman of the Department for External Church Relations of the Moscow Patriarchate; and other clergy.

Also present at the airport were Hegumen Theophan (Lukyanov), Head of the Department’s Protocol Sector, and Priest Alexander Ershov, Assistant to the Chairman of the Department for External Church Relations.

The visit marked a series of high-level contacts between the Patriarchate of Jerusalem, the Russian Orthodox Church, and the Russian political leadership.

Source: Moscow Patriarchate

items.title: British ambassador meets Metropolitan Antonie to discuss religious freedom and social welfare
items.summary: Metropolitan Antonie of Bessarabia and Her Excellency Fern Horine, the United Kingdom’s Ambassador to the Republic of Moldova, discussed religious freedom and the Church’s social mission on Thursday. The meeting took place at the Metropolis’ headquarters in Chișinău, where the…
items.text:
Metropolitan Antonie of Bessarabia and Her Excellency Fern Horine, the United Kingdom’s Ambassador to the Republic of Moldova, discussed religious freedom and the Church’s social mission on Thursday.

The meeting took place at the Metropolis’ headquarters in Chișinău, where the Metropolitan outlined both the challenges facing Church communities and the projects being developed to support them.

Discussions highlighted the social and charitable work carried out by the Metropolis of Bessarabia through its parishes and the Diaconia Social Mission , which is marking its 25th anniversary, as well as initiatives supporting vulnerable families and developing local social services.

Metropolitan Antonie explained that priests, through their ongoing contact with community members, are often well placed to identify people in need of assistance.

The role of clergy in preventing domestic violence and addiction, in cooperation with partner organisations and institutions, was also emphasised.

The discussions also addressed the importance of freedom of religion, combating disinformation and the Republic of Moldova’s European integration process.

Shared ties and values

Ambassador Fern Horine expressed appreciation for the Church’s contribution and its potential to carry out pastoral and social activities for local communities.

In a Facebook post , representatives of the British Embassy in the Republic of Moldova highlighted the ties between the two countries and their shared values.

“The United Kingdom values dialogue, mutual respect and strong connections across Moldova’s society.”

Metropolitan Antonie thanked Ambassador Fern Horine for her visit and for her interest in the work of the Metropolis of Bessarabia.

Photo credit: Metropolis of Bessarabia

items.sum:
Takimi i parë zyrtar i ndërsjelltë midis ekspertëve rumunë e izraelitë mbi restaurimin e Sketës Rumune në Lumin Jordan u zhvillua të mërkurën në ngritjen e manastirit.

Archimandrit Ioan Meiu, Përfaqësues i Patriarkatit Rumun në Tokën e Shenjtë, e njoftoi atë në një post të medias sociale.

Projekti synon të rivendosë kishën e Sketës Rumune në Lumin Jordan dhe të rimarrë pikturat e saj, të cilat janë dëmtuar nga shkatërrimi që monumenti ka vuajtur gjatë dekadave.

Kisha e Sketës Rumune në lumin Jordan u ndërtua në 1935 për projektet e arkitektit Dumitru Ionesku-Berechet dhe u dëmtua rëndë gjatë konfliktit të armatosur të 1967.
items.text_orig:
The first official bilateral meeting between Romanian and Israeli experts on restoring the Romanian Skete at the River Jordan took place on Wednesday at the monastic establishment.

Archimandrite Ioan Meiu, Representative of the Romanian Patriarchate in the Holy Land, announced it in a social media post .

Architect Bogdan Teodorescu and conservator-restorer Cătălin Palamariu attended the meeting; Fortlumturia e Tij Patriarch Daniel appointed them to represent the Romanian side in discussions with Israeli specialists.

The project aims to restore the church of the Romanian Skete at the River Jordan and recover its paintings, which have been damaged by the destruction the monument has suffered over the decades.

Hope for the resumption of liturgical life

The Romanian Patriarchate’s Representative in the Holy Land expressed hope that the initiatives now underway would make it possible to bring the monastic establishment back to life.

“With God’s help, we hope to rekindle the flame of the Romanian people’s vigil lamp in this church too, a church that has suffered greatly from destruction and the passage of time, where regular services have not been held for almost 60 years.”

“May this beginning bear fruit, and may prayer resound once again within the walls of the Romanian Skete at the River Jordan!” Archimandrite Ioan Meiu said.

The church of the Romanian Skete at the River Jordan was built in 1935 to designs by architect Dumitru Ionescu-Berechet and was severely damaged during the armed conflict of 1967.

The area remained mined for several decades, with demining completed in 2020.

In September 2026, after the church was cleaned, the site celebrated its first Lesser Blessing of Water service in decades.

items.summary: The Pan-Orthodox Conference on Heresies and Para-Religions concluded by adopting 17 conclusions in which representatives of the Orthodox Churches called for discernment in the face of occult practices. The final document was unanimously approved on Thursday and sets out the…
items.ex: Konferenca Pan-Oortodox mbi herezitë dhe Para-Religacionet përfundoi duke miratuar 17 përfundime në të cilat përfaqësuesit e kishave orthodhokse bënë thirrje për aftësi dalluese përballë praktikave të okultizmit. Dokumenti përfundimtar u miratua njëzëri të enjten dhe vë në dukje këtë
items.title_orig: Pan-Orthodox conference calls for discernment over astrology, divination and magic
items.sum:
Konferenca Pan-Oortodox mbi herezitë dhe Para-Religacionet përfundoi duke miratuar 17 përfundime në të cilat përfaqësuesit e kishave orthodhokse bënë thirrje për aftësi dalluese përballë praktikave të okultizmit.

Dokumenti përfundimtar u miratua njëzëri të enjten dhe vë në dukje qëndrimin teologjik dhe baritore të Kishës Orthodhokse mbi këto praktika, duke u bazuar në Shkrimet e Shenjta dhe mësimet e Etërve të Shenjtë.

Etërit e Kishës iu kundërvunë astrologjisë, duke pasur parasysh se besimi në vendosmërinë astrologjike të jetës njerëzore e bën të dobët lirinë e vullnetit dhe përgjegjësinë morale të personit, duke zvogëluar edhe domethënien e virtytit dhe të mëkatit.

Pjesëmarrësit theksuan përgjegjësinë baritore të kishës ndaj njerëzve që i drejtohen astrologjisë, magjisë apo praktikave të tjera të okultizmit.
items.text_orig:
The Pan-Orthodox Conference on Heresies and Para-Religions concluded by adopting 17 conclusions in which representatives of the Orthodox Churches called for discernment in the face of occult practices.

The final document was unanimously approved on Thursday and sets out the Orthodox Church’s theological and pastoral position on these practices, drawing on Holy Scripture and the teachings of the Holy Fathers.

Defending the human person as free

Participants emphasised that believing human life is determined by the stars is incompatible with Christian teaching on freedom and responsibility.

“The Fathers of the Church opposed astrology, considering that belief in the astrological determination of human life negates freedom of will and the moral responsibility of the person, while also diminishing the significance of virtue and sin.”

“The rejection of astrology is, ultimately, a defence of the human person as free and responsible,” the signatories emphasised.

The conference also addressed the spread of divination practices in contemporary society, including through digital technologies.

The document mentions card reading, palmistry, coffee-ground reading, dream interpretation, numerology and horoscopes, as well as fortune-telling services promoted through television, the internet and digital applications.

The Church’s pastoral responsibility

Representatives of the Orthodox Churches also warned against the use of biblical texts or religious symbols to lend credibility to divination practices.

They also highlighted interpretations that arbitrarily set dates for the end of the world or promote unverified prophecies, including within groups that present themselves as Orthodox.

Participants emphasised the Church’s pastoral responsibility towards people who turn to astrology, magic or other occult practices.

“The Church must respond with truth and love, without contempt or simplistic characterisations,” the document states.

The signatories recommend developing critical thinking, cultivating discernment and guiding the faithful towards an authentic relationship of trust in God.

At the conclusion of the conference, participants authorised Metropolitan Seraphim of Piraeus to sign the conclusions and submit them to the Standing Holy Synod of the Church of Greece.

Photo credit: Archdeacon Emanuel Văduva / Diocese of Hungary

items.title_orig: Romanian Orthodox community near Paris secures land for church and cultural centre
items.sum:
famullia orthodhokse rumune në La Ferte-sous-Jouarre, Francë, kohët e fundit ka blerë një copë tokë, me mbështetje nga departamenti i Rumanisë për rumunët jashtë vendit, për të ndërtuar vendin e vet të adhurimit.

"Unë isha i kënaqur të bashkohesha me komunitetin në Reuil-en-Brie dhe La Ferté-Jouarre, me ftesë të Fr Ciprian Rebrialorean të Parisit orthodhoks rumun të Shën Gjon Baptist në La Ferte-Jouarre, në një ditë të veçantë që shënoi një fillim të ri: kompletimin e procedurave për blerjen, me mbështetjen e Departamentit për Rumunët, vendi në të cilin do të ndërtohet një kishë dhe qendra kulturore për komunitetin lokal, shkroi në Facebook.
items.text_orig:
The Romanian Orthodox parish in La Ferté-sous-Jouarre, France, has recently purchased a plot of land, with support from Romania’s Department for Romanians Abroad, to build its own place of worship.

Her Excellency Ioana Bivolaru, Romania’s Ambassador to France, visited the community in October, when the parish marked the occasion with prayers, and expressed her support on social media .

Ambassador’s visit

“I was delighted to join the community in Reuil-en-Brie and La Ferté-sous-Jouarre, at the invitation of Fr Ciprian Rebrișorean of the Romanian Orthodox Parish of St John the Baptist in La Ferté-sous-Jouarre, on a special day marking a new beginning: the completion of the procedures for purchasing, with the support of the Department for Romanians Abroad, the land on which a church and cultural centre will be built for the local community,” the Ambassador wrote on Facebook.

“Congratulations to Fr Ciprian Rebrișorean and the community on this new project — a place for gathering and preserving Romanian identity and traditions — which will provide a permanent setting for the development of religious, educational, cultural and social activities.”

The land purchased for the construction of the parish’s St John the Baptist Orthodox Worship and Cultural Centre is located in the commune of Chamigny, in the Seine-et-Marne department of the Île-de-France region, north-central France.

The parish currently holds its liturgical services at 7 Rue de Rohan, 77260 Reuil-en-Brie, France.

Photo credit: La Ferté-sous-Jouarre Parish

items.title_orig: Patriarch of Romania: ‘The future of the human person rests in God’s hands’
items.sum:
Në një mesazh për Konferencën e 36-të Pan-Oortodox në Korint, Greqi, Patriarku Daniel ju drejtua sfidave të paraqitura nga magjia, astrologjia, falli dhe forma të tjera të pseudo-frymës bashkëkohore.

Në mesazhin e tij, patriarku rumun theksoi se jeta e vërtetë shpirtërore është e bazuar në besim, lutje, pendim dhe pjesëmarrje në jetën e shenjtë të kishës.

Kisha Orthodhokse dhe sfidat e bashkëkohorit Pseudo-Spiritualiteti me gëzim të madh në Krishtin Zot, ne morëm ftesën për të marrë pjesë në Konferencën e 36-të Pan-Ortodox mbi herezitë dhe Para-Religacionet, organizuar nga metropolitani i Korintit të Kishës Orthodhokse të Greqisë, nga 3 në 5 nëntor 2026. Kështu, organizimi i kësaj konference pan-orthodhoks ofron një mundësi për bashkësi vëllazërore dhe reflektim teologjik mbi sfidat baritore bashkëkohore, duke kontribuar në forcimin e dëshmisë për besimin orthodhoks dhe zhvillimin e bashkëpunimit midis kishave orthodhokse për të mbrojtur të vërtetën e Ungjillit dhe për të shërbyer për shpëtimin e besimtarëve. I përgëzojmë organizatorët e kësaj konference pan-orthodhoks dhe i lutemi Zotërisë tonë Jezu Krisht që kjo ngjarje akademike, frymore dhe baritore të japë fryt të bollshëm në jetën e Kishës, duke forcuar besimin, duke ndriçuar besnikët dhe duke çuar përpara shërbimin baritore dhe misionar.
items.text_orig:
In a message to the 36th Pan-Orthodox Conference in Corinth, Greece, Patriarch Daniel addressed the challenges posed by magic, astrology, divination and other forms of contemporary pseudo-spirituality.

Bishop Siluan, the Romanian Orthodox Bishop of Hungary, represented Fortlumturia e Tij Patriarch Daniel at the Conference and conveyed the patriarchal message to the participants.

In his message, the Romanian Patriarch emphasised that authentic spiritual life is grounded in faith, prayer, repentance and participation in the sacramental life of the Church.

He also called for stronger catechetical work, so that Christians may distinguish the truth of the Gospel from misleading promises of knowing the future or finding easy solutions to life’s difficulties.

The conference brought together Orthodox representatives to reflect on contemporary pastoral challenges and strengthen cooperation among the Churches.

Please find the English and Greek versions of the text below:

The Orthodox Church and the Challenges of Contemporary Pseudo-Spirituality With great joy in Christ the Lord, we received the invitation to participate in the 36th Pan-Orthodox Conference on Heresies and Para-Religions, organised by the Metropolis of Corinth of the Orthodox Church of Greece, from 3 to 5 November 2026. The theme of this year’s conference, “Magic, Divination, Astrology and the Prediction of the Future”, is highly relevant to the entire Orthodox Church and to the contemporary world, because secularisation and humanity’s estrangement from God have encouraged the spread of practices and beliefs that seek to replace authentic faith with magic, astrology, divination and other forms of pseudo-spirituality. At the same time, these phenomena constitute a serious pastoral challenge, as they create confusion in the lives of Christians and distance people from authentic and living communion with God. Holy Scripture and Holy Tradition consistently testify that the future of the human person rests in God’s hands, and that knowledge and fulfilment of His will are attained through faith, prayer, repentance and participation in the sacramental life of the Church. Therefore, any attempt to discover the future through occult means or to acquire power through magical practices represents a departure from the true faith and a turning away from genuine spiritual life. In this context, the pastoral ministry of the Orthodox Church is called to identify and counter such errors through the clear proclamation of Orthodox teaching and the intensification of catechetical activity. Particular attention must be given to presenting the teachings of the faith in an accessible and convincing manner, so that the faithful may distinguish the truth of the Gospel from deceptive messages that falsely promise knowledge of the future and easy solutions to life’s problems. Thus, the organisation of this Pan-Orthodox conference provides an opportunity for fraternal communion and theological reflection on contemporary pastoral challenges, contributing to the strengthening of the witness to the Orthodox faith and the development of cooperation among the Orthodox Churches in defending the truth of the Gospel and serving the salvation of the faithful. We congratulate the organisers of this Pan-Orthodox conference and pray to our Lord Jesus Christ that this academic, spiritual and pastoral event may bear abundant fruit in the life of the Church, strengthening the faith, enlightening the faithful and furthering the Church’s pastoral and missionary ministry. With paternal blessing and a fraternal embrace in Christ the Lord, † DANIEL Patriarch of the Romanian Orthodox Church

Source: Basilica.ro

items.title_orig: Romanian Orthodox bishop baptises Swedish mother and son after two years of preparation
items.sum:
Peshkopi Makarie i Evropës Veriore pagëzoi dy shtetas suedezë, një nënë e bir, fundjavën e shkuar në kishën orthodhokse rumune në Uppsala, Suedi.

Maria dhe Martin Hoppe zgjodhën të bashkoheshin me Kishën Orthodhokse pas gati dy vjetësh përgatitjeje.

Nëna e tij, Maria, e përshkroi gjithashtu udhëtimin e tyre drejt zbulimit të orthodhoksisë nëpërmjet leximit dhe rritjes më pranë besimtarëve të famullisë Upsala.

Po të mos bëhemi si fëmijë, të pastër në zemër dhe pa dredhi, nuk do të hyjmë në mbretërinë e qiejve, shtoi peshkopi.

Kisha orthodhokse rumune në Uppsala i kushtohet tre Hirarkëve të Shenjtë dhe sinaksive të Metropolitanëve të Shenjtë të Uollaçisë.
items.text_orig:
Bishop Macarie of Northern Europe baptised two Swedish nationals, a mother and son, last weekend at the Romanian Orthodox parish church in Uppsala, Sweden. On the same occasion, seven young Scandinavians became catechumens.

Maria and Martin Hoppe chose to join the Orthodox Church after nearly two years of preparation.

“I was a catechumen for almost two years, and it was a wonderful period. Yet throughout that time, I eagerly awaited the moment when I could become a full member of the Church,” Martin Hoppe told Trinitas TV .

His mother, Maria, also described their journey towards discovering Orthodoxy through reading and growing closer to the faithful of the Uppsala parish.

“When we began reading and learning more about Orthodoxy, we understood that this is the truth, that this is God’s path and that we must follow it.”

Pure in heart and without guile

The liturgical programme also included the celebration of the Divine Liturgy, during which Bishop Macarie emphasised that children can serve as spiritual examples for adults.

“The Mother of God guides and enlightens us so that we may guide children. Yet children themselves, whether openly or quietly, also guide us, because we learn from them, in a special way, purity of heart.”

“Unless we become like children, pure in heart and without guile, we shall not enter the Kingdom of Heaven,” the Bishop added.

The Romanian Orthodox church in Uppsala is dedicated to the Three Holy Hierarchs and the Synaxis of the Holy Metropolitans of Wallachia.

Photo credit: Facebook / Diocese of Northern Europe

items.title_orig: Goodness is not truly good unless it is shared: Bishop Siluan blesses new community centre in Piacenza
items.sum:
Nëse nuk ndahet me të tjerët, mirësia nuk është vërtet e mirë. Sepse edhe gëzimi nuk është me të vërtetë një gëzim nëse nuk e ndan me të tjerët, nëse nuk lejon që të tjerët të marrin pjesë në gëzimin tënd, i tha Hiria e Tij Peshkopi Siluanit të Italisë të dielën.

Hierorku festoi Liturgjinë Hyjnore në kishën orthodhokse rumune të Shën Daniel, Hesikastit në Pakenza, Itali, ku ai bekoi gjithashtu qendrën e re të komunitetit.

Ndëshkimi i ferrit është dënimi që lind në ndërgjegjen e dikujt: keqardhja dhe ankthi që vjen kur nuk ke zgjedhur Perëndinë, që nuk e ke kërkuar Perëndinë apo që ke hedhur poshtë Perëndinë dhe që nuk ke bërë të mirën që mund të kishte bërë, shpjegoi peshkopi.

Të paktën visheni atë të varfër, të paktën vizitoni atë dhe thoni: Ju shpirt të varfër, më lejoni të thërrasë një mjek për t'u kujdesur për ju.

Shpëtimi gjendet në gjëra të vogla dhe shenjtëria, edhe pse është kaq e madhe, saqë është përtej arritjes së mendjes dhe imagjinatës sonë, arrihet nëpërmjet gjërave të vogla dhe të thjeshta, tha Peshkopi Siluan.

Sepse mund të shpëtosh një jetë në varësi të asaj se sa i vëmendshëm je ndaj personit pranë teje, ose mund ta humbasësh atë moment dhe pastaj të pendohesh për pjesën tjetër të jetës, theksoi hierarkia.

Pas Liturgjisë, peshkopi Siluan bekoi qendrën e re të komunitetit të famullisë dhe i dha priftit Frar.
items.text_orig:
“Goodness is not truly good unless it is shared with others. Because joy, too, is not truly joy unless you share it with others, unless you allow others to share in your joy,” said Hirësia e Tij Bishop Siluan of Italy on Sunday.

The hierarch celebrated the Divine Liturgy at the Romanian Orthodox Church of St Daniel the Hesychast in Piacenza, Italy, where he also blessed the parish’s new community centre.

In his homily, Bishop Siluan reflected on the parable of the Rich Man and Poor Lazarus, encouraging the faithful not to hesitate to do good and to be attentive to their neighbours.

What the rich man should have done

“The torment of hell is the torment that arises in a person’s conscience: the regret and anguish of not having chosen God, of not having sought God or of having rejected God, and of not having done the good that one could have done,” the Bishop explained.

“What should the rich man have done to avoid ending up where he did? At least give a piece of bread, at least offer a glass of water, because even a glass of water is recognised and rewarded in the Kingdom of Heaven. At least clothe that poor man, at least visit him and say: You poor soul, let me call a doctor to look after you.”

Salvation lies in small things

The hierarch went on to explain that doing good is not difficult and urged families to raise their children with this understanding, helping them to lead fulfilling lives.

“Salvation lies in small things, and holiness, although it is so great that it is beyond the reach of our minds and imagination, is attained through small and simple things,” Bishop Siluan said.

“Do not forget the small and simple things. Teach children to do small and simple things, and teach them to pay attention to those around them. If someone has less than they do, teach them to share something of their own, from the food they eat, from what they take to school, or from their clothing, and to say: Here, take this to that child.”

Pay attention to those around us

Bishop Siluan recalled that the parable of the Rich Man and Poor Lazarus is read in the period leading up to the Nativity Fast, encouraging the faithful to support those in need.

“Let us spend a little less time looking at our phone screens, and let us teach children to pay attention to those around them. Because you can save a life depending on how attentive you are to the person beside you, or you can miss that moment and then regret it for the rest of your life,” the hierarch emphasised.

Ordinations and distinctions

During the Divine Liturgy, the diocesan bishop ordained Deacon Constantin Bunduc to the priesthood for the Parish of St Pancratius the Hieromartyr in Messina, Sicily.

He also ordained Monk Ilarion, a member of the monastic community of the Nativity of the Mother of God Monastery in Spilimbergo, Italy, as a deacon.

Following the Liturgy, Bishop Siluan blessed the parish’s new community centre and awarded parish priest Fr. Iurie Ursachi the Diocesan Order of St. Dionysius Exiguus for clergy.

The priest’s wife was awarded the Diocesan Order of St Dionysius Exiguus for laypeople.

About the Piacenza parish

The Romanian Orthodox parish in Piacenza celebrates its 20th anniversary this year.

Initially, the parish was granted the use of the Santo Stefano church. In 2016, it received a concession to use another Catholic church, which later underwent extensive renovation and was equipped with everything needed for Orthodox worship.

In 2021, Archbishop Atanasie of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, then an Auxiliary Bishop of the Romanian Orthodox Diocese of Italy, consecrated the church.

The church is located at Via San Nazzaro 18, Piacenza, Italy.

Photo credit: Diocese of Italy

items.text_orig:
Metropolitan Gabriel of Lovech has been hospitalized in Sofia after being diagnosed with acute pancreatitis, according to an official statement issued by the Bulgarian Orthodox Patriarchate.

Responding to inquiries regarding the Metropolitan’s health, the Patriarchate confirmed that he was admitted to the Military Medical Academy in Sofia on Wednesday, November 4, 2026.

According to the statement, Metropolitan Gabriel is currently receiving the necessary medical care, with his treating physicians taking all appropriate measures to support his recovery.

The Bulgarian Patriarchate also called on the faithful to pray for the Metropolitan’s healing and swift recovery.

“We call upon all believers to turn to God in prayer for the healing and speedy recovery of Metropolitan Gabriel,” the statement read.

No further details regarding his condition or the expected duration of his hospitalization were provided.

Source: Bulgarian Orthodox Patriarchate

items.title: Romanian Orthodox parishes in eastern Germany reorganised into two deaneries
items.summary: The Romanian Orthodox Deanery of Eastern Germany has been reorganised into two new ecclesiastical districts: the Saxony-Thuringia Deanery, headed by Fr Cezar Burlacu, and the Berlin-Brandenburg Deanery, headed by Fr Ioan-Dragoș Manu. The reorganisation was announced to clergy on…
items.text:
The Romanian Orthodox Deanery of Eastern Germany has been reorganised into two new ecclesiastical districts: the Saxony-Thuringia Deanery, headed by Fr Cezar Burlacu, and the Berlin-Brandenburg Deanery, headed by Fr Ioan-Dragoș Manu.

The reorganisation was announced to clergy on Saturday during the autumn meeting of the Eastern Germany Deanery, held at the Romanian Orthodox parish in Dresden.

Dean Ioan Forga presented the decisions adopted by the Standing Committee of the Diocesan Council on 15 October 2026, which provided the basis for establishing the two new deaneries.

On this occasion, the priests and deacons thanked Fr Ioan Forga for his service as head of the former deanery and for the support he had given Romanian Orthodox parishes during the early years of the Church’s missionary development in eastern Germany.

Spiritual life in the diaspora

The autumn meeting was preceded by a lecture delivered by Rev. Professor Daniel Benga, entitled “The Divine Liturgy – An Exchange of Lives between God and Humanity”.

The gathering highlighted the importance of participating in the Church’s Eucharistic life and the spiritual transformation of the faithful through receiving the Body and Blood of the Saviour.

Participants also discussed the particular challenges of life in the diaspora and the need to cultivate joy and a sense of belonging within the Church community.

Fr Daniel Benga emphasised the importance of avoiding formalism and routine in liturgical ministry, encouraging priests and deacons to cultivate a continuous life of prayer and remain conscious of the responsibility entrusted to them in their mission.

On Sunday, the priest also delivered a spiritual lecture following the celebration of the Divine Liturgy at the Romanian Orthodox parish in Leipzig.

The parish priest, Fr Ioan Forga, thanked him for his contribution to the spiritual gatherings organised in the two Saxon communities.

Photo credit: Metropolis of Germany

items.sum:
Pasi Presidenti i SH.B.A.-së Trump, patriarku Theophilos i Jerusalemit mori gjithashtu {Y) të presidentit rus Vladimir Putin për të ndërmjetësuar në përpjekjet për të arritur paqen midis Rusisë dhe Ukrainës.

Patriarku Theophilos u takua dje me presidentin rus në Kremlin, ku Putin i dha urdhrin e miqësisë së Federatës Ruse, vlerësimin e kontributit të tij për forcimin e miqësisë, bashkëpunimit dhe lidhjeve frymore me Rusinë.

Patriarku i Jerusalemit deklaron veten një admirues i Putinit

Në atë kohë, Patriarku i Jerusalemit kishte deklaruar se kishte miratimin e qeverive amerikane dhe greke, si dhe të patriarkut ekumenik Bartolomeu, për të kontribuar në gjetjen e një mënyre për të ndërmjetësuar dhe për t'i dhënë fund luftës që Rusia po bën në Ukrainë, e cila ka shkaktuar ndarje të thella, mes të tjerash, brenda Kishës Orthodhokse.

Megjithatë, Patriarku Ekumenik ka dërguar një ftesë për një takim të Patriarkatit të lashtë (Konstantinop, Aleksandrisë, Jerusalemit dhe Antiokisë) në 30 nëntor në Fanar, duke ushtruar të drejtën e çdo Patriarku Ekumenik për të mbledhur takime midis Primatëve të kishave orthodhokse, duke treguar kështu se ai nuk është i përgatitur t'ia lërë këtë rol patriarkut të Jerusalemit.

Duke përshëndetur patriarkun e Jerusalemit, Vladimir Putin foli për marrëdhëniet e ngushta midis Kishës Orthodhokse Ruse dhe Patriarkatit të Jerusalemit, duke vënë në dukje se patriarku Kirill shpesh ngre çështje lidhur me Jerusalemin gjatë takimeve të tyre.

Nga ana e tij, patriarku Theofilos falenderoi presidentin rus për ftesën dhe çmimin, duke theksuar rëndësinë e veçantë të marrëdhënieve midis Patriarkatit të Jerusalemit dhe popullit rus.
items.text_orig:
After US President Trump, Patriarch Theophilos of Jerusalem also received the “blessing” of Russian President Vladimir Putin to mediate in efforts to achieve peace between Russia and Ukraine.

Patriarch Theophilos met with the Russian President yesterday at the Kremlin , where Putin awarded him the Order of Friendship of the Russian Federation, “in recognition of his contribution to strengthening friendship, cooperation, and spiritual ties with Russia.”

Patriarch of Jerusalem Declares Himself an Admirer of Putin

Of particular significance was Patriarch Theophilos’ reference to the prospects for negotiations aimed at ending the war between Russia and Ukraine.

Referring to proposals for talks concerning the war Russia is waging in Ukraine (the Kremlin’s official website did not use the word “war,” but instead employed a vague description referring to “the situation on Russia’s western borders”), the Patriarch emphasized his responsibility as a spiritual leader to listen to those seeking peace.

“We are ready to offer our assistance and fully encourage every effort aimed at facilitating and achieving peace between brothers,” he stated.

Concluding his remarks, Patriarch Theophilos once again thanked Vladimir Putin for the Order of Friendship, stressing that he considered the distinction an honor not only for himself but also for the entire Orthodox Church of Jerusalem.

He also expressed his personal admiration for the Russian President, assuring him that he prays for him daily: “I personally admire you and pray every day for your health, that the Lord may enlighten and inspire you in addressing all the challenges that lie ahead.”

Patriarch Theophilos Once Again Seeks the Role of “Peacemaker”

Moreover, it has not been long since Patriarch Theophilos gave an interview to an American media outlet following his meeting with US President Trump , in which he revealed the mediating role he intends to undertake in the Ukrainian issue, announcing forthcoming meetings with Zelenskyy and Putin.

At the time, the Patriarch of Jerusalem had stated that he had the approval of both the American and Greek governments, as well as Ecumenical Patriarch Bartholomew, to contribute to finding a way to mediate and end the war Russia is waging in Ukraine, which has caused deep divisions, among other things, within the Orthodox Church.

However, the Ecumenical Patriarch has sent an invitation for a meeting of the Ancient Patriarchates (Constantinople, Alexandria, Jerusalem, and Antioch) on November 30 at the Phanar, exercising the prerogative held by each Ecumenical Patriarch to convene meetings among the Primates of the Orthodox Churches, thereby demonstrating that he is not prepared to leave this role to the Patriarch of Jerusalem.

It should also be recalled that Patriarch Theophilos was the one who convened the “fraternal gathering” in Amman, Jordan, a few years ago to discuss the Ukrainian issue, which ended in a fiasco due to low participation.

Putin as the “Protector” of Christians in the Holy Land

Welcoming the Patriarch of Jerusalem, Vladimir Putin spoke about the close relations between the Russian Orthodox Church and the Patriarchate of Jerusalem, noting that Patriarch Kirill frequently raises issues concerning Jerusalem during their meetings.

“We value your commitment to maintaining and developing relations with the Russian Orthodox Church,” the Russian President said, while also acknowledging the difficulties facing the Patriarchate of Jerusalem due to the situation in the Middle East.

Putin also stressed that Russia traditionally attaches particular importance to the situation of Christians in the region, expressing his country’s willingness to contribute to preserving the historic Christian presence in the Holy Land.

“Our cooperation in this area is particularly important today,” he noted.

Patriarch Theophilos to Putin: You Are a “Defender of the Orthodox Faith”

For his part, Patriarch Theophilos thanked the Russian President for the invitation and the award, highlighting the particular significance of the relations between the Patriarchate of Jerusalem and the Russian people.

Addressing Vladimir Putin, he described him as a “defender of the Orthodox faith” and expressed his gratitude for the support he said the Russian President provides to the Patriarchate of Jerusalem.

The Primate of the Church of Jerusalem referred to the spiritual mission of the Patriarchate, which includes protecting Christian holy sites and preserving Jerusalem’s multi-religious character.

“We are guarantors that Jerusalem will remain a city of many religious communities, a mosaic of different religions coexisting in peace and mutual understanding,” he stated.

At the same time, he expressed concern over the continued decline of the Christian population in the Middle East, pointing out that political instability poses serious challenges to the future of Christian communities.

The Patriarch also thanked the Russian President for his continued support, which he linked to the protection of Christian holy sites and stability in Jerusalem and the wider region.

items.title_orig: Patriarchs of Antioch express Concern Over Christians’ Future in Syria
items.sum:
Patriarku Xhon X i Antiokisë dhe i gjithë Lindjes morën patriarkun katolik grek Melkit, Jusef Absi dhe patriarkun siriak orthodhoks Mor Ignatius Afrem II në Rivendsinë Patriarkale në Damask të enjten në mëngjes, më 5 nëntor 2026.

Gjatë takimit të tyre, të tre patriarkët diskutuan situatën e të krishterëve në Lindjen e Mesme, veçanërisht në Siri dhe shprehën shqetësim rreth sfidave që hasin komunitetet e krishtere në rajon.

Diskutimet e tyre pasqyruan shqetësimet e përbashkëta rreth sigurisë, jetesës dhe perspektivave afat-gjata të komuniteteve të krishtere në Siri dhe anembanë Lindjes së Mesme.
items.text_orig:
Patriarch John X of Antioch and All the East received Melkite Greek Catholic Patriarch Youssef Absi and Syriac Orthodox Patriarch Mor Ignatius Aphrem II at the Patriarchal Residence in Damascus on Thursday morning, November 5, 2026.

During their meeting, the three Patriarchs discussed the situation of Christians in the Middle East, particularly in Syria, and expressed concern over the challenges facing Christian communities in the region.

The Church leaders renewed their strong condemnation of the terrorist attack against the Church of Saint George in the village of Al-Hammoud in Jordan.

They also examined the broader situation in Syria, focusing on repeated attacks, arbitrary dismissals from employment, decisions to seize the assets of certain citizens, and delays in bringing detainees to trial.

Particular attention was given to the deteriorating living conditions and rising cost of living affecting the Syrian population.

The Patriarchs discussed the consequences of these developments and explored ways to support and assist the faithful amid growing concerns about their continued presence and future in the region.

Their discussions reflected shared concerns about the security, livelihoods, and long-term prospects of Christian communities in Syria and throughout the Middle East.

The meeting concluded with prayers for peace in Syria, across the Middle East, and throughout the world.

items.title_orig: Patriarch of Alexandria to visit Côte d’Ivoire from 11 to 15 December
items.sum:
Papa dhe patriarku Teodori II i Aleksandrisë dhe e gjithë Afrika do të vizitojnë Bregun e Fildishtë nga 11 në 15 dhjetor 2026, duke ndërmarrë një vizitë zyrtare baritore në vend.

Mbërritja e ardhshme e Patriarkut të Aleksandrisë u njoftua në një letër baritore të botuar nga Metropoliti Daniel i Akrës, i cili i bëri një ftesë klerit dhe besnikëve të Kishës lokale, për t'u përgatitur për patriarkun e tij të mirëpritur.

Siç thekson Metropolitani Daniel i Acrës, prania e Patriarkut të Atdheut përbën një bekim të veçantë frymor, jo vetëm për komunitetin orthodhoks, por edhe për njerëzit e Bregut të Fildishtë në tërësi.

Kjo është me gëzim të veçantë dhe emocion të thellë që unë ju njoftoj se, nga 11 deri në 15 dhjetor 2026, Kisha Orthodhokse në Bregun e Fildishtë do të ketë nderin dhe bekimin e madh të mirëpritjes në këtë vend mikpritës, Fortlumturia e Tij Teodoros II, Papa dhe Patriarku i Aleksandrisë dhe e gjithë Afrikës, që do të ndërmarrë një vizitë zyrtare baritore në vendin tonë.

Ne do të mirëpresim Papën tonë, Patriarkun dhe Atin shpirtëror, i cili vazhdon traditën dy-vjeçare apostolike dhe mban përgjegjësinë solemne për të siguruar udhëheqje shpirtërore, për të ruajtur unitetin kishtar dhe për të çuar përpara dëshminë misionare të Kishës Katolike Orthodhokse në të gjithë Afrikën.

Kjo vizitë është me rëndësi të veçantë sepse Fortlumturia e Tij do të mbajë takime të nivelit të lartë me shtetin dhe udhëheqjen politike të Republikës së Bregut të Fildishtë, duke përcjellë mesazhin universal të Kishës Orthodhokse lidhur me paqen, unitetin kombëtar, vëllazërinë, kohezionin shoqëror dhe respektin reciprok.
items.text_orig:
Pope and Patriarch Theodore II of Alexandria and All Africa will visit Côte d’Ivoire from 11 to 15 December 2026, undertaking an official pastoral visit to the country.

The forthcoming arrival of the Patriarch of Alexandria was announced in a pastoral letter issued by Metropolitan Daniel of Accra, who extended an invitation to the clergy and faithful of the local Church to prepare for the Patriarch’s welcome.

During his stay, the Patriarch is expected to hold meetings with the country’s state and political leadership. His visit is also expected to mark an important milestone in strengthening the Orthodox witness, ecclesiastical unity, and missionary work of the Patriarchate of Alexandria in the region. As Metropolitan Daniel of Accra emphasises, the Patriarch’s presence constitutes a special spiritual blessing, not only for the Orthodox community but also for the people of Côte d’Ivoire as a whole.

Read below the pastoral letter:

To the Reverend Clergy and the Devout Orthodox Faithful of Côte d’Ivoire

“Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord!” (Matthew 21:9) My beloved Fathers and Brethren, My dearly beloved spiritual children in the Lord,

It is with particular joy and profound emotion that I announce to you that, from 11 to 15 December 2026, the Orthodox Church in Côte d’Ivoire will have the great honour and blessing of welcoming to this hospitable land Fortlumturia e Tij Theodoros II, Pope and Patriarch of Alexandria and All Africa, who will undertake an official pastoral visit to our country.

We shall welcome the Successor of the Holy Apostle and Evangelist Mark, the Primate of the historic and ancient Patriarchate of Alexandria and All Africa, the spiritual Father and highest ecclesiastical authority of the Orthodox Christians under the jurisdiction of the Patriarchate of Alexandria throughout the African continent.

We shall welcome our Pope, Patriarch and spiritual Father, who continues the two-thousand-year-old Apostolic Tradition and bears the solemn responsibility of providing spiritual guidance, safeguarding ecclesiastical unity, and advancing the missionary witness of the canonical Orthodox Church throughout Africa. His presence among us is not merely an official visit, but a momentous ecclesiastical event, a living expression of our unity with the Apostolic Church of Alexandria, and a great spiritual blessing for us all.

The special affection that Fortlumturia e Tij holds for the people of Côte d’Ivoire is both profound and enduring. His paternal care embraces not only Orthodox Christians but the entire population of the country, regardless of religious affiliation, social background, or origin. He comes once again among us as a loving and compassionate Father, to bless his spiritual children, strengthen their faith, and support the pastoral, spiritual, and missionary work of our local Church.

This visit is of particular significance because Fortlumturia e Tij will hold high-level meetings with the state and political leadership of the Republic of Côte d’Ivoire, conveying the universal message of the Orthodox Church concerning peace, national unity, fraternity, social cohesion, and mutual respect. At the same time, he will extend his heartfelt wishes for the progress, stability, and prosperity of the country and all its people.

The Patriarchal Visit also presents an important opportunity to highlight the presence and contribution of our Orthodox Church within Ivorian society, as well as its enduring mission to serve humanity with love and without discrimination, contributing to peaceful coexistence and social solidarity.

My beloved in the Lord,

I call upon all of you, clergy and laity alike, young and old, to prepare yourselves through prayer, unity, and love for the reception of our spiritual Father. May his presence among us become an occasion for spiritual renewal, the strengthening of our faith, and the rekindling of our missionary zeal.

The detailed programme of the Patriarchal Visit will be communicated in due course to all our parishes, as soon as it has been finalised, so that all the faithful may have the opportunity to participate in the sacred services and the various events scheduled for this blessed occasion.

Let us welcome Fortlumturia e Tij with the love, profound respect, and genuine hospitality that so beautifully characterise the people of Côte d’Ivoire.

Let us also pray that his visit may become a source of abundant divine blessings for our Church and for the entire country.

Welcome, Your Fortlumturia, our Most Blessed Father and Master, to Your beloved Côte d’Ivoire!

With my paternal blessings and abundant love in Christ,

† DANIEL ARCHBISHOP OF ACCRA AND CÔTE D’IVOIRE

items.title_orig: Metropolitan of Warsaw received delegation of an Orthodox Youth Brotherhood
items.sum:
Të hënën, më 2 nëntor 2026, Metropoliti Saua i Varshavës dhe i gjithë Polonia morën një delegacion të anëtarëve të Bordit të Drejtorëve të Vëllazërisë Orthodhokse të Rinisë të Dioqezës së Varshavës-Bielsk për një audiencë zyrtare.

Gjatë diskutimit, metropolitani u informua mbi nismat dhe veprimtaritë e kryera me sukses deri tani, ndërsa sfidat përpara, si dhe planet dhe veprimtaritë e planifikuara për muajt e ardhshëm, u diskutuan gjithashtu.
items.text_orig:
On Monday, 2 November 2026, Metropolitan Sawa of Warsaw and All Poland received a delegation of members of the Board of Directors of the Orthodox Youth Brotherhood of the Diocese of Warsaw-Bielsk for an official audience.

The meeting provided an opportunity to review the second year of the Board’s term of office. During the discussion, the Metropolitan was briefed on the initiatives and activities successfully carried out to date, while the challenges ahead, as well as plans and scheduled activities for the coming months, were also discussed.

The Metropolitan expressed his gratitude to the members of the Diocesan Board of Directors of the Orthodox Youth Brotherhood for their work and dedication to date, encouraging them to continue their efforts with the same zeal and commitment. The Hierarch emphasised the importance of young people setting an example for their peers through their personal conduct and active involvement.

items.title_orig: Metropolitan of Sliven condemns Ukrainian Hierarch’s interference in Bulgarian Church affairs
items.sum:
Metropoliti Arseni i Slivenit ka kritikuar fuqishëm Metropolitanin Luka të Zaporizhjisë dhe Melitopolit të Kishës Orthodhokse të Ukrainës (nën Metropolitan Onufri) lidhur me deklaratat e tij publike lidhur me patriarkun Daniel të Bullgarisë dhe Sinodën e Shenjtë të Kishës Orthodhokse Bullgare.

Në një deklaratë me fjalë të forta, Metropoliti Arseni shprehu indinjatën e tij ndaj asaj që ai e përshkroi si akuza serioze kundër episkopit bullgar dhe ndërhyrjeve të papranueshme nga një hierarki e huaj në punët e brendshme të një kishe orthodhokse autocepfaloze.

Ai akuzoi Metropolitan Luka për portretizimin e Sinodit të Shenjtë Bullgar si të ndarë nga intrigat prapa skenës dhe duke sugjeruar se patriarku Daniel ishte nën presion nga një shumicë armiqësore peshkopësh në marrjen e vendimeve kundër vullnetit të tij.

Kjo është një fyerje për të dhe për të gjithë kishën orthodhokse bullgare, deklaroi Metropoliti Arseni.

Metropoliti theksoi se Kisha Orthodhokse Bullgare është një kishë e pavarur, autoceptale vendimet e së cilës merren kolektivisht nga autoritetet e ligjshme kishtare.

Duke përfunduar deklaratën e tij, Metropolitan Arseni i kërkoi hierarkisë ukrainase të kërkojë falje për akuzat e tij kundër episkopit bullgar, të respektojë pavarësinë kanonike të kishës orthodhokse bullgare dhe të përmbahet nga ndërhyrja e mëtejshme në punët e saj të brendshme.
items.text_orig:
Metropolitan Arseniy of Sliven has strongly criticized Metropolitan Luke of Zaporizhzhia and Melitopol of the Ukrainian Orthodox Church (under Metropolitan Onufriy) over his public statements concerning Patriarch Daniel of Bulgaria and the Holy Synod of the Bulgarian Orthodox Church.

In a strongly worded statement, Metropolitan Arseniy expressed his indignation at what he described as serious accusations against the Bulgarian episcopate and unacceptable interference by a foreign hierarch in the internal affairs of an autocephalous Orthodox Church.

He accused Metropolitan Luke of portraying the Bulgarian Holy Synod as divided by behind-the-scenes intrigues and suggesting that Patriarch Daniel was being pressured by a hostile majority of bishops into making decisions against his will.

“This is not a defense of the Patriarch. It is an insult to him and to the entire Bulgarian Orthodox Church,” Metropolitan Arseniy declared.

The Metropolitan stressed that the Bulgarian Orthodox Church is an independent, autocephalous Church whose decisions are taken collectively by its legitimate ecclesiastical authorities.

He specifically addressed the decision concerning the canonical visit of Ecumenical Patriarch Bartholomew to Constantinople, emphasizing that it had been adopted unanimously by the Holy Synod, without a single dissenting vote.

“Where, then, is this majority that supposedly forces the Patriarch? Where are the conspirators? Where is the coercion of which Metropolitan Luke speaks?” he asked.

Metropolitan Arseniy argued that portraying the Synod as a place of pressure, blackmail, and intrigue undermines both the authority of Patriarch Daniel and the credibility of the Church’s collective decision-making.

Referring to the Second Canon of the Second Ecumenical Council, he reminded Metropolitan Luke that bishops must respect the canonical boundaries of their jurisdiction and refrain from interfering in the administration of other Churches.

“The Bulgarian Orthodox Church is not some diocese subordinate to an external center,” he emphasized, defending its canonical independence and synodal governance.

He also rejected attempts to portray Patriarch Daniel and the Bulgarian bishops as opposing factions, stressing that the Patriarch and the members of the Holy Synod share responsibility for the governance and unity of the Church.

Metropolitan Arseniy further questioned the reliability of the information on which Metropolitan Luke had based his accusations, suggesting that unverified rumors and allegations should not form the basis of public statements by Orthodox hierarchs.

He called on Metropolitan Luke to concentrate on the pastoral needs of his own diocese, particularly amid the difficult circumstances facing the Orthodox faithful in Ukraine.

Concluding his statement, Metropolitan Arseniy urged the Ukrainian hierarch to apologize for his accusations against the Bulgarian episcopate, respect the canonical independence of the Bulgarian Orthodox Church, and refrain from further interference in its internal affairs.

He emphasized that genuine episcopal ministry is measured by pastoral responsibility, humility, prudence, and commitment to ecclesiastical peace rather than public accusations against fellow bishops.

Despite his sharp criticism, Metropolitan Arseniy expressed solidarity with the Ukrainian people and offered prayers for an end to their suffering.

“We sincerely sympathize with the brotherly Orthodox people of Ukraine and pray wholeheartedly to God that their suffering, which is also our suffering, may end as soon as possible,” he stated.

He concluded by expressing love and compassion for Orthodox Christians in Ukraine and praying that God would grant their bishops the wisdom and strength to care for their people.

“May God protect the people of Ukraine!”

Source: Patriarchate of Bulgaria

items.text_orig:
On Friday, November 6, 2026, Patriarch Daniel of Bulgaria will preside over the Divine Liturgy and the Sacred Memorial Service at the Holy Stavropegic Monastery of the Holy Trinity in Troyan, marking the 14th anniversary of the repose of the late Patriarch Maxim of Bulgaria.

Metropolitans and Bishops of the Bulgarian Orthodox Church will concelebrate and participate in the sacred services.

According to the programme:

08:30 – Official reception of Patriarch Daniel of Bulgaria.

09:00 – Commencement of the Divine Liturgy.

11:00 – Commencement of the Sacred Memorial Service for the repose of the soul of the late Patriarch Maxim.
