items.title_orig: Patriarchate of Bulgaria responds to criticism over Ecumenical Patriarch’s visit
items.sum:
Në përgjigje të reagimeve dhe kritikave të shprehura në disa qarqe kishtarë pas vizitës së fundit të patriarkut ekumenik Bartolomeu në Bullgari dhe pjesëmarrjes së tij në festimet që nderojnë Shën Xhonin e Rilës, Sinodin e Shenjtë të Kishës Orthodhokse Bullgare, ka lëshuar një mesazh baritore drejtuar klerit dhe besimtarëve.

Në mesazhin e tij, Sinodi i Shenjtë thekson rëndësinë e ruajtjes së besimit orthodhoks dhe ruajtjes së unitetit kishtar, duke u kujtuar besimtarëve se kisha orthodhokse bullgare mbetet në një bashkësi të plotë eukarike me Patriarkatin ekumenik dhe të gjitha kishat e tjera orthodhokse lokale.

Këta na janë dorëzuar nga Zoti ynë Jezu Krisht, të trashëguar nga apostujt e shenjtë, të vulosur me gjakun e martirëve të shenjtë dhe të rrëfimtarëve, të vendosur patundshmërisht nëpërmjet përkufizimeve hyjnore të frymëzuara dhe të pagabueshme të Këshillave Ekumenike, të ruajtura në thesarin e mësimeve të Etërve të Shenjtë dhe të shpallura nga njerëzit e shenjtë, jeta e të cilëve ishte e shenjtë.

Të vërtetat e besimit të shenjtë orthodhoks nuk janë një shpikje njerëzore, por më tepër fruti i zbulimit hyjnor të Shpirtit Më të Shenjtë dhe Jetëdhënës të së vërtetës, i cili jeton brenda, banon brenda dhe mbështet Kishën e Shenjtë.

Sinoda e Shenjtë e kishës orthodhokse bullgare ⇩ Patriarkati bullgar organizoi festime solemne në nderim të këtyre përvjetorëve.

Me ftesë të Fortlumturia e Tij Daniel, Patriarku i Bullgarisë dhe Sinodit të Shenjtë të Kishës Orthodhokse Bullgare, një delegacion i Patriarkatit të Parë Ekumenik të Kostandinopojës, mori pjesë në këto festime solemne kryesuar nga Tishenjoria e Patriarkut Ekumenik Bartolomeu.

Ne duam t'i kujtojmë gjithkujt se Patriarkati bullgar i Kishës Orthodhokse është në një bashkësi të plotë e kanonike me patriarkatin ekumenik të Kostandinopojës, si dhe me të gjitha kishat e tjera orthodhokse lokale.
items.text_orig:
In response to the reactions and criticisms expressed in certain ecclesiastical circles following the recent visit of the Ecumenical Patriarch Bartholomew to Bulgaria and his participation in the celebrations honouring Saint John of Rila, the Holy Synod of the Bulgarian Orthodox Church has issued a pastoral message addressed to the clergy and the faithful.

In its message, the Holy Synod emphasises the importance of safeguarding the Orthodox Faith and preserving ecclesiastical unity, reminding the faithful that the Bulgarian Orthodox Church remains in full Eucharistic and canonical communion with the Ecumenical Patriarchate and all the other Local Orthodox Churches.

At the same time, it calls upon all to exercise sobriety, spiritual discernment and restraint, and to refrain from extreme statements, condemnations and divisive conduct. It particularly underscores the responsibility of the clergy to foster unity and strengthen the faithful’s trust in the life of the Church.

Special reference is made to the importance of honouring Saint John of Rila, as well as to the need for the spiritual legacy of this great Saint to remain a constant example of steadfastness in the Faith, humility, obedience and love.

Read below the message of the Holy Synod of the Patriarchate of Bulgaria:

Beloved children of our Holy Church,

“Therefore, brethren, stand firm and hold fast to the traditions” (2 Thess. 2:15), the foremost of the Apostles, Saint Paul, exhorts all of us Orthodox Christians.

For nearly two thousand years, the Church of Christ has faithfully safeguarded and accurately handed down to each new generation of Christians, as her precious inheritance, the unchanging truths of the Faith. These were delivered to us by our Lord Jesus Christ, bequeathed to us by the Holy Apostles, sealed with the blood of the Holy Martyrs and Confessors, firmly established through the divinely inspired and infallible definitions of the Ecumenical Councils, preserved in the treasury of the teachings of the Holy Fathers, and proclaimed by holy men whose lives were themselves holy.

The truths of the Holy Orthodox Faith are not a human invention, but rather the fruit of the divine revelation of the Most Holy and Life-Giving Spirit of Truth, who lives in, dwells within, and sustains the Holy Church.

We give thanks and glory to God every day, for in His great mercy He has deemed us worthy to be baptised in His Most Holy Name and to become heirs to the Orthodox tradition of our people, which spans more than a thousand years. We are also profoundly grateful and immeasurably blessed to be children of our Venerable Father, Saint John of Rila the Wonderworker, the guardian angel of the Bulgarian people, our spiritual guide and our helper in every trial and difficulty along our journey towards the heavenly Jerusalem.

This year, we commemorated two significant anniversaries: 1,150 years since the birth and 1,080 years since the blessed repose of the most renowned and greatest Saint ever raised from among our people. The Holy Synod of the Bulgarian Orthodox Church – Bulgarian Patriarchate organised solemn celebrations in honour of these anniversaries.

At the invitation of Fortlumturia e Tij Daniel, Patriarch of Bulgaria, and the Holy Synod of the Bulgarian Orthodox Church – Bulgarian Patriarchate, a delegation of the First-Throned Ecumenical Patriarchate of Constantinople participated in these solemn celebrations, led by Tërëshenjtëria e Tij Ecumenical Patriarch Bartholomew.

The Divine Liturgy celebrated on 19 October of this year at the Holy Monastery of Rila by Patriarchs Bartholomew and Daniel, with the participation of Metropolitans and Bishops of the Patriarchates of Constantinople and Bulgaria, constituted the most profound expression of our shared love and veneration for the patron Saint of the entire Bulgarian nation, Saint John of Rila, and a testimony to our unity in Christ.

With pastoral concern, we address the clergy and the faithful in response to certain extreme attitudes, rash statements, and unjustified fears that have arisen on the occasion of this visit. We call upon everyone to exercise sobriety and discernment, and to refrain from passing judgement and drawing hasty conclusions.

We wish to remind everyone that the Bulgarian Orthodox Church – Bulgarian Patriarchate is in full Eucharistic and canonical communion with the Ecumenical Patriarchate of Constantinople, as well as with all the other Local Orthodox Churches. This communion is an expression of our unity in the Orthodox Faith and of our incorporation into the One, Holy, Catholic and Apostolic Church. Safeguarding this communion is the responsibility of us all.

Let us beware of misguided zeal for God (cf. Rom. 10:2). Sincere concern for the purity of the Faith is indeed a good thing; however, it must be accompanied by humility, profound knowledge, spiritual maturity and an awareness of the hierarchical order of the Church.

When zeal gives rise to suspicion, hostility and divisions among the faithful, we must all examine ourselves and seek guidance in the teachings and conciliar life of the Church. It is wholly unacceptable for Orthodox Christians to insult their chief shepherds, speak ill of their brothers and sisters, pronounce anathemas and assume the role of self-appointed judges.

In the Church, each person has his or her own place and ministry, “and one order must not displace another; rather, each must remain within his own order and fulfil his own ministry” (Saint Dionysius the Areopagite).

The responsibility of the clergy, to whom human souls have been entrusted, is particularly great. Their pastoral duty requires them to strengthen their spiritual children in the Faith, to listen attentively to their concerns and, with patience and discernment, to help them find answers, rather than inflaming passing emotions, sowing fear or turning them against one another.

The fostering of unfounded fears and anxieties, the fuelling of distrust towards the Church’s Authority, and the drawing of the faithful into confrontations can inflict profound wounds upon their spiritual lives. Let each of us remember the responsibility we bear before God for what we sow in the hearts of the human souls entrusted to our care.

Beloved children in the Lord,

We are called to safeguard the Orthodox Faith handed down to us and our ecclesiastical communion as the apple of our eye.

May our veneration of Saint John of Rila find its continuation in our own lives through following his example and embracing his spiritual legacy: steadfastness in the Faith, accompanied by humility, discernment, and spiritual obedience.

Through his intercessions, may the Lord grant us the grace to remain steadfast in the conciliar mind of the Church, strengthen the love we have for one another, and preserve the peace and unity of the Holy Church!

items.title_orig: Metropolitan of Nea Ionia: “The purpose for which we embarked on this journey 7,5 years ago has been fulfilled” (VIDEO)
items.sum:
Të martën mbrëma, përurimi zyrtar i Qendrës Jon u zhvillua në prani të arkipeshkopit Ieronimos II të Athinës dhe të gjithë Greqisë, përfaqësuesve të komuniteteve politike, sociale e të biznesit dhe një tubim të madh njerëzish.

Kjo qendër e re e adhurimit fetar, kulturës dhe kujtimeve historike u paraqit zyrtarisht në sallën e mbushur të Qendrës për Kulturën dhe Rininë, e cila ndodhet brenda kompleksit më të gjerë.

Metropoliti Gabriel i Nea Ionias, Filadelfias, Heraklionit dhe Kalcedonit, paraqiti vizionin prapa Qendrës Jon dhe udhëtimin drejt realizimit të saj.

Në fjalimin e tij, Metropoliti Gabriel pasqyroi edhe udhëtimin që kishte çuar në përfundimin e Qendrës Jon, duke shprehur mirënjohjen e tij për këdo që kishte kontribuar në ndërtimin e saj.

Kur, me anë të hirit të Perëndisë dhe nëpërmjet votimit të Hierakët e Shenjtë, dhe me nismën e Fortlumturia e Tij Ieronimos II, kryepeshkopi i Athinës dhe i gjithë Greqisë, unë erdha së pari në vitin 2014 në qytetin e madh të refugjatëve dhe në atdheun e refugjatëve, Nea Ionia, në mënyrë që të ndërmerrja shërbimin rajonal të këtij komuniteti të bekuar, unë arrita të kuptoja, të ndjeja, të përqafoja dhe të përqafoja një të vërtetë të thellë: të vërtetën dhe të ecja bashkë me kishën në dorë, për të krijuar atë që është më e mirë në interesat e njeriut.

Është në kujtim të këtyre njerëzve, në kujtim të viktimave të panumërta të Gjenocidit të grekëve të Azisë së Vogël, dhe me vëmendjen tonë të përqendruar fortësisht tek njeriu dhe nevojat e tyre, u krijua Qendra Jon e Kishës sonë lokale.

Para se të vazhdojmë me programin artistik që do të pasojë, më lejoni të shpreh, nga thellësia e zemrës sime, falenderimet e mia më të ngrohta dhe mirënjohjen e tyre për Fortlumturia e Tij Ieronimos II, arqipeshkopi i Athinës dhe i gjithë Greqisë, për mbështetjen e tij atërore dhe dashurinë me të cilën ai ka përqafuar gjithmonë kishën tonë lokale dhe punën e saj.
items.text_orig:
On Tuesday evening, the official inauguration of the Ionian Centre took place in the presence of Archbishop Ieronymos II of Athens and All Greece, representatives of the political, social and business communities, and a large gathering of people.

This new centre of religious worship, culture and historical remembrance was formally presented in the packed auditorium of the Centre for Culture and Youth, which is located within the wider complex.

Metropolitan Gabriel of Nea Ionia, Philadelphia, Heraklion and Chalcedon, presented the vision behind the Ionian Centre and the journey towards its realisation.

“The purpose for which we embarked upon this endeavour seven and a half years ago has now been fulfilled.” These were the opening words of Metropolitan Gabriel, whose voice conveyed deep emotion and evident pride. He went on to express his gratitude to all those who had contributed to the project, including benefactors, engineers and representatives of the political establishment and local government.

“You gave shape to a vision and brought it to life, delivering it to us in tangible form. I thank you most sincerely, from the bottom of my heart,” he emphasised.

A particularly moving moment came when Metropolitan Gabriel expressed his gratitude to businessman Mr Lavrentis Lavrentiadis for his invaluable contribution.

“With great affection and profound appreciation, I wish to extend my special thanks to my dear friend, my brother of many years, Chairman Mr Lavrentis Lavrentiadis, for his generous support, his friendship, his invaluable assistance, and for the unwavering support he has shown me throughout all these years of my journey.

My dear Lavrenti, we thank you very much indeed.”

Metropolitan Gabriel subsequently presented Mr Lavrentiadis with a commemorative award in recognition of his contribution.

In his address, Metropolitan Gabriel also reflected on the journey that had led to the completion of the Ionian Centre, expressing his gratitude to everyone who had contributed to its construction. He also spoke of the Centre’s distinctive character and its significance for the descendants of the Asia Minor refugees who live in the surrounding area.

“When, by the grace of God and through the vote of the Holy Hierarchs, and at the initiative of Fortlumturia e Tij Ieronymos II, Archbishop of Athens and All Greece, I first arrived in 2014 in the great refugee city and motherland of refugees, Nea Ionia, in order to undertake the pastoral ministry of this blessed community, I came to understand, to feel, to recognise and to embrace a profound truth: that ‘refugeehood’ and ‘the Church’ walk hand in hand and work together to create, always guided by what is in the best interests of the human person.

These are people who are poor and who have struggled throughout their lives to make ends meet, yet who possess an unwavering sense of pride and dignity, together with a profound faith in Christ and in their homeland.

They are people who were blessed with the privilege of carrying within them two homelands; people who, even to this day, keep alive the hope of return and vindication, with the keys to their ancestral homes in Asia Minor, Pontus and Eastern Thrace symbolising their unbreakable bond with the homelands they have never forgotten.

They are people who endured genocide, yet found the strength to rise again, rebuild their lives, establish families and enrich mainland Greece with the spirit, culture and traditions of Asia Minor.

It is in memory of these people, in remembrance of the countless victims of the Genocide of the Greeks of Asia Minor, and with our attention firmly focused on the human person and their needs, that the Ionian Centre of our local Church was created.

It is a place of worship, remembrance and culture; a place that brings together the historical legacy of the Greek refugee communities with the living presence of the Church in contemporary society.

It is a modern centre of pastoral ministry, where faith is translated into service, remembrance becomes a creative force, and tradition serves as a source of hope for future generations.

Yesterday, we celebrated the Thyranoixia (the ceremonial opening of the doors) of the new Holy Church of Saint George of Neapolis, the Newly Glorified Martyr and our city’s Patron Saint.

This morning, the first Divine Liturgy was celebrated in the home of our Saint.

And tonight, it is both right and fitting that we honour the individuals and organisations, as well as all those who played a decisive role in bringing this great undertaking to completion.

I must also extend a special word of thanks to my dear neighbours, who, for seven and a half years, demonstrated patience and understanding, enduring the disruption, noise and dust that inevitably accompanied the construction works.

I thank them wholeheartedly for their understanding and forbearance!

Before we proceed to the artistic programme that will follow, allow me to express, from the bottom of my heart, my warmest thanks and filial gratitude to Fortlumturia e Tij Ieronymos II, Archbishop of Athens and All Greece, for his paternal support and the love with which he has always embraced our local Church and its work.

Your Fortlumturia, Your presence and blessing strengthen and inspire us to continue our ministry in service of the human person and society.

I thank You most sincerely and humbly ask You to bestow Your blessing upon us.

May Saint George always be by Your side! And may he be with you all!

Shërbimi u vlerësua nga Metropolitani Antoni i Volokolamskut, kryetari i Departamentit të Patriarkatit të Moskës për Marrëdhëniet me Kishat e Jashtme, Metropolitan Siluani i Malit të Libanit, Metropolitani Antoni i Zahle dhe Baalbek dhe Metropolitani Nifoni i Filipopolis, përfaqësues i Patriarkatit të Antiokisë në Moskë.
items.text_orig:
A festive Divine Liturgy was celebrated on November 1, 2026, at the Church of the Annunciation in Jal El Dib, Lebanon, marking the 80th anniversary of the establishment of the Russian Orthodox Church’s representation in the country.

The service was concelebrated by Metropolitan Anthony of Volokolamsk, Chairman of the Moscow Patriarchate’s Department for External Church Relations, Metropolitan Silouan of Mount Lebanon, Metropolitan Anthony of Zahle and Baalbek, and Metropolitan Niphon of Philippopolis, representative of the Patriarchate of Antioch in Moscow.

Before the Liturgy, Metropolitan Anthony of Volokolamsk consecrated the church’s new iconostasis.

The service was celebrated in Arabic, Church Slavonic, and Slovak, with hymns performed by the Moscow Synodal Choir and the male choir of the Metropolis of Mount Lebanon.

Among those attending were Russian Ambassador Alexander Rudakov, Lebanese Defense Minister Michel Menassa, and former Russian Prime Minister Sergei Stepashin.

Following the Liturgy, Metropolitan Silouan read a message from Patriarch John X of Antioch, emphasizing the historic spiritual bonds between Antioch and Moscow.

“The bonds of faith uniting Antioch and Moscow cannot be broken by any trials of history,” the Patriarch stated, calling for continued cooperation and mutual prayer.

Metropolitan Anthony conveyed greetings from Patriarch Kirill of Moscow, describing the representation as a bridge between the two Patriarchates and a spiritual home for Russian-speaking Orthodox Christians in Lebanon.

The celebrations concluded with ecclesiastical awards, commemorative gifts, performances by parish children, and a concert by the Moscow Synodal Choir.

Një Liturgji solemne Hyjnore u kremtua sot, të martën, më 3 nëntor 2026, në Kishën e sapondërtuar të Shën Gjergjit të Neapopolit, shenjtor mbrojtës dhe mbrojtës i Nea Ionias, Athinë, në prani të presidentit të Republikës Helenike, Konstantinos Talulas.

Metropoliti Gabriel i Nea Ionias, Iraklio, Filadelfia dhe Kaldedoni.

Shërbimi shënon kulmin e festimeve që rrethojnë përurimin e Qendrës Jon, një kompleks i ri shpirtëror dhe kulturor, zemra e të cilit është Kisha e Shën Gjergjit të Neapolit, e përkujtuar nga Kisha Orthodhokse më 2 nëntor.

Presidenti grek: Qendra Jon ruan kujtesën e helenizmit të Azisë së Vogël dhe ofron shpresë për të ardhmen

Presidenti i Republikës Helenike Konstantinos Talulas ndoqi të martën, më 3 nëntor 2026, Liturgjinë hyjnore solemne në kishën e sapondërtuar të Shën Gjergjit të Neapopolit, shenjtori mbrojtës i Nea Ionias.

Sot është një ditë e madhe për rajonin, tha ai, duke iu referuar si kthimit të relikave të shenjta të Shën Xhorxhit të Neapolit, ashtu edhe për përurimit të Qendrës Jon.

Presidenti Talulas shprehu besimin se Qendra do të vazhdonte të lulëzonte nën mbrojtjen e Kishës, Perëndisë, bekime dhe mbështetjen e shtetit grek.

Festimet pasojnë transferimin solemn të relikave të shenjta të Shën Gjergjit të Neapolit të hënën pasdite, më 2 nëntor, nga Kisha e Shën Eustathios Martiri i Madh në Perisos, ku ato ishin mbajtur për dekada.

Gjatë procesionit, Metropolitani Gabriel shprehu emocionet e tij të thella në kthimin e Shën Gjergjit në atë që e përshkroi si shtëpinë e tij, duke theksuar domethënien frymore të rastit për Kishën lokale dhe besnikërinë e Nea Ionias.
items.text_orig:
A solemn Divine Liturgy was celebrated today, Tuesday, November 3, 2026, at the newly built Church of Saint George of Neapolis, patron saint and protector of Nea Ionia, Athens, in the presence of the President of the Hellenic Republic, Konstantinos Tasoulas.

The concelebrated Hierarchical Divine Liturgy was presided over by Metropolitan Gabriel of Nea Ionia, Iraklio, Philadelphia and Chalcedon. Metropolitan Maximos of Ioannina and Metropolitan Makarios of Aneon attended the service.

The service marks the culmination of celebrations surrounding the inauguration of the Ionian Center, a new spiritual and cultural complex whose heart is the Church of Saint George of Neapolis, commemorated by the Orthodox Church on November 2.

Among those attending the celebrations were Minister of Foreign Affairs George Gerapetritis, Minister of Labour Niki Kerameus, Minister of Health Adonis Georgiadis, Civil Administrator of Mount Athos and Honorary Chief of the Hellenic Army General Staff Alkiviadis Stefanis, and PASOK Member of Parliament Milena Apostolaki, alongside numerous clergy and faithful.

Greek President: Ionian Center preserves the memory of Asia Minor Hellenism and offers hope for the future

President of the Hellenic Republic Konstantinos Tasoulas attended the solemn Divine Liturgy at the newly built Church of Saint George of Neapolis, patron saint of Nea Ionia, on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, marking the inauguration of the Ionian Center.

In his remarks, the Greek President described the occasion as a historic moment for the region, emphasizing the religious, cultural, and national significance of the new complex.

“Today is a great day for the region,” he stated, referring both to the return of the holy relics of Saint George of Neapolis and to the inauguration of the Ionian Center.

President Tasoulas praised the completion of the church, which took six years to build, describing it as an architectural and spiritual achievement.

“This church took six years to complete. Today it radiates light. The light entering from every direction fills us with a sense of spiritual uplift,” he remarked.

He emphasized that the Ionian Center represents much more than a religious institution, describing it as a lasting legacy of faith, culture, national identity, and historical memory.

According to the President, the Center serves as a reminder of the suffering and displacement experienced by Greeks from Asia Minor, who were forced to abandon their ancestral homelands following the Asia Minor Catastrophe and subsequent persecutions.

He highlighted the resilience of the refugees who settled in Nea Ionia, rebuilt their lives, and contributed significantly to the development of the region.

“You have created a center that constitutes a religious, cultural, and national legacy, but above all, a legacy of memory,” he said.

The President stressed that preserving this historical experience is essential not only for honoring the past but also for inspiring future generations.

“The memory of yesterday’s hardships and trials gives us strength to face the present and, above all, to overcome difficulties and build a better tomorrow,” he noted.

He further emphasized that the Ionian Center is not merely a guardian of historical memory but also a source of inspiration and opportunity for young people.

“The Ionian Center is not only a guardian of memory. It is also a springboard for the future, for young people, for all those who believe in God,” he stated.

President Tasoulas expressed confidence that the Center would continue to flourish under the protection of the Church, God’s blessings, and the support of the Greek state.

He also paid tribute to the generosity of the Martinos family, thanking Mr. Martinos, his wife, and their family for their longstanding support of the Church and initiatives benefiting Greek society.

Concluding his remarks, the President expressed gratitude to the refugees who established new lives in Nea Ionia despite the hardships they endured.

He stressed that their struggles and sacrifices had laid the foundations for the prosperity of subsequent generations.

“We never forget our ancestral homelands: Ionia, Cappadocia, Eastern Rumelia, and Constantinople,” he declared.

Solemn transfer of the Holy Relics of St. George

The celebrations follow the solemn transfer of the holy relics of Saint George of Neapolis on Monday afternoon, November 2, from the Church of Saint Eustathios the Great Martyr in Perissos, where they had been kept for decades.

Thousands of faithful and local residents participated in the procession, which was led by the municipal band. Metropolitan Gabriel and other hierarchs accompanied the saint’s relics to their new resting place.

During the procession, Metropolitan Gabriel expressed his deep emotion at the return of Saint George to what he described as his “home,” highlighting the spiritual significance of the occasion for the local Church and the faithful of Nea Ionia.

Afterwards, a solemn Great Hierarchical Vespers service was celebrated at the new church.

Photo credit: Iasonas Tsolis/Orthodox Times

items.sum:
Një moment veçanërisht i rëndësishëm dhe historik për Metropolisin e Shenjtë të Nea Ionias, Filadelfias, Heraklionit dhe Kalkidonës u zhvillua të hënën pasdite.

Në prani të mijëra njerëzve besnikë, duke përfshirë banorët dhe adhuruesit nga i gjithë rajoni i Atikës, u bë përkthimi solemn i relikave të shenjta të Shën Xhorxhit të Neapolit këtë pasdite, në prag të festës së tij. Reliktet e tij të shenjta u transferuan nga Kisha e Shën Eustathios Martiri i Madh në Perisos, ku ishin mbajtur prej dekadash, në Kishën e sapondërtuar të Shën Gjergjit të Neapolisit, e cila ndodhet brenda Qendrës së Ilionit (141 Irakliu Avenu).

Reliktet e tij të shenjta u sollën nga Azia e Vogël nga refugjatët, të cilët kishin qenë të mbrojtur prej dekadash në kishën e Shën Eustathios në Nea Ionia, duke përbërë një thesar frymor të çmuar për Kishën lokale dhe për besimin e saj besnik.

Prania e relikave të shenjta të Shën Gjergjit të Neapopolit në kishën e re i jep Qendrës së re të Lionit një domethënie të thellë shpirtërore dhe historike, si nderim të këtij hieromartiri nga Azia e Vogël, ndërthuren me kujtimet, traditat dhe rrënjët e të parëve të familjeve refugjate të Nea Ionias.

Shih videon e transferimit të relikave të shenjta të Shën Xhorxhit të Neapolit dhe të shërbimit të hapjes së dyerve të kishës së re në Qendrën e Ionianëve të Metropolisit të Shenjtë të Nea Ionias
items.text_orig:
A particularly significant and historic moment for the Holy Metropolis of Nea Ionia, Philadelphia, Heraklion and Chalkidona took place on Monday afternoon.

In the presence of thousands of deeply moved faithful, including residents and worshippers from across the Attica region, the solemn translation of the sacred relics of Saint George of Neapolis took place this afternoon, on the eve of his feast day. His sacred relics were transferred from the Church of Saint Eustathios the Great Martyr in Perissos, where they had been kept for decades, to the newly built Church of Saint George of Neapolis, located within the «Ionian Centre» (141 Irakliou Avenue).

Immediately following the translation, a Solemn Hierarchical Great Vespers service was celebrated as part of the liturgical festivities honouring the Saint, who holds a special place in the ecclesiastical and refugee heritage of Nea Ionia.

Among those in attendance were Metropolitan Maximos of Ioannina, Metropolitan Makarios of Aneon, Abbot Alexios of the Holy Monastery of Xenophontos, Mount Athos Governor Alkiviadis Stefanis, Minister of Labour Niki Kerameus, Professor of Epidemiology Athina Linou, and Zafeiria Lavrentiadi.

Saint George of Neapolis, a priest originally from Neapolis in Asia Minor, is inextricably linked to the historical memory of the Asia Minor refugees. His sacred relics were brought from Asia Minor by the refugees’ ancestors and had been safeguarded for decades at the Church of Saint Eustathios in Nea Ionia, constituting a priceless spiritual treasure for the local Church and its faithful. Today’s translation to the new church marks a particularly symbolic milestone, bringing together the legacy of the refugee community and the living liturgical tradition of the local Church.

Tomorrow, Tuesday, November 3, the day on which the Church commemorates Saint George, the first Solemn Hierarchical Divine Liturgy will be celebrated at the new church, in the presence of the President of the Hellenic Republic, Konstantinos Tasoulas.

The “Ionian Centre”: A new home of faith, culture and social outreach

The “Ionian Centre” is a major undertaking of the Holy Metropolis of Nea Ionia, distinguished by its multifaceted spiritual, cultural and social mission. It is a modern complex that brings together Orthodox spirituality, education, culture and social outreach, aspiring to become a vibrant meeting place between the Church and society.

Among its facilities are the newly built Church of Saint George of Neapolis, a Conference and Youth Cultural Centre, a Hospitality Residence, a Nursery School, a Library, a Social and Recreational Club, as well as landscaped green spaces and recreational areas.

At the heart of the project’s vision are the preservation of the historical memory of Asia Minor, support for the younger generation and the strengthening of social cohesion. Through its facilities and activities, the “Ionian Centre” aspires to become a modern hub of culture, education and social service for the wider region.

The presence of the sacred relics of Saint George of Neapolis in the new church gives the “Ionian Centre” profound spiritual and historical significance, as veneration of this hieromartyr from Asia Minor becomes intertwined with the memory, traditions, and ancestral roots of the refugee families of Nea Ionia.

The festivities will conclude tomorrow, Tuesday, 3 November, at 7:00 p.m., with a special commemorative event in the Cultural and Youth Hall of the “Ionian Centre”, marking the official commencement of its operations.

Watch the video of the transfer of the sacred relics of Saint George of Neapolis and the Service of the Opening of the Doors of the new church at the “Ionian Centre” of the Holy Metropolis of Nea Ionia

items.text_orig:
The fifth edition of the Orthodox Festival “Wisdom of God” officially opened at the historic Metropolitan Cathedral of St. Sophia in Sofia, coinciding with the feast day of the Bulgarian National Enlighteners.

The festive event began with the blessing of Patriarch Daniel of Bulgaria. Among those in attendance were Bishop Ioan of Branitsa, First Vicar Bishop of the Metropolitan of Sofia, together with numerous clergy and a large gathering of devout faithful. The event was hosted by Nadezhda Panayotova.

The first of the Festival’s three days was dedicated to spiritual literature. Following a performance by the choir of the Church of the Protection of the Most Holy Theotokos in Sofia, conducted by Dimitar Stoyanov, a discussion was held on the theme: “Day of the National Enlighteners – Presenting New Publications.”

The discussion featured Protopresbyter Professor Stoyan Tsilikov, Doctor of Theology; Anula Hristova, representative of the Publishing House of the Holy Synod; and representatives of other Orthodox publishing houses. The discussion was moderated by Angel Karandakоv.

As part of the Festival, an extensive collection of Orthodox books published by various publishing houses is also on display and available for purchase at the church.

The programme’s remaining two days will be dedicated, respectively, to spiritual culture and the education of children. The scheduled discussions, both beginning at 6:30 p.m., will address the following themes: “Blessed Labour – The Human Being as a Co-Creator” and “How Does One Become an Enlightener?”

Photos: Kaloyan Petrov

items.title_orig: Patriarch of Antioch: Brotherhood between Antioch and Moscow cannot be broken
items.sum:
Patriarku Xhon X i Antiokisë dhe i gjithë Lindjes ripohuan lidhjet shpirtërore historike midis patriarkatëve të Antiokisë dhe Moskës në një mesazh të botuar më 1 nëntor 2026, gjatë Liturgjisë Hyjnore që shënon 80 vjetorin e vendosjes së përfaqësimit të Kishës Orthodhokse Ruse në Liban.

Ai kujtoi se lidhjet midis Antiokisë dhe Rusisë para vendosjes së përfaqësimit rus në Beirut, në maj 1946, duke theksuar kontributin historik të Antiokut në përhapjen e krishterimit në Kiev dhe ngritjen e Patriarkatit të Moskës.

Ai e përshkroi përfaqësimin orthodhoks rus në Beirut si një shtëpi shpirtërore për të krishterët orthodhoksë që flasin rusisht, të cilët e kanë bërë Libanin atdheun e tyre të dytë.
items.text_orig:
Patriarch John X of Antioch and All the East reaffirmed the historic spiritual ties between the Patriarchates of Antioch and Moscow in a message delivered on November 1, 2026, during the Divine Liturgy marking the 80th anniversary of the establishment of the Russian Orthodox Church’s representation in Lebanon.

Although unable to attend in person, Patriarch John emphasized his spiritual presence through prayer and reflected on the centuries-old relationship between the two Churches.

He recalled that the bonds between Antioch and Russia predate the establishment of the Russian representation in Beirut in May 1946, highlighting Antioch’s historical contribution to the spread of Christianity in Kyiv and the establishment of the Moscow Patriarchate.

The Patriarch also praised Russia’s educational and charitable contributions to the Middle East, noting that, beginning in 1882, the Imperial Orthodox Palestine Society established more than 70 schools in Lebanon and Syria, educating approximately 10,000 children.

He described the Russian Orthodox representation in Beirut as a spiritual home for Russian-speaking Orthodox Christians who have made Lebanon their second homeland.

Patriarch John also highlighted the influence of Russian saints on Antiochian Orthodox spirituality, particularly Saint Seraphim of Sarov, Saint John of Kronstadt, and Saint Luke the Surgeon.

“The brotherhood of faith between Antioch and Moscow cannot be broken by the upheavals of history,” he declared, calling for stronger cooperation through mutual prayer and service to those who suffer.

He expressed gratitude to Patriarch Kirill of Moscow, Metropolitan Anthony of Volokolamsk, and the Russian delegation attending the anniversary celebrations.

Concluding his message, Patriarch John prayed for the unity of the Russian Orthodox Church and peace for its people, asking God to protect the Churches from division and preserve the unity of the Body of Christ.

He also prayed for Lebanon and the wider Middle East, expressing hope that the Russian Orthodox representation in Beirut would continue to serve as a beacon of love and prayer.

items.title_orig: Patriarchate of Antioch marks 80th Anniversary of Russian Orthodox Church representation in Beirut
items.sum:
Patriarku Xhon X i Antiokisë dhe i gjithë Lindjes mori një delegacion nga Kisha Orthodhokse Ruse në Balamand më 31 tetor 2026, si pjesë e festimeve që shënojnë 80 vjetorin e ngritjes së përfaqësimit të Kishës Orthodhokse Ruse në Beirut.

Delegacioni u kryesua nga Metropolitani Antoni i Volokolamsk, kryetari i Departamentit për Marrëdhëniet me Kishën e Jashtme të Patriarkatit të Moskës, shoqëruar nga Kryepriftëritori Nikolai Balashov, këshilltar i Patriarkut Kirill të Moskës dhe të gjithë Rusisë.
items.text_orig:
Patriarch John X of Antioch and All the East received a delegation from the Russian Orthodox Church at Balamand on October 31, 2026, as part of celebrations marking the 80th anniversary of the establishment of the Russian Orthodox Church’s representation in Beirut.

The delegation was led by Metropolitan Anthony of Volokolamsk, Chairman of the Department for External Church Relations of the Moscow Patriarchate, accompanied by Archpriest Nikolai Balashov, adviser to Patriarch Kirill of Moscow and All Russia.

Also attending the meeting were former Russian Prime Minister Sergei Stepashin, President of the Imperial Orthodox Palestine Society, and Alexander Rudakov, Ambassador of the Russian Federation to Lebanon.

Discussions focused on the longstanding historical and fraternal relations between the Patriarchate of Antioch and the Russian Orthodox Church, as well as ways to further strengthen cooperation between the two Churches.

The participants also exchanged views on the current situation facing Christians and broader issues concerning relations among the Churches.

The anniversary celebrations continued with a joint musical evening at Balamand, featuring performances by the Moscow Synodal Choir and the Choir of the Saint John of Damascus Institute of Theology.

items.title_orig: Archbishop of Cyprus gives Tychikos ten days to meet before Holy Synod takes action
items.sum:
Kryepeshkopi Georgios i Qipros i ka dhënë Tichikos afërsisht dhjetë ditë për të rregulluar një takim me të, duke paralajmëruar se Sinodit të Shenjtë do t'i drejtohet çështjes nëse nuk bëhet përparim.

Duke folur me gazetarët pas një shërbimi përkujtimor për kryepeshkopin e ndjerë Krisostomos II, kryepeshkopi Georgios theksoi se Kisha e Qipros nuk mund të mbetet në një gjendje të gjatë pasigurie.

Ai shpjegoi se Tichikos fillimisht kishte kërkuar një takim nëpërmjet ndërmjetësve përpara sesionit të fundit të Sinodit të Shenjtë.

" Kisha nuk mund të vazhdojë të jetojë me këtë pasiguri, tha kryepeshkopi Georgios, duke theksuar se edhe një peshkop i pezulluar mbetet përgjegjës për Sinodin e Shenjtë.
items.text_orig:
Archbishop Georgios of Cyprus has given Tychikos approximately ten days to arrange a meeting with him, warning that the Holy Synod will reconvene to address the matter if no progress is made.

Speaking to journalists following a memorial service for the late Archbishop Chrysostomos II, Archbishop Georgios stressed that the Church of Cyprus cannot remain in a prolonged state of uncertainty.

He explained that Tychikos had initially requested a meeting through intermediaries before the Holy Synod’s recent session. Although the Archbishop agreed, Tychikos reportedly failed to respond after returning to Cyprus.

“The Church cannot continue living with this uncertainty,” Archbishop Georgios stated, emphasizing that even a suspended bishop remains accountable to the Holy Synod.

He reiterated that decisions concerning Church governance are taken collectively, declaring: “It is not one person who governs the Church, but the Synod.”

The Archbishop also outlined the conditions under which Tychikos could be offered a position within the Holy Archdiocese.

These include formally renouncing positions questioning the orthodoxy of the Ecumenical Patriarch and rejecting the Holy and Great Council of Crete.

According to Archbishop Georgios, Tychikos must also withdraw allegations of financial irregularities within the Metropolis and formally clarify his position through an ecclesiastical declaration.

Addressing reports about Tychikos’ health, the Archbishop revealed that the Holy Synod had received a fax stating that he was unable to travel to Cyprus due to illness and medical advice to avoid emotionally distressing situations.

He questioned how Tychikos subsequently managed to return to Cyprus despite those reported restrictions.

Archbishop Georgios concluded that the Church would await a concrete response before determining its next steps.

Source: sigmalive.com

items.title_orig: Metropolitan of Corfu inaugurated Ukrainian Monastic House in Corfu at Metropolitan Onufriy’s request
items.sum:
Metropoliti Nektashrios i Korfuzit, Paksos dhe ishujve Diapontian përuruan një shtëpi të re monaste në Korfuz të shtunën, më 31 tetor 2026, me kërkesën dhe me bekimin e Metropolitanit Onufri, Primate i Kishës Orthodhokse ukrainase (UOC).

Sipas një deklarate nga Kisha Orthodhokse Ukrainase, Metropolitane Onufrii dhe Metropolitane Agathangjelos të Odesës bënë të mundur shtëpinë e manastirit, me bekimin e metropolitanit Nektashit të Korfuzit.

Shtatë hierarki të kishës orthodhokse ukrainase ndoqën ceremoninë, duke përfshirë Metropolitan Klementin e Nizhit dhe Prylukit dhe Metropolitan Filaret të Lvivit dhe Galicia, së bashku me pelegrinë të shumtë ukrainas.
items.text_orig:
Metropolitan Nektarios of Corfu, Paxos and the Diapontian Islands inaugurated a new monastic house in Corfu on Saturday, October 31, 2026, at the request and with the blessing of Metropolitan Onufriy, Primate of the Ukrainian Orthodox Church (UOC).

The monastic house includes a chapel dedicated to the Venerable Fathers of the Kyiv Caves Lavra and is located near the Church of Saint Spyridon in Corfu.

According to a statement from the Ukrainian Orthodox Church, Metropolitan Onufriy and Metropolitan Agathangelos of Odesa made the monastic house possible, with the blessing of Metropolitan Nektarios of Corfu.

The inauguration coincided with celebrations marking the 975th anniversary of the founding of the Kyiv Caves Lavra.

Seven hierarchs of the Ukrainian Orthodox Church attended the ceremony, including Metropolitan Clement of Nizhyn and Pryluky and Metropolitan Filaret of Lviv and Galicia, alongside numerous Ukrainian pilgrims.

The service was celebrated in Greek, Church Slavonic, Ukrainian, and Romanian, while hymns were performed by the Byzantine Choir of the Metropolis of Corfu and a monastic choir from Ukraine.

On Sunday, November 1, a Divine Liturgy was celebrated in the newly inaugurated chapel, presided over by Metropolitan Clement of Nizhyn and Pryluky, with the participation of other Ukrainian Orthodox hierarchs.

Following the Divine Liturgy, ecclesiastical distinctions were awarded to benefactors who contributed to the initiative.

The Ukrainian pilgrims also participated in the traditional procession of the sacred relics of Saint Spyridon through the streets of Corfu.

items.title: Patriarch of Romania: The Romanian people have a vocation for hesychasm
items.summary: The Romanian Orthodox Church held its inaugural National Church Assembly meeting in Bucharest on Wednesday, establishing the body that will serve as one of the Church’s central deliberative authorities for the 2026–2030 term. Bishop Iachint of the Pacific, Assistant Bishop of…
items.text:
The Romanian Orthodox Church held its inaugural National Church Assembly meeting in Bucharest on Wednesday, establishing the body that will serve as one of the Church’s central deliberative authorities for the 2026–2030 term.

Bishop Iachint of the Pacific, Assistant Bishop of the Romanian Orthodox Diocese of Australia and New Zealand, led a Te Deum service in the Europa Christiana Hall of the Palace of the Patriarchate.

Romanian Orthodox hierarchs attended the service in person, while members of the National Church Assembly followed the prayers via a video projection in the Patriarch Teoctist Aula Magna.

Patriarch of Romania reflects on the day’s saints

Patriarch Daniel then opened the inaugural meeting of the National Church Assembly in the Aula Magna, in the presence of Romanian Orthodox hierarchs.

“We have offered a common Te Deum today, as could be heard in the prayers that were read. It is very important that we carry out every work in the Church in this spirit of communion in the grace of the Most Holy Trinity,” Patriarch Daniel said.

Fortlumturia e Tij went on to deliver a spiritual address about the saints commemorated that day and the historical period in which they lived.

“We commemorate two great saints who intercede in heaven, St Hyacinth of Vicina and St Theophano Basarab. We pray that they will bless the proceedings establishing the National Church Assembly and the work of the Holy Synod,” Patriarch Daniel said.

He recalled that St Hyacinth established the Metropolis of Wallachia during the 14th-century hesychast movement, which also included members of Wallachia’s ruling family.

“Metropolitan Hyacinth of Vicina was a hesychast, and the children of Prince Basarab I, especially St Theodora, who later became the nun Theophano, were devoted to prayer,” Patriarch Daniel explained.

“This shows us that the Romanian people have a vocation for hesychasm, which would manifest itself to varying degrees throughout history, in different periods, up to the 18th century, when Neamț Monastery had more than 1,000 monks from several countries, most of them predominantly Orthodox.”

Romanian Orthodox Christians’ important role in worldwide Orthodoxy

“As the French theologian Olivier Clément states in the preface to the French edition of the Philokalia, it was precisely during this period of extensive secularisation of minds and hearts in Western Europe that the Holy Fathers, in the 18th century, rediscovered the importance of the Philokalic writings,” Patriarch Daniel emphasised.

Fortlumturia e Tij recalled the Paisian movement, which Romanian monks supported in spreading the Slavonic translation of the Philokalia.

He also highlighted the scholarly and spiritual work of St Dumitru Stăniloae the Confessor, who interpreted the Philokalia for contemporary readers.

These developments, Patriarch Daniel explained, demonstrate that Romanian Orthodox Christians have played an important role in preserving and promoting the spiritual heritage of worldwide Orthodoxy.

What is the National Church Assembly?

The National Church Assembly is a central deliberative body of the Romanian Orthodox Church responsible for administrative, social, cultural, economic and property-related matters.

It consists of three representatives from each diocese — one cleric and two laypeople — delegated by their respective Diocesan Assemblies for four-year terms.

Representatives may serve a maximum of two terms.

The President of the National Church Assembly is the Patriarch of Romania. Members of the Holy Synod also participate in its proceedings.

The Church’s other central deliberative bodies are the Holy Synod and the Permanent Synod.

Photo credit: Basilica / Mircea Florescu

items.title_orig: WHO Regional Director for Europe Hans Kluge visits Georgian Patriarchate
items.text_orig:
Dr. Hans Kluge, Regional Director of the World Health Organization (WHO) for Europe and a candidate for the position of WHO Director-General, visited the Georgian Patriarchate in Tbilisi on Friday, October 30, 2026.

The visit took place as part of Dr. Kluge’s official trip to Georgia in connection with his campaign for the leadership of the World Health Organization.

The meeting was attended by Bishop Grigol (Katsia) of Tsalka; Archpriest Mikael Botkoveli, Secretary to the Catholicos-Patriarch of All Georgia; Archpriest Andria Jaghmaidze, Head of the Patriarchate’s Public Relations Department; Archpriest Archil Khachidze, Deputy Head of the Patriarchate’s Department of Foreign Affairs; and Archimandrite Adam (Akhaladze), Rector of the Patriarchate’s St. Queen Tamar University.

During the meeting, Dr. Kluge presented his vision for the future of global healthcare and outlined the priorities and initiatives included in his electoral platform.

The discussion provided an opportunity for the WHO official to share his plans for the development of the global health system with representatives of the Georgian Orthodox Church.

The representatives of the Patriarchate thanked Dr. Kluge for his visit and wished him success in the upcoming election for WHO Director-General.

Source: Georgian Patriarchate, Photo: Nino Sozashvili

items.text_orig:
Archbishop Georgios of Cyprus received Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas during his visit to Cyprus, with the two leaders holding a meeting at the Archbishop’s office.

Welcoming the Palestinian President, Archbishop Georgios expressed his pleasure at the visit and highlighted the historical, religious, and cultural ties between Cyprus and Palestine.

The Archbishop emphasized the significance of the Christian holy sites and religious monuments in Palestine, noting their importance to the Greek Orthodox tradition and the longstanding connections between the two peoples.

He also referred to what he described as ancestral ties between Palestinians and Crete, presenting the two peoples as historically related.

For his part, President Mahmoud Abbas thanked Archbishop Georgios for his warm welcome and recalled the close relationship between the late Archbishop Makarios III of Cyprus and Yasser Arafat, the historic leader of the Palestine Liberation Organization.

The meeting highlighted the longstanding relations between Cyprus and Palestine, particularly their historical connections and shared religious heritage.

At the conclusion of their discussions, Archbishop Georgios and President Abbas exchanged gifts.

Source: ant1live.com

items.title_orig: Archbishop of Cyprus expected to meet former Metropolitan Tychikos
items.text_orig:
Archbishop Georgios of Cyprus is expected to meet with former Metropolitan Tychikos of Paphos in the coming days, following mediation efforts aimed at resolving the ongoing ecclesiastical dispute.

Speaking on SIGMA television’s Protoselido program, Archdiocese spokesperson Christakis Efstathiou confirmed that the Holy Synod had been informed of an initiative to arrange a private meeting between the two hierarchs.

During the Synod’s recent session, a letter from Tychikos was read aloud, in which he expressed reservations about his situation and maintained that he had been treated unfairly.

“The further course of events will depend on this meeting,” Efstathiou stated, describing the initiative as a significant development.

Although no date has been set, the meeting is expected to take place soon. Efstathiou expressed hope for a positive outcome, stressing that the prolonged dispute has caused fatigue among the faithful and that restoring calm within the Church is essential.

However, he remained cautious, recalling that previous attempts at reconciliation had failed despite commitments and assurances made before the Holy Synod.

According to the spokesperson, a central issue will be whether Tychikos accepts his status as a bishop and the responsibilities associated with it, including recognition of the authority of the Holy Synod and the principle of synodality.

Should an agreement be reached, Efstathiou suggested that Tychikos could be assigned episcopal duties acceptable to both sides.

He further clarified that, following the anticipated meeting with Archbishop Georgios, Tychikos is expected to appear before the Holy Synod to personally inform its members of the outcome.

The proposed meeting is seen as a potentially important step toward resolving the dispute and restoring stability within the Church of Cyprus.

Source: sigmalice.com , translated by: Konstantinos Menyktas

items.title: Patriarch of Alexandria concludes official visit to Angola
items.summary: Pope and Patriarch Theodore II of Alexandria and All Africa concluded his official visit to Angola on Thursday, October 29, 2026, with the celebration of the Divine Liturgy at the chapel of the Honorary Consulate of Greece in Luanda. The Divine Liturgy was celebrated in Greek…
items.text:
Pope and Patriarch Theodore II of Alexandria and All Africa concluded his official visit to Angola on Thursday, October 29, 2026, with the celebration of the Divine Liturgy at the chapel of the Honorary Consulate of Greece in Luanda.

The Divine Liturgy was celebrated in Greek and Portuguese, bringing together members of the small Greek Orthodox community, local catechumens, a representative of the Angolan government, and a Roman Catholic bishop.

The occasion also provided an opportunity to commemorate Greece’s national holiday of October 28, marking the historic “Ohi” of 1940.

Addressing those gathered, Patriarch Theodore expressed his joy at meeting members of the Greek community in Angola and emphasized the importance of preserving Orthodox faith, patriotism, and national identity among Greeks living abroad.

The visit held particular personal significance for the Patriarch, who returned to places associated with his early episcopal ministry in Africa, when he served as Metropolitan of Zimbabwe and Angola.

Among those attending were Greek Ambassador to the Democratic Republic of the Congo, concurrently accredited to Angola, Antonios Papadopoulos, and Honorary Consul of Greece in Angola Georgios Dosopoulos. The Patriarch thanked both diplomats for their contribution to the successful organization of his pastoral visit.

During his stay in Angola, Patriarch Theodore also held important institutional meetings, including talks with Angolan President João Lourenço, and participated in pastoral and charitable activities.

The visit concluded with renewed prospects for strengthening the spiritual, missionary, and social presence of the Patriarchate of Alexandria in Angola, as well as promoting cooperation and dialogue with local authorities and communities.

items.title: Romanian Orthodox children celebrate Queen Marie’s ties to Malta at Presidential Palace
items.summary: Queen Marie of Romania was commemorated on 24 October at San Anton Palace, Malta’s Presidential Palace, during an event hosted by President Myriam Spiteri Debono and attended by members of the Romanian community and children from the Romanian Orthodox Parish School in Valletta…
items.text:
Queen Marie of Romania was commemorated on 24 October at San Anton Palace, Malta’s Presidential Palace, during an event hosted by President Myriam Spiteri Debono and attended by members of the Romanian community and children from the Romanian Orthodox Parish School in Valletta, the Maltese capital.

Those attending included Assistant Bishop Maxim of Danubius of the Romanian Orthodox Diocese of Italy; Eugen Roșca, Minister Plenipotentiary at the Romanian Embassy in Italy, which is also accredited to Malta and San Marino; Lino Bianco, former Maltese Ambassador to Romania and current Ambassador of Malta to Bosnia and Herzegovina; Fr George-Alexandru Popescu, parish priest of the Romanian Orthodox community of St John the Baptist in Valletta; and members of the Romanian community.

The event, entitled Queen Marie of Romania – Faith, Family and Identity: A Bridge Between Romania and Malta, was held under the patronage of the President of Malta and commemorated the 140th anniversary of Queen Marie of Romania’s arrival in Malta in 1886.

Faith is passed on within the family

Assistant Bishop Maxim of Danubius conveyed a message of blessing and gratitude on behalf of Bishop Siluan of Italy, thanking those who support the Romanian community.

The bishop emphasised that, in a world marked by individualism and increasingly fragile human relationships, the family remains a community of life and love, blessed by God, in which faith, responsibility, forgiveness and communion are cultivated.

“Children learn to pray by watching their parents pray, and they discover God’s love through the love they receive.”

The bishop also recalled the witness of the Myrrh-Bearing Women, the holy women martyrs, venerable monastic women and Christian mothers.

He stressed that holiness is the calling of every Christian and can be cultivated both in monastic life and within the family, through prayer, raising children and serving others.

A moment of cultural diplomacy

A highlight of the event was the cultural and artistic programme prepared by children from the Romanian Orthodox parish.

Dressed in traditional Romanian costumes, they presented aspects of Romania and Malta’s shared history in Maltese and English, alongside songs and other artistic performances.

“Through presentations in Maltese and English, tailored for children, as well as traditional Romanian attire and music, the event celebrated the values ​​of family, faith, hospitality, cultural heritage, and the friendship between Malta and Romania,” President Myriam Spiteri Debono wrote on Facebook .

Parish priest Fr George-Alexandru Popescu presented the President of Malta with an icon of the Holy Great Martyr George.

The project and the local parish

The event formed part of a wider project funded by Romania’s Department for Romanians Abroad, entitled Romanian Identity and Culture in the Diaspora in Malta.

The project also provides for the distribution of 400 Romanian cultural identity packages, intended to help preserve and promote the Romanian language, culture and traditions among diaspora communities.

The Romanian Orthodox Parish in Valletta, dedicated to the Nativity of St John the Baptist, worships at St Rocco Church on St Ursula Street.

Fr George-Alexandru Popescu also occasionally celebrates services at St Enrico Mizzi in Ir-Rabat (Victoria), on the island of Gozo.

This was the fourth time that children from Malta’s Romanian Orthodox community had been invited to San Anton Palace.

A former President of Malta also visited the Romanian Orthodox parish in Valletta, describing the Romanian community as an example of successful integration.

Around Christmas 2024, children from the Romanian Orthodox parish school in Valletta sang Christmas carols at the palace’s Orthodox chapel, known as the Russian Chapel, a place associated with Queen Marie of Romania’s childhood.

Queen Marie and Malta

The chapel served as a place of prayer for Grand Duchess Maria Alexandrovna of Russia and her daughter, Princess Marie of Edinburgh, the future Queen Marie of Romania, during the family’s holidays in Malta.

Queen Marie, granddaughter of Queen Victoria of the United Kingdom and Tsar Alexander II of Russia, first arrived in Malta at age 11.

Her father, Alfred, Duke of Edinburgh, was then commander of the British Mediterranean Fleet.

Queen Marie remembered Malta fondly, describing it as “the paradise of our childhood”.

In her memoirs, she recalled the beauty of the gardens of San Anton Palace, filled with flowers, particularly daffodils and orange trees in blossom, whose fragrance delighted her.

Source: Basilica.ro / Photo credit: Bellizzi Photo Studio

items.title: Romanian Orthodox Holy Synod warns against heretical and schismatic groups posing as Orthodox
items.summary: The Holy Synod of the Romanian Orthodox Church expressed concern over the activities of heretical and schismatic groups presenting themselves as Orthodox during its meeting on Thursday, October 29, 2026, chaired by Patriarch Daniel of Romania at the Patriarchal Palace in…
items.text:
The Holy Synod of the Romanian Orthodox Church expressed concern over the activities of heretical and schismatic groups presenting themselves as Orthodox during its meeting on Thursday, October 29, 2026, chaired by Patriarch Daniel of Romania at the Patriarchal Palace in Bucharest.

The Synod warned that these groups conduct religious services resembling those of the Orthodox Church while improperly using Orthodox ecclesiastical titles, vestments, liturgical practices, and icons, creating confusion among the faithful.

According to the Synod, such groups also solicit donations for the construction of places of worship and for social and religious activities, potentially misleading believers about their ecclesiastical affiliation.

In response, the Holy Synod instructed diocesan authorities to undertake local pastoral initiatives aimed at informing the faithful about the risks of participating in or joining groups falsely claiming to be Orthodox.

The Synod emphasized the importance of maintaining full communion with the canonical Orthodox Church and observing the canonical traditions established by the Holy Fathers.

During the same meeting, the Synod also approved a draft Pastoral Code of Responsible Communication, bringing together existing regulations governing public communication by clergy.

Other decisions included designating 2028 as a commemorative year dedicated to the use of biblical texts in the Church’s liturgical life and to translators and printers of biblical and liturgical books, as well as reviewing pastoral initiatives concerning foreign Orthodox Christians and immigrants living in Romania.

Source: Basilica.ro

items.title_orig: Patriarchate of Georgia: We were not consulted on casino bill and “cannot stand aside”
items.text_orig:
“The legislative initiative on casinos came as a complete surprise to us, as there was no prior communication with the Patriarchate on the matter,” said Archpriest Andria Jaghmaidze, head of the Patriarchate’s Public Relations Service.

Jaghmaidze stated that since 2017, the Georgian Patriarchate has actively initiated and served as a primary participant in the process of drafting and implementing gambling regulations.

“Work on this issue went on for several years. On the Patriarchate’s side, the process was led by Shio III, Catholicos-Patriarch of All Georgia, who was then Locum Tenens of the Patriarchal Throne. A number of studies were conducted, with the resulting statistical data collected, analysed, and shared with the public. In the end, the government adopted a whole package of regulations, which was very welcome.

As for the current legislative initiative, it came as a complete surprise to us. There was no prior communication with the Patriarchate on the matter. The Patriarchate hasn’t yet fully discussed this issue, but let me assure you: the Patriarchate cannot simply stand by during such a process.

We have read the Public Defender’s position, and I personally largely share her arguments. We hope that dialogue with the authors of the bill will produce a positive outcome,” Archpriest Jaghmaidze said.

Parliament has passed the amendments to the Law on Organising Lotteries, Gambling and Other Prize Games at third reading.

Source: 1tv.ge

items.title: Patriarch of Alexandria visits an Orphanage in Angola
items.summary: Some places never fade from memory, and faces remain indelibly etched upon the heart and mind, no matter how many years may pass or how far life’s journey may lead us. One such deeply moving moment unfolded on Wednesday, October 28, 2026, during the official visit of Pope and…
items.text:
Some places never fade from memory, and faces remain indelibly etched upon the heart and mind, no matter how many years may pass or how far life’s journey may lead us.

One such deeply moving moment unfolded on Wednesday, October 28, 2026, during the official visit of Pope and Patriarch Theodore II of Alexandria and All Africa to Angola.

Despite His exceptionally demanding schedule, which includes important meetings and official engagements, the Patriarch wished to travel many kilometres beyond the capital, Luanda, in order to visit an orphanage with which He shares deep bonds of love, remembrance and service.

This is a place He visited and actively supported more than twenty-two years ago, during His ministry as Metropolitan of Zimbabwe and Angola, when His care for children and those in need was an integral part of His daily pastoral ministry.

The children of that time have now grown up and embarked upon their own paths in life. Yet the place remains familiar, and those who continue to be associated with the institution still recall with deep emotion the presence, concern, and love shown by Metropolitan Theodore at that time.

More than two decades later, the Patriarch returned to the same place, now bearing the responsibility of steering the entire Church of Alexandria and All Africa, yet preserving unchanged the same fatherly tenderness, the same simplicity and the same love for every human being.

During His visit, He spent time with the children, spoke with them, shared moments of joy and offered them His fatherly love and blessing. For a brief while, away from the formality of official meetings, His presence became a living expression of the Church that embraces, comforts, and stands alongside every person, especially those most in need of love and care.

This is the beauty of true pastoral ministry: responsibilities may expand, and concerns may multiply, yet the heart remains ever close to the people it once embraced. The years may pass, and circumstances may change, but the faces and places to which love was once given are never forgotten.

Today’s visit to the orphanage was not merely a return to a familiar place. It was a quiet testament to steadfastness, humanity, and genuine pastoral love. It served as a reminder that missionary work cannot be measured solely by the churches that are built or the projects that are accomplished, but also by the hearts missionaries touch, the tears they wipe away, the hope they offer, and the bonds that remain alive throughout the passage of time.

The love of Christ never forgets, never abandons, and never ceases to give.

In the person of Pope and Patriarch Theodore II of Alexandria and All Africa, we see the living continuation of a missionary journey spanning many years, founded upon selfless service and love for humanity expressed through concrete acts of compassion. His presence today in a place so closely connected with the early years of His pastoral ministry in Angola demonstrates that, despite the weight of His patriarchal responsibilities and the demands of daily life, personal care for each human being remains His unwavering priority.

For Patriarch Theodore, missionary work has never been merely an ecclesiastical duty, but a way of life, one He continues to serve with the same faith, devotion, and love.

items.title_orig: Archbishop of Athens: The message of October 28 belongs above all to the future
items.text_orig:
Archbishop Ieronymos of Athens and All Greece emphasized the importance of historical remembrance, national unity and hope for future generations in a statement marking Greece’s national holiday of October 28.

Reflecting on the historic events of 1940, the Archbishop stressed the need to preserve the memory of those who fought and sacrificed their lives for Greece’s freedom, while highlighting unity as one of the Greek people’s greatest strengths.

“My wish is that we remember those who fought and sacrificed themselves for our freedom. Unity, because it has been the great strength of the Greek people during the most difficult moments of their history,” he stated.

Archbishop Ieronymos emphasized that the significance of October 28 extends beyond commemorating the past, carrying a message of responsibility toward future generations.

“Hope, because the message of October 28 belongs not only to the past, but above all to the future that we must build, especially for our children,” he said.

Concluding his message, the Archbishop expressed his hope that remembrance, unity and optimism would continue to guide Greek society.

“I wholeheartedly wish that we honor the past with dignity, face the present with unity, and look toward the future with hope. Many happy and blessed returns to us all,” he concluded.

Photo: Rafail Georgiadis/EUROKINISSI

items.title_orig: Greece marks Ohi Day with official doxology at Athens Metropolitan Cathedral (VIDEO)
items.text_orig:
An official Doxology service was held at the Metropolitan Cathedral of Athens on Wednesday, October 28, 2026, to commemorate the 86th anniversary of Greece’s historic “Ohi” (No) of 1940.

The service was celebrated by Bishop Barnabas of Christoupolis, Protosyncellus of the Holy Archdiocese of Athens, while Protopresbyter Thomas Synodinos, Dean of the Metropolitan Cathedral, served as master of ceremonies.

The Greek government was represented by Minister of Education, Religious Affairs and Sports Sofia Zacharaki, while the Hellenic Parliament was represented by its President, Nikitas Kaklamanis.

Also attending were Athens Mayor Haris Doukas, Deputy Regional Governor of Attiki Christina Kefalogianni, Vice Chief of the Hellenic National Defence General Staff Vice Admiral Theodoros Mikropoulos, and representatives of political parties in the Hellenic Parliament.

Military honor guards were stationed outside the cathedral, while adverse weather conditions across Attiki limited public attendance.

As part of the national commemorations, a wreath-laying ceremony was also held at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier in Syntagma Square, honoring those who fought and sacrificed their lives for Greece’s freedom.

The celebrations marking the 86th anniversary of the historic “Ohi” also included the traditional student parade in front of the Hellenic Parliament.

October 28 commemorates Greece’s rejection of an Italian ultimatum in 1940, marking the country’s entry into World War II and symbolizing the Greek people’s resistance against fascist aggression.

items.title: Patriarch of Alexandria met with the President of the Republic of Angola
items.summary: As part of His official visit to the Republic of Angola, Pope and Patriarch Theodore II of Alexandria and All Africa was warmly received today, Tuesday, 27 October 2026, in the nation’s capital, Luanda, by João Lourenço, President of the Republic of Angola, in an atmosphere of…
items.text:
As part of His official visit to the Republic of Angola, Pope and Patriarch Theodore II of Alexandria and All Africa was warmly received today, Tuesday, 27 October 2026, in the nation’s capital, Luanda, by João Lourenço, President of the Republic of Angola, in an atmosphere of cordiality and mutual respect.

The Patriarch was accompanied by Antonios Papadopoulos, Ambassador of the Hellenic Republic to the Democratic Republic of the Congo, concurrently accredited to the Republic of Angola, and Mr. Georgios Dossopoulos, Honorary Consul of Greece in Angola.

The meeting held particular significance for the Alexandrian Primate, as Angola occupies a special place in His heart, having forged a profound connection with the country during His pastoral ministry as Metropolitan of Zimbabwe and Angola. This personal bond, His intimate understanding of the circumstances prevailing in the country, and the meaningful relationship He had established with its people lent the visit a distinctive emotional and spiritual significance.

During their discussions, the two leaders addressed matters of mutual interest, with particular emphasis on the prospects for developing the Orthodox Church’s presence in Angola and expanding the multifaceted ministry of the Patriarchate of Alexandria.

The Patriarch presented the Patriarchate’s vision and strategic plans to President João Lourenço for organizing and consolidating its ecclesiastical presence in the country, expanding its missionary outreach, promoting education and charitable work, and implementing social and humanitarian initiatives. He emphasized that the Church of Alexandria wishes to stand alongside the people of Angola in tangible and practical ways, offering spiritual guidance, social support, and meaningful relief to those in need, without discrimination or exclusion.

The Patriarch emphasized the historical identity and mission of the Patriarchate of Alexandria, one of the oldest ecclesiastical institutions in Christendom, historically based in Egypt and entrusted with pastoral responsibility throughout the African continent. The Patriarch highlighted the enduring witness of the Church of Saint Mark, which, from its historic seat in Alexandria, reaches out to all the peoples of Africa, proclaiming the message of the Gospel and fostering peace, brotherhood, and mutual respect.

During the meeting, the Patriarch expressed His profound gratitude to Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, President of the Arab Republic of Egypt, for his steadfast and substantive support for the Patriarchate of Alexandria and its wide-ranging ministry. He commended the Egyptian President’s efforts to safeguard peace and stability and to promote religious coexistence and mutual respect. At the same time, He underscored Egypt’s importance as the historic cradle of the Patriarchate and as a steadfast point of reference for the continuation and fulfillment of its ecclesiastical mission throughout Africa.

The Patriarch also conveyed His heartfelt thanks to the Government of Greece for its longstanding solidarity with and tangible support for the Patriarchate of Alexandria. He stressed that this support makes a substantial contribution to the continuation of the Alexandrian Church’s ministry, through which it serves the peoples of the African continent with respect for their history, culture, and distinctive traditions.

For his part, the President of the Republic of Angola warmly thanked the Patriarch for His visit and expressed his profound esteem. He also demonstrated keen interest in the initiatives and plans presented, expressing a positive attitude toward the prospect of developing the Patriarchate’s ecclesiastical, missionary, and humanitarian work in the country.

During the discussion, the President referred to the friendly relations between Angola and Egypt, emphasizing the importance of further strengthening bilateral cooperation. He also announced his intention to undertake an official visit to Egypt in the near future.

As the culmination of the meeting, the Patriarch bestowed upon the President of the Republic of Angola the Grand Cross of Saint Mark the Holy and Glorious Apostle and Evangelist. The distinction was conferred as an expression of honor and gratitude for the cordial reception extended to the Patriarch and for the President’s expressed willingness to contribute to the development of the Alexandrian Church’s presence and ministry in Angola.

This distinguished honor carried particular symbolic significance, reflecting the shared aspiration to cultivate deeper and more substantive relations of cooperation, centered on service to humanity, social solidarity, the defense of noble ideals, and the peaceful coexistence of peoples.

This historic visit by the Patriarch of Love to Angola marks the beginning of a new chapter in the presence and witness of Orthodoxy in the country. It reaffirms that the Patriarchate of Alexandria and All Africa, faithful to its apostolic heritage, continues to forge new paths of faith, build bridges between peoples, and translate the message of the Gospel into tangible expressions of love, service, and generosity toward every human being.

items.title_orig: Church of Cyprus: Reports of plans for separate Ecclesiastical Structure
items.text_orig:
New tensions have emerged within the Church of Cyprus following reports of efforts to establish a separate ecclesiastical structure and allegations that Divine Liturgies are being celebrated in a private residence in Paphos.

According to the Cypriot newspaper Phileleftheros , a letter signed by five individuals has reportedly been circulated among priests in Paphos and other districts, encouraging them to leave the Church of Cyprus and join a new ecclesiastical organization opposed to decisions of the Holy Synod.

The initiative is reportedly linked to supporters of apotichisis (separation from ecclesiastical authorities), who oppose the removal and suspension of former Metropolitan Tychikos of Paphos.

The letters are believed to have been circulating for approximately three months, while the Holy Synod has reportedly been monitoring the situation without intervening.

Meanwhile, the newspaper reports that a priest from a Slavic country has been celebrating Divine Liturgies, including the Eucharist, at a private residence in Paphos belonging to a supporter of the former Metropolitan.

These gatherings are reportedly associated with opposition to the appointment of Bishop Gregory to the metropolitan throne of Paphos.

However, there is no evidence linking Tychikos himself to the reported efforts to establish a separate Church.

Former Metropolitan Tychikos Summoned Before Holy Synod

Against this backdrop, Tychikos has been summoned to appear before the Holy Synod on Tuesday, October 27.

Although the precise reasons for the summons have not been disclosed, the proceedings are believed to concern his refusal to sign a declaration of faith in the form requested by the Synod.

According to Phileleftheros , Tychikos had not confirmed whether he would attend. However, in a letter dated October 14, 2026, he reportedly raised several procedural concerns and outlined conditions regarding any further appearance before the Holy Synod.

Translated by: Konstantinos Menyktas

Patriarch John X of Antioch and All the East has sent a message of condolence to Patriarch Theophilos III of Jerusalem following the martyrdom of the faithful in the church in Karak.

In his message, the Patriarch stated:

“It was with profound sorrow and grief that I received the news of the tragic incident at the church in Karak. We unite our prayers with yours, beseeching Christ our God to have mercy on this suffering East.

On my own behalf and on behalf of the faithful of the Greek Orthodox Church of Antioch and All the East, both in its historic homeland and throughout the diaspora, I extend my heartfelt condolences to you and to our brothers in the Church of Jerusalem.

I pray that the Almighty Lord will enfold the martyrs of this heinous attack in His mercy, grant divine consolation to their bereaved families, and bestow healing upon the injured.”
